```text
1	# Context
2	
3	`dev` already presents tasks as `HOT / WARM / COLD / DONE`, but the legal edges and their preconditions are distributed across `park`, `resume`, `done`, `retire`, `adopt`, `wt rm`, `sweep`, and a separate dashboard Park callback. Completion filters suggest the intended graph, yet explicitly named tasks can currently traverse undocumented paths such as `DONE -> HOT` or `DONE -> WARM`. At the same time, checkout dirtiness, publication, worktree registration, runtime/agent occupancy, artifact readiness, merge evidence, and PR observability are not lifecycle states; they are live facts with independent freshness and failure modes.
4	
5	Build an experimental, independent `dev flow [repo]` TUI that makes this model visible and actionable. The selected product shape is:
6	
7	- context-aware repository startup;
8	- every registered worktree plus managed tasks with no checkout;
9	- full guarded apply for the normal managed lifecycle;
10	- separate Adopt / Remove Checkout actions for unmanaged worktrees;
11	- no coupling to the existing six-view dashboard model;
12	- local-only startup and `r` refresh, with remote work only after an explicit action;
13	- `HOT / WARM / COLD / DONE` remain the only persisted task states.
14	
15	The implementation must first advance this no-ahead feature branch from v0.2.2 to the v0.2.3 `main` baseline, preserving the existing `.specstory` working-tree files. The v0.2.3 generation/cancellation/readiness infrastructure should be reused rather than reimplemented.
16	
17	## Product and interaction model
18	
19	### Hybrid state machine
20	
21	Model three layers explicitly:
22	
23	1. **Recorded intent** — task mode, `HOT / WARM / COLD / DONE`, owner, next action, branch/base, and expected checkout.
24	2. **Observed facts** — checkout identity/registration, dirty/conflicted/Git-operation state, upstream and ahead/behind with freshness, local containment in an explicit base, runtime sessions, recognized agents, artifact readiness, and remote/review capability. Every fact is `known`, `unknown`, `error`, `skipped`, or `loading`; failed probes must never become false/clean/closed.
25	3. **Guarded actions** — legal source/target edge, required inputs, conditions, blockers/remediation, ordered effects, retained/removed resources, confirmation class, and exact fallback CLI command.
26	
27	`READY` is action readiness, `REVIEW` is a state-preserving handoff/result, `MERGED` is DONE plus named ancestry evidence, and `RETIRED` is successful task removal. They are overlays/milestones, not new TOML states.
28	
29	Encode one mode-aware transition table and enforce it in the shared service and every CLI/TUI caller:
30	
31	- worktree/branch: `HOT|WARM -> WARM` (park warm), `HOT|WARM -> COLD` (park cold), `WARM|COLD -> HOT` (resume), `HOT|WARM -> DONE` (directly integrated or verified merged), `DONE -> RETIRED`;
32	- direct: `HOT|WARM -> WARM` (warm park), `WARM -> HOT` (resume), `HOT|WARM -> DONE` (direct completion), `DONE -> RETIRED`; direct never becomes COLD;
33	- review handoff from HOT/WARM pushes/opens review but preserves the current state;
34	- COLD must resume before completion; DONE cannot park/resume/complete;
35	- reconciliation is a named action, not an undocumented backward transition.
36	
37	### Repository rows
38	
39	Identify repositories by canonical Git common directory and checkouts by canonical registered path. The repository screen is the exact union of authoritative `git worktree list --porcelain` records and unresolved/task-only records:
40	
41	- **canonical** — the worktree Git marks Main, regardless of branch name; never removable;
42	- **managed checkout** — exactly one valid task binding; receives lifecycle actions;
43	- **unmanaged checkout** — registered non-main, non-harness worktree; receives Inspect/Open, Adopt, and guarded Remove Checkout (branch always retained);
44	- **harness checkout** — strict canonical containment under `.claude/worktrees`; visible and openable, never adoptable/removable from this UI;
45	- **cold task / done task** — no checkout is expected; still visible for Resume or Retire;
46	- **drift/conflict** — stale path, branch/mode mismatch, duplicate claims, incomplete inventory, missing registration, or harness overlap; visible but fail-closed except for a narrowly proven reconciliation.
47	
48	Bind a task exactly once: exact canonical worktree path first, then a unique branch match only when the recorded path is absent/stale; branch/direct tasks normally bind only to the canonical row on the live branch. Preserve ambiguity instead of guessing.
49	
50	### Screen and keys
51	
52	- In a canonical or linked checkout, `dev flow` opens that canonical repository and focuses the exact current surface. Outside Git, it asynchronously opens a repository picker. `dev flow <repo>` overrides cwd. An unconfigured current repository is still inspectable.
53	- Layout: worktree/task rows on the left; mode-aware lifecycle rail and evidence in the center; candidate actions and selected condition details on the right, stacking on narrow terminals.
54	- Up/down or `j/k` changes rows; left/right or `h/l` changes actions; Tab changes pane; Enter opens a plan and never mutates immediately; a second action-specific confirmation applies; Esc backs out; `r` reloads local facts; `R` opens a remote menu for **Fetch refs**, **Refresh PR/MR**, or **Both**; `?` shows evidence/key semantics; `q` exits.
55	- Render text labels as well as color: READY, NEEDS INPUT, BLOCKED, UNKNOWN, ERROR, STALE, DRIFT.
56	- “Close” is not a lifecycle node. A DONE managed task offers Retire; an unmanaged row offers Remove Checkout; runtime closure is an effect of those plans. Branch deletion is a separately confirmed managed-retirement variant only.
57	- Startup/local refresh never fetches or contacts a forge. Network work may be a declared effect of Resume, cold push, review handoff, or a confirmed `R` choice. A manual provider query records only a portable minimum—PR/MR existence, open/draft/merged/closed state, URL, provider, and observation time. Unsupported, unauthenticated, failed, and not-yet-refreshed review evidence remains explicitly UNKNOWN; review/check details not consistently available across providers are not inferred.
58	
59	## Implementation
60	
61	### 0. Reconcile the v0.2.3 baseline
62	
63	- Record and preserve the current `.specstory/statistics.json` and `.specstory/history/...` changes; do not clean, overwrite, or use an ambiguous shared stash.
64	- Fast-forward the no-ahead feature branch to `main`/v0.2.3 with `git merge --ff-only main`; stop rather than resolve any unexpected local-file collision automatically.
65	- Run the v0.2.3 TUI loader/readiness/trace race tests before feature edits.
66	
67	### 1. Add revision-aware task writes and pure safety observations
68	
69	Extend `internal/task/store.go` without changing task TOML:
70	
71	- return `Record{Task, Revision}` where Revision hashes the exact record bytes and ID;
72	- expose list diagnostics instead of printing/skipping corrupt records invisibly;
73	- add cross-process locked create-only, compare-and-update, and compare-and-delete transactions using `internal/lockx`;
74	- make existing Save/Delete compatibility methods participate in the same lock, while new lifecycle code uses revision-aware transactions.
75	
76	Make planning side-effect-free and preserve observation failures:
77	
78	- split pure artifact readiness/receipt inspection from artifact finalization/reconciliation;
79	- extend runtime inspection to retain runtime-list/agent-list capability and errors and to use live recognized-agent observations;
80	- add exact worktree path/branch/HEAD/Main/locked/prunable lookup helpers;
81	- keep existing no-data-loss behavior: normal TUI removal is non-force, dirty/uncommitted and unresolved artifact state block, and caller/mixed-runtime protections remain absolute. Writer claims and adoption fail closed on any other recognized agent regardless of displayed status; removal/retirement keeps the existing action-specific policy—active or unrecognized agents block, idle/done agents may be externally closed after structural checks, and unknown status requires an explicit external CLI acknowledgement.
82	
83	### 2. Make repository topology authoritative
84	
85	Refactor `internal/inventory/repo_context.go` around a topology skeleton plus bounded enrichment:
86	
87	- always use Git’s worktree records for the selected repository, including bare worktree hubs; retain Git’s real Main record instead of synthesizing one from a navigation path;
88	- add stable RepoKey/RowKey values, typed observation completeness/errors, task binding, ownership evidence, drift/conflict reasons, and task-only rows;
89	- use canonical common-directory identity for repository/task joins and preserve unresolved task groups;
90	- use a strict path-based harness detector; a `worktree-` branch prefix may warn but is not ownership proof;
91	- preserve runtime unavailable/failed separately from “closed.”
92	
93	Reuse `gitx.Discover`, `pathx.Canonical`, `gitx.Worktrees`, `inventory.RepoContext`, and the v0.2.3 shared limiter. Add a dedicated context resolver because existing `FindByWorktree` can choose the wrong canonical task and existing repo helpers lose linked-worktree focus.
94	
95	### 3. Create the single `internal/taskflow` authority
96	
97	Add a UI-agnostic domain package with value-only, copy-safe types:
98	
99	- `Locator`, `Action`, action-specific options, `Observation`, `Condition`, `Effect`, `Plan`, `Approval`, `StepResult`, `Handoff`, and `Result`;
100	- `Plan` contains the exact task revision, source/target state, exact repo/path/branch/base/upstream identities, blockers, inputs, ordered effects, retained resources, confirmation requirement, fallback command, and an authority fingerprint/PlanID;
101	- `Result` records every attempted/completed effect, partial success, warnings/recovery, milestone, optional post-alt-screen handoff, and a fresh after-snapshot.
102	
103	The service exposes context/repository inspection plus `Plan(Request)` and `Apply(Plan, Approval)`. `Apply` must:
104	
105	1. validate the approved PlanID/typed confirmation;
106	2. lock by canonical repo and task in a fixed order;
107	3. reload the task revision and freshly re-resolve Git/worktree/runtime/agent/artifact/remote identity;
108	4. reject a changed authority fingerprint before mutation;
109	5. execute in the existing no-data-loss order, repeating safety-critical checks after runtime closure and immediately before removal;
110	6. persist task state/path last where applicable;
111	7. return a step ledger and fresh snapshot on success or error.
112	
113	Reuse rather than duplicate:
114	
115	- `gitx.AnalyzeFinish` and its fingerprint for completion;
116	- `retire.Inspect` / `CloseAndWait` and `retire.Service` ordering, refactoring them into mechanisms whose caller-supplied identity is re-derived by taskflow;
117	- `wt.Manager.Create` for COLD resume reconstruction;
118	- `experiment.TransitionPlan/Result` and lock/revalidation patterns;
119	- existing runtime-handle coverage, artifact, Git-operation, and branch-containment checks after moving them out of CLI-local policy.
120	
121	Implement the selected action sets:
122	
123	- managed: Park Warm/Cold (including explicit WIP/push options), Resume, Direct/FF/Review/Verify-Merged completion, and Retire with optional contained-branch deletion;
124	- unmanaged: metadata-only Adopt and exact branch-preserving Remove Checkout;
125	- drift: only typed, proven reconciliation plans; prunable/missing registrations remain inspect/recovery-only because Git prune is repository-wide;
126	- remote: an explicit Refresh action with independent `FetchRefs` and `QueryReview` options, so the `R` menu can run either or both and return separate outcomes/freshness;
127	- no generic TUI force. Existing CLI compatibility flags (`--force`, `--close-unknown`, `--assume-no-runtime`, fetch defaults, etc.) remain supported and map to explicit typed options/confirmations; this feature does not silently change command syntax or defaults.
128	
129	Extend `internal/forge` with a query-oriented, capability-aware review boundary shared by GitHub, GitLab, and Azure adapters. Resolve by canonical remote identity plus exact head/base branch, normalize only the portable status fields (existence, state, draft, URL, provider, observed time), and preserve ambiguous/multiple matches and CLI/auth/provider failures as typed UNKNOWN/ERROR evidence. Keep review observations in the flow model for the current run; do not add a persistent cache or infer a PR from a pushed branch.
130	
131	### 4. Cut existing mutation paths over before exposing the TUI
132	
133	Refactor these callers into parse/render/confirm adapters over taskflow, preserving documented output, flags, direct-vs-report behavior, and non-interactive compatibility:
134	
135	- `internal/cli/park.go`, `resume.go`, `done_flow.go`, `retire.go`, `adopt.go`, and `worktree.go` (`wt rm` only);
136	- overlapping state/removal suggestions in `internal/cli/sweep.go`, replacing captured mutable closures with frozen plans revalidated at apply time and removing synthetic DONE authorization for unmanaged worktrees;
137	- the existing dashboard’s Park callback and lifecycle-relevant SetNext write in `internal/cli/tui.go`.
138	
139	Do not pull `dev start`, `wt create`, repo sync, configurable tools, notes, stats, or dashboard layout into this feature. Add an architecture/boundary test that prevents CLI/TUI handlers from directly assigning lifecycle state, deleting lifecycle tasks, closing runtimes, or removing worktrees on these migrated paths.
140	
141	### 5. Build the independent `internal/flowtui`
142	
143	Create a small Bubble Tea model with injected callbacks for launch resolution, repository load/enrichment, Plan, and Apply. Do not embed or add a mode to `internal/tui.Model`.
144	
145	Reuse the v0.2.3 protocols as patterns:
146	
147	- return the first View before repository/runtime/Git work starts;
148	- monotonically tagged request generations plus cancellation and stale-result rejection;
149	- valid-empty replacement and stale snapshot retention;
150	- stable RowKey/TaskID selection so a COLD task follows its rebuilt checkout;
151	- one shared runtime snapshot and bounded per-surface enrichment;
152	- expensive finish/removal/remote probes only for the selected action.
153	
154	Read generations never authorize Apply. A mutation is bound to exact identities, cannot be canceled/discarded by refresh or row switching, disables conflicting actions while running, renders its partial-result ledger, then starts a fresh local generation. Directory/runtime activation occurs only after Bubble Tea leaves the alternate screen.
155	
156	Add `internal/cli/flow.go` and register visible, preview-labelled `dev flow [repo]` through the v0.2.3 `newRootCommand(app)` seam. Treat `flow` as a full-screen command for deferred release checks and privacy-safe TUI tracing. Reject non-TTY invocation before emitting control sequences, with a pointer to non-interactive inventory commands.
157	
158	### 6. Synchronize user-facing contracts
159	
160	- Add the feature to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`; do not commit, push, tag, or publish a release unless separately requested.
161	- Update README, root/embedded help, `internal/skill/dev-cli/SKILL.md`, authored task-lifecycle/worktree-ownership/runtime-retirement references, and generated command help via `make skill-sync`.
162	- Add paired English/zh-TW repository-flow documentation and update mental-model, workflow, TUI, compatibility, and source-freshness pages where they describe lifecycle/cleanup authority.
163	- Document row taxonomy, local/remote freshness, the manual Git/forge remote menu, portable PR/MR fields and UNKNOWN/error semantics, branch-preserving removal, partial results, confirmation rules, and that raw Git/configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated safety.
164	
165	## Critical files
166	
167	- `internal/taskflow/{types,service,transitions,park,resume,complete,adopt,remove,retire}.go` — one graph/plan/apply authority.
168	- `internal/task/store.go` — locked raw-revision create/update/delete.
169	- `internal/inventory/repo_context.go` — authoritative all-worktree plus task-only projection.
170	- `internal/retire/{safety,service}.go`, `internal/artifact/service.go`, `internal/gitx/worktree.go` — reusable safety mechanisms and pure observations.
171	- `internal/forge/{forge,github,gitlab,azure}.go` — capability-aware manual PR/MR lookup and normalized review evidence.
172	- `internal/flowtui/{model,load,actions,overlay,view}.go` — independent interaction/rendering only.
173	- `internal/cli/{flow,park,resume,done_flow,retire,adopt,worktree,sweep,tui}.go` — thin adapters and command registration.
174	
175	## Verification
176	
177	1. **Transition and condition matrices**
178	   - Exhaustively test every checkout mode × recorded state × action; reject direct+COLD, DONE park/resume/complete, COLD complete, and other undocumented explicit-task paths before any effect.
179	   - Test READY/NEEDS INPUT/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN/ERROR aggregation; required unknown/error can never enable Apply.
180	
181	2. **Identity, topology, and binding**
182	   - Cover canonical/linked/nested cwd, symlink aliases, same-name clones, unconfigured repos, separate-git-dir and bare hubs, detached/locked/prunable/missing rows, exact-once Git records, task-only COLD/DONE rows, moved paths, wrong branches, duplicate task claims, and harness conflicts.
183	   - Assert canonical Main is never removable and incomplete inventory can never prove “unmanaged.”
184	
185	3. **Plan/apply race and no-data-loss tests**
186	   - Mutate task revision/state/path, worktree registration/path/branch/HEAD, dirty/conflict/Git-operation state, artifact receipts, runtime sessions/current pane/agent activity, and base/upstream refs between Plan and Apply and again after runtime closure.
187	   - Assert stale plans perform zero effects; unmanaged removal preserves branch ref/OID; completion never removes runtime/worktree/branch; retirement deletes task last; partial failures report completed stages and yield a safe retry plan.
188	   - Cover runtime none/list failure, caller/mixed sessions, and every recognized-agent status under both policies: all statuses block writer/adopt claims; active/unrecognized block cleanup, idle/done may be safely closed, and unknown requires the existing external acknowledgement. Also cover close failure, timeout, and session reappearance.
189	
190	4. **CLI parity and architecture boundary**
191	   - Preserve focused tests for park/resume/done/retire/adopt/wt rm/sweep and dashboard Park while asserting they call the same taskflow plans.
192	   - Add a source/AST boundary test for migrated handlers and compatibility tests for existing flags/output/structured contracts.
193	
194	5. **Flow TUI behavior**
195	   - Model tests for picker/filter/focus, row/action navigation, blocked-plan inspection, action-specific confirmations, stale generation rejection, valid-empty and stale retention, stable selection after COLD resume, in-flight result retention, narrow/monochrome rendering, and deferred handoff.
196	   - PTY test: immediate first frame and clean quit while context/runtime/topology/enrichment are blocked.
197	   - Instrument network fakes: startup and `r` make zero fetch/forge calls; only a confirmed network-bearing transition or `R` does. Test Fetch-only, PR/MR-only, and Both; normalize GitHub/GitLab/Azure results; retain separate success/error/freshness when one half fails; and treat zero, ambiguous, unsupported, unauthenticated, and stale results truthfully.
198	
199	6. **End-to-end and repository gates**
200	   - In an isolated HOME, display canonical/managed/unmanaged/harness/COLD rows; adopt an eligible external checkout; run HOT → WARM → HOT → DONE → Retire; verify branch retention; exercise manual Git/PR refresh; and prove canonical/harness/active-agent/stale-plan attempts make no unauthorized change.
201	   - Run focused race tests, `go test -race ./...`, formatting check, `go vet ./...`, build, `make e2e`, `make skill-sync`, `make skill-check`, and strict bilingual MkDocs/source/site checks.
202	   - Run an independent safety/code review after implementation and address confirmed findings before declaring the feature complete.
```

380	1	# Context
381	2	
382	3	`dev` already presents tasks as `HOT / WARM / COLD / DONE`, but the legal edges and their preconditions are distributed across `park`, `resume`, `done`, `retire`, `adopt`, `wt rm`, `sweep`, and a separate dashboard Park callback. Completion filters suggest the intended graph, yet explicitly named tasks can currently traverse undocumented paths such as `DONE -> HOT` or `DONE -> WARM`. At the same time, checkout dirtiness, publication, worktree registration, runtime/agent occupancy, artifact readiness, merge evidence, and PR observability are not lifecycle states; they are live facts with independent freshness and failure modes.
383	4	
384	5	Build an experimental, independent `dev flow [repo]` TUI that makes this model visible and actionable. The selected product shape is:
385	6	
386	7	- context-aware repository startup;
387	8	- every registered worktree plus managed tasks with no checkout;
388	9	- full guarded apply for the normal managed lifecycle;
389	10	- separate Adopt / Remove Checkout actions for unmanaged worktrees;
390	11	- no coupling to the existing six-view dashboard model;
391	12	- local-only startup and `r` refresh, with remote work only after an explicit action;
392	13	- `HOT / WARM / COLD / DONE` remain the only persisted task states.
393	14	
394	15	The implementation must first advance this no-ahead feature branch from v0.2.2 to the v0.2.3 `main` baseline, preserving the existing `.specstory` working-tree files. The v0.2.3 generation/cancellation/readiness infrastructure should be reused rather than reimplemented.
395	16	
396	17	## Product and interaction model
397	18	
398	19	### Hybrid state machine
399	20	
400	21	Model three layers explicitly:
401	22	
402	23	1. **Recorded intent** — task mode, `HOT / WARM / COLD / DONE`, owner, next action, branch/base, and expected checkout.
403	24	2. **Observed facts** — checkout identity/registration, dirty/conflicted/Git-operation state, upstream and ahead/behind with freshness, local containment in an explicit base, runtime sessions, recognized agents, artifact readiness, and remote/review capability. Every fact is `known`, `unknown`, `error`, `skipped`, or `loading`; failed probes must never become false/clean/closed.
404	25	3. **Guarded actions** — legal source/target edge, required inputs, conditions, blockers/remediation, ordered effects, retained/removed resources, confirmation class, and exact fallback CLI command.
405	26	
406	27	`READY` is action readiness, `REVIEW` is a state-preserving handoff/result, `MERGED` is DONE plus named ancestry evidence, and `RETIRED` is successful task removal. They are overlays/milestones, not new TOML states.
407	28	
408	29	Encode one mode-aware transition table and enforce it in the shared service and every CLI/TUI caller:
409	30	
410	31	- worktree/branch: `HOT|WARM -> WARM` (park warm), `HOT|WARM -> COLD` (park cold), `WARM|COLD -> HOT` (resume), `HOT|WARM -> DONE` (directly integrated or verified merged), `DONE -> RETIRED`;
411	32	- direct: `HOT|WARM -> WARM` (warm park), `WARM -> HOT` (resume), `HOT|WARM -> DONE` (direct completion), `DONE -> RETIRED`; direct never becomes COLD;
412	33	- review handoff from HOT/WARM pushes/opens review but preserves the current state;
413	34	- COLD must resume before completion; DONE cannot park/resume/complete;
414	35	- reconciliation is a named action, not an undocumented backward transition.
415	36	
416	37	### Repository rows
417	38	
418	39	Identify repositories by canonical Git common directory and checkouts by canonical registered path. The repository screen is the exact union of authoritative `git worktree list --porcelain` records and unresolved/task-only records:
419	40	
420	41	- **canonical** — the worktree Git marks Main, regardless of branch name; never removable;
421	42	- **managed checkout** — exactly one valid task binding; receives lifecycle actions;
422	43	- **unmanaged checkout** — registered non-main, non-harness worktree; receives Inspect/Open, Adopt, and guarded Remove Checkout (branch always retained);
423	44	- **harness checkout** — strict canonical containment under `.claude/worktrees`; visible and openable, never adoptable/removable from this UI;
424	45	- **cold task / done task** — no checkout is expected; still visible for Resume or Retire;
425	46	- **drift/conflict** — stale path, branch/mode mismatch, duplicate claims, incomplete inventory, missing registration, or harness overlap; visible but fail-closed except for a narrowly proven reconciliation.
426	47	
427	48	Bind a task exactly once: exact canonical worktree path first, then a unique branch match only when the recorded path is absent/stale; branch/direct tasks normally bind only to the canonical row on the live branch. Preserve ambiguity instead of guessing.
428	49	
429	50	### Screen and keys
430	51	
431	52	- In a canonical or linked checkout, `dev flow` opens that canonical repository and focuses the exact current surface. Outside Git, it asynchronously opens a repository picker. `dev flow <repo>` overrides cwd. An unconfigured current repository is still inspectable.
432	53	- Layout: worktree/task rows on the left; mode-aware lifecycle rail and evidence in the center; candidate actions and selected condition details on the right, stacking on narrow terminals.
433	54	- Up/down or `j/k` changes rows; left/right or `h/l` changes actions; Tab changes pane; Enter opens a plan and never mutates immediately; a second action-specific confirmation applies; Esc backs out; `r` reloads local facts; `R` opens a remote menu for **Fetch refs**, **Refresh PR/MR**, or **Both**; `?` shows evidence/key semantics; `q` exits.
434	55	- Render text labels as well as color: READY, NEEDS INPUT, BLOCKED, UNKNOWN, ERROR, STALE, DRIFT.
435	56	- “Close” is not a lifecycle node. A DONE managed task offers Retire; an unmanaged row offers Remove Checkout; runtime closure is an effect of those plans. Branch deletion is a separately confirmed managed-retirement variant only.
436	57	- Startup/local refresh never fetches or contacts a forge. Network work may be a declared effect of Resume, cold push, review handoff, or a confirmed `R` choice. A manual provider query records only a portable minimum—PR/MR existence, open/draft/merged/closed state, URL, provider, and observation time. Unsupported, unauthenticated, failed, and not-yet-refreshed review evidence remains explicitly UNKNOWN; review/check details not consistently available across providers are not inferred.

```text
244	func (s *lifecycleService) observeCheckout(ctx context.Context, request Request, observed *lifecycleObservation) {
245		switch observed.mode {
246		case task.ModeBranch, task.ModeDirect:
247			registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.repoPath)
248			observed.worktree, observed.worktreeErr = registered, err
249			if err == nil {
250				observed.worktreeFound = true
251				observed.checkout = registered.Path
252			}
253		case task.ModeWorktree:
254			if observed.task.WorktreePath != "" {
255				registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.WorktreePath)
256				observed.worktree, observed.worktreeErr = registered, err
257				if err == nil {
258					observed.worktreeFound = true
259					observed.checkout = registered.Path
260				}
261			}
262			if observed.worktreeFound || request.Action != Resume ||
263				(observed.task.State != task.Warm && observed.task.State != task.Cold) {
264				return
265			}
266			worktrees, err := s.gitWorktrees(ctx, observed.repoPath)
267			if err != nil {
268				observed.worktreeErr = fmt.Errorf("list worktrees for parked-task resume: %w", err)
269				return
270			}
271			var candidate string
272			for _, worktree := range worktrees {
273				if worktree.Branch == observed.task.Branch {
274					observed.branchMatches++
275					candidate = worktree.Path
276				}
277			}
278			switch observed.branchMatches {
279			case 0:
280				if observed.worktreeErr == nil {
281					observed.worktreeErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: branch %s has no checkout", gitx.ErrWorktreeNotFound, observed.task.Branch)
282				}
283			case 1:
284				registered, resolveErr := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, candidate)
285				observed.worktree, observed.worktreeErr = registered, resolveErr
286				if resolveErr == nil {
287					observed.worktreeFound = true
288					observed.checkout = registered.Path
289				}
290			default:
291				observed.worktreeErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: branch %s has %d registered checkouts", gitx.ErrWorktreeAmbiguous, observed.task.Branch, observed.branchMatches)
292			}
293		}
294	}

296	func validateLiveLocator(locator Locator, observed lifecycleObservation) error {
297		if observed.statusErr == nil && observed.hasCheckout() {
298			checks := []struct {
299				name     string
300				expected string
301				actual   string
302				required bool
303			}{
304				{"upstream", locator.Upstream, observed.status.Upstream, true},
305				{"HEAD", locator.HeadOID, observed.head, locator.HeadOID != ""},
306				{"base OID", locator.BaseOID, observed.baseOID, locator.BaseOID != ""},
307				{"upstream OID", locator.UpstreamOID, observed.upstreamOID, locator.UpstreamOID != ""},
308			}
309			for _, check := range checks {
310				if check.required && check.expected != check.actual {
311					return &StalePlanError{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("selected %s changed from %q to %q", check.name, check.expected, check.actual)}
312				}
313			}
314			return nil
315		}
316		if !observed.hasCheckout() && locator.HeadOID != "" {
317			if observed.localBranchOIDErr != nil || locator.HeadOID != observed.localBranchOID {
318				return &StalePlanError{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("selected local branch OID changed from %q to %q", locator.HeadOID, observed.localBranchOID)}
319			}
320		}
321		if !observed.hasCheckout() && locator.UpstreamOID != "" && locator.Upstream == observed.remoteBranch {
322			if observed.remoteBranchOIDErr != nil || locator.UpstreamOID != observed.remoteBranchOID {
323				return &StalePlanError{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("selected remote branch OID changed from %q to %q", locator.UpstreamOID, observed.remoteBranchOID)}
324			}
325		}
326		return nil
327	}
```

```text
12	func (s *lifecycleService) resumeSpec(request Request, observed lifecycleObservation) PlanSpec {
13		options := request.Options.(ResumeOptions)
14		conditions := []Condition{
15			condition(ConditionTaskCurrent, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
16				"task "+observed.task.ID+" revision "+observed.record.Revision, ""),
17			condition(ConditionRepoIdentity, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
18				"Git common directory "+observed.gitCommonDir, ""),
19		}
20		conditions = append(conditions, resumeOwnerCondition(observed, options))
21		conditions = append(conditions, s.resumeCheckoutConditions(observed, options)...)
22		conditions = append(conditions, s.resumeRuntimeConditions(observed)...)
23	
24		var effects []Effect
25		if options.FetchRefs {
26			effects = append(effects, NewEffect(EffectFetchRefs,
27				"fetch and prune origin before resuming", observed.repoPath, false, true,
28				map[string]string{"remote": "origin", "warning-on-failure": "true"}))
29		}
30		if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree && !observed.hasCheckout() &&
31			(observed.task.State == task.Warm || observed.task.State == task.Cold) {
32			effects = append(effects, NewEffect(EffectCreateWorktree,
33				"rebuild the missing linked worktree", observed.desiredWorktree, false, false,
34				map[string]string{
35					"repo": observed.repoPath, "branch": observed.task.Branch,
36					"preferred-base": observed.remoteBranch, "fallback-base": observed.task.Base,
37					"selected-base": observed.baseRef,
38					"provision":     boolString(!options.NoProvision), "runtime": "false",
39				}))
40		}
41		if resumeNeedsBranchSwitch(observed) {
42			effects = append(effects, NewEffect(EffectSwitchBranch,
43				"switch the clean canonical checkout to the task branch", observed.repoPath, false, false,
44				map[string]string{"from": observed.status.Branch, "to": observed.task.Branch}))
45		}
46		if shouldOpenResumeRuntime(observed) {
47			effects = append(effects, NewEffect(EffectOpenRuntime,
48				"open a runtime surface for the checkout", resumeEffectCheckout(observed), false, false,
49				map[string]string{"backend": runtimeName(observed.runtime), "label": resumeRuntimeLabel(observed.task)}))
50		}
51		runtimeDisposition := "clear"
52		if observed.runtime != nil && observed.runtime.Name() != "none" {
53			if observed.savedRuntimeLive {
54				runtimeDisposition = "reuse:" + observed.runtime.Name() + ":" + observed.task.RuntimeHandle
55			} else {
56				runtimeDisposition = "open:" + observed.runtime.Name()
57			}
58		}
59		path := observed.task.WorktreePath
60		if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree {
61			if observed.hasCheckout() {
62				path = observed.checkout
63			} else {
64				path = observed.desiredWorktree
65			}
66		} else {
67			path = ""
68		}
69		effects = append(effects, taskUpdateEffect(observed, task.Hot, path, runtimeDisposition,
70			observed.task.Next, observed.task.Note))
71	
72		retained := []string{"branch:" + observed.task.Branch}
73		if checkout := resumeEffectCheckout(observed); checkout != "" {
74			retained = append(retained, "checkout:"+checkout)
75		}
76		if observed.runtime != nil && observed.runtime.Name() != "none" {
77			retained = append(retained, "runtime:"+observed.runtime.Name())
78		}
79		return PlanSpec{
80			Authority:         s.baseAuthority(request, observed),
81			Conditions:        conditions,
82			Effects:           effects,
83			RetainedResources: retained,
84			Confirmation:      Confirmation{Kind: ConfirmationApproval, Prompt: "Resume this task and claim its checkout?"},
85			FallbackCommand:   resumeFallback(observed.task.ID, options),
86			Summary:           "Resume " + observed.task.Title() + " HOT",
87			DisplayedAt:       s.now(),
88		}
89	}
90	
91	func resumeOwnerCondition(observed lifecycleObservation, options ResumeOptions) Condition {
92		if observed.task.OwnedBy(observed.taskflowHost) {
93			owner := observed.task.Owner
94			if owner == "" {
95				owner = "unclaimed"
96			}
97			return condition(ConditionOwner, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired, "task owner is "+owner, "")
98		}
99		if options.TakeOwnership {
100			return condition(ConditionOwner, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
101				"ownership transfer from "+observed.task.Owner+" was explicitly requested", "")
102		}
103		return condition(ConditionOwner, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
104			"task is owned by "+observed.task.Owner, "confirm the other machine pushed its work, then take ownership explicitly")
105	}
```

```text
41			yes             bool

50			Short: "Review stale tasks and drifted state, and act on them",
51			Long: `Show which tasks have gone stale or drifted, and what dev would do about it.
52	
53	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
54	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
55	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
56	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
57			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
58			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

63					return err
64				}
65				rt := app.Runtime()
66				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
67				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
68				retireOptions := sweepRetireOptions{

70				}
71

83				}
84

148	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration, retireOptions sweepRetireOptions) []suggestion {
149		t := r.Task
150		var out []suggestion
151		current, currentErr := app.Tasks.GetRecord(t.ID)
152		if currentErr != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(current.Task, *t) {
153			detail := "task changed after the sweep inventory snapshot"
154			if currentErr != nil {
155				detail = "task could not be reloaded after the sweep inventory snapshot: " + currentErr.Error()
156			}
157			return []suggestion{{
158				row: r, reason: detail,
159				action: "rerun sweep to inspect the current task revision — not changed automatically",
160			}}
161		}
162		revision := current.Revision
163	
164		// A task whose repository is gone cannot be finished, resumed, parked or
165		// retired: every one of those resolves the repository first, and `dev done`
166		// refuses outright once the checkout is missing. Nothing else in this
167		// function reaches it either — the dead-branch rule below excludes direct
168		// mode, and the stale-worktree rule needs a recorded worktree path. Left
169		// alone, the record is unreachable by any command in the binary.
170		//
171		// Reaping removes dev's record of intent and nothing else; the branch, the
172		// commits and the remote are untouched. A live session proves the directory
173		// is there, so it is the one condition that rules this out.
174		if t.RepoPath != "" && !r.Live() && !dirExists(t.RepoPath) {
175			out = append(out, suggestion{
176				row:    r,
177				reason: fmt.Sprintf("repository %s no longer exists", config.Contract(t.RepoPath)),
178				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s (Git keeps any work; this drops only dev's record)", t.ID),
179				apply:  func() error { return sweepDeleteTask(ctx, app.Tasks, t.ID, revision) },
180			})
181			return out
182		}
183	
184		out = append(out, orphanSuggestions(app, r)...)
185	
186		switch {
187		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
188		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
189		case t.State == task.Hot && r.StateDrift() == "no live session":
190			out = append(out, suggestion{
191				row:    r,
192				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
193				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
194				apply: func() error {
195					return sweepUpdateTask(ctx, app.Tasks, t.ID, revision, func(candidate *task.Task) {
196						candidate.State = task.Warm
197					})
198				},
199			})
200	
201		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
202		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
203		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
204			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
205			if t.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeDirect {
206				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but direct tasks cannot go cold",
207					action: "keep it warm or finish it — not changed automatically"})
208				break
209			}
210			if r.Status.Dirty() {
211				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
212					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
213				break
214			}
215			if !r.Status.Synced() {
216				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
217					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
218				break
219			}
220			session, plan, planErr := sweepTaskPlan(ctx, app, t.ID, flow.ParkColdOptions{})
221			if planErr != nil || plan.Availability != flow.AvailabilityReady {
222				detail := sweepPlanBlocker(plan, planErr)
223				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but guarded cold parking is blocked",
224					action: detail + " — not changed automatically"})
225				break
226			}
227			out = append(out, suggestion{
228				row:    r,
229				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
230				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
231				apply: func() error {
232					result, err := session.apply(ctx, plan, flow.Approve(plan.PlanID))
233					renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
234					return err
235				},
236			})
237	
238		// DONE means integrated; runtime/worktree cleanup is a separate,
239		// externally coordinated retirement step.
240		case t.State == task.Done:
241			action := fmt.Sprintf("retire runtime/worktree for %s", t.ID)
242			if retireOptions.deleteBranches && t.Branch != "" && t.Branch != t.Base {
243				action += fmt.Sprintf(" and delete %s", t.Branch)
244			}
245			session, plan, planErr := sweepTaskPlan(ctx, app, t.ID, flow.RetireOptions{
246				CloseUnknown: retireOptions.closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: retireOptions.assumeNoRuntime,
247				DeleteBranch: retireOptions.deleteBranches,
248			})
249			if planErr != nil || plan.Availability != flow.AvailabilityReady {
250				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: "merged, but guarded retirement is blocked",
251					action: sweepPlanBlocker(plan, planErr) + " — not changed automatically"})
252				break
253			}
254			out = append(out, suggestion{
255				row: r, reason: "merged, cleanup pending", action: action,
256				apply: func() error {
257					approval := flow.Approve(plan.PlanID)
258					if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped {
259						approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, plan.Confirmation.Token)
260					}
261					result, err := session.apply(ctx, plan, approval)
262					renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
263					return err
264				},
265			})
266		}
267	
268		// A branch-backed task whose branch git no longer has is dead: the branch
269		// was deleted after integration, so the record holds intent for work that
270		// no longer exists anywhere. It cannot be finished, resumed, or retired,
271		// because every one of those paths resolves the branch first.
272		noCheckout := t.WorktreePath == "" || r.WorktreeMissing
273		if noCheckout && t.Branch != "" && t.RepoPath != "" &&
274			t.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeDirect && !gitx.BranchExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, t.Branch) {
275			out = append(out, suggestion{
276				row:    r,
277				reason: fmt.Sprintf("branch %s no longer exists", t.Branch),
278				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
279				apply:  func() error { return sweepDeleteTask(ctx, app.Tasks, t.ID, revision) },
280			})
281			return out
282		}
283	
284		// A cold task keeps no checkout by definition: that is what going cold
285		// means. One still on disk is drift inventory already reports and nothing
286		// could act on.
287		if t.State == task.Cold && t.WorktreePath != "" && r.CheckoutExists && !r.WorktreeMissing &&
288			!r.Live() && !r.Status.Dirty() && r.Status.Synced() {
289			out = append(out, suggestion{
290				row:    r,
291				reason: "cold, but its worktree is still on disk",
292				action: fmt.Sprintf("reconcile %s with an exact guarded plan — not changed automatically", config.Contract(t.WorktreePath)),
293			})
294		}
295	
296		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
297		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
298			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
299			out = append(out, suggestion{
300				row:    r,
301				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
302				action: fmt.Sprintf("inspect repository-wide prune scope before clearing %s — not changed automatically", config.Contract(wtPath)),
303			})
304		}
305		return out
306	}
307	
308	func sweepTaskPlan(ctx context.Context, app *App, id string, options flow.ActionOptions) (lifecycleSession, flow.Plan, error) {
309		session, err := newLifecycleSession(ctx, app, func() (*task.Task, error) {
310			return app.Tasks.Get(id)
311		})
312		if err != nil {
313			return lifecycleSession{}, flow.Plan{}, err
314		}
315		plan, err := session.plan(ctx, options)
316		return session, plan, err
317	}
318	
319	func sweepPlanBlocker(plan flow.Plan, err error) string {
320		if err != nil {
321			return err.Error()
322		}
323		var parts []string
324		for _, condition := range append(plan.InputConditions(), plan.BlockingConditions()...) {
325			parts = append(parts, string(condition.Code)+": "+condition.Evidence)
326		}
327		if len(parts) == 0 {
328			return "guarded plan is " + string(plan.Availability)
329		}
330		return strings.Join(parts, "; ")
331	}
332	
333	func sweepUpdateTask(ctx context.Context, store *task.Store, id, revision string, update func(*task.Task)) error {
334		if revision == "" {
335			return fmt.Errorf("task %s had no report-time revision; rerun sweep", id)
336		}
337		current, err := store.GetRecord(id)
338		if err != nil {
339			return err
340		}
341		if current.Revision != revision {
342			return &task.StaleRevisionError{ID: id, Expected: revision, Actual: current.Revision}
343		}
344		candidate := current.Task
345		update(&candidate)
346		_, err = store.Update(ctx, &candidate, revision)
347		return err
348	}
349	
350	func sweepDeleteTask(ctx context.Context, store *task.Store, id, revision string) error {
351		if revision == "" {
352			return fmt.Errorf("task %s had no report-time revision; rerun sweep", id)
353		}
354		return store.DeleteIfRevision(ctx, id, revision)
355	}
356	
357	// dirExists reports whether path is a directory that can be read right now.
358	func dirExists(path string) bool {
359		info, err := os.Stat(path)
360		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
361	}
362	
363	// orphanSuggestions handles the residue of a worktree removed while its
364	// transcript writer was still running: the path exists, Git has no record of
365	// it, and it holds only agent artifacts. Removing it is offered only once every
366	// file in it is proven byte-identical to one the repository already has.
367	func orphanSuggestions(app *App, r inventory.Row) []suggestion {
368		t := r.Task
369		if t.WorktreePath == "" || !r.WorktreeMissing || !r.CheckoutExists {
370			return nil
371		}
372		orphan, ok, err := retirement.InspectOrphan(t.WorktreePath)
373		if err != nil || !ok {
374			return nil
375		}
376		unsalvaged, err := retirement.Unsalvaged(orphan, t.RepoPath)
377		if err != nil {
378			return nil
379		}
380		if len(unsalvaged) > 0 {
381			return []suggestion{{
382				row: r,
383				reason: fmt.Sprintf("%s is an abandoned agent workspace holding %d file(s) the repository does not have",
384					config.Contract(t.WorktreePath), len(unsalvaged)),
385				action: fmt.Sprintf("salvage %s first — not removed automatically", strings.Join(unsalvaged, ", ")),
386			}}
387		}
388		return []suggestion{{
389			row:    r,
390			reason: fmt.Sprintf("%s is an abandoned agent workspace git does not know", config.Contract(t.WorktreePath)),
391			action: fmt.Sprintf("remove the empty shell %s (its %d artifact file(s) are already in the repository)",
392				config.Contract(t.WorktreePath), len(orphan.Files)),
393			apply: func() error { return os.RemoveAll(t.WorktreePath) },
394		}}
395	}
396	
397	func suggestMergedWorktrees(app *App, ctx context.Context, rows []inventory.Row, requestedBase string, options sweepRetireOptions) ([]suggestion, error) {
398		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, mustGetwd())
399		if err != nil {
400			return nil, fmt.Errorf("--merged-worktrees requires a Git repository: %w", err)
401		}
402		if repository.IsLinkedWorktree {
403			return nil, fmt.Errorf("--merged-worktrees must run from the canonical checkout, not linked worktree %s", config.Contract(repository.Root))
404		}
405		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, repository.Root)
406		if err != nil {
407			return nil, err
408		}
409		base := requestedBase
410		if base == "" {
411			base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repository.Root)
412			if status.Branch != base {
413				return nil, fmt.Errorf("--merged-worktrees defaults to %s; switch the canonical checkout to it or pass --base explicitly", base)
414			}
415		}
416		if !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repository.Root, base) {
417			return nil, fmt.Errorf("merged-worktree base %s does not resolve to a commit", base)
418		}
419	
420		claimed := make(map[string]inventory.Row)
421		for _, row := range rows {
422			if row.Task == nil || row.Checkout == "" {
423				continue
424			}
425			canonical, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(row.Checkout)
426			if canonicalErr == nil {
427				claimed[canonical] = row
428			}
429		}
430		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, repository.Root)
```

```text
720	func (s *lifecycleService) revalidateColdArtifact(ctx context.Context, observed lifecycleObservation) error {
721		if observed.mode != task.ModeWorktree {
722			return nil
723		}
724		fresh, err := s.inspectArtifacts(ctx, s.artifacts, observed.checkout)
725		if err != nil {
726			return err
727		}
728		if !fresh.Ready() {
729			return errors.New("artifact readiness changed to blocked")
730		}
731		if artifactAuthority(fresh, nil) != artifactAuthority(observed.artifact, observed.artifactErr) {
732			return staleBoundary("artifact intent or receipt authority changed")
733		}
734		return nil
735	}

738		options := observed.cleanupOptions(closeUnknown, assumeNoRuntime, timeout)
739		fresh, err := s.inspectCleanup(ctx, observed.runtime, observed.checkout, options)
740		if err != nil {
741			return err

744			return staleBoundary("runtime occupancy, caller, agent, or session evidence changed")
745		}

755		if !fresh.Ready() || fresh.CallerContained || len(fresh.Sessions) > 0 {
756			return errors.New("runtime coverage reappeared after closure")
757		}
758		observed.cleanup = fresh
759		observed.cleanupErr = nil
760		return nil
761	}
762	
763	func (s *lifecycleService) ensureColdRemovalBoundary(ctx context.Context, observed *lifecycleObservation, options ParkColdOptions, runtimeWasClosed bool) error {
764		if err := s.ensureColdGitReady(ctx, observed); err != nil {
765			return err
766		}
767		if err := s.revalidateColdArtifact(ctx, *observed); err != nil {
768			return err
769		}
770		fresh, err := s.inspectCleanup(ctx, observed.runtime, observed.checkout,
771			observed.cleanupOptions(options.CloseUnknown, options.AssumeNoRuntime, options.Timeout))
772		if err != nil {
773			return err
774		}
775		if !fresh.Ready() || fresh.CallerContained || len(fresh.Sessions) > 0 {
776			return errors.New("cleanup occupancy is no longer empty and safe")
777		}
778		if !runtimeWasClosed && cleanupAuthority(fresh, nil) != cleanupAuthority(observed.cleanup, observed.cleanupErr) {
779			return staleBoundary("runtime occupancy changed before cleanup")
780		}
781		observed.cleanup = fresh
782		observed.cleanupErr = nil
783		return nil
784	}
785	
786	func (s *lifecycleService) revalidateResumeCheckout(ctx context.Context, observed *lifecycleObservation) error {
787		expected := observed.task.Branch
788		if err := s.refreshCheckout(ctx, observed, expected); err != nil {
789			return staleBoundary("resume checkout identity changed: " + err.Error())
790		}
791		return nil
792	}
793	
794	func (s *lifecycleService) revalidateResumeOccupancy(ctx context.Context, observed *lifecycleObservation, compareAuthority bool) error {
795		fresh, err := s.inspectOccupancy(ctx, observed.runtime, observed.checkout, runtime.OccupancyOptions{
796			Profile:           runtime.OccupancyStrict,
797			CallerWorkspaceID: s.callerWorkspace,
798			CallerPaneID:      s.callerPane,
799		})
800		if occupancyErr := s.writerOccupancyError(fresh, err); occupancyErr != nil {
801			return occupancyErr
802		}
803		if compareAuthority && occupancyAuthority(fresh, nil) != occupancyAuthority(observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr) {
804			return staleBoundary("runtime session, caller, or recognized-agent occupancy changed")
805		}
806		observed.occupancy = fresh
807		observed.occupancyErr = nil
808		observed.savedRuntimeLive = savedHandleLive(fresh, observed.task.RuntimeHandle)
809		return nil
810	}
811	
812	func (s *lifecycleService) ensureBranchSwitchBoundary(ctx context.Context, observed *lifecycleObservation) error {
813		if err := s.revalidateGitBaseline(ctx, *observed); err != nil {
814			return err
815		}
816		if observed.status.Dirty() || observed.status.Detached || observed.inProgress || observed.status.Conflicted > 0 {
817			return errors.New("canonical checkout is no longer clean and switchable")
818		}
819		if !s.gitRefExists(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Branch) {
820			return staleBoundary("local task branch disappeared before switch")
821		}
822		return nil
823	}

825	func (s *lifecycleService) revalidateResumeBranchRefs(ctx context.Context, observed *lifecycleObservation, allowRemoteChange bool) error {
826		localExists := s.gitRefExists(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Branch)
827		localOID, localErr := "", error(nil)
828		if localExists {
829			localOID, localErr = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Branch)
830		}
831		if localExists != observed.localBranchExists || localOID != observed.localBranchOID ||
832			errorString(localErr) != errorString(observed.localBranchOIDErr) {
833			return staleBoundary("local task branch OID changed before worktree reconstruction")
834		}
835		if allowRemoteChange {
836			return nil
837		}
838		remoteExists := s.gitRefExists(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteBranch)
839		remoteOID, remoteErr := "", error(nil)
840		if remoteExists {
841			remoteOID, remoteErr = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteBranch)
842		}
843		if remoteExists != observed.remoteBranchExists || remoteOID != observed.remoteBranchOID ||
844			errorString(remoteErr) != errorString(observed.remoteBranchOIDErr) {
845			return staleBoundary("remote task branch OID changed before worktree reconstruction")
846		}
847		return nil
848	}

850	func (s *lifecycleService) branchCheckoutCount(ctx context.Context, observed lifecycleObservation) (int, error) {
851		worktrees, err := s.gitWorktrees(ctx, observed.repoPath)
852		if err != nil {
853			return 0, err
854		}
855		count := 0
856		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
857			if worktree.Branch == observed.task.Branch {
858				count++
859			}
860		}
861		return count, nil
862	}

865		if observed.mode == task.ModeBranch && observed.statusErr == nil {
866			return observed.status.Branch
867		}
868		return observed.task.Branch
```

```text
16	type lifecycleExecution struct {
17		Selected task.Task

21	}

31		Selected task.Task

34	}
35	
36	func newLifecycleSession(ctx context.Context, app *App, resolve lifecycleTaskResolver) (lifecycleSession, error) {
37		var session lifecycleSession
38		selected, err := resolve()
39		if err != nil {
40			return session, err
41		}
42		if selected == nil {
43			return session, errors.New("task resolver returned no task")
44		}
45		session.Selected = *selected
46	
47		service, err := newCLILifecycleService(app)
48		if err != nil {
49			return session, err
50		}
51		session.service = service
52		session.Locator, err = service.LocateTask(ctx, selected.ID)
53		if err != nil {
54			return session, err
55		}
56		return session, nil
57	}
58	
59	func (s lifecycleSession) plan(ctx context.Context, options flow.ActionOptions) (flow.Plan, error) {
60		request, err := flow.NewRequest(s.Locator, options)
61		if err != nil {
62			return flow.Plan{}, presentLifecycleRequestError(s.Selected, options.Action(), err)
63		}
64		return s.service.Plan(ctx, request)
65	}
66	
67	func (s lifecycleSession) apply(ctx context.Context, plan flow.Plan, approval flow.Approval) (flow.Result, error) {
68		return s.service.Apply(ctx, plan, approval)
69	}
70	
71	func (s lifecycleSession) finalTask(app *App) (task.Task, error) {
72		final, err := app.Tasks.GetRecord(s.Locator.TaskID)
73		if err != nil {
74			return task.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("load final exact task %s: %w", s.Locator.TaskID, err)
75		}
76		return final.Task, nil
77	}
78	
79	func (s lifecycleSession) requireRetired(app *App, result flow.Result) error {
80		if result.Milestone != flow.MilestoneRetired {
81			return fmt.Errorf("task %s retirement returned milestone %s, want %s",
82				s.Locator.TaskID, result.Milestone, flow.MilestoneRetired)
83		}
84		if _, err := app.Tasks.GetRecord(s.Locator.TaskID); !errors.Is(err, task.ErrNotFound) {
85			if err == nil {
86				return fmt.Errorf("task %s retirement completed but the task record still exists", s.Locator.TaskID)
87			}
88			return fmt.Errorf("verify retired task %s is absent: %w", s.Locator.TaskID, err)
89		}
90		return nil
91	}
92	
93	func executeTaskLifecycle(
94		ctx context.Context,
95		app *App,
96		resolve lifecycleTaskResolver,
97		options flow.ActionOptions,
98	) (lifecycleExecution, error) {
99		var execution lifecycleExecution
100		session, err := newLifecycleSession(ctx, app, resolve)
101		if err != nil {
102			return execution, err
103		}
104		execution.Selected = session.Selected
105		execution.Plan, err = session.plan(ctx, options)
106		if err != nil {
107			return execution, err
108		}
109		execution.Result, err = session.apply(ctx, execution.Plan, flow.Approve(execution.Plan.PlanID))
110		renderLifecycleResult(app, execution.Plan, execution.Result)
111		if err != nil {
112			return execution, presentLifecycleApplyError(execution.Plan, err)
113		}
114	
115		execution.Task, err = session.finalTask(app)
116		if err != nil {
117			return execution, err
118		}
119		return execution, nil
120	}

122	// exactUnmanagedWorktreeLocator converts a branch-selected checkout into the
123	// canonical identity taskflow requires. Branch lookup is only selection; fresh
124	// Git registry evidence supplies every authority field used by the plan.
125	func exactUnmanagedWorktreeLocator(ctx context.Context, repoPath, checkoutPath string) (flow.Locator, error) {
126		registered, err := gitx.ResolveRegisteredWorktree(ctx, repoPath, checkoutPath)
127		if err != nil {
128			return flow.Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve exact registered worktree %s: %w", config.Contract(checkoutPath), err)
129		}
130		return flow.Locator{
131			RepoKey:      registered.GitCommonDir,
132			RowKey:       registered.Path,
133			RowKind:      "unmanaged",
134			RepositoryID: registered.GitCommonDir,
135			GitCommonDir: registered.GitCommonDir,
136			RepoPath:     registered.RepositoryPath,
137			CheckoutPath: registered.Path,
138			Branch:       registered.Worktree.Branch,
139			HeadOID:      registered.Worktree.Head,
140		}, nil
141	}

143	// executeNonTaskLifecycle applies an exact non-task plan as an explicitly
144	// invoked CLI action. Destructive compatibility flags authorize only the typed
145	// token sealed into that same plan; they do not change readiness or blockers.
146	func executeNonTaskLifecycle(
147		ctx context.Context,
148		app *App,
149		locator flow.Locator,
150		options flow.ActionOptions,
151		authorizeTyped bool,
152	) (nonTaskLifecycleExecution, error) {
153		var execution nonTaskLifecycleExecution
154		service, err := newCLILifecycleService(app)
155		if err != nil {
156			return execution, err
157		}
158		request, err := flow.NewRequest(locator, options)
159		if err != nil {
160			return execution, err
161		}
162		execution.Plan, err = service.Plan(ctx, request)
163		if err != nil {
164			return execution, err
165		}
166		approval := flow.Approve(execution.Plan.PlanID)
167		if execution.Plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped {
168			if !authorizeTyped {
169				return execution, fmt.Errorf("%s requires its exact typed confirmation", execution.Plan.Summary)
170			}
171			approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(execution.Plan.PlanID, execution.Plan.Confirmation.Token)
172		}
173		execution.Result, err = service.Apply(ctx, execution.Plan, approval)
174		renderLifecycleResult(app, execution.Plan, execution.Result)
175		if err != nil {
176			return execution, presentLifecycleApplyError(execution.Plan, err)
177		}
178		return execution, nil
179	}

181	func newCLILifecycleService(app *App) (*flow.Service, error) {
182		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
183		if err != nil {
184			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve lifecycle caller directory: %w", err)
185		}
186		return flow.NewLifecycleService(flow.LifecycleConfig{
187			Config:              app.Cfg,
188			Tasks:               app.Tasks,

203	func renderLifecycleResult(app *App, plan flow.Plan, result flow.Result) {
204		style := app.outStyle()
205		for _, step := range result.AttemptedSteps() {
206			if step.Status == flow.StepFailed {
207				label := step.Effect.Description
208				if label == "" {
209					label = string(step.Effect.Code)
210				}
211				failure := step.Failure
212				if failure == "" {
213					failure = "operation failed"
214				}
215				app.warnf("%s failed: %s", label, failure)
216				continue
217			}
218			if step.Status != flow.StepCompleted {
219				continue
220			}
221	
222			details := step.Effect.Details.Map()
223			switch step.Effect.Code {
224			case flow.EffectCommitWIP, flow.EffectCommitAll:
225				message := details["message"]
226				if message == "" {
227					message = step.Detail
228				}
229				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s  %s\n", style.label("committed"), message)
230			case flow.EffectDiscardAll:
231				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s  checkout changes\n", style.label("discarded"))
232			case flow.EffectPushBranch, flow.EffectPushBase:
233				pushed := strings.TrimPrefix(step.Detail, "pushed ")
234				pushed = strings.TrimPrefix(pushed, "published ")
235				if pushed == step.Detail || pushed == "" {
236					pushed = "origin/" + step.Effect.Target
237				}
238				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s     %s\n", style.label("pushed"), pushed)
239			case flow.EffectCloseRuntime:
240				closed := strings.TrimPrefix(step.Detail, "closed ")
```

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, catalog, experiment, diskusage, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can
4	// be tested without a terminal.
5	package cli
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"fmt"
10		"io"

12		"path/filepath"

23		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
24	)
25	
26	// App is the state shared by every command.
27	type App struct {
28		Cfg      config.Config
29		Tasks    *task.Store
30		Catalog  *catalog.Store
31		Registry *catalog.Registry
32		Notes    *note.Service
33		Sizes    *diskusage.Manager
34	
35		In  io.Reader
36		Out io.Writer
37		Err io.Writer
38	
39		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
40		configPath string
41		// remotesPath is the --remotes override; empty means dev/remotes.toml.
42		remotesPath string
43		// scaffoldsPath is the --scaffolds override; empty means dev/scaffolds.toml.
44		scaffoldsPath string
45		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
46		runtimeOverride string
47		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
48		noRuntime bool
49		// allowSharedCheckout is an explicit escape hatch for coordinated agents
50		// whose file ownership is known to be disjoint.
51		allowSharedCheckout bool
52		// colorMode controls styling of human-readable output.
53		colorMode string
54		// interactiveCheck is a test seam for commands that prompt only when a real
55		// terminal is attached. Production falls back to interactive().
56		interactiveCheck func() bool
57		// runtimeInstance and runtimesByName are injection seams used by focused
58		// command tests.
59		runtimeInstance runtime.Runtime
60		runtimesByName  map[string]runtime.Runtime
61		// trace is an opt-in, process-local performance recorder. It is deliberately
62		// separate from durable activity stats and ordinary command output.
63		trace                  *perftrace.Recorder
64		tracePath              string
65		traceOnce              *sync.Once
66		traceTUI               bool
67		deferredReleaseRefresh bool
68	}
69	
70	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
71	func (a *App) Load() error {
72		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
73		if err != nil {
74			return err
75		}
76		a.Cfg = cfg
77		if a.In == nil {
78			a.In = os.Stdin
79		}
80		if a.Out == nil {
81			a.Out = os.Stdout
82		}
83		if a.Err == nil {
84			a.Err = os.Stderr
85		}
86		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
87		a.Catalog = catalog.NewStore(cfg.AssetsDir(), catalog.WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic catalog.Diagnostic) {
88			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev: warning:"), diagnostic.Error())
89		}))
90		a.Registry = catalog.NewRegistry(a.Catalog)
91		noteStore := note.NewStore(cfg.NotesDir(), note.WithDiagnosticSink(func(path string, err error) {
92			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: skipping note %s: %v\n", filepath.Base(path), err)
93		}))
94		a.Notes = note.NewService(noteStore, cfg.NotesIndexFile())
95		a.Notes.IndexDiagnostic = func(err error) {
96			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: note search index: %v\n", err)
97		}
98		if a.Sizes == nil {
99			cache := diskusage.NewCache(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "sizes-v1.json"), 10*time.Minute)
100			a.Sizes = diskusage.NewManager(cache, 2)
101		}
102		return nil
103	}
104	
105	func (a *App) interactive() bool {
106		if a.interactiveCheck != nil {
107			return a.interactiveCheck()
108		}
109		return interactive()
110	}
111	
112	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
113	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
114	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
115		if a.runtimeInstance != nil {
116			return a.runtimeInstance
117		}
118		if a.noRuntime {
119			return runtime.None{}
120		}
121		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
122		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
123			backend = a.runtimeOverride
124		}
125		return a.runtimeNamed(backend)
126	}
127	
128	// runtimeNamed resolves the backend that owns a persisted opaque handle. It
129	// deliberately bypasses the current backend override: feeding a Herdr handle to
130	// tmux after a config change is never valid.
131	func (a *App) runtimeNamed(name string) runtime.Runtime {
132		if rt := a.runtimesByName[name]; rt != nil {
133			return rt
134		}
135		if a.runtimeInstance != nil && (name == "" || a.runtimeInstance.Name() == name) {
136			return a.runtimeInstance
137		}
138		rt := runtime.Select(name)
139		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
140			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
141		}
142		return rt
143	}
144	
145	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
146	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
147		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
148	}
149	
150	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
151	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
152		message := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
153		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev:"), message)
154	}
155	
156	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
157	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
158	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
159	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
160	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
161	// integrations.
162	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
163		// Windows shells do not inherit an extra descriptor the way the POSIX
164		// wrapper's `3>file` redirection does, so the PowerShell wrapper names a
165		// temp file instead and reads it back after dev exits.
166		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
167			return os.WriteFile(path, append([]byte(dir), 0), 0o600)
168		}
169		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
170			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
171			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
172				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
173			}
174			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
175			if file == nil {
176				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
177			}
178			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
179				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
180			}
181			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
182				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
183			}
184			return nil
185		}
186		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
187		return err
188	}
189	
190	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
191	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
192
```

```text
441		var rt runtime.Runtime
442		if candidate.RuntimeHandle != "" && candidate.RuntimeName != "" {
443			rt = s.namedRuntime(candidate.RuntimeName)
444			if rt == nil {
445				return nil, fmt.Errorf("recorded runtime backend %q is unavailable", candidate.RuntimeName)
446			}
447			if rt.Name() != candidate.RuntimeName {
448				return nil, fmt.Errorf("recorded runtime backend %q resolved to %q", candidate.RuntimeName, rt.Name())
449			}
450		} else {
451			rt = s.defaultRuntime()
452		}
453		if rt == nil || strings.TrimSpace(rt.Name()) == "" {
454			return nil, errors.New("taskflow runtime resolver returned no backend")
455		}
456		return rt, nil
457	}
```

```text
11	func runtimeForTask(app *App, t *task.Task) runtime.Runtime {
12		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
13			t.RuntimeName = ""
14			return app.Runtime()
15		}
16		if t.RuntimeName != "" {
17			return app.runtimeNamed(t.RuntimeName)
18		}
19		return app.Runtime()
20	}

22	func setTaskRuntime(t *task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opened runtime.OpenResult) {
23		t.RuntimeHandle = persistedRuntimeHandle(rt, opened)
24		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
25			t.RuntimeName = ""
26			return
27		}
28		t.RuntimeName = rt.Name()
29	}
30	
31	func clearTaskRuntime(t *task.Task) {
32		t.RuntimeHandle = ""
33		t.RuntimeName = ""
34	}
35	
36	func runtimeHandleCovers(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, handle, checkout string) (bool, error) {
37		if handle == "" || rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" {
38			return false, nil
39		}
40		sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
41		if err != nil {
42			return false, err
43		}
44		for _, session := range sessions {
45			if session.Handle == handle && session.Covers(checkout) {
46				return true, nil
47			}
48		}
49		return false, nil
50	}
51	
52	// closeTaskRuntime validates an opaque persisted handle before sending it back
53	// to its recorded backend. A stale handle is cleared without being fed to a
54	// different backend; a close error leaves both provenance fields intact.
55	func closeTaskRuntime(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout string) (runtime.Runtime, bool, error) {
56		rt := runtimeForTask(app, t)
57		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
58			return rt, false, nil
59		}
60		live, err := runtimeHandleCovers(ctx, rt, t.RuntimeHandle, checkout)
61		if err != nil {
62			return rt, false, fmt.Errorf("validate %s runtime session %s: %w", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle, err)
63		}
64		if !live {
65			if t.RuntimeName == "" {
66				return rt, false, fmt.Errorf("legacy runtime handle %s has no backend provenance and is not live in %s; reconcile it before cleanup", t.RuntimeHandle, rt.Name())
67			}
68			clearTaskRuntime(t)
69			return rt, false, nil
70		}
71		if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
72			return rt, false, err
73		}
74		clearTaskRuntime(t)
75		return rt, true, nil
76	}
```

```text
1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"strings"
16	
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
18	)
19	
20	// Pane is one terminal surface inside a runtime session.
21	type Pane struct {
22		ID           string
23		CWD          string
24		ShellCWD     string
25		Agent        string
26		AgentStatus  string
27		AgentSession string
28	}
29	
30	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
31	type Session struct {
32		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
33		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
34		Handle string
35		Label  string
36		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
37		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
38		// value.
39		Dirs []string
40		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
41		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
42		AgentStatus string
43		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
44		AgentSessions []string
45		// Panes retain the exact runtime IDs and cwd values used for caller and
46		// mixed-workspace retirement checks.
47		Panes   []Pane
48		Focused bool
49	}
50	
51	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
52	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
53		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
54			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
55			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
56			// $HOME active.
57			if inside, err := pathx.Contains(dir, d); err == nil && inside {
58				return true
59			}
60		}
61		return false
62	}
63	
64	// OpenResult is the transient result of making a checkout live. Handle may be
65	// persisted by callers, but the pane belongs to this one creation response and
66	// must never be treated as durable state.
67	type OpenResult struct {
68		Handle     string
69		Surface    string
70		Opened     bool
71		Created    bool
72		RootPaneID string
73	}
74	
75	// AgentActivity is one recognized live coding agent occupying a runtime pane.
76	// Every activity returned by a backend is occupied regardless of Status; idle,
77	// done and unknown describe lifecycle state, not permission to share a checkout.
78	type AgentActivity struct {
79		PaneID      string
80		WorkspaceID string
81		Agent       string
82		Name        string
83		Status      string
84		CWD         string
85	}
86	
87	// AgentActivityLister is an optional runtime capability. Core runtimes need not
88	// know about agents; Herdr implements it because its pane model can identify the
89	// exact process and checkout involved.
90	type AgentActivityLister interface {
91		AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error)
92	}
93	
94	// CurrentPaneResolver is an optional runtime capability for resolving the live
95	// pane behind inherited caller context. Herdr pane IDs can change after a move,
96	// so collision exclusions must not trust HERDR_PANE_ID alone.
97	type CurrentPaneResolver interface {
98		CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
99	}
100	
101	// Activator is the optional interactive half of opening a runtime surface.
102	// Open deliberately remains detached so creation commands can run in the
103	// background. Navigation commands call Activate after their own terminal UI
104	// has been torn down: inside a multiplexer this switches the current client;
105	// outside it attaches a new client and blocks until the user detaches.
106	type Activator interface {
107		Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
108	}
109	
110	// PaneRunner is the optional exact-pane command surface. The command is shell
111	// text for the pane's existing interactive shell, not argv for a child process
112	// started by dev. Implementations must not include command text in errors.
113	type PaneRunner interface {
114		RunInPane(ctx context.Context, paneID, command string) error
115	}
116	
117	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
118	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
119	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
120	type Runtime interface {
121		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
122		Name() string
123		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
124		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
125		Available() bool
126		// Open makes dir live. Its result distinguishes a newly created surface from
127		// a reused one and may carry a root pane proven by that same create response.
128		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
129		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
130		// task entry.
131		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
132		// List enumerates live sessions.
133		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
134		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
135		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
136		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
137	}
138	
139	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
140	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
141	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
142	type WorktreeOpener interface {
143		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error)
144	}
145	
146	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
147	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
148	
149	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
150		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
151	}
152	
153	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
154	//
155	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
156	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then zellij,
157	// then None.
158	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
159	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
160		herdr, tmux, zellij, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), NewZellij(), None{}
161		switch backend {
162		case "herdr":
163			return herdr
164		case "tmux":
165			return tmux
166		case "zellij":
167			return zellij
168		case "none":
169			return none
170		case "", "auto":
171			if herdr.Available() {
172				return herdr
173			}
174			if tmux.Available() {
175				return tmux
176			}
177			if zellij.Available() {
178				return zellij
179			}
180			return none
```
