160	// CloseAndWait closes every eligible covering session and proves that no
161	// runtime surface still covers target before returning.
162	func CloseAndWait(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, target string, opts Options) (Inspection, error) {
163		inspection, err := Inspect(ctx, rt, target, opts)
164		if err != nil {
165			return inspection, err
166		}
167		if !inspection.Ready() {
168			return inspection, fmt.Errorf("retirement blocked: %s", strings.Join(inspection.Blockers, "; "))
169		}
170		if inspection.RuntimeUnknown || rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" {
171			return inspection, nil
172		}
173		interval := opts.PollInterval
174		if interval <= 0 {
175			interval = 100 * time.Millisecond
176		}
177		timeout := opts.Timeout
178		if timeout <= 0 {
179			timeout = 5 * time.Second
180		}
181		deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
182		closed := make(map[string]bool)
183		for {
184			fresh, inspectErr := Inspect(ctx, rt, inspection.Target, opts)
185			if inspectErr != nil {
186				return inspection, fmt.Errorf("reinspect before %s runtime close: %w", rt.Name(), inspectErr)
187			}
188			if !fresh.Ready() {
189				return fresh, fmt.Errorf("retirement blocked after runtime state changed: %s", strings.Join(fresh.Blockers, "; "))
190			}
191			if len(fresh.Sessions) == 0 {
192				inspection.Sessions = nil
193				inspection.ClosedSessions = len(closed)
194				return inspection, nil
195			}
196			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
197				return inspection, fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for %d %s session(s) to release %s",
198					len(fresh.Sessions), rt.Name(), inspection.Target)
199			}
200			for _, session := range fresh.Sessions {
201				handle := session.Runtime.Handle
202				if closed[handle] {
203					continue
204				}
205				if err := rt.Close(ctx, handle); err != nil {
206					return inspection, fmt.Errorf("close %s runtime %s: %w", rt.Name(), handle, err)
207				}
208				closed[handle] = true
209				break // re-list before authorizing the next destructive close.
210			}
211			select {
212			case <-ctx.Done():
213				return inspection, ctx.Err()
214			case <-time.After(interval):
215			}
216		}
217	}

219	func coveringAgentStatuses(panes []runtime.Pane, fallback string) []string {
220		set := make(map[string]bool)
221		for _, pane := range panes {
222			if pane.Agent != "" || pane.AgentSession != "" || pane.AgentStatus != "" {
223				set[strings.ToLower(pane.AgentStatus)] = true
224			}
225		}
226		if len(set) == 0 {
227			set[strings.ToLower(fallback)] = true
228		}
229		out := make([]string, 0, len(set))
230		for status := range set {
231			out = append(out, status)
232		}
233		sort.Strings(out)
234		return out
235	}

67	func resolveRetireCommandTarget(ctx context.Context, app *App, args []string) (retireCommandTarget, error) {
68		if len(args) == 1 {
69			expanded := config.Expand(args[0])
70			if info, statErr := os.Stat(expanded); statErr == nil && info.IsDir() {
71				return retireCommandTargetForPath(ctx, app, expanded)
72			}
73			candidate, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
74			if err != nil {
75				return retireCommandTarget{}, err
76			}
77			return retireCommandTarget{Task: candidate}, nil
78		}
79	
80		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
81		if err != nil {
82			return retireCommandTarget{}, err
83		}
84		return retireCommandTargetForPath(ctx, app, cwd)
85	}
86	
87	func retireCommandTargetForPath(ctx context.Context, app *App, path string) (retireCommandTarget, error) {
88		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path)
89		if err != nil {
90			return retireCommandTarget{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree %s: %w", config.Contract(path), err)
91		}
92		candidate, err := exactTaskForRetirementCheckout(app, repository.Root)
93		if err != nil {
94			return retireCommandTarget{}, err
95		}
96		if candidate != nil {
97			return retireCommandTarget{Task: candidate}, nil
98		}
99		return retireCommandTarget{Path: repository.Root}, nil
100	}
101	
102	func exactTaskForRetirementCheckout(app *App, checkout string) (*task.Task, error) {
103		canonicalCheckout, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout)
104		if err != nil {
105			return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize retirement checkout %s: %w", config.Contract(checkout), err)
106		}
107		records, _, err := app.Tasks.ListRecords()
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, err
110		}
111		var matched *task.Task
112		for _, record := range records {
113			candidate := record.Task
114			if candidate.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeWorktree && candidate.WorktreePath == "" {
115				// A COLD/DONE worktree task with no checkout does not claim the
116				// canonical repository merely because checkoutOf falls back there.
117				continue
118			}
119			candidateCheckout, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(checkoutOf(&candidate))
120			if canonicalErr != nil || candidateCheckout != canonicalCheckout {
121				continue
122			}
123			if matched != nil {
124				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkout %s is claimed by multiple tasks (%s, %s); name one explicitly or reconcile task metadata",
125					config.Contract(canonicalCheckout), matched.ID, candidate.ID)
126			}
127			matched = &candidate
128		}
129		return matched, nil
130	}
131	
132	func retireTaskWithTaskflow(
133		ctx context.Context,
134		app *App,
135		selected *task.Task,
136		options flow.RetireOptions,
137		authorizeBranchDeletion bool,
138	) error {
139		session, err := newLifecycleSession(ctx, app, func() (*task.Task, error) { return selected, nil })
140		if err != nil {
141			return err
142		}
143		plan, err := session.plan(ctx, options)
144		if err != nil {
145			return err
146		}
147		approval := flow.Approve(plan.PlanID)
148		if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped {
149			if !authorizeBranchDeletion {
150				return fmt.Errorf("%s requires its exact typed confirmation", plan.Summary)
151			}
152			approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, plan.Confirmation.Token)
153		}
154		result, applyErr := session.apply(ctx, plan, approval)
155		if applyErr != nil {
156			renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
157			return presentLifecycleApplyError(plan, applyErr)
158		}
159		if err := session.requireRetired(app, result); err != nil {
160			return err
161		}
162	
163		style := app.outStyle()
164		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s\n", style.success("RETIRED"), config.Contract(checkoutOf(selected)))
165		renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
166		return nil
167	}
168	
169	// retireUnmanagedPathCompatibility preserves the contained-only path contract
170	// while routing every mutation through taskflow's exact unmanaged transaction.
171	func retireUnmanagedPathCompatibility(
172		ctx context.Context,
173		app *App,
174		path string,
175		closeUnknown, assumeNoRuntime, deleteBranch bool,
176		timeout time.Duration,
177	) error {
178		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path)
179		if err != nil {
180			return fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree %s: %w", config.Contract(path), err)
181		}
182		if !repository.IsLinkedWorktree {
183			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a linked worktree; retire explicit paths only from their linked checkout", config.Contract(path))
184		}
185		locator, err := exactUnmanagedWorktreeLocator(ctx, repository.MainRoot, repository.Root)
186		if err != nil {
187			return err
188		}
189		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repository.MainRoot)
190		if base == "" {
191			return fmt.Errorf("cannot prove unmanaged retirement without an explicit repository default branch")
192		}
193		execution, err := executeNonTaskLifecycle(ctx, app, locator, flow.RemoveCheckoutOptions{
194			RequireContained: true, ContainmentBase: base, DeleteContainedBranch: deleteBranch,
195			CloseUnknown: closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: assumeNoRuntime, Timeout: timeout,
196		}, deleteBranch)
197		if err != nil {
198			return err
199		}
200		if execution.Result.Milestone != flow.MilestoneNone {
201			return fmt.Errorf("unmanaged retirement returned unexpected milestone %s", execution.Result.Milestone)
202		}
203		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s\n", app.outStyle().success("RETIRED"), config.Contract(locator.CheckoutPath))
204		return nil
205	}

15	// Field is one stable key/value member of an immutable Fields value.
16	type Field struct {
17		Key   string
18		Value string
19	}
20	
21	// Fields is a map-shaped value whose backing storage is not exposed. Entries
22	// are kept in key order so fingerprints do not depend on map iteration order.
23	type Fields struct {
24		entries []Field
25	}
26	
27	// NewFields copies values into a deterministic immutable representation.
28	func NewFields(values map[string]string) Fields {
29		entries := make([]Field, 0, len(values))
30		for key, value := range values {
31			entries = append(entries, Field{Key: key, Value: value})
32		}
33		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Key < entries[j].Key })
34		return Fields{entries: entries}
35	}
36	
37	// Entries returns a copy in stable key order.
38	func (f Fields) Entries() []Field {
39		return append([]Field(nil), f.entries...)
40	}
41	
42	// Map returns a mutable copy of the fields.
43	func (f Fields) Map() map[string]string {
44		out := make(map[string]string, len(f.entries))
45		for _, entry := range f.entries {
46			out[entry.Key] = entry.Value
47		}
48		return out
49	}
50	
51	func (f Fields) clone() Fields { return Fields{entries: f.Entries()} }
52	
53	// StringList is an ordered string value whose backing slice is not exposed.
54	type StringList struct {
55		values []string
56	}
57	
58	// NewStringList copies values without changing their order.

64	func (s StringList) Values() []string { return append([]string(nil), s.values...) }
65

98	func (s *lifecycleService) inspectDestructive(ctx context.Context, input destructiveInspectInput) (destructiveObservation, error) {
99		observed := destructiveObservation{locator: input.locator, runtime: input.runtime, runtimeErr: input.rtErr}
100		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
101			return observed, err
102		}
103	
104		repository, err := s.gitDiscover(ctx, input.locator.RepoPath)
105		if err != nil {
106			observed.repoErr = err
107			return observed, nil
108		}
109		observed.repo = repository
110		observed.repoPath, err = s.canonicalPath(repository.MainRoot)
111		if err != nil {
112			observed.repoErr = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git main checkout: %w", err)
113			return observed, nil
114		}
115		observed.gitCommonDir, err = s.canonicalPath(repository.GitCommonDir)
116		if err != nil {
117			observed.repoErr = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git common directory: %w", err)
118			return observed, nil
119		}
120		requestedRepo, err := s.canonicalPath(input.locator.RepoPath)
121		if err != nil {
122			return observed, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize requested repository: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, err)
123		}
124		requestedCommon, err := s.canonicalPath(input.locator.GitCommonDir)
125		if err != nil {
126			return observed, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize requested Git common directory: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, err)
127		}
128		if requestedRepo != observed.repoPath || requestedCommon != observed.gitCommonDir {
129			return observed, &StalePlanError{Reason: fmt.Sprintf(
130				"selected repository identity changed: main %q -> %q, common directory %q -> %q",
131				requestedRepo, observed.repoPath, requestedCommon, observed.gitCommonDir,
132			)}
133		}
134		if filepath.IsAbs(input.locator.RepoKey) {
135			key, keyErr := s.canonicalPath(input.locator.RepoKey)
136			if keyErr != nil {
137				return observed, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize repository key: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, keyErr)
138			}
139			if key != observed.gitCommonDir {
140				return observed, &StalePlanError{Reason: "selected repository key no longer names the Git common directory"}
141			}
142		}

144		observed.worktrees, observed.worktreesErr = s.gitWorktrees(ctx, observed.repoPath)

165		if input.inspectArtifacts && observed.worktreeFound {
166			observed.artifact, observed.artifactErr = s.inspectArtifacts(ctx, s.artifacts, observed.checkout)
167		}
168		if !input.noCheckout && !input.skipCleanup {
169			if observed.runtimeErr == nil {
170				if observed.runtime == nil || strings.TrimSpace(observed.runtime.Name()) == "" {
171					observed.runtimeErr = errors.New("destructive inspection has no runtime backend")
172				} else {
173					observed.runtimeAvailable = observed.runtime.Available()
174					observed.cleanup, observed.cleanupErr = s.inspectCleanup(ctx, observed.runtime, observed.checkout, input.cleanup)

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |
| Electron / desktop GUI | Playwright `_electron` REPL under xvfb | [examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) |
| Browser-driven | dev server + `chromium-cli` script | [examples/playwright.md](examples/playwright.md) |
| Library / SDK | import-and-call smoke script at the package boundary | [examples/library.md](examples/library.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web

`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) - it has the `_electron`

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app - it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to
a point where a user would see something:

- CLI -> type a representative command, check the exit code and output.
- Server -> hit the route the diff touches with `curl`, read the body.
- TUI -> `send-keys` a navigation, `capture-pane` the result.
- GUI -> click the button, screenshot the window. **Look at the
  screenshot.** A blank frame is a failure to launch.

If the fallback pattern didn't work out of the box - you had to
install packages, set env vars, patch config, or write a driver -
recommend `/run-skill-generator` in your report so that work gets
captured as a project skill. If it just worked, don't.

1	# Example: CLI tool
2	
3	CLIs are the simplest case - there's usually no background process to
4	manage, no ports, no lifecycle. The skill focuses on **installation**,
5	**representative invocations**, and **testing**.
6	
7	## What matters
8	
9	- **How to get the binary on `PATH`.** Installed globally? Run via
10	  `npx`/`uv run`? Built to `./target/release/foo`? Be explicit.
11	- **Two or three example invocations** that cover the main use cases.
12	  Include expected output so a reader can tell it worked.
13	- **Exit codes** if they're meaningful (e.g. linter returns 1 on findings).
14	- **Stdin behavior** if the tool reads from stdin.
15	
16	## Example snippet
17

20	> description: Build, install, and run mytool. Use when asked to run mytool, test it, or verify it's installed correctly.

27	> ```

43	> ```

1	# Example: TUI / interactive terminal app
2	
3	Interactive terminal apps (text editors, REPLs, curses-based UIs) can't
4	be driven directly by an agent's bash tool - they take over the terminal.
5	The skill must show how to wrap them in `tmux` so the agent can send
6	input, capture output, and take screenshots.
7	
8	## The tmux pattern
9	
10	This is the standard approach:
11	
12	1. Start the TUI inside a detached tmux session
13	2. Send keystrokes with `tmux send-keys`
14	3. Read screen contents with `tmux capture-pane`
15	4. Clean up with `tmux kill-session`
16	
17	The skill's `SKILL.md` should present this as the primary way to drive
18	the app. A small `driver.sh` that wraps the launch+attach sequence can
19	live in the skill directory, but for most TUIs the raw tmux commands in
20	the skill body are enough.
21	
22	## Example snippet
23	
24	> ## Run (interactive, for agents)
25	>
26	> Start the TUI inside tmux:
27	>
28	> ```bash
29	> tmux new-session -d -s app -x 120 -y 40 './myapp'
30	> ```
31	>
32	> Poll until the ready marker appears (faster + more reliable than a fixed sleep -
33	> returns the instant the app is up, fails loudly if it isn't):
34	>
35	> ```bash
36	> timeout 10 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -q "Ready"; do sleep 0.2; done'
37	> tmux capture-pane -t app -p
38	> ```
39	>
40	> Send input (this example navigates to the Settings screen and toggles
41	> an option):
42	>
43	> ```bash
44	> tmux send-keys -t app 's'
45	> timeout 5 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -q "Settings"; do sleep 0.2; done'
46	> tmux send-keys -t app 'Down' 'Down' 'Space'  # navigate + toggle
47	> timeout 5 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -qF "[x]"; do sleep 0.2; done'
48	> tmux capture-pane -t app -p
49	> ```
50	>
51	> If you find yourself writing more than a couple of these poll lines, pull
52	> them into a `wait_for()` helper in a `driver.sh` next to the skill.
53	>
54	> Quit:
55	>
56	> ```bash
57	> tmux send-keys -t app 'q'
58	> tmux kill-session -t app 2>/dev/null || true
59	> ```
60	>
61	> ### Key reference
62	>
63	> | Key | Action |
64	> |---|---|
65	> | `j` / `k` or `Down` / `Up` | Navigate list |
66	> | `Enter` | Select |
67	> | `s` | Settings |
68	> | `q` | Quit |
69	
70	## Details worth documenting
71	
72	- **Terminal size.** Some TUIs break or hide content at small widths.
73	  Specify a known-good size in the `tmux new-session -x -y` args.

package cli

import (
	"go/ast"
	"go/parser"
	"go/token"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestMigratedLifecycleHandlersUseTaskflowMutationBoundary(t *testing.T) {
	files := map[string][]string{
		"park.go":      {"executeTaskLifecycle(", "flow.ParkWarmOptions", "flow.ParkColdOptions"},
		"resume.go":    {"executeTaskLifecycle(", "flow.ResumeOptions"},
		"done_flow.go": {"session.plan(", "session.apply("},
		"retire.go":    {"session.plan(", "session.apply(", "executeNonTaskLifecycle(", "flow.RemoveCheckoutOptions"},
		"adopt.go":     {"executeNonTaskLifecycle(", "flow.AdoptOptions"},
		"worktree.go":  {"executeNonTaskLifecycle(", "flow.RemoveCheckoutOptions"},
		"sweep.go":     {"sweepTaskPlan(", "session.apply("},
	}
	for name, required := range files {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			source, err := os.ReadFile(name)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			text := string(source)
			for _, boundary := range required {
				if !strings.Contains(text, boundary) {
					t.Errorf("%s does not use taskflow boundary %q", name, boundary)
				}
			}
			for _, forbidden := range []string{
				"Tasks.Save(", "Tasks.Update(", "Tasks.Delete(",
				"gitx.RemoveWorktree(", "retirement.Service{", "retire.Service{",
			} {
				if strings.Contains(text, forbidden) {
					t.Errorf("%s contains direct lifecycle mutation %q", name, forbidden)
				}
			}

			parsed, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), name, source, 0)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			ast.Inspect(parsed, func(node ast.Node) bool {
				assignment, ok := node.(*ast.AssignStmt)
				if !ok {
					return true
				}
				for _, expression := range assignment.Lhs {
					selector, ok := expression.(*ast.SelectorExpr)
					if ok && (selector.Sel.Name == "State" || selector.Sel.Name == "WorktreePath") {
						t.Errorf("%s directly assigns lifecycle field %s at %s", name, selector.Sel.Name,
							token.NewFileSet().Position(selector.Pos()))
					}
				}
				return true
			})
		})
	}
}

func TestDashboardLifecycleCallbacksKeepGuardedBoundaries(t *testing.T) {
	source, err := os.ReadFile("tui.go")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	text := string(source)
	parkStart := strings.Index(text, "\t\tPark: func(")
	setNextStart := strings.Index(text, "\t\tSetNext: func(")
	startStart := strings.Index(text, "\t\tStart: func(")
	if parkStart < 0 || setNextStart <= parkStart || startStart <= setNextStart {
		t.Fatalf("could not isolate dashboard Park and SetNext callbacks")
	}
	park := text[parkStart:setNextStart]
	for _, required := range []string{"executeTaskLifecycle(", "flow.ParkWarmOptions"} {
		if !strings.Contains(park, required) {
			t.Errorf("dashboard Park callback does not use %q", required)
		}
	}
	for _, forbidden := range []string{"Tasks.Save(", "Tasks.Update(", "gitx.RemoveWorktree("} {
		if strings.Contains(park, forbidden) {
			t.Errorf("dashboard Park callback contains direct mutation %q", forbidden)
		}
	}

	setNext := text[setNextStart:startStart]
	for _, required := range []string{"Tasks.GetRecord(", "Tasks.Update("} {
		if !strings.Contains(setNext, required) {
			t.Errorf("dashboard SetNext callback does not use revision-aware %q", required)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(setNext, "Tasks.Save(") {
		t.Error("dashboard SetNext callback bypasses compare-and-update with Tasks.Save")
	}
}

_**Agent - sidechain (2026-09-02 04:29:34Z)**_

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-state-machine/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

5	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.
6	
7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race ./...                # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
56	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
57	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
58	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
59	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
60	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
61	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
62	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
63	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
64	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
65	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
66	
67	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
68	
69	State is split intentionally:
70	
71	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
72	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
73	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
74	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
75	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
76	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
77	
78	## Behavioral contracts
79	
80	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
81	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
82	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
83	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
84	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
85	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
86	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
87	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
88	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
89	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
90	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
91	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
92	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
93	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
94	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
95	
96	## Versioning and changelog
97	
98	The current published baseline is `v0.2.3` (2026-09-01). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
99	
100	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
101	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
102	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
103	
104	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
105	
106	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
107	
108	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
109	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
110	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
111	
112	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
113	
114	For a release:
115	
116	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
117	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
118	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
119	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
120	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, and create the GitHub release.
121	
122	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
123	
124	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
125	
126	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
127	
128	| Change | Required synchronization |
129	|---|---|
130	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
131	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
132	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
133	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
134	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
135	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
136	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
137	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
138	
139	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
140	
141	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
142

1	// Package taskflow defines the side-effect-free lifecycle graph and the values
2	// exchanged between lifecycle planners, callers, and action executors.
3	package taskflow
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"regexp"
8		"sort"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
13	)
14	
15	// Field is one stable key/value member of an immutable Fields value.
16	type Field struct {
17		Key   string
18		Value string
19	}
20	
21	// Fields is a map-shaped value whose backing storage is not exposed. Entries
22	// are kept in key order so fingerprints do not depend on map iteration order.
23	type Fields struct {
24		entries []Field
25	}
26	
27	// NewFields copies values into a deterministic immutable representation.
28	func NewFields(values map[string]string) Fields {
29		entries := make([]Field, 0, len(values))
30		for key, value := range values {
31			entries = append(entries, Field{Key: key, Value: value})
32		}
33		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Key < entries[j].Key })
34		return Fields{entries: entries}
35	}
36	
37	// Entries returns a copy in stable key order.
38	func (f Fields) Entries() []Field {
39		return append([]Field(nil), f.entries...)
40	}
41	
42	// Map returns a mutable copy of the fields.
43	func (f Fields) Map() map[string]string {
44		out := make(map[string]string, len(f.entries))
45		for _, entry := range f.entries {
46			out[entry.Key] = entry.Value
47		}
48		return out
49	}
50	
51	func (f Fields) clone() Fields { return Fields{entries: f.Entries()} }
52	
53	// StringList is an ordered string value whose backing slice is not exposed.
54	type StringList struct {
55		values []string
56	}
57	
58	// NewStringList copies values without changing their order.
59	func NewStringList(values ...string) StringList {
60		return StringList{values: append([]string(nil), values...)}
61	}
62	
63	// Values returns a mutable copy of the strings.
64	func (s StringList) Values() []string { return append([]string(nil), s.values...) }
65	
66	func (s StringList) clone() StringList { return NewStringList(s.values...) }
67	
68	// Action names one guarded operation. Values are stable external identifiers,
69	// not presentation labels.
70	type Action string
71	
72	const (
73		ParkWarm       Action = "park-warm"
74		ParkCold       Action = "park-cold"
75		Resume         Action = "resume"
76		CompleteDirect Action = "complete-direct"

78		ReviewHandoff  Action = "review-handoff"

80		Retire         Action = "retire"
81		Adopt          Action = "adopt"
82		RemoveCheckout Action = "remove-checkout"
83		RefreshRemote  Action = "refresh-remote"
84		Reconcile      Action = "reconcile"
85	)

88		ParkWarm,
89		ParkCold,
90		Resume,
91		CompleteDirect,
92		CompleteFF,
93		ReviewHandoff,

95		Retire,

97		RemoveCheckout,
98		RefreshRemote,
99		Reconcile,
100	}
101	
102	// Actions returns every supported action in stable display order.
103	func Actions() []Action { return append([]Action(nil), actionOrder...) }
104	
105	// Valid reports whether the action is part of this protocol version.
106	func (a Action) Valid() bool {
107		for _, candidate := range actionOrder {
108			if a == candidate {
109				return true
110			}
111		}
112		return false
113	}

146	// ObservationState says what happened when one live fact was requested. A
147	// skipped, loading, unknown, or failed observation is never equivalent to a
148	// known false value.
149	type ObservationState string
150	
151	const (
152		ObservationKnown   ObservationState = "known"
153		ObservationUnknown ObservationState = "unknown"
154		ObservationError   ObservationState = "error"
155		ObservationSkipped ObservationState = "skipped"
156		ObservationLoading ObservationState = "loading"
157	)
158	
159	// Valid reports whether the observation state has defined semantics.
160	func (s ObservationState) Valid() bool {
161		switch s {
162		case ObservationKnown, ObservationUnknown, ObservationError, ObservationSkipped, ObservationLoading:
163			return true
164		default:
165			return false
166		}
167	}
168	
169	// Observation is one fact and its provenance. ObservedAt is display/freshness
170	// metadata and is deliberately not itself plan authority.
171	type Observation struct {
172		State      ObservationState
173		Value      string
174		Evidence   string
175		Failure    string
176		ObservedAt time.Time
177		attributes Fields
178	}
179	
180	// NewObservation copies attributes so later probe or UI mutation cannot alter
181	// the observation.
182	func NewObservation(state ObservationState, value, evidence, failure string, observedAt time.Time, attributes map[string]string) Observation {
183		return Observation{
184			State: state, Value: value, Evidence: evidence, Failure: failure,
185			ObservedAt: observedAt, attributes: NewFields(attributes),
186		}
187	}
188	
189	// Attributes returns a mutable copy of observation metadata.
190	func (o Observation) Attributes() map[string]string { return o.attributes.Map() }
191	
192	// Clone returns an independent observation value.
193	func (o Observation) Clone() Observation {
194		o.attributes = o.attributes.clone()
195		return o
196	}

198	// ConditionCode is a stable machine-readable safety or readiness check.
199	type ConditionCode string
200	
201	// Verdict is the result of evaluating one condition.
202	type Verdict string
203	
204	const (
205		VerdictMet         Verdict = "met"
206		VerdictNeedsInput  Verdict = "needs-input"
207		VerdictBlocked     Verdict = "blocked"
208		VerdictUnknown     Verdict = "unknown"
209		VerdictError       Verdict = "error"
210		VerdictUnsupported Verdict = "unsupported"
211		VerdictCurrent     Verdict = "current"
212	)
213	
214	// Requirement determines whether a condition can prevent Apply.
215	type Requirement string
216	
217	const (
218		RequirementRequired Requirement = "required"
219		RequirementAdvisory Requirement = "advisory"
220	)
221	
222	// Condition carries a stable decision plus operator-facing evidence and the
223	// narrow remediation for an unmet result.
224	type Condition struct {
225		Code        ConditionCode
226		Verdict     Verdict
227		Requirement Requirement
228		Evidence    string
229		Remediation string
230	}
231	
232	var stableCode = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$`)
233	
234	// Validate rejects conditions that cannot be fingerprinted or aggregated with
235	// defined semantics.
236	func (c Condition) Validate() error {
237		if !stableCode.MatchString(string(c.Code)) {
238			return fmt.Errorf("condition code %q is not a stable lowercase code", c.Code)
239		}
240		switch c.Verdict {
241		case VerdictMet, VerdictNeedsInput, VerdictBlocked, VerdictUnknown, VerdictError, VerdictUnsupported, VerdictCurrent:
242		default:
243			return fmt.Errorf("condition %s has unknown verdict %q", c.Code, c.Verdict)
244		}
245		switch c.Requirement {
246		case RequirementRequired, RequirementAdvisory:
247		default:
248			return fmt.Errorf("condition %s has unknown requirement %q", c.Code, c.Requirement)
249		}
250		return nil
251	}
252	
253	// ConditionFromObservation maps observation completeness to a fail-closed
254	// verdict. Capability policy such as unsupported remains an explicit condition
255	// decision rather than an inferred observation result.
256	func ConditionFromObservation(code ConditionCode, requirement Requirement, observation Observation, remediation string) Condition {
257		verdict := VerdictUnknown
258		switch observation.State {
259		case ObservationKnown:
260			verdict = VerdictMet
261		case ObservationError:
262			verdict = VerdictError
263		case ObservationUnknown, ObservationSkipped, ObservationLoading:
264			verdict = VerdictUnknown
265		default:
266			verdict = VerdictError
267		}
268		evidence := observation.Evidence
269		if evidence == "" {
270			switch {
271			case observation.Failure != "":
272				evidence = observation.Failure
273			case observation.Value != "":
274				evidence = observation.Value
275			default:
276				evidence = string(observation.State)
277			}
278		}
279		return Condition{
280			Code: code, Verdict: verdict, Requirement: requirement,
281			Evidence: evidence, Remediation: remediation,
282		}
283	}
284	
285	// Availability is the aggregate action status shown by any caller.
286	type Availability string
287	
288	const (
289		AvailabilityReady       Availability = "ready"
290		AvailabilityNeedsInput  Availability = "needs-input"
291		AvailabilityBlocked     Availability = "blocked"
292		AvailabilityUnknown     Availability = "unknown"
293		AvailabilityError       Availability = "error"
294		AvailabilityUnsupported Availability = "unsupported"
295		AvailabilityCurrent     Availability = "current"
296	)
297	
298	// AvailabilityFor derives action readiness from required conditions only. The
299	// order is fail-closed and deterministic when more than one required condition
300	// is unmet; advisory evidence never changes the result.
301	func AvailabilityFor(conditions []Condition) Availability {
302		availability := AvailabilityReady
303		priority := func(value Availability) int {
304			switch value {
305			case AvailabilityError:
306				return 6
307			case AvailabilityBlocked:
308				return 5
309			case AvailabilityNeedsInput:
310				return 4
311			case AvailabilityUnknown:
312				return 3
313			case AvailabilityUnsupported:
314				return 2
315			case AvailabilityCurrent:
316				return 1
317			default:
318				return 0
319			}
320		}
321		for _, condition := range conditions {
322			if condition.Requirement == RequirementAdvisory {
323				continue
324			}
325			candidate := AvailabilityReady
326			if condition.Requirement != RequirementRequired {
327				candidate = AvailabilityError
328			} else {
329				switch condition.Verdict {
330				case VerdictMet:
331					continue
332				case VerdictNeedsInput:
333					candidate = AvailabilityNeedsInput
334				case VerdictBlocked:
335					candidate = AvailabilityBlocked
336				case VerdictUnknown:
337					candidate = AvailabilityUnknown
338				case VerdictError:
339					candidate = AvailabilityError
340				case VerdictUnsupported:
341					candidate = AvailabilityUnsupported
342				case VerdictCurrent:
343					candidate = AvailabilityCurrent
344				default:
345					candidate = AvailabilityError
346				}
347			}
348			if priority(candidate) > priority(availability) {
349				availability = candidate
350			}
351		}
352		return availability
353	}
354	
355	// EffectCode is a stable machine-readable mutation or external operation.
356	type EffectCode string
357	
358	// Effect is one ordered operation proposed by a plan. Details are immutable by
359	// interface and may carry exact refs, handles, or paths needed by an executor.
360	type Effect struct {
361		Code        EffectCode
362		Description string
363		Target      string
364		Destructive bool
365		Network     bool
366		Details     Fields
367	}
368	
369	// NewEffect copies details into deterministic storage.
370	func NewEffect(code EffectCode, description, target string, destructive, network bool, details map[string]string) Effect {
371		return Effect{
372			Code: code, Description: description, Target: target,
373			Destructive: destructive, Network: network, Details: NewFields(details),
374		}
375	}
376	
377	// Clone returns an independent effect value.
378	func (e Effect) Clone() Effect {
379		e.Details = e.Details.clone()
380		return e
381	}
382	
383	// Validate rejects effects without a stable code.
384	func (e Effect) Validate() error {
385		if !stableCode.MatchString(string(e.Code)) {
386			return fmt.Errorf("effect code %q is not a stable lowercase code", e.Code)
387		}
388		for _, field := range e.Details.entries {
389			if strings.TrimSpace(field.Key) == "" {
390				return fmt.Errorf("effect %s has an empty detail key", e.Code)
391			}
392		}
393		return nil
394	}
395

254	func (e *executionState) run(effect Effect, operation func() (string, error)) error {
255		step := StepResult{Effect: effect.Clone(), Status: StepAttempted, StartedAt: e.service.now()}
256		detail, err := operation()
257		step.FinishedAt = e.service.now()
258		step.Detail = detail
259		if err != nil {
260			step.Status = StepFailed
261			step.Failure = err.Error()
262			e.steps = append(e.steps, step)
263			return err
264		}
265		step.Status = StepCompleted
266		e.steps = append(e.steps, step)
267		return nil
268	}
269	
270	func (e *executionState) runWarning(effect Effect, operation func() (string, error), warningPrefix string) {
271		err := e.run(effect, operation)
272		if err != nil {
273			e.warnings = append(e.warnings, warningPrefix+": "+err.Error())
274		}
275	}
276	
277	func (e *executionState) result() Result {
278		spec := ResultSpec{
279			Steps: e.steps, Warnings: e.warnings, Recovery: e.recovery,
280			PartialSuccess: e.partial,
281			Milestone:      e.milestone, Handoff: e.handoff, Remote: e.remote, FreshSnapshotRef: e.snapshot,
282		}
283		for _, step := range e.steps {
284			if step.Status == StepCompleted {
285				spec.PartialSuccess = true
286				break
287			}
288		}
289		if len(e.steps) > 0 && e.steps[len(e.steps)-1].Status == StepCompleted &&
290			(e.snapshot != "" || e.remote != nil) && len(e.recovery) == 0 {
291			// Successful completion is not partial merely because it had effects.
292			// Remote refresh is intentionally run-local and therefore completes with
293			// structured data rather than a persisted snapshot reference.
294			spec.PartialSuccess = false
295		}
296		return NewResult(spec)
297	}

476	func occupancyObservationError(occupancy runtime.Occupancy, err error) error {
477		if err != nil {
478			return err
479		}
480		if occupancy.CurrentPane.Err != nil {
481			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current %s runtime pane: %w", occupancy.Backend, occupancy.CurrentPane.Err)
482		}
483		if occupancy.SessionCoverageErr != nil {
484			return fmt.Errorf("classify %s checkout coverage: %w", occupancy.Backend, occupancy.SessionCoverageErr)
485		}
486		if occupancy.SessionList.Err != nil {
487			return fmt.Errorf("list %s runtime sessions: %w", occupancy.Backend, occupancy.SessionList.Err)
488		}
489		if occupancy.AgentActivityList.Err != nil {
490			return fmt.Errorf("list %s recognized agents: %w", occupancy.Backend, occupancy.AgentActivityList.Err)
491		}
492		return nil
493	}

495	func strictOccupancyError(occupancy runtime.Occupancy, err error) error {
496		if observationErr := occupancyObservationError(occupancy, err); observationErr != nil {
497			return observationErr
498		}
499		var blockers []string
500		for _, agent := range occupancy.Agents {
501			if !agent.Blocking {
502				continue
503			}
504			label := agent.Activity.Name
505			if label == "" {
506				label = agent.Activity.Agent
507			}
508			if label == "" {
509				label = "agent"
510			}
511			blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s, pane %s)", label, agent.Status, agent.Activity.PaneID))
512		}
513		if len(blockers) > 0 {
514			return fmt.Errorf("checkout is occupied by %s", strings.Join(blockers, ", "))
515		}
516		return nil
517	}

1	package taskflow
2	
3	import "context"
4	
5	// PlanHook performs action-specific observation and returns only construction
6	// input. BuildPlan remains the single graph, availability, and identity
7	// authority.
8	type PlanHook func(context.Context, Request) (PlanSpec, error)
9	
10	// ApplyHook executes one already validated plan and may return a partial Result
11	// together with an error.
12	type ApplyHook func(context.Context, Plan) (Result, error)
13	
14	// Handler contains the narrow hooks for one exact action. Either hook may be
15	// omitted; no production or unsafe fallback is installed.
16	type Handler struct {
17		Plan  PlanHook
18		Apply ApplyHook
19	}
20	
21	// Handlers maps stable action codes to injected behavior.
22	type Handlers map[Action]Handler
23	
24	// LocateTaskHook builds one exact managed-task locator from fresh durable and
25	// Git evidence. It is intentionally not accepted by NewService: only the
26	// guarded lifecycle constructor may install it.
27	type LocateTaskHook func(context.Context, string) (Locator, error)
28	
29	// Service is the UI-agnostic locate/plan/apply dispatcher.
30	type Service struct {
31		handlers   map[Action]Handler
32		locateTask LocateTaskHook
33	}
34	
35	// NewService copies handlers so later mutation of the caller's map cannot
36	// redirect a planned action.
37	func NewService(handlers Handlers) *Service {
38		copied := make(map[Action]Handler, len(handlers))
39		for action, handler := range handlers {
40			copied[action] = handler
41		}
42		return &Service{handlers: copied}
43	}
44	
45	// LocateTask returns an exact locator only when this service came from
46	// NewLifecycleService. Generic dispatch services deliberately have no fallback
47	// locator because guessing task, repository, or checkout identity is unsafe.
48	func (s *Service) LocateTask(ctx context.Context, taskID string) (Locator, error) {
49		if s == nil || s.locateTask == nil {
50			return Locator{}, ErrLocatorUnavailable
51		}
52		return s.locateTask(ctx, taskID)
53	}
54	
55	// Plan validates and freezes a request, delegates action-specific observations,
56	// then centrally builds the immutable plan.
57	func (s *Service) Plan(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Plan, error) {
58		normalized, err := normalizeRequest(request)
59		if err != nil {
60			return Plan{}, err
61		}
62		handler, ok := s.handlers[normalized.Action]
63		if !ok || handler.Plan == nil {
64			return Plan{}, &HandlerUnavailableError{Action: normalized.Action, Stage: "plan"}
65		}
66		spec, err := handler.Plan(ctx, normalized.Clone())
67		if err != nil {
68			return Plan{}, err
69		}
70		return BuildPlan(normalized, spec)
71	}
72	
73	// Apply validates identity and approval, rejects every status except READY, and
74	// delegates only to the handler registered for the plan's exact action. A
75	// handler's partial Result is returned unchanged in meaning alongside errors.
76	func (s *Service) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, approval Approval) (Result, error) {
77		frozen := plan.Clone()
78		if err := frozen.Validate(); err != nil {
79			return Result{}, err
80		}
81		if err := frozen.ValidateApproval(approval); err != nil {
82			return Result{}, err
83		}
84		if frozen.Availability != AvailabilityReady {
85			notReady := &PlanNotReadyError{
86				PlanID: frozen.PlanID, Availability: frozen.Availability,
87				conditions: frozen.Conditions(),
88			}
89			return Result{}, &InvalidPlanError{
90				PlanID: frozen.PlanID, Reason: "required conditions are not ready", Cause: notReady,
91			}
92		}
93		handler, ok := s.handlers[frozen.Action]
94		if !ok || handler.Apply == nil {
95			return Result{}, &HandlerUnavailableError{Action: frozen.Action, Stage: "apply"}
96		}
97		result, err := handler.Apply(ctx, frozen.Clone())
98		result = result.Clone()
99		if err != nil && len(result.CompletedSteps()) > 0 {
100			result.PartialSuccess = true
101		}
102		return result, err
103	}
104
