5	// TransitionRule is one cell in the exhaustive persisted lifecycle table. An
6	// empty Target on an allowed rule means the task record is removed rather than
7	// assigned another persisted state.
8	type TransitionRule struct {
9		Mode            task.CheckoutMode
10		Source          task.State
11		Action          Action
12		Target          task.State
13		Allowed         bool
14		StatePreserving bool
15		RemovesTask     bool
16		Milestone       Milestone
17		Reason          string
18	}
19	
20	// HasTarget reports whether an allowed edge writes a persisted target state.
21	func (r TransitionRule) HasTarget() bool { return r.Allowed && r.Target != "" }
22	
23	type transitionKey struct {
24		mode   task.CheckoutMode
25		state  task.State
26		action Action
27	}
28	
29	var (
30		modeOrder = []task.CheckoutMode{
31			task.ModeWorktree,
32			task.ModeBranch,
33			task.ModeDirect,
34		}
35		stateOrder = []task.State{
36			task.Hot,
37			task.Warm,
38			task.Cold,
39			task.Done,
40		}
41		transitionActionOrder = []Action{
42			ParkWarm,
43			ParkCold,
44			Resume,
45			CompleteDirect,
46			CompleteFF,
47			ReviewHandoff,
48			VerifyMerged,
49			Retire,
50		}
51		transitionTable = buildTransitionTable()
52	)
53	
54	// TransitionActions returns the actions represented in every mode/state row.
55	// Adopt, RemoveCheckout, RefreshRemote, and Reconcile are deliberately absent
56	// because they operate on row ownership, repository context, or drift rather
57	// than persisted-state edges.
58	func TransitionActions() []Action {
59		return append([]Action(nil), transitionActionOrder...)
60	}
61	
62	// PersistedLifecycleActions is the stable action dimension of the lifecycle
63	// table, including state-preserving review handoff but excluding repository
64	// context actions such as remote refresh.
65	func PersistedLifecycleActions() []Action { return TransitionActions() }
66	
67	// Transitions returns all table cells in mode, state, and action order. Denied
68	// cells are retained so additions cannot silently fall through a switch.
69	func Transitions() []TransitionRule {
70		out := make([]TransitionRule, 0, len(modeOrder)*len(stateOrder)*len(transitionActionOrder))
71		for _, mode := range modeOrder {
72			for _, state := range stateOrder {
73				for _, action := range transitionActionOrder {
74					out = append(out, transitionTable[transitionKey{mode: mode, state: state, action: action}])
75				}
76			}
77		}
78		return out
79	}

81	// LookupTransition returns the exhaustive table cell for known dimensions.
82	func LookupTransition(mode task.CheckoutMode, source task.State, action Action) (TransitionRule, bool) {
83		if !validMode(mode) || !validState(source) || !isTransitionAction(action) {
84			return TransitionRule{Mode: mode, Source: source, Action: action}, false
85		}
86		rule, ok := transitionTable[transitionKey{mode: mode, state: source, action: action}]
87		return rule, ok
88	}
89	
90	// RequireTransition returns the allowed table cell or a typed graph error.
91	func RequireTransition(mode task.CheckoutMode, source task.State, action Action) (TransitionRule, error) {
92		rule, found := LookupTransition(mode, source, action)
93		if !found {
94			rule.Reason = "unknown mode, state, or non-transition action"
95			return rule, &InvalidTransitionError{Rule: rule}
96		}
97		if !rule.Allowed {
98			return rule, &InvalidTransitionError{Rule: rule}
99		}
100		return rule, nil
101	}

130	func buildTransitionTable() map[transitionKey]TransitionRule {
131		table := make(map[transitionKey]TransitionRule, len(modeOrder)*len(stateOrder)*len(transitionActionOrder))

138					}
139					table[transitionKey{mode: mode, state: source, action: action}] = rule
140				}
141			}
142		}
143	
144		allow := func(mode task.CheckoutMode, source task.State, action Action, target task.State, preserving, removes bool, milestone Milestone) {
145			key := transitionKey{mode: mode, state: source, action: action}
146			table[key] = TransitionRule{
147				Mode: mode, Source: source, Action: action, Target: target,
148				Allowed: true, StatePreserving: preserving, RemovesTask: removes,
149				Milestone: milestone,
150			}
151		}
152	
153		for _, mode := range []task.CheckoutMode{task.ModeWorktree, task.ModeBranch} {
154			allow(mode, task.Hot, ParkWarm, task.Warm, false, false, MilestoneNone)
155			// Existing park accepts WARM tasks so it can update parking metadata and
156			// close a residual runtime without manufacturing a backward transition.
157			allow(mode, task.Warm, ParkWarm, task.Warm, true, false, MilestoneNone)
158			allow(mode, task.Hot, ParkCold, task.Cold, false, false, MilestoneNone)
159			allow(mode, task.Warm, ParkCold, task.Cold, false, false, MilestoneNone)
160			allow(mode, task.Warm, Resume, task.Hot, false, false, MilestoneNone)
161			allow(mode, task.Cold, Resume, task.Hot, false, false, MilestoneNone)
162			allow(mode, task.Hot, CompleteFF, task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
163			allow(mode, task.Warm, CompleteFF, task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
164			allow(mode, task.Hot, VerifyMerged, task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
165			allow(mode, task.Warm, VerifyMerged, task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
166			allow(mode, task.Hot, ReviewHandoff, task.Hot, true, false, MilestoneReviewReady)

168			allow(mode, task.Done, Retire, "", false, true, MilestoneRetired)
169		}
170	
171		allow(task.ModeDirect, task.Hot, ParkWarm, task.Warm, false, false, MilestoneNone)
172		allow(task.ModeDirect, task.Warm, ParkWarm, task.Warm, true, false, MilestoneNone)
173		allow(task.ModeDirect, task.Warm, Resume, task.Hot, false, false, MilestoneNone)
174		allow(task.ModeDirect, task.Hot, CompleteDirect, task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
175		allow(task.ModeDirect, task.Warm, CompleteDirect, task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
176		allow(task.ModeDirect, task.Done, Retire, "", false, true, MilestoneRetired)
177	
178		return table
179	}

181	func deniedTransitionReason(mode task.CheckoutMode, source task.State, action Action) string {
182		if mode == task.ModeDirect && source == task.Cold {
183			return "direct tasks cannot be COLD"
184		}
185		if action == ParkCold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
186			return "direct tasks use the canonical checkout and cannot be parked COLD"
187		}
188		if source == task.Done {
189			return "DONE tasks can only be retired through the persisted lifecycle graph"
190		}
191		if source == task.Cold {
192			return "COLD tasks must resume before any completion or review action"
193		}
194		if action == CompleteDirect && mode != task.ModeDirect {
195			return "direct completion is only valid for direct tasks"
196		}
197		if (action == CompleteFF || action == ReviewHandoff || action == VerifyMerged) && mode == task.ModeDirect {
198			return "direct tasks have no separate branch to integrate or hand off"
199		}
200		return "the edge is not in the approved lifecycle graph"
201	}

15	// expected path (or an intentionally empty COLD path) so Plan can explain the
16	// drift instead of losing the task before transition validation.
17	func (s *lifecycleService) locateExactTask(ctx context.Context, taskID string) (Locator, error) {

33		mode := candidate.EffectiveMode()

35			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: exact task %q has invalid mode or state", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID)
36		}
37

123	func (s *lifecycleService) locateRegisteredCheckout(
124		ctx context.Context,
125		candidate task.Task,
126		repoPath string,
127		expectedCheckout string,
128	) (gitx.RegisteredWorktree, bool) {
129		if expectedCheckout != "" {
130			registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, expectedCheckout)
131			return registered, err == nil
132		}
133		if candidate.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeWorktree || candidate.State != task.Cold {
134			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
135		}
136	
137		worktrees, err := s.gitWorktrees(ctx, repoPath)
138		if err != nil {
139			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
140		}
141		match := ""
142		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
143			if worktree.Branch != candidate.Branch {
144				continue
145			}
146			if match != "" {
147				return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
148			}
149			match = worktree.Path
150		}
151		if match == "" {
152			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
153		}
154		registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, match)
155		return registered, err == nil
156	}
157	
158	func (s *lifecycleService) branchUpstream(ctx context.Context, repoPath, branch string) string {
159		if branch == "" {
160			return ""
161		}
162		value, err := s.gitRun(ctx, repoPath,
163			"for-each-ref", "--format=%(upstream:short)", localBranchRef(branch),
164		)
165		if err != nil {
166			return ""
167		}
168		return strings.TrimSpace(value)
169	}

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)

90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98		// Sessions lets a coordinating caller share one runtime query across task,
99		// repository, and Try inventories.
100		Sessions        []runtime.Session
101		SessionsSet     bool
102		SessionsTracked bool
103		// Limiter shares one process-heavy enrichment bound across collectors.
104		Limiter *Limiter
105	}
106	
107	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
108	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
109	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
110	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
111		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
112	
113		sessions := opts.Sessions
114		tracked := opts.SessionsTracked
115		if !opts.SessionsSet && !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
116			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
117				sessions, tracked = s, true
118			}
119		}
120	
121		var wg sync.WaitGroup
122		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
123		// large inventory would thrash. Coordinated TUI loads share this limiter with
124		// repository enrichment.
125		limiter := opts.Limiter
126		if limiter == nil {
127			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
128		}
129	
130		for i, t := range tasks {
131			rows[i].Task = t
132			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
133	
134			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			wg.Add(1)
138			go func(i int) {
139				defer wg.Done()
140				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
141				if !ok {
142					return
143				}
144				defer release()
145				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
146			}(i)
147		}
148		wg.Wait()
149	
150		for i := range rows {
151			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
152			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
153		}
154		return rows
155	}
156	
157	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
158		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
159			return t.WorktreePath
160		}
161		return t.RepoPath
162	}
163	
164	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
165		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
166		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
167		if !r.CheckoutExists {
168			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
169				r.WorktreeMissing = true
170			}
171			return
172		}
173		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
174			r.StatusErr = err
175		} else {
176			r.Status = st
177		}
178		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
179			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
180		}
181		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
182		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
183		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
184			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
185				r.WorktreeMissing = true
186			}
187		}
188	}

121			if resolveErr != nil {
122				result.CurrentPane.Err = resolveErr
123			} else if paneID == "" {
124				result.CurrentPane.Err = fmt.Errorf("current pane resolver returned an empty pane id")
125			} else {
126				result.CallerPaneID = paneID
127			}
128		}
129	
130		result.SessionList.Attempted = true
131		sessions, listErr := rt.List(ctx)
132		if listErr != nil {
133			result.SessionList.Err = listErr
134		} else {
135			for _, observed := range sessions {
136				covering, mixed, classifyErr := classifyOccupancySession(ctx, checkout, observed)
137				if classifyErr != nil {
138					result.SessionCoverageErr = classifyErr
139					result.Sessions = nil
140					break
141				}
142				if len(covering) == 0 {
143					continue
144				}
145				result.Sessions = append(result.Sessions, OccupancySession{
146					Runtime: observed,
147					Panes:   covering,
148					Mixed:   mixed,
149					IsCaller: observed.Handle == opts.CallerWorkspaceID ||
150						occupancyPanePresent(observed.Panes, result.CallerPaneID),
151				})
152			}
153		}
154	
155		lister, listsAgents := rt.(AgentActivityLister)
156		result.AgentActivityList.Supported = listsAgents
157		if !listsAgents {
158			// Some backends can identify an agent on a pane without providing the
159			// richer recognized-agent inventory. Preserve that live evidence as the
160			// strict-profile fallback rather than treating an unsupported lister as an
161			// observed empty list.
162			for _, session := range result.Sessions {
163				for _, pane := range session.Panes {
164					if pane.Agent == "" && pane.AgentSession == "" {
165						continue
166					}
167					cwd := pane.CWD
168					if cwd == "" {
169						cwd = pane.ShellCWD
170					}
171					activity := AgentActivity{
172						PaneID: pane.ID, WorkspaceID: session.Runtime.Handle,
173						Agent: pane.Agent, Status: pane.AgentStatus, CWD: cwd,
174					}
175					if coverageErr := appendOccupancyAgent(ctx, &result, checkout, opts, activity); coverageErr != nil {
176						result.SessionCoverageErr = coverageErr
177						result.Agents = nil
178						return result, nil
179					}
180				}
181			}
182			return result, nil
183		}
184		result.AgentActivityList.Attempted = true
185		activities, activityErr := lister.AgentActivities(ctx)
186		if activityErr != nil {
187			result.AgentActivityList.Err = activityErr
188			return result, nil
189		}
190		for _, activity := range activities {
191			if coverageErr := appendOccupancyAgent(ctx, &result, checkout, opts, activity); coverageErr != nil {
192				result.AgentActivityList.Err = coverageErr
193				result.Agents = nil
194				return result, nil
195			}
196		}
197		return result, nil
198	}

200	func appendOccupancyAgent(ctx context.Context, result *Occupancy, checkout checkoutIdentity, opts OccupancyOptions, activity AgentActivity) error {
201		covered, err := activityCoversCheckout(ctx, checkout, activity.CWD)
202		if err != nil {
203			return fmt.Errorf("classify recognized agent pane %s: %w", activity.PaneID, err)
204		}
205		if !covered {
206			return nil
207		}
208		status := normalizeOccupancyStatus(activity.Status)
209		caller := result.CallerPaneID != "" && activity.PaneID == result.CallerPaneID
210		handle := correlatedSession(result.Sessions, activity)
211		result.Agents = append(result.Agents, OccupancyAgent{
212			Activity:      activity,
213			Status:        status,
214			SessionHandle: handle,
215			IsCaller:      caller,
216			Blocking:      occupancyAgentBlocks(opts, status, caller, handle != ""),
217		})
218		return nil
219	}

221	type checkoutIdentity struct {
222		path string
223		git  bool
224	}
225	
226	func inspectCheckoutIdentity(ctx context.Context, dir string) (checkoutIdentity, error) {
227		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(dir)
228		if err != nil {
229			return checkoutIdentity{}, err
230		}
231		repo, discoverErr := gitx.Discover(ctx, canonical)
232		if discoverErr == nil && repo.Root != "" {
233			root, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(repo.Root)
234			if canonicalErr != nil {
235				return checkoutIdentity{}, canonicalErr
236			}
237			return checkoutIdentity{path: root, git: true}, nil
238		}
239		if discoverErr != nil && !errors.Is(discoverErr, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
240			return checkoutIdentity{}, discoverErr
241		}
242		return checkoutIdentity{path: canonical}, nil
243	}
244	
245	func activityCoversCheckout(ctx context.Context, target checkoutIdentity, cwd string) (bool, error) {
246		if cwd == "" {
247			return false, fmt.Errorf("recognized agent has no cwd")
248		}
249		activity, err := inspectCheckoutIdentity(ctx, cwd)
250		if err != nil {
251			return false, err
252		}
253		if target.git && activity.git {
254			return target.path == activity.path, nil
255		}
256		return pathx.Contains(target.path, activity.path)
257	}
258	
259	func classifyOccupancySession(ctx context.Context, target checkoutIdentity, session Session) ([]Pane, []Pane, error) {
260		panes := session.Panes
261		if len(panes) == 0 {
262			for i, dir := range session.Dirs {
263				panes = append(panes, Pane{ID: fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", session.Handle, i), CWD: dir})
264			}
265		}
266		var covering, mixed []Pane
267		for _, pane := range panes {
268			paths := []string{pane.CWD}
269			if pane.ShellCWD != "" && pane.ShellCWD != pane.CWD {
270				paths = append(paths, pane.ShellCWD)
271			}
272			paneCovers, paneOutside, observed := false, false, false
273			for _, path := range paths {
274				if path == "" {
275					continue
276				}
277				observed = true
278				inside, err := activityCoversCheckout(ctx, target, path)
279				if err != nil {
280					return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("compare runtime pane %s path: %w", pane.ID, err)
281				}
282				if inside {
283					paneCovers = true
284				} else {
285					paneOutside = true
286				}
287			}
288			if paneCovers {
289				covering = append(covering, pane)
290			}
291			if paneOutside || !observed {
292				mixed = append(mixed, pane)
293			}
294		}
295		return covering, mixed, nil
296	}
297	
298	func occupancyPanePresent(panes []Pane, id string) bool {
299		if id == "" {
300			return false
301		}
302		for _, pane := range panes {
303			if pane.ID == id {
304				return true
305			}
306		}
307		return false
308	}
309	
310	func correlatedSession(sessions []OccupancySession, activity AgentActivity) string {
311		for _, session := range sessions {
312			if activity.WorkspaceID != "" && session.Runtime.Handle == activity.WorkspaceID {
313				return session.Runtime.Handle
314			}
315			if occupancyPanePresent(session.Runtime.Panes, activity.PaneID) {
316				return session.Runtime.Handle
317			}
318		}
319		return ""
320	}
321	
322	func normalizeOccupancyStatus(status string) string {
323		status = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(status))
324		if status == "" {
325			return "unknown"
326		}
327		return status
328	}
329	
330	func occupancyAgentBlocks(opts OccupancyOptions, status string, caller, correlated bool) bool {
331		if opts.Profile != OccupancyCleanup {
332			return !caller
333		}
334		// Cleanup can never close the caller or an activity that does not correlate
335		// with a freshly listed covering session.
336		if caller || !correlated {
337			return true
338		}
339		switch status {
340		case "idle", "done":
341			return false
342		case "unknown":
343			return !opts.CloseUnknown
344		default:
345			return true
346		}
347	}

70	// ReadinessInspection is a complete read-only observation for one exact
71	// checkout. KnownEmpty is true only when the store was read successfully and no
72	// intent matched the checkout; it distinguishes absence from failed observation.
73	type ReadinessInspection struct {
74		Checkout         string
75		KnownEmpty       bool
76		Intents          []IntentReadiness
77		ObservationError error
78	}

80	// Ready applies only the existing artifact finalization contract: an exact
81	// checkout is ready when it has no intents, or every intent was explicitly
82	// discarded or has a finalized receipt that is still reachable. Missing or
83	// incomplete evidence fails closed.
84	func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {
85		if i.ObservationError != nil {
86			return false
87		}
88		if len(i.Intents) == 0 {
89			return i.KnownEmpty
90		}
91		if i.KnownEmpty {
92			return false
93		}
94		for _, intent := range i.Intents {
95			if intent.ObservationError != nil {
96				return false
97			}
98			switch intent.State {
99			case ReadinessDiscarded:
100				// Discard is the existing explicit operator escape hatch.
101			case ReadinessFinalizedReachable:
102				if !intent.Finalized || !intent.ReceiptReachable {
103					return false
104				}
105			default:
106				return false
107			}
108		}
109		return true
110	}

112	// InspectReadiness gathers artifact finalization evidence for one exact
113	// checkout. It never reconciles receipts, finalizes intents, or writes either
114	// source files or intent records. The returned inspection retains partial
115	// evidence and the same wrapped error returned separately to ordinary callers.
116	func InspectReadiness(ctx context.Context, store *Store, checkout string) (ReadinessInspection, error) {
117		inspection := ReadinessInspection{}
118		if ctx == nil {
119			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a context")
120			inspection.ObservationError = err
121			return inspection, err
122		}
123		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
124			inspection.ObservationError = err
125			return inspection, err
126		}
127		if store == nil {
128			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a store")
129			inspection.ObservationError = err
130			return inspection, err
131		}
132	
133		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout)
134		if err != nil {
135			err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness checkout: %w", err)
136			inspection.ObservationError = err
137			return inspection, err
138		}
139		inspection.Checkout = canonical
140	
141		intents, err := store.List()
142		if err != nil {
143			err = fmt.Errorf("list artifact intents: %w", err)
144			inspection.ObservationError = err
145			return inspection, err
146		}
147		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
148			inspection.ObservationError = err
149			return inspection, err
150		}
151	
152		for _, intent := range intents {
153			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
154				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
155				break
156			}
157			intentCheckout, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
158			if err != nil {
159				err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact intent %s checkout: %w", intent.ID, err)
160				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
161				continue
162			}
163			if intentCheckout != canonical {
164				continue
165			}
166	
167			evidence := IntentReadiness{Intent: intent, Finalized: intent.Status == Finalized}
168			switch intent.Status {
169			case Armed, Finalizing:
170				evidence.State = ReadinessPending
171			case Failed:
172				evidence.State = ReadinessFailed
173			case Discarded:
174				evidence.State = ReadinessDiscarded
175			case Finalized:
176				evidence.ReceiptReachable, err = receiptRemainsReachable(ctx, canonical, intent)
177				switch {
178				case err != nil:
179					err = fmt.Errorf("inspect artifact intent %s receipt: %w", intent.ID, err)
180					evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
181					evidence.ObservationError = err
182					inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
183				case evidence.ReceiptReachable:
184					evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedReachable
185				default:
186					evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable
187				}
188			default:
189				// Store.List validates statuses, but fail closed if another Store
190				// implementation is introduced without preserving that contract.
191				err = fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s has unrecognized status %q", intent.ID, intent.Status)
192				evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
193				evidence.ObservationError = err
194				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
195			}
196			inspection.Intents = append(inspection.Intents, evidence)
197		}
198	
199		inspection.KnownEmpty = len(inspection.Intents) == 0 && inspection.ObservationError == nil
200		return inspection, inspection.ObservationError
201	}

203	func receiptRemainsReachable(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (bool, error) {
204		if intent.ArtifactCommit == "" {
205			return false, nil
206		}
207		candidates := []struct {
208			dir string
209			ref string
210		}{
211			{checkout, "HEAD"},
212			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
213			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
214		}
215		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(candidates))
216		var observationErr error
217		for _, candidate := range candidates {
218			if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
219				continue
220			}
221			key := candidate.dir + "\x00" + candidate.ref
222			if seen[key] {
223				continue
224			}
225			seen[key] = true
226			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
227				return false, joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
228			}
229			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
230				return true, nil
231			} else if !gitNotAncestor(err) {
232				observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr,
233					fmt.Errorf("check %s against %s in %s: %w", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref, candidate.dir, err))
234			}
235		}
236		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
237			observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
238		}
239		return false, observationErr
240	}
241	
242	func gitNotAncestor(err error) bool {
243		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
244		return errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1
245	}
246	
247	func joinReadinessError(current, next error) error {
248		if current == nil {
249			return next
250		}
251		if next == nil {
252			return current
253		}
254		return errors.Join(current, next)
255	}

257	func (s *Service) Prepare(ctx context.Context, request PrepareRequest) (*Intent, error) {
258		if s.Store == nil {
259			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact service needs a store")
260		}

262		if err != nil {

264		}

266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, err
268		}

271			return nil, err

273		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {

280		}

284		}
285		changes, err := statusPaths(ctx, repository.Root)
286		if err != nil {
287			return nil, err
288		}
289		var unrelated []string
290		for _, change := range changes {
291			if change.Staged {
292				return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation requires an empty index; staged path: %s", change.Path)
293			}
294			if !isRecognizedArtifact(change.Path) {
295				return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit product changes before prepare; dirty path: %s", change.Path)
296			}

298		}
299		transcript, err := FindTranscript(repository.Root, provider, sessionID)
300		if err != nil {

302		}
303		tracked, err := gitTracked(ctx, repository.Root, transcript.Path)
304		if err != nil {

306		}
307		info, err := os.Stat(transcript.Path)
308		if err != nil {
309			return nil, err
310		}
311		limit := s.LargeLimit
312		if limit <= 0 {
313			limit = DefaultLargeLimit
314		}
315		if !tracked && info.Size() > limit && !request.AllowLarge {
316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("untracked transcript is %d bytes; re-run with --allow-large after reviewing repository growth", info.Size())
317		}
318		plans, err := normalizePlans(repository.Root, request.Plans)
319		if err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		runID := request.RunID
323		if runID == "" {
324			runID = os.Getenv("DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID")
325		}
326		if runID == "" {
327			runID = fmt.Sprintf("run-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
328		}
329		selected := make(map[string]bool, len(plans)+1)
330		relTranscript, _ := filepath.Rel(repository.Root, transcript.Path)
331		selected[filepath.ToSlash(relTranscript)] = true
332		for _, plan := range plans {
333			rel, _ := filepath.Rel(repository.Root, plan)
334			selected[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = true
335		}
336		filtered := unrelated[:0]
337		for _, path := range unrelated {
338			if !selected[path] {
339				filtered = append(filtered, path)
340			}
341		}
342		intent := &Intent{
343			RunID: runID, Provider: provider, SessionID: sessionID, TaskID: request.TaskID,
344			RepoPath: repository.MainRoot, GitCommonDir: repository.GitCommonDir,
345			WorktreePath: repository.Root, Branch: status.Branch, Base: request.Base,
346			Head: head, PlanPaths: plans, UnrelatedArtifacts: filtered, AllowLarge: request.AllowLarge,
347		}
348		if err := s.Store.Create(ctx, intent); err != nil {
349			return nil, err

351		return intent, nil
352	}

354	func (s *Service) ObserveSessionEnd(ctx context.Context, runID string, when time.Time) error {
355		intent, err := s.Store.FindByRunID(runID)
356		if err != nil {
357			return nil // SessionEnd without an armed intent is deliberately a no-op.
358		}

362		return s.Store.Update(ctx, intent.ID, func(candidate *Intent) error {

368	func (s *Service) Finalize(ctx context.Context, request FinalizeRequest) (*Intent, error) {
369		if s.Store == nil {
370			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact service needs a store")
371		}
372		intent, err := s.resolveIntent(request)
373		if err != nil {
374			return nil, err
375		}
376		lockDir := filepath.Join(intent.GitCommonDir, "dev-artifact-finalize")
377		var finalized *Intent
378		err = catalog.NewStore(lockDir).WithLock(ctx, func() error {
379			current, err := s.resolveIntent(request)
380			if err != nil {
381				return err
382			}
383			finalized, err = s.finalizeLocked(ctx, request, current)
384			return err
385		})
386		return finalized, err
387	}

393					return nil, err

425			return nil, err
426		}
427		if _, err := StableSnapshot(ctx, transcript.Path, request.Settle); err != nil {
428			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "writer-active", err)
429		}
430		paths := append([]string{transcript.Path}, intent.PlanPaths...)
431		if err := ensureOnlyAllowedIndex(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, nil); err != nil {
432			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "index-not-empty", err)
433		}
434		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, append([]string{"add", "--"}, paths...)...); err != nil {
435			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "stage-failed", err)
436		}
437		cleanup := func() {
438			_, _ = gitx.Run(context.Background(), intent.WorktreePath, append([]string{"reset", "--"}, paths...)...)
439		}
440		if err := s.ScanStaged(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, paths); err != nil {
441			cleanup()
442			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "scan-failed", err)
443		}
444		if _, err := StableSnapshot(ctx, transcript.Path, request.Settle); err != nil {
445			cleanup()
446			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "writer-active", err)
447		}
448		if err := ensureOnlyAllowedIndex(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, paths); err != nil {
449			cleanup()
450			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "index-drift", err)
451		}
452		if err := stagedFilesMatch(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, paths); err != nil {
453			cleanup()
454			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "index-drift", err)
455		}
456		message := fmt.Sprintf("chore: finalize %s agent session", intent.Provider)
457		trailers := fmt.Sprintf("Agent-Artifact-Session: %s:%s\nDev-Artifact-Intent: %s", intent.Provider, intent.SessionID, intent.ID)
458		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "commit", "-m", message, "-m", trailers); err != nil {
459			cleanup()
460			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "commit-failed", err)
461		}
462		commit, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
463		if err != nil {
464			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "receipt-failed", err)
465		}
466		if err := s.markFinalized(ctx, intent.ID, transcript.Path, commit); err != nil {
467			return nil, err
468		}
469		return s.Store.Get(intent.ID)
470	}

472	func (s *Service) resolveIntent(request FinalizeRequest) (*Intent, error) {
473		if request.IntentID != "" {
474			return s.Store.Get(request.IntentID)
475		}
476		if request.RunID != "" {
477			return s.Store.FindByRunID(request.RunID)
478		}
479		return nil, fmt.Errorf("finalize requires an intent or run id")
480	}

482	func (s *Service) revalidate(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
483		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
484		if err != nil {
485			return err
486		}
487		if repository.GitCommonDir != intent.GitCommonDir {
488			return fmt.Errorf("Git common-dir changed")
489		}
490		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
491		if err != nil {
492			return err
493		}
494		if status.Branch != intent.Branch || status.Detached {
495			return fmt.Errorf("branch changed from %s to %s", intent.Branch, status.Branch)
496		}
497		if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(intent.WorktreePath); err != nil {
498			return err
499		} else if active {
500			return fmt.Errorf("Git operation %s is in progress", operation)
501		}
502		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
503		if err != nil {
504			return err
505		}
506		if head != intent.Head {
507			return fmt.Errorf("HEAD changed from %s to %s", intent.Head, head)
508		}
509		return nil
510	}

512	func (s *Service) fail(ctx context.Context, id, code string, cause error) error {
513		_ = s.Store.Update(ctx, id, func(intent *Intent) error {
514			intent.Status = Failed
515			intent.FailureCode = code
516			return nil
517		})
518		return fmt.Errorf("artifact finalization %s: %w", code, cause)
519	}

523			intent.Status = Finalized
524			intent.TranscriptPath = transcript
525			intent.ArtifactCommit = commit

527			return nil
528		})

531	type statusPath struct {
532		Path   string
533		Staged bool
534	}

536	func statusPaths(ctx context.Context, repo string) ([]statusPath, error) {
537		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repo, "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
538		if err != nil {
539			return nil, err
540		}
541		fields := strings.Split(out, "\x00")
542		var paths []statusPath
543		for i := 0; i < len(fields); i++ {
544			entry := fields[i]
545			if len(entry) < 4 {
546				continue
547			}
548			code, path := entry[:2], filepath.ToSlash(entry[3:])
549			paths = append(paths, statusPath{Path: path, Staged: code[0] != ' ' && code[0] != '?'})
550			if code[0] == 'R' || code[0] == 'C' {
551				i++ // porcelain -z emits the source path as the next field.
552			}
553		}
554		return paths, nil
555	}

557	func isRecognizedArtifact(path string) bool {
558		path = filepath.ToSlash(strings.TrimPrefix(path, "./"))
559		for _, prefix := range []string{
560			".specstory/history/", ".claude/plans/", ".cursor/plans/", ".cursor/rules/",
561			".opencode/plans/", ".specify/", ".codex/",
562		} {
563			if strings.HasPrefix(path, prefix) {
564				return true
565			}
566		}
567		return path == ".specstory/statistics.json"
568	}

570	func normalizePlans(root string, paths []string) ([]string, error) {
571		var out []string
572		for _, path := range paths {
573			if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
574				path = filepath.Join(root, path)
575			}
576			inside, err := pathx.Contains(filepath.Join(root, ".claude", "plans"), path)
577			if err != nil || !inside {
578				return nil, fmt.Errorf("plan %s is outside .claude/plans", path)
579			}
580			canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(path)
581			if err != nil {
582				return nil, err
583			}
584			info, err := os.Stat(canonical)
585			if err != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
586				return nil, fmt.Errorf("plan %s is not a regular file", path)
587			}
588			out = append(out, canonical)
589		}
590		sort.Strings(out)
591		return out, nil
592	}

594	func gitTracked(ctx context.Context, repo, path string) (bool, error) {
595		rel, err := filepath.Rel(repo, path)
596		if err != nil {
597			return false, err
598		}
599		_, err = gitx.Run(ctx, repo, "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", rel)
600		if err == nil {
601			return true, nil
602		}
603		var gitErr *gitx.Error
604		if errors.As(err, &gitErr) {
605			return false, nil
606		}
607		return false, err
608	}

610	func ensureOnlyAllowedIndex(ctx context.Context, repo string, allowed []string) error {
611		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repo, "diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "-z")
612		if err != nil {
613			return err
614		}
615		allow := make(map[string]bool, len(allowed))
616		for _, path := range allowed {
617			rel, _ := filepath.Rel(repo, path)
618			allow[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = true
619		}
620		for _, path := range strings.Split(out, "\x00") {
621			if path != "" && !allow[filepath.ToSlash(path)] {
622				return fmt.Errorf("index contains unrelated path %s", path)
623			}
624		}
625		return nil
626	}
627	
628	func stagedFilesMatch(ctx context.Context, repo string, paths []string) error {
629		for _, path := range paths {
630			rel, err := filepath.Rel(repo, path)
631			if err != nil {
632				return err
633			}
634			workingBlob, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repo, "hash-object", "--", rel)
635			if err != nil {
636				return err
637			}
638			stagedBlob, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repo, "rev-parse", ":"+filepath.ToSlash(rel))
639			if err != nil {
640				return err
641			}
642			if workingBlob != stagedBlob {
643				return fmt.Errorf("staged artifact %s no longer matches scanned working bytes", filepath.ToSlash(rel))
644			}
645		}
646		return nil
647	}
648	
649	func findReceipt(ctx context.Context, repo, intentID string) (string, bool) {
650		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repo, "log", "-n", "100", "--format=%H%x00%B%x00")
651		if err != nil {
652			return "", false
653		}
654		fields := strings.Split(out, "\x00")
655		for i := 0; i+1 < len(fields); i += 2 {
656			if strings.Contains(fields[i+1], "Dev-Artifact-Intent: "+intentID) {
657				return fields[i], true
658			}
659		}
660		return "", false
661	}

65	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
66	//
67	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
68	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
69	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
70	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
71	type Store struct{ Dir string }
72	
73	// Tx is a task-store transaction whose caller holds the store's cross-process
74	// lock. It lets a lifecycle operation reload, revalidate and perform its final
75	// conditional write without another dev process changing task intent between
76	// those steps.
77	type Tx struct{ store *Store }

79	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.

82	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)

84	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
85	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
86		clean := func(s string) string {
87			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
88			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
89				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
90			}
91			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
92		}
93		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
94		if r == "" {
95			r = "repo"
96		}
97		if b == "" {
98			b = "branch"
99		}
100		return r + "__" + b
101	}

105	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write). Save is a
106	// compatibility upsert; callers that need collision or lost-update protection
107	// should use Create or Update.
108	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {

115	// Create atomically writes t only when its derived ID is unused. The caller's

118		var created *Record

154	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent. Corrupt
155	// records retain the historical warning behavior; ListRecords exposes them as
156	// typed diagnostics to callers that need to aggregate or retain the failures.
157	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
158		records, diagnostics, err := s.ListRecords()
159		if err != nil {

164		}

172	// ListRecords returns every valid task and a typed diagnostic for each task
173	// file that could not be read or decoded. Directory-level failures are fatal.
174	func (s *Store) ListRecords() ([]Record, []Diagnostic, error) {
175		return s.listRecordsUnlocked()
176	}
177	
178	// listRecordsUnlocked implements both the public read-only inventory and the
179	// transaction-scoped inventory. Callers using it for mutation authority must
180	// hold the store lock through the guarded operation.
181	func (s *Store) listRecordsUnlocked() ([]Record, []Diagnostic, error) {
182		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
183		if err != nil {
184			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
185				return nil, nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
186			}
187			return nil, nil, err
188		}
189		var records []Record
190		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
191		for _, entry := range entries {
192			name := entry.Name()
193			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
194				continue
195			}
196			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
197			record, err := s.getRecordUnlocked(id)
198			if err != nil {
199				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{
200					ID: id, Path: filepath.Join(s.Dir, name), Err: err,
201				})
202				continue
203			}
204			records = append(records, *record)
205		}
206		sortRecords(records)
207		sort.Slice(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool { return diagnostics[i].Path < diagnostics[j].Path })
208		return records, diagnostics, nil
209	}

260	// Create writes a task only when its derived ID is not already present.
261	func (tx *Tx) Create(t *Task) (*Record, error) {
262		if t == nil {
263			return nil, errors.New("create nil task")
264		}
265		candidate := cloneTask(*t)
266		if candidate.ID == "" {
267			candidate.ID = MakeID(candidate.Repo, candidate.Branch)
268		}
269		if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
270			return nil, err
271		}
272		if _, err := os.Lstat(tx.store.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
273			return nil, fmt.Errorf("task %q: %w", candidate.ID, ErrAlreadyExists)
274		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
275			return nil, fmt.Errorf("check task %s: %w", candidate.ID, err)
276		}
277		record, err := tx.store.saveUnlocked(&candidate)
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, err
280		}
281		*t = cloneTask(candidate)
282		return record, nil
283	}

285	// Update replaces a task only when the expected revision is still current.
286	func (tx *Tx) Update(t *Task, expectedRevision string) (*Record, error) {
287		if t == nil {
288			return nil, errors.New("update nil task")
289		}
290		candidate := cloneTask(*t)
291		if candidate.ID == "" {
292			candidate.ID = MakeID(candidate.Repo, candidate.Branch)
293		}
294		current, err := tx.store.getRecordUnlocked(candidate.ID)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		if current.Revision != expectedRevision {
299			return nil, &StaleRevisionError{
300				ID: candidate.ID, Expected: expectedRevision, Actual: current.Revision,
301			}
302		}
303		record, err := tx.store.saveUnlocked(&candidate)
304		if err != nil {
305			return nil, err
306		}
307		*t = cloneTask(candidate)
308		return record, nil
309	}

311	// Delete removes a task unconditionally inside a compatibility transaction.
312	func (tx *Tx) Delete(id string) error {
313		return tx.store.deleteUnlocked(id)
314	}

316	// DeleteIfRevision removes a task only while its revision remains current.
317	func (tx *Tx) DeleteIfRevision(id, expectedRevision string) error {
318		current, err := tx.store.getRecordUnlocked(id)
319		if err != nil {
320			return err
321		}
322		if current.Revision != expectedRevision {
323			return &StaleRevisionError{ID: id, Expected: expectedRevision, Actual: current.Revision}
324		}
325		return tx.store.deleteUnlocked(id)
326	}

328	// saveUnlocked atomically persists t. The caller must hold the store lock.
329	func (s *Store) saveUnlocked(t *Task) (*Record, error) {
330		if t.ID == "" {
331			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
332		}
333		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
334			return nil, err
335		}
336		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
337		if t.Created.IsZero() {
338			t.Created = now
339		}
340		t.Updated = now
341	
342		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
343			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
344		}
345		var encoded bytes.Buffer
346		if err := toml.NewEncoder(&encoded).Encode(t); err != nil {
347			return nil, fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
348		}
349		data := encoded.Bytes()
350	
351		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
352		// a half-parsed task behind.
353		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
354		if err != nil {
355			return nil, err
356		}
357		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
358		if _, err := tmp.Write(data); err != nil {
359			_ = tmp.Close()
360			return nil, fmt.Errorf("write task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
361		}
362		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
363			return nil, err
364		}
365		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
366			return nil, err
367		}
368		if err := os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID)); err != nil {
369			return nil, err
370		}
371		return &Record{Task: cloneTask(*t), Revision: revisionFor(t.ID, data)}, nil
372	}
373	
374	// getRecordUnlocked reads a complete record without taking the mutation lock.
375	// Atomic rename makes concurrent reads see either the previous or next bytes.
376	func (s *Store) getRecordUnlocked(id string) (*Record, error) {
377		data, err := os.ReadFile(s.path(id))
378		if err != nil {
379			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
380				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
381			}
382			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
383		}
384		var t Task
385		if _, err := toml.Decode(string(data), &t); err != nil {
386			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
387		}
388		t.ID = id
389		return &Record{Task: t, Revision: revisionFor(id, data)}, nil
390	}
391	
392	// deleteUnlocked removes one record. The caller must hold the store lock.
393	func (s *Store) deleteUnlocked(id string) error {
394		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
395		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
396			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
397		}
398		return err
399	}
400	
401	// revisionFor hashes the task ID, a NUL domain separator, and the exact bytes
402	// persisted in the task file. A byte-for-byte rewrite keeps the revision;
403	// any byte or filename-ID change produces a different optimistic token.
404	func revisionFor(id string, data []byte) string {
405		payload := make([]byte, 0, len(id)+1+len(data))
406		payload = append(payload, id...)
407		payload = append(payload, 0)
408		payload = append(payload, data...)
409		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256(payload))
410	}
411	
412	func cloneTask(t Task) Task {
413		t.Tags = append([]string(nil), t.Tags...)
414		return t
415	}
416	
417	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
418	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
419	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
420	// than a silent pick.
421	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
422		if ref == "" {
423			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
424		}
425		all, err := s.List()
426		if err != nil {
427			return nil, err
428		}
429		for _, t := range all {
430			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
431				return t, nil
432			}
433		}
434		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
435		var hits []*Task
436		for _, t := range all {
437			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
438			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
439				hits = append(hits, t)
440			}
441		}
442		switch len(hits) {
443		case 1:
444			return hits[0], nil
445		case 0:
446			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
447		default:
448			names := make([]string, len(hits))
449			for i, t := range hits {
450				names[i] = t.ID
451			}
452			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
453		}
454	}
455	
456	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
457	//
458	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
459	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
460	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
461	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
462	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
463	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
464		all, err := s.List()
465		if err != nil {
466			return nil, err
467		}
468		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
469			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
470		}
471		var best *Task
472		var bestLen int
473		for _, t := range all {
474			root := t.WorktreePath
475			if root == "" {
476				root = t.RepoPath
477			}
478			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
479				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
480			}
481		}
482		if best == nil {
483			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
484		}
485		return best, nil
486	}
487	
488	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
489	func stateRank(s State) int {
490		switch s {
491		case Hot:
492			return 0
493		case Warm:
494			return 1
495		case Cold:
496			return 2
497		case Done:
498			return 3
499		}
500		return 4
501	}
502	
503	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
504	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
505		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
506			return taskLess(*ts[i], *ts[j])
507		})
508	}
509	
510	func sortRecords(records []Record) {
511		sort.SliceStable(records, func(i, j int) bool {
512			return taskLess(records[i].Task, records[j].Task)
513		})
514	}
515	
516	func taskLess(left, right Task) bool {
517		rl, rr := stateRank(left.State), stateRank(right.State)
518		if rl != rr {
519			return rl < rr
520		}
521		if !left.Updated.Equal(right.Updated) {
522			return left.Updated.After(right.Updated)
523		}
524		return left.ID < right.ID
525	}
526

12	
13	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
14	type Worktree struct {
15		Path string
16		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
17		Head string
18		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
19		Branch   string
20		Detached bool
21		Bare     bool
22		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
23		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
24		Locked         bool
25		LockedReason   string
26		Prunable       bool
27		PrunableReason string
28		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
29		Main bool
30	}
31	
32	var (
33		// ErrWorktreeNotFound reports that Git's current registry has no worktree at
34		// the requested canonical path.
35		ErrWorktreeNotFound = errors.New("registered worktree not found")
36		// ErrWorktreeAmbiguous reports that multiple Git records resolve to the same
37		// canonical path. Callers must not choose one of the aliases implicitly.
38		ErrWorktreeAmbiguous = errors.New("registered worktree path is ambiguous")
39	)
40	
41	// RegisteredWorktree is an identity snapshot from Git's worktree registry.
42	// Worktree preserves the complete parsed Git record; the other fields are canonical
43	// filesystem identities suitable for exact comparison across symlink and macOS
44	// path aliases. A snapshot proves registration, not permission to remove it.
45	type RegisteredWorktree struct {
46		Worktree       Worktree
47		RepositoryPath string
48		GitCommonDir   string
49		Path           string
50	}
51	
52	// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether the record is a linked checkout rather than
53	// Git's main checkout or a bare repository. It is classification, not a removal
54	// safety decision.
55	func (w RegisteredWorktree) IsLinkedWorktree() bool {
56		return !w.Worktree.Main && !w.Worktree.Bare
57	}
58	
59	// ResolveRegisteredWorktree resolves exactPath against a fresh authoritative
60	// `git worktree list --porcelain` query for the repository containing repoPath.
61	// Matching is exclusively by canonical filesystem identity, never by branch.
62	// It performs no prune, removal, or other mutation.
63	func ResolveRegisteredWorktree(ctx context.Context, repoPath, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
64		worktrees, err := Worktrees(ctx, repoPath)
65		if err != nil {
66			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("query registered worktrees: %w", err)
67		}
68		commonDir, err := run(ctx, repoPath, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
69		if err != nil {
70			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve Git common directory: %w", err)
71		}
72		return resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees, commonDir, exactPath)
73	}
74	
75	func resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees []Worktree, commonDir, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
76		path, err := pathx.Canonical(exactPath)
77		if err != nil {
78			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize requested worktree %q: %w", exactPath, err)
79		}
80		canonicalCommonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
81		if err != nil {
82			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git common directory %q: %w", commonDir, err)
83		}
84	
85		type match struct {
86			worktree Worktree
87			path     string
88		}
89		var (
90			repositoryPath string
91			matches        []match
92		)
93		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
94			canonicalPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(worktree.Path)
95			if canonicalErr != nil {
96				return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize registered worktree %q: %w", worktree.Path, canonicalErr)
97			}
98			if worktree.Main {
99				repositoryPath = canonicalPath
100			}
101			if sameCanonicalPath(path, canonicalPath) {
102				matches = append(matches, match{worktree: worktree, path: canonicalPath})
103			}
104		}
105	
106		switch len(matches) {
107		case 0:
108			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrWorktreeNotFound, path)
109		case 1:
110			if repositoryPath == "" {
111				return RegisteredWorktree{}, errors.New("registered worktree query has no main repository record")
112			}
113			return RegisteredWorktree{
114				Worktree:       matches[0].worktree,
115				RepositoryPath: repositoryPath,
116				GitCommonDir:   canonicalCommonDir,
117				Path:           matches[0].path,
118			}, nil
119		default:
120			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s resolves to %d records", ErrWorktreeAmbiguous, path, len(matches))
121		}
122	}
123	
124	func sameCanonicalPath(left, right string) bool {
125		if left == right {
126			return true
127		}
128		leftInfo, leftErr := os.Stat(left)
129		rightInfo, rightErr := os.Stat(right)
130		return leftErr == nil && rightErr == nil && os.SameFile(leftInfo, rightInfo)
131	}
132	
133	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
134	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
135	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
136		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
137		if err != nil {
138			return nil, err
139		}
140		var (
141			list []Worktree
142			cur  *Worktree
143		)
144		flush := func() {
145			if cur != nil {
146				list = append(list, *cur)
147				cur = nil
148			}
149		}
150		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
151			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
152				flush()
153				continue
154			}
155			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
156			switch key {
157			case "worktree":
158				flush()
159				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
160			case "HEAD":
161				if cur != nil {
162					cur.Head = val
163				}
164			case "branch":
165				if cur != nil {
166					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
167				}
168			case "detached":
169				if cur != nil {
170					cur.Detached = true
171				}
172			case "bare":
173				if cur != nil {
174					cur.Bare = true
175				}
176			case "locked":
177				if cur != nil {
178					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
179				}
180			case "prunable":
181				if cur != nil {
182					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
183				}
184			}
185		}
186		flush()
187		return list, nil
188	}
189	
190	// WorktreeFor finds the first worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git
191	// normally refuses duplicate branch checkouts, but --force can create them;
192	// identity-sensitive callers must use ResolveRegisteredWorktree instead.
193	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
194		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
195		if err != nil {
196			return Worktree{}, false, err
197		}
198		for _, w := range list {
199			if w.Branch == branch {
200				return w, true, nil
201			}
202		}
203		return Worktree{}, false, nil
204	}
205	
206	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
207	//
208	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
209	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
210	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
211	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
212	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
213		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
214		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
215		if exists {
216			args = append(args, path, branch)
217		} else {
218			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
219			if base != "" {
220				args = append(args, base)
221			}
222		}
223		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
224		return err
225	}
226	
227	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
228	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
229	// be any checkout of the same repository.
230	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
231		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
232		return err
233	}
234	
235	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
236	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
237	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
238		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
239		if err != nil {
240			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
241		}
242		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
243		if err != nil {
244			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
245		}
246		if inside {
247			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
248		}
249		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
250		if force {
251			args = append(args, "--force")
252		}
253		args = append(args, path)
254		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
255		return err
256	}
257	
258	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
259	// were deleted behind git's back.
260	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
261		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
262		return err
263	}
264	
265	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
266	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
267		if branch == "" {
268			return false
269		}
270		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
271		return err == nil
272	}
273	
274	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
275	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
276		if ref == "" {
277			return false
278		}
279		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
280		return err == nil
281	}

1	// Package retire coordinates destructive cleanup from outside the runtime and
2	// worktree being retired.
3	package retire
4	
5	import (
6		"context"
7		"fmt"
8		"os"
9		"sort"
10		"strings"
11		"time"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15	)
16	
17	// Options controls only fail-closed observations. Caller protection and active
18	// agent states are never bypassable.
19	type Options struct {
20		CWD               string
21		CallerWorkspaceID string
22		CallerPaneID      string
23		CloseUnknown      bool
24		AssumeNoRuntime   bool
25		PollInterval      time.Duration
26		Timeout           time.Duration
27	}
28	
29	// Session is one runtime session that currently covers the target checkout.
30	type Session struct {
31		Runtime runtime.Session
32		Panes   []runtime.Pane
33		Mixed   []runtime.Pane
34	}
35	
36	// Inspection is a fresh view of every runtime surface covering a checkout.
37	type Inspection struct {
38		Target          string
39		Sessions        []Session
40		ClosedSessions  int
41		Blockers        []string
42		RuntimeUnknown  bool
43		CallerContained bool
44	}
45	
46	// Ready reports whether destructive cleanup may proceed.
47	func (i Inspection) Ready() bool { return len(i.Blockers) == 0 }
48	
49	// Inspect discovers covering sessions and applies caller, mixed-workspace, and
50	// agent-state safety policy.
51	func Inspect(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, target string, opts Options) (Inspection, error) {
52		runtimeName := ""
53		if rt != nil {
54			runtimeName = rt.Name()
55		}
56		if opts.CallerWorkspaceID == "" && runtimeName != "tmux" && runtimeName != "zellij" && runtimeName != "none" {
57			opts.CallerWorkspaceID = os.Getenv("HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID")
58		}
59		if opts.CallerPaneID == "" {
60			switch runtimeName {
61			case "herdr":
62				opts.CallerPaneID = os.Getenv("HERDR_PANE_ID")
63			case "tmux":
64				opts.CallerPaneID = os.Getenv("TMUX_PANE")
65			case "zellij", "none":
66			default:
67				opts.CallerPaneID = os.Getenv("HERDR_PANE_ID")
68				if opts.CallerPaneID == "" {
69					opts.CallerPaneID = os.Getenv("TMUX_PANE")
70				}
71			}
72		}
73		evidence, err := runtime.InspectOccupancy(ctx, rt, target, runtime.OccupancyOptions{
74			Profile:           runtime.OccupancyCleanup,
75			CallerWorkspaceID: opts.CallerWorkspaceID,
76			CallerPaneID:      opts.CallerPaneID,
77			CloseUnknown:      opts.CloseUnknown,
78		})
79		if err != nil {
80			return Inspection{}, fmt.Errorf("inspect retirement occupancy: %w", err)
81		}
82		result := Inspection{Target: evidence.Target}
83		cwd := opts.CWD
84		if cwd == "" {
85			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
86			if err != nil {
87				return Inspection{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve caller directory: %w", err)
88			}
89		}
90		if inside, compareErr := pathx.Contains(evidence.Target, cwd); compareErr != nil {
91			return Inspection{}, fmt.Errorf("compare caller directory: %w", compareErr)
92		} else if inside {
93			result.CallerContained = true
94			result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
95				fmt.Sprintf("caller is inside target checkout %s", evidence.Target))
96		}
97	
98		if evidence.CurrentPane.Err != nil {
99			return Inspection{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve current %s runtime pane: %w", evidence.Backend, evidence.CurrentPane.Err)
100		}
101		if evidence.SessionCoverageErr != nil {
102			return Inspection{}, evidence.SessionCoverageErr
103		}

107		if evidence.SessionList.Err != nil {

109				return Inspection{}, fmt.Errorf("list %s runtime sessions: %w", evidence.Backend, evidence.SessionList.Err)
110			}

112		}
113		if evidence.AgentActivityList.Err != nil {
114			return Inspection{}, fmt.Errorf("list %s recognized agents: %w", evidence.Backend, evidence.AgentActivityList.Err)
115		}
116		for _, observed := range evidence.Sessions {
117			result.Sessions = append(result.Sessions, Session{
118				Runtime: observed.Runtime,
119				Panes:   observed.Panes,
120				Mixed:   observed.Mixed,
121			})
122			if observed.IsCaller {
123				result.CallerContained = true
124				result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
125					fmt.Sprintf("caller runtime %s contains the target checkout", observed.Runtime.Handle))
126			}
127			if len(observed.Mixed) > 0 {
128				result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
129					fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s also contains %d pane(s) outside the target", observed.Runtime.Handle, len(observed.Mixed)))
130			}
131			for _, status := range coveringAgentStatuses(observed.Panes, observed.Runtime.AgentStatus) {
132				appendAgentStatusBlocker(&result, observed.Runtime.Handle, status, opts.CloseUnknown)
133			}
134		}
135		for _, agent := range evidence.Agents {
136			if !agent.Blocking {
137				continue
138			}
139			if agent.IsCaller {
140				result.CallerContained = true
141				if agent.SessionHandle != "" {
142					result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
143						fmt.Sprintf("caller runtime %s contains the target checkout", agent.SessionHandle))
144				} else {
145					result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
146						fmt.Sprintf("caller runtime pane %s contains the target checkout", agent.Activity.PaneID))
147				}
148				continue
149			}
150			if agent.SessionHandle == "" {
151				result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
152					fmt.Sprintf("recognized agent in pane %s covers the target without a closeable runtime session", agent.Activity.PaneID))
153				continue
154			}
155			appendAgentStatusBlocker(&result, agent.SessionHandle, agent.Status, opts.CloseUnknown)
156		}
157		return dedupe(result), nil
158	}
159	
160	// CloseAndWait closes every eligible covering session and proves that no
161	// runtime surface still covers target before returning.
162	func CloseAndWait(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, target string, opts Options) (Inspection, error) {
163		inspection, err := Inspect(ctx, rt, target, opts)
164		if err != nil {
165			return inspection, err
166		}
167		if !inspection.Ready() {
168			return inspection, fmt.Errorf("retirement blocked: %s", strings.Join(inspection.Blockers, "; "))
169		}
170		if inspection.RuntimeUnknown || rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" {
171			return inspection, nil
172		}
173		interval := opts.PollInterval
174		if interval <= 0 {
175			interval = 100 * time.Millisecond
176		}
177		timeout := opts.Timeout
178		if timeout <= 0 {
179			timeout = 5 * time.Second
180		}
181		deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
182		closed := make(map[string]bool)
183		for {
184			fresh, inspectErr := Inspect(ctx, rt, inspection.Target, opts)
185			if inspectErr != nil {
186				return inspection, fmt.Errorf("reinspect before %s runtime close: %w", rt.Name(), inspectErr)
187			}
188			if !fresh.Ready() {
189				return fresh, fmt.Errorf("retirement blocked after runtime state changed: %s", strings.Join(fresh.Blockers, "; "))
190			}
191			if len(fresh.Sessions) == 0 {
192				inspection.Sessions = nil
193				inspection.ClosedSessions = len(closed)
194				return inspection, nil
195			}
196			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
197				return inspection, fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for %d %s session(s) to release %s",
198					len(fresh.Sessions), rt.Name(), inspection.Target)
199			}
200			for _, session := range fresh.Sessions {
201				handle := session.Runtime.Handle
202				if closed[handle] {
203					continue
204				}
205				if err := rt.Close(ctx, handle); err != nil {
206					return inspection, fmt.Errorf("close %s runtime %s: %w", rt.Name(), handle, err)
207				}
208				closed[handle] = true
209				break // re-list before authorizing the next destructive close.
210			}
211			select {
212			case <-ctx.Done():
213				return inspection, ctx.Err()
214			case <-time.After(interval):
215			}
216		}
217	}
218	
219	func coveringAgentStatuses(panes []runtime.Pane, fallback string) []string {
220		set := make(map[string]bool)
221		for _, pane := range panes {
222			if pane.Agent != "" || pane.AgentSession != "" || pane.AgentStatus != "" {
223				set[strings.ToLower(pane.AgentStatus)] = true
224			}
225		}
226		if len(set) == 0 {
227			set[strings.ToLower(fallback)] = true
228		}
229		out := make([]string, 0, len(set))
230		for status := range set {
231			out = append(out, status)
232		}
233		sort.Strings(out)
234		return out
235	}
236	
237	func appendAgentStatusBlocker(result *Inspection, handle, rawStatus string, closeUnknown bool) {
238		status := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(rawStatus))
239		switch status {
240		case "idle", "done":
241			// Eligible after all structural checks pass.
242		case "working", "running", "busy", "blocked", "waiting":
243			result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
244				fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s has agent status %s", handle, status))
245		case "", "unknown":
246			if !closeUnknown {
247				result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
248					fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s has unknown agent status; pass --close-unknown from outside it", handle))
249			}
250		default:
251			result.Blockers = append(result.Blockers,
252				fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s has unrecognized agent status %s", handle, status))
253		}
254	}
255	
256	func dedupe(inspection Inspection) Inspection {
257		seen := make(map[string]bool)
258		out := inspection.Blockers[:0]
259		for _, blocker := range inspection.Blockers {
260			if !seen[blocker] {
261				seen[blocker] = true
262				out = append(out, blocker)
263			}
264		}
265		inspection.Blockers = out
266		return inspection
267	}
268
