513	// IdentityFromURL returns a forge and owner/name identity for an HTTPS or SSH
514	// Git remote. It is used to match remote inventories to local clones without
515	// assuming the checkout directory has the same name.
516	func IdentityFromURL(raw string) (Kind, string) {
517		kind := FromURL(raw)
518		if kind == Unknown {
519			return Unknown, ""
520		}
521		if kind == AzureDevOps {
522			identity, _, ok := parseAzureDevOpsRemote(raw)
523			if !ok {
524				return Unknown, ""
525			}
526			return kind, identity
527		}
528		s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
529		if strings.Contains(s, "://") {
530			if parsed, err := url.Parse(s); err == nil {
531				s = strings.TrimPrefix(parsed.Path, "/")
532			}
533		} else if at := strings.IndexByte(s, '@'); at >= 0 {
534			// SCP-style SSH: git@github.com:owner/repo.git
535			s = s[at+1:]
536			if colon := strings.IndexByte(s, ':'); colon >= 0 {
537				s = s[colon+1:]
538			}
539		}
540		s = strings.Trim(strings.TrimSuffix(s, ".git"), "/")
541		return kind, s
542	}

137	func (h *remoteTestHarness) newService(t *testing.T) *Service {
138		t.Helper()
139		service, err := NewLifecycleService(LifecycleConfig{
140			Config: h.cfg, Tasks: h.tasks, Artifacts: h.artifacts,
141			Host: "test-host", CWD: h.repo,
142			Clock: func() time.Time { return h.clock },
143			Hooks: LifecycleHooks{
144				RepoLock: func(_ context.Context, commonDir string, operation func() error) error {
145					h.calls = append(h.calls, "repo-lock:"+commonDir)
146					return operation()
147				},
148				GitDiscover: func(_ context.Context, dir string) (gitx.Repo, error) {
149					root := h.discoverAt
150					gitDir := h.common
151					linked := false
152					if dir == h.checkout {
153						root = h.checkout
154						gitDir = filepath.Join(h.common, "worktrees", "topic")
155						linked = true
156					}
157					return gitx.Repo{
158						Root: root, GitDir: gitDir, GitCommonDir: h.common,
159						MainRoot: h.discoverAt, Name: "repo", IsLinkedWorktree: linked,
160					}, nil
161				},
162				GitRun: func(_ context.Context, _ string, args ...string) (string, error) {
163					if len(args) == 0 {
164						return "", errors.New("empty Git invocation")
165					}
166					switch args[0] {
167					case "check-ref-format":
168						if len(args) != 2 || strings.Contains(args[1], "..") || strings.ContainsAny(args[1], " ~^:?*[\\") {
169							return "", errors.New("invalid ref")
170						}
171						return "", nil
172					case "rev-parse":
173						if len(args) != 3 || args[1] != "--verify" {
174							return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected rev-parse args %q", args)
175						}
176						ref := strings.TrimSuffix(args[2], "^{commit}")
177						if ref == "HEAD" {
178							ref = "refs/heads/topic"
179						}
180						oid, ok := h.refs[ref]
181						if !ok {
182							return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown ref %s", ref)
183						}
184						return oid, nil
185					case "fetch":
186						h.calls = append(h.calls, "fetch:"+strings.Join(args[1:], " "))
187						if h.fetchErr != nil {
188							return "", h.fetchErr
189						}
190						return "", nil
191					default:
192						return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected Git invocation %q", args)
193					}
194				},
195				GitRemote: func(_ context.Context, _ string, name string) string {
196					h.remoteNames = append(h.remoteNames, name)
197					return h.remoteURL
198				},
199				GitRefExists: func(_ context.Context, _ string, ref string) bool {
200					_, ok := h.refs[ref]
201					return ok
202				},
203				ResolveWorktree: func(_ context.Context, _ string, exact string) (gitx.RegisteredWorktree, error) {
204					want, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(h.checkout)
205					if canonicalErr != nil || exact != want {
206						return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", gitx.ErrWorktreeNotFound, exact)
207					}
208					repoPath, _ := pathx.Canonical(h.repo)
209					commonDir, _ := pathx.Canonical(h.common)
210					return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{
211						RepositoryPath: repoPath, GitCommonDir: commonDir, Path: want,
212						Worktree: gitx.Worktree{Path: want, Head: h.refs["refs/heads/topic"], Branch: "topic"},
213					}, nil
214				},
215				ResolveForge: func(kind forge.Kind) (forge.Forge, error) {
216					if h.resolveErr != nil {
217						return nil, h.resolveErr
218					}
219					if h.provider == nil {
220						return nil, nil
221					}
222					if h.provider.Kind() != kind {
223						return h.provider, nil
224					}
225					return h.provider, nil
226				},
227				QueryReview: func(_ context.Context, _ forge.Forge, _ string, query forge.ReviewQuery) (*forge.Review, error) {
228					h.calls = append(h.calls, "query:"+query.Repository+":"+query.Head+":"+query.Base)
229					h.queries = append(h.queries, query)
230					if h.queryReview == nil {
231						return nil, h.queryErr
232					}
233					copy := *h.queryReview
234					return &copy, h.queryErr
235				},
236				TaskCreate: func(*task.Tx, *task.Task) (*task.Record, error) {
237					h.taskWriteCalls++
238					return nil, errors.New("unexpected task create")
239				},
240				TaskUpdate: func(*task.Tx, *task.Task, string) (*task.Record, error) {
241					h.taskWriteCalls++
242					return nil, errors.New("unexpected task update")
243				},
244				TaskDelete: func(*task.Tx, string, string) error {
245					h.taskWriteCalls++
246					return errors.New("unexpected task delete")
247				},
248			},
249		})
250		if err != nil {
251			t.Fatalf("NewLifecycleService: %v", err)
252		}
253		return service
254	}

116	func TestRetireHookOrderAndLocksCoverEveryDestructiveEffect(t *testing.T) {
117		fixture := newLifecycleGitFixture(t, task.ModeWorktree, task.Done)
118		fake := newLifecycleFakeRuntime()
119		fake.setSessions(idleRuntimeSession("retire-order", fixture.worktree))
120		var (
121			mu           sync.Mutex
122			calls        []string
123			taskLockHeld atomic.Bool
124		)
125		record := func(value string) {
126			mu.Lock()
127			calls = append(calls, value)
128			mu.Unlock()
129		}
130		service := fixture.serviceWith(t, fake, fixture.root, LifecycleHooks{
131			RepoLock: func(_ context.Context, _ string, operation func() error) error {
132				record("repo-lock")
133				return operation()
134			},
135			CloseAndWait: func(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, path string, options retire.Options) (retire.Inspection, error) {
136				record("close")
137				return retire.CloseAndWait(ctx, rt, path, options)
138			},
139			RemoveWorktree: func(ctx context.Context, repoPath, path string, force bool) error {
140				record("remove")
141				probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 25*time.Millisecond)
142				defer cancel()
143				probeErr := fixture.tasks.WithLock(probeCtx, func(*task.Tx) error { return nil })
144				taskLockHeld.Store(errors.Is(probeErr, context.DeadlineExceeded))
145				return gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, force)
146			},
147			GitRun: func(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
148				if len(args) > 1 && args[0] == "branch" && args[1] == "-d" {
149					record("delete-branch")
150				}
151				return gitx.Run(ctx, dir, args...)
152			},
153			TaskDelete: func(tx *task.Tx, id, revision string) error {
154				record("delete-task")
155				return tx.DeleteIfRevision(id, revision)
156			},
157		})
158		plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), fixture.request(t, RetireOptions{DeleteBranch: true}))
159		if err != nil {
160			t.Fatal(err)
161		}
162		mu.Lock()
163		calls = nil
164		mu.Unlock()
165		result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan, ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, plan.Confirmation.Token))
166		if err != nil {
167			t.Fatalf("Apply: %v steps=%+v", err, result.AttemptedSteps())
168		}
169		mu.Lock()
170		got := append([]string(nil), calls...)
171		mu.Unlock()
172		want := []string{"repo-lock", "close", "remove", "delete-branch", "delete-task"}
173		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
174			t.Fatalf("hook order=%v want=%v", got, want)
175		}
176		if !taskLockHeld.Load() {
177			t.Fatal("worktree removal did not run while the task-store lock was held")
178		}
179		if result.Milestone != MilestoneRetired {
180			t.Fatalf("milestone=%s", result.Milestone)
181		}
182	}

250			deletion, ok := conditionByCode(plan, ConditionBranchDeletion)
251			if !ok || deletion.Verdict != VerdictBlocked || containsEffect(plan, EffectDeleteBranch) {
252				t.Fatalf("condition=%+v present=%t effects=%v", deletion, ok, effectCodes(plan))
253			}
254		})
255	}

487	func TestRemoveCheckoutRuntimeRetirementPolicy(t *testing.T) {
488		tests := []struct {
489			name       string
490			status     string
491			mixed      bool
492			caller     bool
493			listErr    bool
494			options    RemoveCheckoutOptions
495			want       Availability
496			apply      bool
497			wantCloses int
498		}{
499			{name: "caller", status: "idle", caller: true, want: AvailabilityBlocked},
500			{name: "mixed", status: "idle", mixed: true, want: AvailabilityBlocked},
501			{name: "active", status: "working", want: AvailabilityBlocked},
502			{name: "unrecognized", status: "sleeping", want: AvailabilityBlocked},
503			{name: "idle", status: "idle", want: AvailabilityReady, apply: true, wantCloses: 1},
504			{name: "done", status: "done", want: AvailabilityReady, apply: true, wantCloses: 1},
505			{name: "unknown default", status: "", want: AvailabilityBlocked},
506			{name: "unknown acknowledged", status: "", options: RemoveCheckoutOptions{CloseUnknown: true}, want: AvailabilityReady, apply: true, wantCloses: 1},
507			{name: "list error", listErr: true, want: AvailabilityError},
508			{name: "list error acknowledged", listErr: true, options: RemoveCheckoutOptions{AssumeNoRuntime: true}, want: AvailabilityReady, apply: true},
509		}
510		for _, test := range tests {
511			t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
512				fixture := newLifecycleGitFixture(t, task.ModeDirect, task.Done)
513				checkout := filepath.Join(fixture.root, "runtime-"+strings.ReplaceAll(test.name, " ", "-"))
514				locator := addUnmanagedCheckout(t, fixture, "runtime-"+strings.ReplaceAll(test.name, " ", "-"), checkout, false)
515				fake := newLifecycleFakeRuntime()
516				if test.listErr {
517					fake.listErr = errors.New("runtime list failed")
518				} else {
519					panes := []runtime.Pane{{
520						ID: "runtime-pane", CWD: checkout, Agent: "claude", AgentStatus: test.status,
521						AgentSession: "claude:1234567890abcdef",
522					}}
523					if test.mixed {
524						panes = append(panes, runtime.Pane{ID: "outside-pane", CWD: fixture.root})
525					}
526					fake.setSessions(runtime.Session{
527						Handle: "runtime-session", Dirs: []string{checkout}, Panes: panes, AgentStatus: test.status,
528					})
529				}
530				cwd := fixture.root
531				if test.caller {
532					cwd = checkout
533				}
534				service := fixture.serviceWith(t, fake, cwd, LifecycleHooks{})
535				request, _ := NewRequest(locator, test.options)
536				plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), request)
537				if err != nil {
538					t.Fatalf("Plan: %v", err)
539				}
540				if plan.Availability != test.want {
541					t.Fatalf("availability=%s want=%s conditions=%+v", plan.Availability, test.want, plan.Conditions())
542				}
543				if !test.apply {
544					return
545				}
546				result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan, Approve(plan.PlanID))
547				if err != nil {
548					t.Fatalf("Apply: %v steps=%+v", err, result.AttemptedSteps())
549				}
550				_, closes := fake.counts()
551				if closes != test.wantCloses {
552					t.Fatalf("close calls=%d want=%d", closes, test.wantCloses)
553				}
554			})
555		}
556	}

558	func TestDestructivePostCloseIdentityAndArtifactRacesBlockRemoval(t *testing.T) {
559		for _, race := range []string{"identity", "artifact"} {
560			t.Run(race, func(t *testing.T) {
561				fixture := newLifecycleGitFixture(t, task.ModeWorktree, task.Done)
562				fake := newLifecycleFakeRuntime()
563				fake.setSessions(idleRuntimeSession("post-close", fixture.worktree))
564				var removes atomic.Int32
565				service := fixture.serviceWith(t, fake, fixture.root, LifecycleHooks{
566					CloseAndWait: func(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, path string, options retire.Options) (retire.Inspection, error) {
567						inspection, err := retire.CloseAndWait(ctx, rt, path, options)
568						if err != nil {
569							return inspection, err
570						}
571						switch race {
572						case "identity":
573							if _, lockErr := gitx.Run(ctx, fixture.repo, "worktree", "lock", "--reason", "post-close-race", fixture.worktree); lockErr != nil {
574								t.Fatalf("lock worktree: %v", lockErr)
575								t.Cleanup(func() { _ = execGitForCleanup(fixture.repo, "worktree", "unlock", fixture.worktree) })
576							}
577						case "artifact":
578							createPendingArtifact(t, fixture, fixture.worktree, "feature", "post-close-artifact")
579						}
580						return inspection, nil
581					},
582					RemoveWorktree: func(context.Context, string, string, bool) error {
583						removes.Add(1)
584						return nil
585					},
586				})
587				plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), fixture.request(t, RetireOptions{}))
588				if err != nil {
589					t.Fatal(err)
590				}
591				result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan, Approve(plan.PlanID))
592				if err == nil {
593					t.Fatal("post-close race unexpectedly applied")
594				}
595				if removes.Load() != 0 || result.Milestone != MilestoneNone ||
596					!reflect.DeepEqual(stepCodes(result), []EffectCode{EffectCloseRuntime}) || !result.PartialSuccess {
597					t.Fatalf("removes=%d milestone=%s partial=%t steps=%+v error=%v", removes.Load(), result.Milestone, result.PartialSuccess, result.AttemptedSteps(), err)
598				}
599			})
600		}
601	}

603	func TestRemoveCheckoutHoldsRepositoryThenTaskStoreLockThroughRemoval(t *testing.T) {
604		fixture := newLifecycleGitFixture(t, task.ModeDirect, task.Done)
605		checkout := filepath.Join(fixture.root, "unmanaged-locks")
606		locator := addUnmanagedCheckout(t, fixture, "unmanaged-locks", checkout, false)
607		var (
608			mu           sync.Mutex
609			calls        []string
610			taskLockHeld atomic.Bool
611		)
612		recordCall := func(value string) {
613			mu.Lock()
614			calls = append(calls, value)
615			mu.Unlock()
616		}
617		service := fixture.serviceWith(t, runtime.None{}, fixture.root, LifecycleHooks{
618			RepoLock: func(_ context.Context, _ string, operation func() error) error {
619				recordCall("repo-lock")
620				return operation()
621			},
622			RemoveWorktree: func(ctx context.Context, repoPath, path string, force bool) error {
623				recordCall("remove")
624				probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 25*time.Millisecond)
625				defer cancel()
626				claim := &task.Task{Repo: "example", RepoPath: fixture.repo, Branch: "unmanaged-locks", Base: "main", Mode: task.ModeWorktree, State: task.Done, WorktreePath: checkout}
627				_, probeErr := fixture.tasks.Create(probeCtx, claim)
628				taskLockHeld.Store(errors.Is(probeErr, context.DeadlineExceeded))
629				return gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, force)
630			},
631		})
632		request, _ := NewRequest(locator, RemoveCheckoutOptions{})
633		plan, err := service.Plan(context.Background(), request)
634		if err != nil {
635			t.Fatal(err)
636		}
637		result, err := service.Apply(context.Background(), plan, Approve(plan.PlanID))
638		if err != nil {
639			t.Fatalf("Apply: %v steps=%+v", err, result.AttemptedSteps())
640		}
641		mu.Lock()
642		got := append([]string(nil), calls...)
643		mu.Unlock()
644		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"repo-lock", "remove"}) || !taskLockHeld.Load() {
645			t.Fatalf("calls=%v task-lock-held=%t", got, taskLockHeld.Load())
646		}
647	}

11	func TestTransitionTableExhaustive(t *testing.T) {
12		modes := []task.CheckoutMode{task.ModeWorktree, task.ModeBranch, task.ModeDirect}
13		states := []task.State{task.Hot, task.Warm, task.Cold, task.Done}
14		actions := []Action{
15			ParkWarm,
16			ParkCold,
17			Resume,
18			CompleteDirect,
19			CompleteFF,
20			ReviewHandoff,
21			VerifyMerged,
22			Retire,
23		}
24	
25		got := Transitions()
26		wantCount := len(modes) * len(states) * len(actions)
27		if len(got) != wantCount {
28			t.Fatalf("transition count = %d, want %d", len(got), wantCount)
29		}
30		seen := make(map[transitionKey]bool, wantCount)
31		for _, rule := range got {
32			key := transitionKey{mode: rule.Mode, state: rule.Source, action: rule.Action}
33			if seen[key] {
34				t.Fatalf("duplicate transition cell: %+v", key)
35			}
36			seen[key] = true
37		}
38	
39		for _, mode := range modes {
40			for _, state := range states {
41				for _, action := range actions {
42					rule, ok := LookupTransition(mode, state, action)
43					if !ok {
44						t.Fatalf("missing transition for %s/%s/%s", mode, state, action)
45					}
46					want := expectedTransition(mode, state, action)
47					if rule.Allowed != want.Allowed || rule.Target != want.Target ||
48						rule.StatePreserving != want.StatePreserving || rule.RemovesTask != want.RemovesTask ||
49						rule.Milestone != want.Milestone {
50						t.Errorf("transition %s/%s/%s = %+v, want %+v", mode, state, action, rule, want)
51					}
52				}
53			}
54		}
55	}

57	func TestRequestValidationUsesEveryTransitionCell(t *testing.T) {
58		for _, rule := range Transitions() {
59			request := Request{
60				Locator: Locator{Mode: rule.Mode, State: rule.Source},
61				Action:  rule.Action,
62				Options: transitionOptions(rule.Action),
63			}
64			err := request.Validate()
65			if rule.Allowed {
66				if err != nil {
67					t.Errorf("allowed request %s/%s/%s: %v", rule.Mode, rule.Source, rule.Action, err)
68				}
69				continue
70			}
71			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRequest) || !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidTransition) {
72				t.Errorf("denied request %s/%s/%s error = %v, want invalid request and transition", rule.Mode, rule.Source, rule.Action, err)
73			}
74		}
75	}

77	func transitionOptions(action Action) ActionOptions {
78		switch action {
79		case ParkWarm:
80			return ParkWarmOptions{}
81		case ParkCold:
82			return ParkColdOptions{}
83		case Resume:
84			return ResumeOptions{}
85		case CompleteDirect:
86			return CompleteDirectOptions{}
87		case CompleteFF:
88			return CompleteFFOptions{}
89		case ReviewHandoff:
90			return ReviewHandoffOptions{}
91		case VerifyMerged:
92			return VerifyMergedOptions{}
93		case Retire:
94			return RetireOptions{}
95		default:
96			panic("non-transition action " + action)
97		}
98	}

100	func expectedTransition(mode task.CheckoutMode, state task.State, action Action) TransitionRule {
101		rule := TransitionRule{Mode: mode, Source: state, Action: action}
102		allow := func(target task.State, preserving, removes bool, milestone Milestone) TransitionRule {
103			rule.Allowed = true
104			rule.Target = target
105			rule.StatePreserving = preserving
106			rule.RemovesTask = removes
107			rule.Milestone = milestone
108			return rule
109		}
110	
111		if mode == task.ModeDirect && state == task.Cold {
112			return rule
113		}
114		if action == Retire && state == task.Done {
115			return allow("", false, true, MilestoneRetired)
116		}
117		if state == task.Done || state == task.Cold && action != Resume {
118			return rule
119		}
120	
121		switch action {
122		case ParkWarm:
123			if state == task.Hot {
124				return allow(task.Warm, false, false, MilestoneNone)
125			}
126			if state == task.Warm {
127				return allow(task.Warm, true, false, MilestoneNone)
128			}
129		case ParkCold:
130			if mode != task.ModeDirect && (state == task.Hot || state == task.Warm) {
131				return allow(task.Cold, false, false, MilestoneNone)
132			}
133		case Resume:
134			if state == task.Warm || mode != task.ModeDirect && state == task.Cold {
135				return allow(task.Hot, false, false, MilestoneNone)
136			}
137		case CompleteDirect:
138			if mode == task.ModeDirect && (state == task.Hot || state == task.Warm) {
139				return allow(task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
140			}
141		case CompleteFF, VerifyMerged:
142			if mode != task.ModeDirect && (state == task.Hot || state == task.Warm) {
143				return allow(task.Done, false, false, MilestoneMerged)
144			}
145		case ReviewHandoff:
146			if mode != task.ModeDirect && (state == task.Hot || state == task.Warm) {
147				return allow(state, true, false, MilestoneReviewReady)
148			}
149		}
150		return rule
151	}

153	func TestTransitionTableRejectsInvalidColdAndDoneEdges(t *testing.T) {
154		for _, action := range TransitionActions() {
155			rule, ok := LookupTransition(task.ModeDirect, task.Cold, action)
156			if !ok || rule.Allowed {
157				t.Errorf("direct/COLD/%s should be denied, got %+v, found=%t", action, rule, ok)
158			}
159		}
160	
161		for _, mode := range []task.CheckoutMode{task.ModeWorktree, task.ModeBranch, task.ModeDirect} {
162			for _, action := range TransitionActions() {
163				rule, _ := LookupTransition(mode, task.Done, action)
164				want := action == Retire
165				if rule.Allowed != want {
166					t.Errorf("%s/DONE/%s allowed=%t, want %t", mode, action, rule.Allowed, want)
167				}
168			}
169		}
170	
171		for _, mode := range []task.CheckoutMode{task.ModeWorktree, task.ModeBranch} {
172			for _, action := range TransitionActions() {
173				rule, _ := LookupTransition(mode, task.Cold, action)
174				want := action == Resume
175				if rule.Allowed != want {
176					t.Errorf("%s/COLD/%s allowed=%t, want %t", mode, action, rule.Allowed, want)
177				}
178			}
179		}
180	}

182	func TestTransitionStatePreservationAndDomainActions(t *testing.T) {
183		for _, rule := range Transitions() {
184			if !rule.Allowed || !rule.HasTarget() || rule.Target != rule.Source {
185				continue
186			}
187			if !rule.StatePreserving {
188				t.Errorf("same-state rule is not marked preserving: %+v", rule)
189			}
190			switch rule.Action {
191			case ParkWarm:
192				if rule.Source != task.Warm {
193					t.Errorf("ParkWarm same-state edge starts at %s", rule.Source)
194				}
195			case ReviewHandoff:
196			default:
197				t.Errorf("undocumented same-state action: %+v", rule)
198			}
199		}
200	
201		for _, action := range []Action{Adopt, RemoveCheckout, RefreshRemote, Reconcile} {
202			if _, ok := LookupTransition(task.ModeWorktree, task.Hot, action); ok {
203				t.Errorf("domain action %s unexpectedly appears in persisted table", action)
204			}
205		}
206	
207		_, err := RequireTransition(task.ModeDirect, task.Cold, Resume)
208		if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidTransition) {
209			t.Fatalf("direct COLD error = %v, want ErrInvalidTransition", err)
210		}
211		var transitionErr *InvalidTransitionError
212		if !errors.As(err, &transitionErr) {
213			t.Fatalf("direct COLD error type = %T, want *InvalidTransitionError", err)
214		}
215	}

1	---
2	description: Choose the owner and location of each worktree, then provision ignored files and dependencies safely.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-29
6	---
7	
8	# Worktrees and provisioning
9	
10	A Git worktree begins as a clean checkout. `dev` owns durable change-stream worktrees and builds an inspectable plan for the ignored files and dependencies needed to make them usable.
11	
12	## Choose one lifecycle owner
13	
14	| Worktree kind | Owner | Typical location | Lifetime |
15	|---|---|---|---|
16	| feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | `dev` | configured `paths.worktree_path` | until `dev done`, `dev wt rm`, or an approved sweep |
17	| harness-scoped isolation | Claude Code or another harness | harness-owned directory such as `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` | governed by that harness's retention and safe-cleanup rules |
18	| externally created linked worktree | external until adopted | tool-specific | visible to `dev`, unmanaged until explicit adoption |
19	
20	Use `dev` when code, history, or plans must remain reviewable or a human may return later. Do not nest a long-lived `dev` worktree inside a repository; file watchers, language servers, backup tools, and searches in the outer checkout would see a second copy of the tree.
21	
22	`dev` creates the checkout with Git at its configured path. Herdr only opens that existing path, so worktree placement remains identical on machines without Herdr.
23	
24	## Inspect before creating
25	
26	```bash
27	dev wt plan
28	dev wt plan --write          # seed repository-owned .dev-cli/config.toml
29	dev wt create feat/auth --base main
30	dev wt list
31	```
32	
33	`dev wt plan` reads lockfiles, tool availability, configured include/link rules, and Git ignore state without changing the checkout. The resulting plan shows every runnable or skipped step and any safety downgrade.
34	
35	## Carry ignored files by allowlist
36	
37	```toml
38	[worktree]
39	include = [".env", ".env.local", "config/local.json"]
40	link = []
41	post_create = "auto"
42	strategy = "reinstall"
43	```
44	
45	Only paths that are both listed and confirmed by Git as ignored are copied. A tracked file already arrives through the branch; copying a different checkout's version over it would violate branch isolation.
46	
47	Included files are copied as files, not logged. Current provisioning also rechecks the source and destination path shape while opening/copying so source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused.
48	
49	Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` globally. Include that exact file only for a deliberately chosen launcher whose behavior depends on it, and verify the copy in the plan.
50	
51	## Select dependency strategy by correctness
52	
53	| Strategy | Effect | Guidance |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| `reinstall` | run the lockfile-derived install command | safe default |
56	| `copy` | duplicate an installed dependency directory | use only where paths are portable |
57	| `link` | share one dependency directory | fastest and usually unsafe for concurrent writers |
58	| `skip` | leave dependencies absent | container- or CI-driven development |
59	
60	Per-ecosystem overrides live in the project or global config:
61	
62	```toml
63	[worktree.strategies]
64	node = "copy"
65	```
66	
67	New project-owned overrides belong in `.dev-cli/config.toml`; legacy
68	`.dev.toml` remains readable under its compatibility behavior. A `post_create`
69	command from `.dev-cli/config.toml` does not run until its exact
70	executable-config hash is approved with `dev config trust . --yes`. Changing
71	the command invalidates that approval.
72	
73	Important built-in decisions:
74	
75	- Python virtual environments cannot be copied or linked because they embed absolute paths; `uv sync` can reuse its global cache.
76	- Node `node_modules` may be copied, but sharing is refused because either checkout can mutate it.
77	- Go uses a global content-addressed module cache, so there is no checkout-local dependency tree to copy.
78	- Cargo `target/` may be copied, but sharing concurrent build output is refused.
79	
80	An invalid or unsound request narrows to `reinstall` with a warning instead of silently creating a broken environment.
81	
82	## Auto-detected setup
83	
84	`post_create = "auto"` recognizes one manager per ecosystem, in priority order:
85	
86	| Marker | Command |
87	|---|---|
88	| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` |
89	| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` |
90	| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
91	| `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
92	| `yarn.lock` | `yarn install --immutable` |
93	| `go.mod` | `go mod download` |
94	| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fetch` |
95	| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` |
96	
97	A missing tool is reported and skipped. A failed setup command leaves the worktree in place so the branch and checkout can be repaired rather than discarded.
98	
99	## Reprovision or remove
100	
101	```bash
102	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree --dry-run
103	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree
104	dev wt rm feat/auth
105	```
106	
107	Removing a worktree and deleting a branch are separate decisions. `dev wt rm` preserves the branch and refuses a dirty checkout without explicit force. If the directory disappeared outside Git, it prunes the stale administrative entry.
108	
109	## Sources
110	
111	- [`internal/wt/plan.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/wt/plan.go)
112	- [`internal/wt/ecosystem.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/wt/ecosystem.go)
113	- [`internal/wt/provision.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/wt/provision.go)
114	- [`internal/wt/manager.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/wt/manager.go)
115	- [Claude Code worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees)
116
```
</details></tool-use>

8	
9	# Worktree 與環境佈建
10	
11	!!! note "術語規則"
12	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
13	
14	Git worktree 一開始是乾淨 checkout。`dev` 擁有持久變更流 (change stream) 的 worktree，並建立可檢查的 provisioning plan，說明要加入哪些 ignored files 與 dependencies。
15	
16	## 只選一個 lifecycle owner
17	
18	| Worktree 類型 | Owner | 常見位置 | Lifetime |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| feature、fix、experiment、跨機器 handoff | `dev` | 設定的 `paths.worktree_path` | `dev done` 只記錄 MERGED；直到後續 `dev retire`、明確 `dev wt rm` 或核准的 sweep 才移除 |
21	| harness-scoped isolation | Claude Code 或其他 harness | harness-owned path，例如 `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` | 由該 harness 的 retention 與 safe-cleanup 規則管理；Flow 不會 Adopt/Remove |
22	| 外部建立的 linked worktree | adoption 前由外部管理 | tool-specific | `dev`/`dev flow` 可看見；只有明確 Adopt 後才有 managed lifecycle |
23	
24	Code、history 或 plans 需要保持可 review，或人之後可能回來時，使用 `dev`。不要把長期 `dev` worktree 巢狀放在 repository 內；外層 checkout 的 file watcher、language server、backup tool 與搜尋會看到第二份 tree。
25	
26	`dev` 使用 Git 在設定路徑建立 checkout；Herdr 只開啟現有 path，因此沒有 Herdr 的機器仍維持相同 placement policy。
27	
28	`dev flow [repo]` 以 Git 的 authoritative worktree records 顯示 canonical、managed、unmanaged 與 strict `.claude/worktrees/` harness rows，另加入沒有 checkout 的 task-only rows。它不以 `worktree-*` branch prefix 猜 ownership；path/task binding 有歧義時標示 CONFLICT 並停止 lifecycle mutation。詳見 [Repository Flow 預覽](repository-flow.zh-TW.md)。
29	
30	## 建立前先檢查
31	
32	```bash
33	dev wt plan
34	dev wt plan --write          # 建立 repository-owned .dev-cli/config.toml
35	dev wt create feat/auth --base main
36	dev wt list
37	```
38	
39	`dev wt plan` 會讀取 lockfile、tool availability、include/link 規則與 Git ignore state，但不修改 checkout。Plan 列出每個可執行或 skipped step，以及任何 safety downgrade。
40	
41	## 用 allowlist 攜帶 ignored files
42	
43	```toml
44	[worktree]
45	include = [".env", ".env.local", "config/local.json"]
46	link = []
47	post_create = "auto"
48	strategy = "reinstall"
49	```
50	
51	只有明確列出、且 Git 確認為 ignored 的 path 才會被複製。Tracked file 已透過 branch 進入 checkout；用另一個 checkout 的版本覆蓋它會破壞 branch isolation。
52	
53	Included files 以檔案方式複製，內容不寫入 log。現行 provisioning 在 open/copy 過程也會再次檢查 source 與 destination path shape，拒絕 source swap 與 symlinked destination parent。
54	
55	不要全域加入 `.claude/settings.local.json`。只有刻意選擇且確實依賴它的 launcher 才加入該精確 path，並在 plan 中驗證。
56	
57	## 依 correctness 選 dependency strategy
58	
59	| Strategy | 效果 | 建議 |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| `reinstall` | 執行 lockfile 推導出的 install command | 安全預設 |
62	| `copy` | 複製 installed dependency directory | 只用於 path 可攜的情況 |
63	| `link` | 共用同一個 dependency directory | 最快，但通常不適合 concurrent writers |
64	| `skip` | 不安裝 dependencies | container 或 CI-driven development |
65	
66	每個 ecosystem 的 override 可放在 project 或 global config：
67	
68	```toml
69	[worktree.strategies]
70	node = "copy"
71	```
72	
73	新的 project-owned overrides 應放在 `.dev-cli/config.toml`；legacy `.dev.toml`
74	仍以 compatibility behavior 讀取。來自 `.dev-cli/config.toml` 的 `post_create`
75	command 必須先用 `dev config trust . --yes` 核准其 exact executable-config hash
76	才會執行；command 變更後原核准立即失效。
77	
78	重要內建判斷：
79	
80	- Python virtual environment 內嵌 absolute path，不能 copy 或 link；`uv sync` 可重用 global cache。
81	- Node `node_modules` 可以 copy，但拒絕共享，因為任何 checkout 都可能修改它。
82	- Go 使用 global content-addressed module cache，沒有需要複製的 checkout-local dependency tree。
83	- Cargo `target/` 可以 copy，但拒絕讓 concurrent build 共用 output。
84	
85	無效或不安全的設定會附 warning 縮限到 `reinstall`，不會偷偷建立壞環境。
86	
87	## 自動偵測 setup
88	
89	`post_create = "auto"` 依 priority 為每個 ecosystem 選一個 manager：
90	
91	| Marker | Command |
92	|---|---|
93	| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` |
94	| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` |
95	| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
96	| `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
97	| `yarn.lock` | `yarn install --immutable` |
98	| `go.mod` | `go mod download` |
99	| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fetch` |
100	| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` |
101	
102	缺少 tool 時會回報並 skip。Setup command 失敗時 worktree 仍保留，讓 branch 與 checkout 能被修復，而不是直接丟棄。
103	
104	## 重新 provision 或移除
105	
106	```bash
107	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree --dry-run
108	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree
109	dev wt rm feat/auth
110	```
111	
112	移除 worktree 與刪除 branch 是兩個決定。`dev wt rm` 會保留 branch，且沒有 explicit force 時拒絕 dirty checkout。Directory 若在 Git 之外消失，它會 prune stale administrative entry。
113	
114	在 `dev flow` 中，UNMANAGED row 的 Remove Checkout 只對 exact、clean、unlocked、non-prunable、non-harness linked checkout 出現，並在移除前後 revalidate task claims、Git/agent/runtime/artifact facts；branch 與其 OID 必須保留。Flow 不提供 force/dirty-discard/unknown-runtime override。Managed DONE row 不是 Remove Checkout，而是最後才 reap task record 的 Retire plan；可選 branch deletion 是另一個 typed confirmation。Raw `git worktree remove --force` 會繞過這些 guarantees。
115

7	
8	# Commands and configuration
9	
10	Use the authored map for intent and the embedded generated reference for exact flags. The generated block comes from the binary's Cobra command tree and is checked by `dev skill sync --check`.
11	
12	## Command map
13	
14	| Goal | Commands |
15	|---|---|
16	| task lifecycle | `start`, `park`, `resume`, `done`, `retire`, `sweep`, `ls`, `status` |
17	| agent artifacts | `prepare`, `artifact finalize`, `artifact list`, `artifact discard` |
18	| guarded Git transactions | `git uncommit`, `git recommit`, `git pull-rebase`, `git amend-all`, `git setup` |
19	| linked worktrees | `wt list`, `wt create`, `wt open`, `wt rm`, `wt plan`, `wt provision` |
20	| repositories/remotes | `repo list`, `repo context`, `repo new`/`repo create`, `repo clone`, `repo setup`, `repo open`, `repo sync`, `repo remote`, `repo mark` |
21	| repository quick notes | `note add`, `note list`, `note show`, `note search`, `note edit`, `note delete`, `note path`, `note reindex` |
22	| machine inventory | `bootstrap`, `adopt`, `doctor` |
23	| experiments | `try`, `tries …`, `graduate` |
24	| terminal UI | `tui`, `tui tools` |
25	| configuration/shell | `config init/show/path/edit/trust`, `config scaffolds init/show/path/edit`, `shell-init`, completion |
26	| remote fleet | `fleet list`, `fleet status`, `fleet sync`, `fleet open`, `fleet config …` |
27	| agent skills | `skill list`, `skill add`, `skill update`, `skill install`, `skill sync`, `skill print` |
28	| generated policy/assets | `gitignore`, `skill install/sync` |
29	| activity/data | `summary`, `journal`, `stats …`, `cache …` |
30	| help | `help [topic]` |
31	
32	Run `dev <command> --help` for the installed binary; this site describes the repository version identified in its freshness metadata.
33	
34	## High-value structured interfaces
35	
36	```bash
37	dev ls --json
38	dev repo list --json
39	dev repo context [repo]
40	dev repo remote --json
41	dev repo new NAME --json
42	dev repo clone <ref> --json
43	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
44	dev note list [repo] --json
45	dev note search <query> --json
46	dev note show <note-id> --json
47	dev bootstrap --json
48	```
49	
50	Prefer JSON or the agent-ready Markdown context over parsing human tables. Tables are optimized for terminals and may change columns/width without changing the structured contract.
51	
52	Every `dev repo list --json` row includes `notes.count`. When a latest note exists, the same object adds `notes.latest_id`, `notes.latest_preview`, and `notes.latest_updated`; these optional fields are omitted when the count is zero. `dev note list --json` and `dev note search --json` return arrays of complete note records, while `dev note show --json` returns one complete record.
53	
54	## Repository bootstrap
55	
56	Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
57	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
58	reference:
59	
60	| Command | Behavior |
61	|---|---|
62	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
63	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
64	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
65	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
66	
67	A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
68	new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
69	meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”
70	
71	Across these commands, controls include `--preset`, `--path`, typed input values through
72	`--set`, item selection through `--enable`/`--disable`, `--check-in
73	<auto|commit|stage|none>`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--handoff
74	<stay|cd|open|start>`. `repo new` additionally accepts `--template`,
75	`--template-ref`, and `--template-subdir`. JSON mode is non-interactive and
76	never changes directory or opens a runtime. Dry-run performs no target
77	repository mutation; clone setup can only be planned in detail after the clone
78	exists. Use the generated reference below for each command's exact flag
79	availability.
80	
81	The wizard renders the selected scaffold and workflow summary before target
82	repository mutation. The built-in presets are:
83	
84	- `minimal`: `main`, README, and an initial commit; this preserves existing
85	  scripted `repo new NAME` behavior.
86	- `agent-ready`: extends `minimal` with common ignores, starter `AGENTS.md`,
87	  and project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` plus `.claude/plans/`.
88	  `agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` are offered but are
89	  not selected silently. When selected, dev installs them and runs reviewed
90	  built-in initializers for their project surfaces before the initial commit;
91	  downloaded skill scripts are not executed for these built-ins. Matching
92	  skills with the same source and identical agent targets share one installer
93	  invocation, while their setup phases still run per skill. The history
94	  initializer creates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.gitleaks.toml`, then
95	  ensures `.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's `.project.json`
96	  and `statistics.json`, never the trackable `.specstory/history/` directory.
97	  Existing custom ignore content and its mode are preserved; only missing
98	  managed rules are appended.
99	
100	After preset selection, the new-repository wizard asks “Customize preset and
101	template options?” with a default of no. The ordinary `agent-ready` flow uses
102	its reviewed template, file, input, and skill defaults without presenting each
103	question. Answer yes—or provide customization flags—to expand those controls.
104	
105	Presets can add typed `string`, `bool`, and `choice` inputs, text templates,
106	hooks, and project skills. Hooks run in fixed `before_commit`, `after_commit`,
107	and `after_remote` phases. The safe hook form is an argv `command`; a shell
108	`run` is explicit, and only `interactive = true` loads an interactive shell.
109	Required failures stop later commit/remote steps; optional failures are
110	reported as warnings. Produced local files are retained for recovery. Native
111	initializers and preset files are repeat-safe; custom hooks and skill setup are
112	responsible for their own idempotency.
113	
114	### Snapshot templates
115	
116	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` seeds a fresh repository from a content
117	snapshot. `SOURCE` may be a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name.
118	For a Git source, `--template-ref` selects an arbitrary branch, tag, or commit;
119	`--template-subdir` selects a clean relative directory as the new repository
120	root. Without a ref, a local Git working tree includes existing tracked files
121	plus untracked files that are not ignored by Git; ignored build/cache content
122	is omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots its complete current tree.
123	
124	The new repository does not inherit source history or remotes. Dev excludes
125	every source `.git` entry, rejects traversal, symlinks and special files,
126	preserves regular-file modes, and validates the complete snapshot before
127	creating the destination. Snapshot files take precedence when the selected
128	scaffold would write the same path; the scaffold still fills missing files and
129	runs the selected initializers. Source and destination traversal is performed
130	relative to held `os.Root` handles, and file bytes come from the already-open
131	validated source handle rather than a second mutable pathname lookup.
132	
133	Confirmation and human dry-run output show a bounded preview of selected paths
134	and warn when a local source is a live working-tree/directory snapshot rather
135	than a commit. Credential-bearing URL userinfo is removed from summaries,
136	structured output, and clone/template errors.
137	
138	Presets expose the same operation through scalar `template`, `template_ref`,
139	and `template_subdir` fields. They inherit normally and explicit CLI flags win,
140	which supports one starter catalog repository plus a child preset for each
141	subfolder.
142	
143	### Check-in policy
144	
145	The interactive wizard offers `commit`, `stage`, and `none`; scripts may also
146	pass `auto`. The behavior is:
147	
148	| Value | Behavior |
149	|---|---|
150	| `commit` | `git add -A`, commit with `--message`/the preset message, then run `after_commit` setup |
151	| `stage` | run `before_commit` setup, then `git add -A`; leave the checkout staged and do not run `after_commit` |
152	| `none` | leave generated changes unstaged and uncommitted |
153	| `auto` | for `repo new`, use `initial_check_in` and compatible `initial_commit`; clone/setup otherwise perform no automatic check-in |
154	
155	In `stage` mode, dev best-effort writes `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in the exact
156	worktree Git directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 reads this
157	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)
158	as the initial message for lowercase `c`; uppercase `C` and Git itself do not use this integration. An
159	existing different draft is preserved and reported rather than overwritten.
160	This is an implementation-detail adapter, not `commit.template`.
161	
162	Staging is the durable outcome: if the optional lazygit draft cannot be
163	written, dev emits a warning and retains the staged index instead of rolling it
164	back.
165	
166	Staged setup cannot create an upstream, and `handoff=start` requires committed
167	setup because a new worktree would omit the staged files. `stay`, `cd`, and
168	`open` remain available for review. `repo setup --commit` is retained as a
169	compatibility alias for `--check-in=commit`; `--message` applies to both commit
170	and stage. Structured results retain `committed` and add `staged`,
171	`staged_paths`, `commit_message`, `commit_draft_provider`, and a content-free
172	`template` summary where applicable.
173	
174	### Upstream publishing
175	
176	Before offering publication, dev probes `gh` and `glab` without changing
177	state. A provider is offered only when its CLI is installed and authenticated;
178	otherwise the wizard gives the relevant installation or login guidance.
179	Local-only is the default, and a newly published repository defaults private.
180	
181	Publishing uses the local repository name and configured description, then asks
182	for the provider namespace/owner, visibility, and whether to push the
183	initial/current branch. Dev creates the empty GitHub or GitLab repository after
184	required local setup and commit steps succeed, then adds/verifies `origin` and
185	optionally pushes with upstream tracking. A
186	provider, name-conflict, or push failure never deletes the local checkout or
187	an upstream that was already created.
188	
189	Publishing from `repo setup` requires `--check-in=commit` (or the compatible
190	`--commit` flag), so the newly created upstream cannot omit the generated setup
191	changes. `--check-in=stage` is incompatible with any new upstream; for a new
192	repository, `none` may create an intentionally empty upstream only with
193	`--push=false`.
194	
195	### Handoff
196	
197	`stay` prints the result only. `cd` uses the trusted `shell-init` wrapper to
198	change the parent shell. `open` opens the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime
199	and falls back to `cd` when runtime is `none`. `start` continues into the
200	existing task wizard with the repository fixed, and is unavailable when setup
201	leaves uncommitted files that a new worktree would omit. Neither repository
202	bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. Explicit
203	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches one command only
204	when a newly created first-class Herdr worktree returns its exact root pane;
205	`--focus` independently controls navigation afterward.
206	
207	All shared TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards
208	use an inline editor: Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, insertion at the
209	cursor, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation work as terminal actions rather than being
210	inserted as raw escape bytes. Buffered and piped non-TTY input retains its
211	line-oriented behavior.
212	
213	## `dev done` finish flags
214	
215	`dev done` for branch/worktree tasks integrates through exactly one of `--ff` (rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it) or `--pr` (push and open a pull/merge request). Omitting both opens the interactive finish wizard on a TTY — see [Change-stream workflow](../guides/change-stream-workflow.md) for the prompts.
216	
217	A dirty checkout is handled by `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` (default `auto`):
218	
219	| Value | Behavior |
220	|---|---|
221	| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
222	| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
223	| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
224	| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |
225	
226	`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive confirmation step. `--keep-worktree` keeps the worktree after `--ff` integration (default: removed once merged), `--push` also pushes the resulting branch, and `--delete-branch` deletes the branch once its commits are contained in the base — never a branch with unpushed commits.
227	
228	## Configuration
229	
230	```bash
231	dev config init
232	dev config show
233	dev config path
234	dev config scaffolds init
235	dev config scaffolds show
236	dev config scaffolds path
237	dev config scaffolds edit
238	```
239	
240	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
241	
242	Key sections:
243	
244	| Section | Controls |
245	|---|---|
246	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
247	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
248	| `[worktree]` | ignored includes, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
249	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
250	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
```

24	| repositories/remotes | `repo list`、`repo context`、`repo new`/`repo create`、`repo clone`、`repo setup`、`repo open`、`repo sync`、`repo remote`、`repo mark` |
25	| repository quick notes | `note add`、`note list`、`note show`、`note search`、`note edit`、`note delete`、`note path`、`note reindex` |
26	| machine inventory | `bootstrap`、`adopt`、`doctor` |
27	| experiments | `try`、`tries …`、`graduate` |
28	| terminal UI | `tui`、`tui tools`、獨立 preview `flow [repo]` |
29	| configuration/shell | `config init/show/path/edit/trust`、`config scaffolds init/show/path/edit`、`shell-init`、completion |
30	| remote fleet | `fleet list`、`fleet status`、`fleet sync`、`fleet open`、`fleet config …` |
31	| agent skills | `skill list`、`skill add`、`skill update`、`skill install`、`skill sync`、`skill print` |
32	| generated policy/assets | `gitignore`、`skill install/sync` |
33	| activity/data | `summary`、`journal`、`stats …`、`cache …` |
34	| help | `help [topic]` |
35	
36	已安裝 binary 的精確資訊請執行 `dev <command> --help`；本站描述的是 freshness metadata 指定的 repository version。
37	
38	## 高價值 structured interfaces
39	
40	```bash
41	dev ls --json
42	dev repo list --json
43	dev repo context [repo]
44	dev repo remote --json
45	dev repo new NAME --json
46	dev repo clone <ref> --json
47	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
48	dev note list [repo] --json
49	dev note search <query> --json
50	dev note show <note-id> --json
51	dev bootstrap --json
52	```
53	
54	不要解析 human table，應優先使用 JSON 或 agent-ready Markdown context。Table 針對 terminal 最佳化，columns/width 可能變化，但 structured contract 不一定改變。
55	
56	每個 `dev repo list --json` row 都包含 `notes.count`。最新 note 存在時，同一 object 會加入 `notes.latest_id`、`notes.latest_preview` 與 `notes.latest_updated`；count 為零時省略這些 optional fields。`dev note list --json` 與 `dev note search --json` 回傳完整 note records 的 arrays，`dev note show --json` 則回傳一筆完整 record。
57	
58	## Repository bootstrap
59	
60	Repository setup 仍與 acquisition 分開。Acquisition 部分，`new`/`create` 會區分
61	plain repository name 與清楚的 clone reference：
62	
63	| Command | 行為 |
64	|---|---|
65	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard；第一個欄位可輸入新 name 或 clone reference |
66	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | 建立新的 local repository；若輸入清楚的 Git URL、local Git path 或 owner/name，則改走 clone 並保留 history/remote |
67	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone 至 configured destination，再選擇是否套 preset；setup 預設關閉 |
68	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers 與 preset files 至既有 clean checkout；預設目前 repository，沒有明確要求時不 commit |
69	
70	改走 clone 的 `new` 會保留 source `origin`，因此拒絕 new-upstream creation flags；也會
71	拒絕 `--template*`，因為後者的明確語意是「把 content 複製進 fresh history」。
72	
73	這些 commands 的 controls 包含 `--preset`、`--path`、用 `--set` 傳入 typed input、用
74	`--enable`/`--disable` 選擇 item、`--check-in <auto|commit|stage|none>`、
75	`--dry-run`、`--yes`、`--json`，以及 `--handoff <stay|cd|open|start>`。
76	`repo new` 另支援 `--template`、`--template-ref`、`--template-subdir`。JSON mode
77	不互動，也不會改變 directory 或開啟 runtime。Dry-run 不會修改 target repository；
78	clone setup 必須等 clone 存在後才能產生詳細 plan。每個 command 實際支援的精確 flags
79	請看下方 generated reference。
80	
81	Wizard 會在 target repository mutation 前顯示 selected scaffold 與 workflow
82	summary。Built-in presets 為：
83	
84	- `minimal`：`main`、README 與 initial commit；保留既有 scripted
85	  `repo new NAME` behavior。
86	- `agent-ready`：在 `minimal` 上加入 common ignores、starter `AGENTS.md`，以及
87	  project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` 與 `.claude/plans/`。
88	  `agent-history-hygiene`、`project-knowledge-harness` 會出現在選項中，但不會靜默
89	  啟用。選取後 dev 會安裝 skill，並在 initial commit 前執行經 review 的內建
90	  initializer 來建立對應 project surfaces；這兩個 built-ins 不會執行剛下載的
91	  skill scripts。同一 source 且 agent targets 完全相同的 skills 會共用一次 installer
92	  invocation，各 skill 的 setup phase 仍分別執行。History initializer 會建立
93	  `.pre-commit-config.yaml`、`.gitleaks.toml`，再確保 `.specstory/.gitignore` 含有
94	  SpecStory 的 `.project.json`、`statistics.json` 規則，不會忽略應納入追蹤的
95	  `.specstory/history/`。既有 custom ignore content 與 mode 會保留，只補上缺少的
96	  managed rules。
97	
98	選完 preset 後，new-repository wizard 會詢問預設為 no 的「Customize preset and
99	template options?」。一般 `agent-ready` flow 會直接使用 reviewed template、file、input
100	與 skill defaults，不逐一顯示問題；回答 yes（或傳入 customization flags）才會展開。
101	
102	Preset 可加入 `string`、`bool`、`choice` typed inputs、text templates、hooks 與
103	project skills。Hooks 依固定 `before_commit`、`after_commit`、`after_remote` phases
104	執行。安全形式是 argv `command`；shell `run` 必須明確宣告，且只有
105	`interactive = true` 才載入 interactive shell。Required failure 會停止後續
106	commit/remote steps；optional failure 只回報 warning。已產生的 local files 會保留供
107	recovery。Native initializers 與 preset files 可 repeat-safe 套用；custom hooks 與
108	skill setup 必須自行保證 idempotency。
109	
110	### Snapshot templates
111	
112	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` 會用 content snapshot 建立全新 repository。
113	`SOURCE` 可為 local directory/repository、Git URL 或 owner/name。Git source 可用
114	`--template-ref` 指定任意 branch、tag 或 commit；`--template-subdir` 則指定作為新
115	repository root 的乾淨 relative directory。未指定 ref 時，local Git working tree 會
116	包含現存 tracked files，以及未被 Git ignore 的 untracked files；ignored build/cache
117	content 會省略。Non-Git directory 則 snapshot 完整 current tree。
118	
119	新 repository 不會繼承 source history 或 remotes。Dev 會排除每個 source `.git`
120	entry、拒絕 traversal、symlink 與 special files、保留 regular-file modes，並在建立
121	destination 前驗證完整 snapshot。若 snapshot 與 selected scaffold 寫入同一路徑，
122	snapshot 優先；scaffold 仍會補齊缺少的 files 並執行 selected initializers。
123	Source 與 destination traversal 都相對於 held `os.Root` handles 進行；file bytes 來自
124	已開啟且驗證過的 source handle，不會再次依 mutable pathname lookup。
125	
126	Confirmation 與 human dry-run output 會顯示 bounded selected-path preview；local source
127	若是 live working-tree/directory snapshot 而非 commit，也會明確 warning。含 credential
128	的 URL userinfo 會從 summaries、structured output 與 clone/template errors 移除。
129	
130	Preset 可用 scalar `template`、`template_ref`、`template_subdir` 宣告同一操作。它們依
131	一般 inheritance 規則 resolve，explicit CLI flags 優先，因此可以一個 starter catalog
132	repository 搭配每個 subfolder 各一個 child preset。
133	
134	### Check-in policy
135	
136	Interactive wizard 提供 `commit`、`stage`、`none`；script 也可傳 `auto`：
137	
138	| 值 | 行為 |
139	|---|---|
140	| `commit` | `git add -A`，以 `--message`／preset message commit，再執行 `after_commit` setup |
141	| `stage` | 執行 `before_commit` setup 後 `git add -A`；保留 staged checkout，不執行 `after_commit` |
142	| `none` | generated changes 保持 unstaged、uncommitted |
143	| `auto` | `repo new` 使用 `initial_check_in` 與相容的 `initial_commit`；clone/setup 則不自動 check-in |
144	
145	`stage` mode 會 best-effort 在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入
146	`LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`。[Lazygit v0.59.0 會讀取此
147	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，並將它作為小寫 `c` 的 initial message；大寫
148	`C` 與 Git 本身不使用此 integration。不同內容的既有 draft 會保留並回報 warning，
149	不會被覆寫。這是 implementation-detail adapter，不是 `commit.template`。
150	
151	Staging 才是 durable outcome：optional lazygit draft 若無法寫入，dev 會發出 warning
152	並保留 staged index，不會 rollback。
153	
154	Staged setup 不能建立 upstream；`handoff=start` 也要求已 commit 的 setup，因為新
155	worktree 會漏掉 staged files。`stay`、`cd`、`open` 仍可供 review。`repo setup
156	--commit` 保留為 `--check-in=commit` 的 compatibility alias；`--message` 同時適用於
157	commit 與 stage。Structured result 保留 `committed`，並在適用時加入 `staged`、
158	`staged_paths`、`commit_message`、`commit_draft_provider` 與不含 file content 的
159	`template` summary。
160	
161	### Upstream publishing
162	
163	提供 publishing 選項前，dev 會以 read-only 方式 probe `gh` 與 `glab`。只有 CLI 已
164	安裝且完成 authentication 的 provider 才會出現；否則 wizard 顯示對應的安裝或 login
165	指引。預設 local-only，新 publish 的 repository 預設 private。
166	
167	Publishing 會沿用 local repository name 與 configured description，再詢問 provider
168	namespace/owner、visibility，以及是否 push initial/current branch。Dev 會在必要的
169	local setup 與 commit steps 成功後建立空的 GitHub 或 GitLab repository，再新增／驗證
170	`origin`，並可選擇以 upstream tracking push。Provider、name-conflict 或 push failure
171	絕不刪除 local checkout，也不會刪除已建立的 upstream。
172	
173	從 `repo setup` publish 時必須使用 `--check-in=commit`（或相容的 `--commit` flag），
174	避免新建 upstream 漏掉本次產生的 setup changes。`--check-in=stage` 與任何新 upstream
175	不相容；對新 repository 而言，`none` 只有搭配 `--push=false` 才能建立刻意保持空白的
176	upstream。
177	
178	### Handoff
179	
180	`stay` 只輸出結果；`cd` 透過受信任的 `shell-init` wrapper 改變 parent shell；
181	`open` 開啟 configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime，runtime 為 `none` 時退回 `cd`；
182	`start` 會固定此 repository 並接續現有 task wizard。Setup 留下 uncommitted files、
183	導致新 worktree 會遺漏它們時，`start` 不可用。Repository bootstrap 與
184	預設的 `dev start` 都不會啟動 coding agent。明確使用 worktree mode 的
185	`dev start --run '<shell command>'` 時，只有本次新建 first-class Herdr worktree
186	回傳 exact root pane 才會 dispatch command；之後是否轉跳仍由 `--focus` 獨立控制。
187	
188	Repository、task-start 與 finish wizard 共用的 TTY text fields 都使用 inline editor：
189	Left/Right、Home/End、Delete/Backspace、cursor 位置插入與 Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation 會
190	被解讀為 terminal actions，不會成為 raw escape bytes。Buffered 或 piped non-TTY input
191	仍維持 line-oriented behavior。
192	
193	## `dev flow [repo]` preview
194	
195	`dev flow [repo]` 是獨立 full-screen command，只接受 interactive TTY；它沒有 JSON/non-interactive contract。省略 `repo` 時，canonical/linked checkout 會開啟同一 Git common-directory repository 並 focus exact current surface；Git 之外則非同步開 repository picker。明確 `repo` 會覆蓋 cwd。
196	
197	Startup 與 `r` 只載入 local topology/evidence。`R` 才提供 Fetch refs、Refresh PR/MR 或 Both；每個 choice 都先產生 exact guarded plan，再要求 approval。Provider review observation 只在 current run 保存最低限度的 existence、`open`/`draft`/`merged`/`closed`、URL、provider 與 observed time，不代表 CI checks 或 approvals。`runtime=none` 保持 unobserved，也不提供 `--assume-no-runtime` 等 expert override。詳細 keys、row kinds、partial ledger 與 escape boundary 見 [Repository Flow 預覽](../guides/repository-flow.zh-TW.md)。
198	
199	## `dev done` finish flags
200	
201	`dev done` 對 branch/worktree task 透過 `--ff`（rebase 到 base 再 fast-forward）、`--pr`（push 並開啟 pull/merge request）或 `--merged`（依 `--base-ref` 驗證外部 integration）處理。未指定 integration choice 時，在 TTY 上會開啟 interactive finish wizard —— 提示內容見[變更流工作流程](../guides/change-stream-workflow.zh-TW.md)。
202	
203	Dirty checkout 由 `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` 處理（預設 `auto`）：
204	
205	| 值 | 行為 |
206	|---|---|
207	| `auto` | interactive：提示 commit 或 discard；non-interactive：直接失敗，等同 `fail` |
208	| `fail` | dirty checkout 時拒絕 finish |
209	| `commit` | 用 `--message`/`-m` commit 全部變更（未指定時 interactive 會提示輸入） |
210	| `discard` | reset tracked 變更並移除 untracked files；具破壞性，沒有 TTY 時需要 `--yes` |
211	
212	`--yes`/`-y` 用來確認選定的 finish plan；non-interactive 的 `--dirty discard` 必須要有它，其他情況則是跳過 interactive 確認步驟。`--push` 會依 selected integration push 對應 branch/base。成功的 local 或 externally verified integration 只記錄 DONE/MERGED，永遠保留 runtime、worktree 與 branch 給獨立的 `dev retire`；`--keep-worktree` 只保留為 no-op compatibility warning，`--delete-branch` 則會報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`。`--merged` 可用 `--confirm-squash <merge-commit>` 對 squash result 作明確 operator attestation，不能由 provider status 自動推斷。
213	
214	## Configuration
215	
216	```bash
217	dev config init
218	dev config show
219	dev config path
220	dev config scaffolds init
221	dev config scaffolds show
222	dev config scaffolds path
223	dev config scaffolds edit
224	```
225	
226	`config init` 偵測 local roots 並寫出 explicit defaults。Config file 不存在仍可運作；built-in defaults 讓核心 Git behavior 可用，但 generated config 能讓 machine policy 可 review，因此較推薦。
227	
228	主要 sections：
229	
230	| Section | 控制內容 |
231	|---|---|
232	| `[paths]` | scan roots、project/tries/worktree roots、worktree template、state path |
233	| `[runtime]` | `auto`、Herdr、tmux、Zellij 或 none，以及 metadata settings |
234	| `[worktree]` | ignored includes、linked dirs、setup commands、strategies、timeout |
235	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | 完整 remote inventory 的 cache TTL，以及 opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
236	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion、symlink handling、index/layout policy |
237	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns、sorting 與 external-tool bindings |
238	| `[stats]` | sampler 與 optional WakaTime import |
239	| `[update]` | `check`（預設 `true`）— 允許每天一次的「有新版」提示與其背景 cache refresh；`DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` 可覆寫 |
240	
241	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` 會啟用單次 TUI startup/readiness trace。
242	Target 必須是 absolute 且尚不存在；dev 絕不 overwrite。Private、bounded document
243	在 TUI teardown 後才寫入，只包含 relative categorical timings 與 aggregate row
244	counts，不包含 names、paths 或 raw payloads；它不是 configuration、cache、durable
245	stats、stdout 或 network telemetry。
246	Dashboard 與 `dev flow` 這類 full-screen invocation 的 optional update-cache network refresh 也會延後到 initial view return 之後；這不會把 Flow 自己的 local `r` 變成 remote refresh。
247	
248	Repository quick-note Markdown 是 configured `paths.state_dir/notes` 下的 durable data；該路徑預設為 `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`。`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` 的 full-text index 是 disposable，會從 Markdown 重建；調整 `paths.state_dir` 不會移動 cache。

375	func renderWidePanels(leftTitle string, left []string, middleTitle string, middle []string, rightTitle string, right []string, width int) string {
376		gutter := " | "
377		usable := width - 2*lipgloss.Width(gutter)
378		if usable < 60 {
379			usable = 60
380		}
381		leftWidth := usable * 30 / 100
382		middleWidth := usable * 36 / 100
383		rightWidth := usable - leftWidth - middleWidth
384		left = append([]string{leftTitle, strings.Repeat("-", max(1, leftWidth))}, left...)
385		middle = append([]string{middleTitle, strings.Repeat("-", max(1, middleWidth))}, middle...)
386		right = append([]string{rightTitle, strings.Repeat("-", max(1, rightWidth))}, right...)
387		count := max(len(left), len(middle), len(right))
388		var builder strings.Builder
389		for index := 0; index < count; index++ {
390			builder.WriteString(fitPanelLine(lineAt(left, index), leftWidth))
391			builder.WriteString(gutter)
392			builder.WriteString(fitPanelLine(lineAt(middle, index), middleWidth))
393			builder.WriteString(gutter)
394			builder.WriteString(fitPanelLine(lineAt(right, index), rightWidth))
395			if index+1 < count {
396				builder.WriteByte('\n')
397			}
398		}
399		return builder.String()
400	}

407		if index < 0 || index >= len(lines) {

410		return lines[index]

414		value = truncateDisplay(value, width)

12		colorAlways = "always"
13		colorNever  = "never"
14	
15		ansiReset   = "\x1b[0m"
16		ansiBold    = "\x1b[1m"
17		ansiDim     = "\x1b[2m"
18		ansiRed     = "\x1b[31m"
19		ansiGreen   = "\x1b[32m"
20		ansiYellow  = "\x1b[33m"
21		ansiMagenta = "\x1b[35m"
22		ansiCyan    = "\x1b[36m"
23	)
24	
25	type cliStyle struct {
26		enabled bool
27	}
28	
29	func validateColorMode(mode string) error {
30		switch mode {
31		case "", colorAuto, colorAlways, colorNever:
32			return nil
33		default:
34			return fmt.Errorf("invalid --color value %q: use auto, always, or never", mode)
35		}
36	}
37	
38	func styleForWriter(w io.Writer, mode string) cliStyle {
39		switch mode {
40		case colorAlways:
41			return cliStyle{enabled: true}
42		case colorNever:
43			return cliStyle{}
44		}
45		if os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") != "" || os.Getenv("TERM") == "dumb" {
46			return cliStyle{}
47		}
48		f, ok := w.(*os.File)
49		if !ok {
50			return cliStyle{}
51		}
52		info, err := f.Stat()
53		return cliStyle{enabled: err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice != 0}
54	}
55	
56	func (s cliStyle) paint(code, text string) string {
57		if !s.enabled || text == "" {
58			return text
59		}
60		return code + text + ansiReset
61	}
62	
63	func (s cliStyle) title(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
64	func (s cliStyle) header(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
65	func (s cliStyle) prompt(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
66	func (s cliStyle) label(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiDim, text) }
67	func (s cliStyle) dim(text string) string     { return s.paint(ansiDim, text) }
68	func (s cliStyle) success(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiGreen, text) }
69	func (s cliStyle) warning(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiYellow, text) }
70	func (s cliStyle) danger(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiRed, text) }
71	func (s cliStyle) review(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiMagenta, text) }
72	
73	// strong and code are the two roles the Markdown renderer needs. They are named
74	// for what they mark rather than for a colour so the palette stays in one file.
75	func (s cliStyle) strong(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiBold, text) }
76	func (s cliStyle) code(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiCyan, text) }
77	
78	func (s cliStyle) taskState(text string) string {
79		return s.taskStateFor(text, text)
80	}
81	
82	func (s cliStyle) taskStateFor(state, text string) string {
83		switch strings.ToLower(state) {
84		case "hot", "done":
85			return s.success(text)
86		case "warm", "cold", "parked":
87			return s.warning(text)
88		default:
89			return text
90		}
91	}
92	
93	// hostState colors a fleet host by what it means for the answer: a reachable
94	// host is green, a degraded-but-usable one is yellow, and a host whose data
95	// dev could not obtain at all is red.
96	func (s cliStyle) hostState(text string) string {
97		switch strings.ToLower(text) {
98		case "ok":
99			return s.success(text)
100		case "stale", "no-dev":
101			return s.warning(text)
102		case "unreachable", "timeout", "incompatible", "invalid-response":
103			return s.danger(text)
104		default:
105			return text
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// updateState colors a skill row by whether it needs attention. The values are
110	// the short display forms shortUpdate produces, not the raw enum.
111	func (s cliStyle) updateState(text string) string {
112		switch strings.ToLower(text) {
113		case "current":
114			return s.success(text)
115		case "update":
116			return s.warning(text)
117		case "missing", "failed":
118			return s.danger(text)
119		default: // unchecked, unknown
120			return s.dim(text)
121		}
122	}
123	
124	// artifactState colors an intent by whether it still blocks integration.
125	func (s cliStyle) artifactState(text string) string {
126		switch strings.ToLower(text) {

128			return s.success(text)
129		case "armed", "finalizing":
130			return s.warning(text)
131		case "failed":
132			return s.danger(text)
133		case "discarded":
134			return s.dim(text)
135		default:
136			return text
137		}
138	}
139	
140	func colorModeFromArgs(args []string) string {
141		for i, arg := range args {
142			if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--color=") {
143				return strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--color=")
144			}
145			if arg == "--color" && i+1 < len(args) {
146				return args[i+1]
147			}
148		}
149		return colorAuto
150	}
151	
152	func (s cliStyle) git(text string) string {
153		lower := strings.ToLower(text)
154		switch {
155		case text == "—", text == "", lower == "local":
156			return s.dim(text)
157		case lower == "clean":
158			return s.success(text)
159		case text == "?", strings.Contains(text, "="), strings.Contains(lower, "conflict"), strings.Contains(lower, "error"):
160			return s.danger(text)
161		case strings.Contains(lower, "dirty"), strings.Contains(lower, "ahead"),
162			strings.Contains(lower, "behind"), strings.Contains(lower, "no checkout"),
163			strings.Contains(lower, "prunable"), strings.Contains(lower, "locked"),
164			strings.Contains(text, "!"), strings.Contains(text, "?"):
165			return s.warning(text)
166		default:
167			return text
168		}
169	}
170	
171	func (a *App) outStyle() cliStyle { return styleForWriter(a.Out, a.colorMode) }
172	func (a *App) errStyle() cliStyle { return styleForWriter(a.Err, a.colorMode) }

175		return &Table{head: header, style: a.outStyle()}
176	}

41	// RegisteredWorktree is an identity snapshot from Git's worktree registry.
42	// Worktree preserves the complete parsed Git record; the other fields are canonical
43	// filesystem identities suitable for exact comparison across symlink and macOS
44	// path aliases. A snapshot proves registration, not permission to remove it.
45	type RegisteredWorktree struct {
46		Worktree       Worktree
47		RepositoryPath string
48		GitCommonDir   string

52	// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether the record is a linked checkout rather than
53	// Git's main checkout or a bare repository. It is classification, not a removal

56		return !w.Worktree.Main && !w.Worktree.Bare

59	// ResolveRegisteredWorktree resolves exactPath against a fresh authoritative
60	// `git worktree list --porcelain` query for the repository containing repoPath.
61	// Matching is exclusively by canonical filesystem identity, never by branch.
62	// It performs no prune, removal, or other mutation.
63	func ResolveRegisteredWorktree(ctx context.Context, repoPath, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
64		worktrees, err := Worktrees(ctx, repoPath)
65		if err != nil {
66			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("query registered worktrees: %w", err)
67		}
68		commonDir, err := run(ctx, repoPath, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
69		if err != nil {
70			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve Git common directory: %w", err)
71		}
72		return resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees, commonDir, exactPath)

75	func resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees []Worktree, commonDir, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
76		path, err := pathx.Canonical(exactPath)
77		if err != nil {
78			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize requested worktree %q: %w", exactPath, err)
79		}
80		canonicalCommonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
81		if err != nil {

83		}

85		type match struct {
86			worktree Worktree
87			path     string
88		}

91			matches        []match

95			if canonicalErr != nil {
96				return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize registered worktree %q: %w", worktree.Path, canonicalErr)

133	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
134	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
135	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
136		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
137		if err != nil {
138			return nil, err
139		}
140		var (
141			list []Worktree
142			cur  *Worktree
143		)
144		flush := func() {
145			if cur != nil {
146				list = append(list, *cur)
147				cur = nil
148			}
149		}
150		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
151			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
152				flush()
153				continue
154			}
155			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
156			switch key {
157			case "worktree":
158				flush()
159				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
160			case "HEAD":
161				if cur != nil {
162					cur.Head = val
163				}
164			case "branch":
165				if cur != nil {
166					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
167				}
168			case "detached":
169				if cur != nil {
170					cur.Detached = true
171				}
172			case "bare":
173				if cur != nil {
174					cur.Bare = true
175				}
176			case "locked":
177				if cur != nil {
178					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
179				}
180			case "prunable":
181				if cur != nil {
182					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
183				}
184			}
185		}
186		flush()
187		return list, nil
188	}

190	// WorktreeFor finds the first worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git
191	// normally refuses duplicate branch checkouts, but --force can create them;
192	// identity-sensitive callers must use ResolveRegisteredWorktree instead.
193	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
194		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
195		if err != nil {
196			return Worktree{}, false, err
197		}
198		for _, w := range list {
199			if w.Branch == branch {
200				return w, true, nil
201			}
202		}
203		return Worktree{}, false, nil

206	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
207	//
208	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
209	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
210	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
211	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
212	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
213		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
214		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
215		if exists {
216			args = append(args, path, branch)
217		} else {
218			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
219			if base != "" {
220				args = append(args, base)
221			}
222		}
223		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
224		return err
225	}

227	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
228	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
229	// be any checkout of the same repository.
230	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
231		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)

233	}

235	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
236	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
237	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
238		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
239		if err != nil {
240			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
241		}
242		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
243		if err != nil {
244			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
245		}
246		if inside {
247			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
248		}
249		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
250		if force {
251			args = append(args, "--force")
252		}
253		args = append(args, path)
254		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
255		return err
256	}
257	
258	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
259	// were deleted behind git's back.

261		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")

263	}
