# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

16	// BranchRelation describes committed history between a task branch and base.
17	type BranchRelation struct {
18		BaseOnly   int
19		BranchOnly int
20	}
21	
22	// Contained reports that every branch commit is already reachable from base.
23	func (r BranchRelation) Contained() bool { return r.BranchOnly == 0 }
24	
25	// DirtyPath is one staged, unstaged, conflicted, or untracked checkout path.
26	// BaseEquivalent is true only when neither its index snapshot nor the final
27	// git-add-all worktree snapshot contains content absent from base.
28	type DirtyPath struct {
29		Path           string
30		OldPath        string
31		Staged         bool
32		Unstaged       bool
33		Untracked      bool
34		Conflicted     bool
35		BaseEquivalent bool
36	}

38	// DisplayPath renders a rename without losing either side.
39	func (p DirtyPath) DisplayPath() string {
40		if p.OldPath != "" && p.OldPath != p.Path {
41			return p.OldPath + " -> " + p.Path
42		}
43		return p.Path
44	}

46	// FinishAnalysis is the immutable preflight for a done operation.
47	type FinishAnalysis struct {
48		Status      Status
49		Relation    BranchRelation
50		Changes     []DirtyPath
51		Fingerprint string
52	}
53	
54	// UniqueDirty counts paths with content not represented by the base tree.
55	func (a FinishAnalysis) UniqueDirty() int {
56		n := 0
57		for _, change := range a.Changes {
58			if !change.BaseEquivalent {
59				n++
60			}
61		}
62		return n
63	}
64	
65	// EquivalentDirty counts dirty paths whose index and worktree snapshots both
66	// agree with the base.
67	func (a FinishAnalysis) EquivalentDirty() int {
68		return len(a.Changes) - a.UniqueDirty()
69	}

71	// AnalyzeFinish compares both committed history and every uncommitted layer
72	// without changing the real index. The alternate index models the exact tree
73	// produced by `git add -A`, including untracked files but excluding ignored
74	// files according to Git's normal rules.
75	func AnalyzeFinish(ctx context.Context, dir, base, branch string) (FinishAnalysis, error) {
76		relation, err := compareBranches(ctx, dir, base, branch)
77		if err != nil {
78			return FinishAnalysis{}, err
79		}

85		if status.Conflicted > 0 {
86			analysis.Fingerprint = finishFingerprint(rawStatus, "conflicted", "conflicted")
87			return analysis, nil
88		}
89

91		if err != nil {
92			return FinishAnalysis{}, err
93		}
94		for i := range analysis.Changes {
95			change := &analysis.Changes[i]
96			unique := worktreeDiff[change.Path]
97			if change.Staged {
98				unique = unique || indexDiff[change.Path]
99			}
100			if change.OldPath != "" {
101				unique = unique || worktreeDiff[change.OldPath]
102				if change.Staged {
103					unique = unique || indexDiff[change.OldPath]
104				}
105			}
106			change.BaseEquivalent = !unique
107		}
108		analysis.Fingerprint = finishFingerprint(rawStatus, indexTree, worktreeTree)
109		return analysis, nil
110	}

112	func compareBranches(ctx context.Context, dir, base, branch string) (BranchRelation, error) {
113		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", base+"..."+branch)
114		if err != nil {
115			return BranchRelation{}, err
116		}
117		fields := strings.Fields(out)
118		if len(fields) != 2 {
119			return BranchRelation{}, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list returned %q, want two counts", out)
120		}
121		baseOnly, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[0])
122		if err != nil {
123			return BranchRelation{}, fmt.Errorf("parse base-only count %q: %w", fields[0], err)
124		}
125		branchOnly, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
126		if err != nil {
127			return BranchRelation{}, fmt.Errorf("parse branch-only count %q: %w", fields[1], err)
128		}
129		return BranchRelation{BaseOnly: baseOnly, BranchOnly: branchOnly}, nil
130	}
131	
132	func finishDirtyPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]DirtyPath, Status, string, error) {
133		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=all", "-z")
134		if err != nil {
135			return nil, Status{}, "", err
136		}
137		records := nulLines(out)
138		changes := make([]DirtyPath, 0, len(records))
139		for i := 0; i < len(records); i++ {
140			rec := records[i]
141			if rec == "" {
142				continue
143			}
144			var change DirtyPath
145			switch rec[0] {
146			case '1', '2':
147				fields := strings.Fields(rec)
148				if len(fields) < 2 || len(fields[1]) < 2 {
149					continue
150				}
151				change.Path = statusPath(rec)
152				change.Staged = fields[1][0] != '.'
153				change.Unstaged = fields[1][1] != '.'
154				if rec[0] == '2' && i+1 < len(records) {
155					i++
156					change.OldPath = records[i]
157				}
158			case 'u':
159				change.Path, change.Conflicted = statusPath(rec), true
160			case '?':
161				change.Path = strings.TrimPrefix(rec, "? ")
162				change.Untracked = true
163			default:
164				continue
165			}
166			if change.Path != "" {
167				changes = append(changes, change)
168			}
169		}
170		sort.Slice(changes, func(i, j int) bool { return changes[i].DisplayPath() < changes[j].DisplayPath() })
171		return changes, statusFromOutput(dir, out), out, nil
172	}

174	func finishTrees(ctx context.Context, dir, base string) (string, string, map[string]bool, map[string]bool, error) {
175		tempDir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-finish-index-*")
176		if err != nil {
177			return "", "", nil, nil, err
178		}
179		defer os.RemoveAll(tempDir)
180		objectDir := filepath.Join(tempDir, "objects")
181		if err := os.MkdirAll(objectDir, 0o755); err != nil {
182			return "", "", nil, nil, err
183		}
184		commonDir, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
185		if err != nil {
186			return "", "", nil, nil, err
187		}
188		if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
189			commonDir = filepath.Join(dir, commonDir)
190		}
191		repoObjects := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(commonDir, "objects"))
192		alternates := repoObjects
193		if inherited := os.Getenv("GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES"); inherited != "" {
194			alternates += string(os.PathListSeparator) + inherited
195		}
196		objectEnv := []string{
197			"GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY=" + objectDir,
198			"GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES=" + alternates,
199		}
200		indexSource, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "index")
201		if err != nil {
202			return "", "", nil, nil, err
203		}
204		if !filepath.IsAbs(indexSource) {
205			indexSource = filepath.Join(dir, indexSource)
206		}
207		indexBytes, err := os.ReadFile(indexSource)
208		if err != nil {
209			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("read index snapshot: %w", err)
210		}
211		index := filepath.Join(tempDir, "index")
212		if err := os.WriteFile(index, indexBytes, 0o600); err != nil {
213			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("copy index snapshot: %w", err)
214		}
215		env := append(append([]string(nil), objectEnv...), "GIT_INDEX_FILE="+index)
216		indexTree, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "write-tree")
217		if err != nil {
218			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot index: %w", err)
219		}
220		indexDiff, err := treeDiffPaths(ctx, dir, env, base, indexTree)
221		if err != nil {
222			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("compare index snapshot: %w", err)
223		}
224	
225		if _, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
226			return "", "", nil, nil, err
227		}
228		worktreeTree, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "write-tree")
229		if err != nil {
230			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot worktree: %w", err)
231		}
232		worktreeDiff, err := treeDiffPaths(ctx, dir, env, base, worktreeTree)
233		if err != nil {
234			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("compare worktree snapshot: %w", err)
235		}
236		return indexTree, worktreeTree, indexDiff, worktreeDiff, nil
237	}
238	
239	func treeDiffPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string, env []string, base, tree string) (map[string]bool, error) {
240		out, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-z", base, tree)
241		if err != nil {
242			return nil, err
243		}
244		paths := make(map[string]bool)
245		for _, path := range nulLines(out) {
246			if path != "" {
247				paths[path] = true
248			}
249		}
250		return paths, nil
251	}
252	
253	func finishFingerprint(status, indexTree, worktreeTree string) string {
254		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(status + "\x00" + indexTree + "\x00" + worktreeTree))
255		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
256	}
257	
258	// CommitAllChanges creates a normal user commit, preserving configured hooks.
259	func CommitAllChanges(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) error {
260		if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
261			return errors.New("commit message is required")
262		}
263		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
264			return err
265		}
266		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", message)
267		return err
268	}
269	
270	// DiscardAllChanges restores tracked/index state and removes non-ignored
271	// untracked files. Callers must obtain explicit destructive confirmation.
272	func DiscardAllChanges(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
273		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "reset", "--hard", "HEAD"); err != nil {
274			return err
275		}
276		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "clean", "-fd")
277		return err
278	}

13	// ReviewQuery identifies one exact head/base relationship in one repository.
14	// Repository is the forge's stable repository identity: owner/repository for
15	// GitHub, group/repository for GitLab, or organization/project/repository for
16	// Azure DevOps. Adapters must still verify the returned branches because CLI
17	// filters are not sufficient evidence on their own.
18	type ReviewQuery struct {
19		Repository string `json:"repository"`
20		Head       string `json:"head"`
21		Base       string `json:"base"`
22	}
23	
24	// ReviewState is the portable lifecycle state observed for a provider review.
25	type ReviewState string
26	
27	const (
28		ReviewOpen   ReviewState = "open"
29		ReviewDraft  ReviewState = "draft"
30		ReviewMerged ReviewState = "merged"
31		ReviewClosed ReviewState = "closed"
32	)
33	
34	// Valid reports whether s has defined portable review semantics.
35	func (s ReviewState) Valid() bool {
36		switch s {
37		case ReviewOpen, ReviewDraft, ReviewMerged, ReviewClosed:
38			return true
39		default:
40			return false
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// Review is the minimal provider evidence for an exact head/base relationship.
45	// ID is the provider-stable identity and Number is the repository-local human
46	// identifier. Head, Base, State and Draft are observations from the provider
47	// response rather than values copied from ReviewQuery.
48	type Review struct {
49		Provider   Kind        `json:"provider"`
50		Repository string      `json:"repository"`
51		ID         string      `json:"id"`
52		Number     int         `json:"number"`
53		State      ReviewState `json:"state"`
54		Draft      bool        `json:"draft"`
55		URL        string      `json:"url"`
56		Head       string      `json:"head"`
57		Base       string      `json:"base"`
58		ObservedAt time.Time   `json:"observed_at"`
59	}
60	
61	// ReviewQuerier is an optional forge capability. A nil Review and nil error is
62	// a successful observation that no exact review exists. One exact match returns
63	// provider evidence; multiple exact matches fail with AmbiguousReviewError.
64	type ReviewQuerier interface {
65		QueryReview(ctx context.Context, dir string, query ReviewQuery) (*Review, error)
66	}
67	
68	var (
69		// ErrAmbiguousReview identifies a query with multiple exact head/base
70		// matches. Callers must not select one by recency or provider ordering.
71		ErrAmbiguousReview = errors.New("multiple reviews match")
72		// ErrMalformedReviewResponse identifies provider JSON that cannot supply the
73		// critical portable fields without guessing.
74		ErrMalformedReviewResponse = errors.New("malformed review response")
75	)
76	
77	// AmbiguousReviewError carries every exact match while keeping Error text free
78	// of provider response values such as private URLs and branch names.
79	type AmbiguousReviewError struct {
80		Provider Kind
81		Query    ReviewQuery
82		Matches  []Review
83	}
84	
85	func (e *AmbiguousReviewError) Error() string {
86		return fmt.Sprintf("%s review query returned %d exact matches", e.Provider, len(e.Matches))
87	}
88	
89	func (e *AmbiguousReviewError) Unwrap() error { return ErrAmbiguousReview }
90	
91	// MalformedReviewResponseError identifies the unusable response field without
92	// embedding its value or the response body. Index is zero-based and is -1 when
93	// the whole JSON document is malformed. Err retains safe decoder diagnostics.
94	type MalformedReviewResponseError struct {
95		Provider Kind
96		Index    int
97		Field    string
98		Err      error
99	}
100	
101	func (e *MalformedReviewResponseError) Error() string {
102		location := "response"
103		if e.Index >= 0 {
104			location = fmt.Sprintf("response item %d", e.Index+1)
105		}
106		detail := "missing or invalid " + e.Field
107		if e.Err != nil {
108			detail = e.Err.Error()
109		}
110		return fmt.Sprintf("%s review %s is malformed: %s", e.Provider, location, detail)
111	}
112	
113	func (e *MalformedReviewResponseError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
114	
115	func (e *MalformedReviewResponseError) Is(target error) bool {
116		return target == ErrMalformedReviewResponse
117	}
118	
119	// QueryReview invokes the optional capability without widening Forge. It never
120	// caches or initiates a query unless a caller explicitly calls this function.
121	func QueryReview(ctx context.Context, f Forge, dir string, query ReviewQuery) (*Review, error) {
122		querier, ok := f.(ReviewQuerier)
123		if !ok {
124			return nil, &ErrUnsupported{Kind: f.Kind(), Operation: "review queries"}
125		}
126		return querier.QueryReview(ctx, dir, query)
127	}
128	
129	type reviewCandidate struct {
130		ID     string
131		Number int
132		State  string
133		Draft  *bool
134		URL    string
135		Head   string
136		Base   string
137	}
138	
139	type reviewStateNormalizer func(state string, draft bool) (ReviewState, error)
140	
141	func validateReviewQuery(query ReviewQuery) error {
142		switch {
143		case strings.TrimSpace(query.Repository) == "":
144			return errors.New("review query repository is required")
145		case strings.TrimSpace(query.Head) == "":
146			return errors.New("review query head is required")
147		case strings.TrimSpace(query.Base) == "":
148			return errors.New("review query base is required")
149		default:
150			return nil
151		}
152	}
153	
154	func decodeReviewJSON(provider Kind, out string, target any) error {
155		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(out)
156		if trimmed == "" || trimmed == "null" {
157			return malformedReviewResponse(provider, -1, "JSON array", nil)
158		}
159		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(trimmed), target); err != nil {
160			return malformedReviewResponse(provider, -1, "JSON", err)
161		}
162		return nil
163	}
164	
165	func selectExactReview(provider Kind, query ReviewQuery, candidates []reviewCandidate, normalize reviewStateNormalizer) (*Review, error) {
166		matches := make([]Review, 0, 1)
167		observedAt := time.Now().UTC()
168		for index, candidate := range candidates {
169			if candidate.Head == "" {
170				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "head branch", nil)
171			}
172			if candidate.Base == "" {
173				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "base branch", nil)
174			}
175			if candidate.Head != query.Head || candidate.Base != query.Base {
176				continue
177			}
178			if strings.TrimSpace(candidate.ID) == "" {
179				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "identifier", nil)
180			}
181			if candidate.Number <= 0 {
182				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "number", nil)
183			}
184			if candidate.Draft == nil {
185				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "draft flag", nil)
186			}
187			if !validReviewURL(candidate.URL) {
188				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "URL", nil)
189			}
190			state, err := normalize(candidate.State, *candidate.Draft)
191			if err != nil {
192				return nil, malformedReviewResponse(provider, index, "state", err)
193			}
194			matches = append(matches, Review{
195				Provider: provider, Repository: query.Repository,
196				ID: candidate.ID, Number: candidate.Number,
197				State: state, Draft: *candidate.Draft, URL: candidate.URL,
198				Head: candidate.Head, Base: candidate.Base, ObservedAt: observedAt,
199			})
200		}
201	
202		switch len(matches) {
203		case 0:
204			return nil, nil
205		case 1:
206			return &matches[0], nil
207		default:
208			return nil, &AmbiguousReviewError{
209				Provider: provider, Query: query,
210				Matches: append([]Review(nil), matches...),
211			}
212		}
213	}
214	
215	func malformedReviewResponse(provider Kind, index int, field string, err error) error {
216		return &MalformedReviewResponseError{Provider: provider, Index: index, Field: field, Err: err}
217	}
218	
219	func validReviewURL(raw string) bool {
220		parsed, err := url.Parse(raw)
221		if err != nil || parsed.Host == "" {
222			return false
223		}
224		return parsed.Scheme == "https" || parsed.Scheme == "http"
225	}

708	func (s *lifecycleService) revalidateRemoteQueryContext(ctx context.Context, observed remoteRefreshObservation, allowFetchedRefs bool) error {
709		repository, err := s.gitDiscover(ctx, observed.repoPath)
710		if err != nil {
711			return staleBoundary("repository became unavailable before review query: " + err.Error())
712		}
713		mainPath, err := s.canonicalPath(repository.MainRoot)
714		if err != nil {
715			return staleBoundary("repository main path became unavailable before review query: " + err.Error())
716		}
717		commonDir, err := s.canonicalPath(repository.GitCommonDir)
718		if err != nil {
719			return staleBoundary("Git common directory became unavailable before review query: " + err.Error())
720		}
721		if mainPath != observed.repoPath || commonDir != observed.gitCommonDir {
722			return staleBoundary("repository identity changed before review query")
723		}
724		remoteURL := strings.TrimSpace(s.gitRemote(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteName))
725		kind, repositoryIdentity := forge.IdentityFromURL(remoteURL)
726		if remoteURL != observed.remoteURL || kind != observed.providerKind || repositoryIdentity != observed.providerRepository {
727			return staleBoundary("remote URL or provider repository identity changed before review query")
728		}
729		if observed.provider == nil || observed.provider.Kind() != observed.providerKind {
730			return staleBoundary("review provider identity changed before query")
731		}
732		if _, ok := observed.provider.(forge.ReviewQuerier); !ok {
733			return staleBoundary("review provider capability changed before query")
734		}
735		if !observed.provider.Available() {
736			return staleBoundary("review provider CLI became unavailable before query")
737		}
738		if !allowFetchedRefs {
739			freshRefs := s.observeRemoteRefs(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteName, observed.head, observed.base)
740			if remoteRefsAuthority(freshRefs) != remoteRefsAuthority(observed.refs) {
741				return staleBoundary("local or remote-tracking ref authority changed before query")
742			}
743		}
744		return nil
745	}
746	
747	func (e *executionState) setRemoteReviewFailure(data *RemoteObservation, observed remoteRefreshObservation, err error) {
748		data.Review = RemoteReviewObservation{
749			State: ObservationError, Exists: false,
750			Provider: observed.providerKind, Repository: observed.providerRepository,
751			Head: observed.head, Base: observed.base, ObservedAt: e.service.now(),
752			FailureKind: classifyRemoteReviewFailure(err), Failure: err.Error(),
753		}
754		data.HasReview = true
755	}
756	
757	func classifyRemoteReviewFailure(err error) RemoteReviewFailureKind {
758		if errors.Is(err, forge.ErrAmbiguousReview) {
759			return RemoteReviewFailureAmbiguous
760		}
761		if errors.Is(err, forge.ErrMalformedReviewResponse) {
762			return RemoteReviewFailureMalformed
763		}
764		var unsupported *forge.ErrUnsupported
765		if errors.As(err, &unsupported) {
766			return RemoteReviewFailureUnsupported
767		}
768		var missingCLI *forge.ErrNoCLI
769		if errors.As(err, &missingCLI) {
770			return RemoteReviewFailureMissingCLI
771		}
772		var missingExtension *forge.ErrNoExtension
773		if errors.As(err, &missingExtension) {
774			return RemoteReviewFailureMissingExtension
775		}
776		return RemoteReviewFailureProvider
777	}
778	
779	func validateRemoteReview(observed remoteRefreshObservation, review forge.Review) error {
780		switch {
781		case review.Provider != observed.providerKind:
782			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "provider")
783		case review.Repository != observed.providerRepository:
784			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "repository identity")
785		case review.Head != observed.head:
786			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "head branch")
787		case review.Base != observed.base:
788			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "base branch")
789		case strings.TrimSpace(review.ID) == "" || review.ID != strings.TrimSpace(review.ID):
790			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "identifier")
791		case review.Number <= 0:
792			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "number")
793		case !review.State.Valid():
794			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "state")
795		case review.State == forge.ReviewDraft && !review.Draft:
796			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "draft flag")
797		case review.State == forge.ReviewOpen && review.Draft:
798			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "draft state")
799		case !validRemoteReviewURL(review.URL):
800			return malformedRemoteReview(observed.providerKind, "URL")
801		}
802		return nil
803	}
804	
805	func malformedRemoteReview(provider forge.Kind, field string) error {
806		return &forge.MalformedReviewResponseError{Provider: provider, Index: 0, Field: field}
807	}
808	
809	func validRemoteReviewURL(raw string) bool {
810		parsed, err := url.Parse(raw)
811		return err == nil && parsed.Host != "" && (parsed.Scheme == "https" || parsed.Scheme == "http")
812	}
813	
814	func remoteRefCount(refs RemoteRefsObservation) int {
815		count := 0
816		for _, ref := range []NamedRefObservation{refs.LocalHead, refs.LocalBase, refs.RemoteHead, refs.RemoteBase} {
817			if ref.Exists && ref.Failure == "" && ref.OID != "" {
818				count++
819			}
820		}
821		return count
822	}
823	
824	func remoteRefSummary(refs RemoteRefsObservation) string {
825		return strconv.Itoa(remoteRefCount(refs)) + " named ref OID(s) observed"
826	}

+// ReadinessState classifies one intent without changing its durable record.
+type ReadinessState string
+
+const (
+	ReadinessPending              ReadinessState = "pending"
+	ReadinessFailed               ReadinessState = "failed"
+	ReadinessDiscarded            ReadinessState = "discarded"
+	ReadinessFinalizedReachable   ReadinessState = "finalized-reachable"
+	ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable ReadinessState = "finalized-unreachable"
+	ReadinessObservationError     ReadinessState = "observation-error"
+)
+
+// IntentReadiness is the read-only finalization evidence for one intent whose
+// recorded worktree is the exact checkout being inspected.
+type IntentReadiness struct {
+	Intent           Intent
+	State            ReadinessState
+	Finalized        bool
+	ReceiptReachable bool
+	ObservationError error
+}
+
+// ReadinessInspection is a complete read-only observation for one exact
+// checkout. KnownEmpty is true only when the store was read successfully and no
+// intent matched the checkout; it distinguishes absence from failed observation.
+type ReadinessInspection struct {
+	Checkout         string
+	KnownEmpty       bool
+	Intents          []IntentReadiness
+	ObservationError error
+}
+
+// Ready applies only the existing artifact finalization contract: an exact
+// checkout is ready when it has no intents, or every intent was explicitly
+// discarded or has a finalized receipt that is still reachable. Missing or
+// incomplete evidence fails closed.
+func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {
+	if i.ObservationError != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	if len(i.Intents) == 0 {
+		return i.KnownEmpty
+	}
+	if i.KnownEmpty {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, intent := range i.Intents {
+		if intent.ObservationError != nil {
+			return false
+		}
+		switch intent.State {
+		case ReadinessDiscarded:
+			// Discard is the existing explicit operator escape hatch.
+		case ReadinessFinalizedReachable:
+			if !intent.Finalized || !intent.ReceiptReachable {
+				return false
+			}
+		default:
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+// InspectReadiness gathers artifact finalization evidence for one exact
+// checkout. It never reconciles receipts, finalizes intents, or writes either
+// source files or intent records. The returned inspection retains partial
+// evidence and the same wrapped error returned separately to ordinary callers.
+func InspectReadiness(ctx context.Context, store *Store, checkout string) (ReadinessInspection, error) {
+	inspection := ReadinessInspection{}
+	if ctx == nil {
+		err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a context")
+		inspection.ObservationError = err
+		return inspection, err
+	}
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		inspection.ObservationError = err
+		return inspection, err
+	}
+	if store == nil {
+		err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a store")
+		inspection.ObservationError = err
+		return inspection, err
+	}
+
+	canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout)
+	if err != nil {
+		err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness checkout: %w", err)
+		inspection.ObservationError = err
+		return inspection, err
+	}
+	inspection.Checkout = canonical
+
+	intents, err := store.List()
+	if err != nil {
+		err = fmt.Errorf("list artifact intents: %w", err)
+		inspection.ObservationError = err
+		return inspection, err
+	}
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		inspection.ObservationError = err
+		return inspection, err
+	}
+
+	for _, intent := range intents {
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
+			break
+		}
+		intentCheckout, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
+		if err != nil {
+			err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact intent %s checkout: %w", intent.ID, err)
+			inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
+			continue
+		}
+		if intentCheckout != canonical {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		evidence := IntentReadiness{Intent: intent, Finalized: intent.Status == Finalized}
+		switch intent.Status {
+		case Armed, Finalizing:
+			evidence.State = ReadinessPending
+		case Failed:
+			evidence.State = ReadinessFailed
+		case Discarded:
+			evidence.State = ReadinessDiscarded
+		case Finalized:
+			evidence.ReceiptReachable, err = receiptRemainsReachable(ctx, canonical, intent)
+			switch {
+			case err != nil:
+				err = fmt.Errorf("inspect artifact intent %s receipt: %w", intent.ID, err)
+				evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
+				evidence.ObservationError = err
+				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
+			case evidence.ReceiptReachable:
+				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedReachable
+			default:
+				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable
+			}
+		default:
+			// Store.List validates statuses, but fail closed if another Store
+			// implementation is introduced without preserving that contract.
+			err = fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s has unrecognized status %q", intent.ID, intent.Status)
+			evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
+			evidence.ObservationError = err
+			inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
+		}
+		inspection.Intents = append(inspection.Intents, evidence)
+	}
+
+	inspection.KnownEmpty = len(inspection.Intents) == 0 && inspection.ObservationError == nil
+	return inspection, inspection.ObservationError
+}
+
+func receiptRemainsReachable(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (bool, error) {
+	if intent.ArtifactCommit == "" {
+		return false, nil
+	}
+	candidates := []struct {
+		dir string
+		ref string
+	}{
+		{checkout, "HEAD"},
+		{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
+		{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
+	}
+	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(candidates))
+	var observationErr error
+	for _, candidate := range candidates {
+		if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
+			continue
+		}
+		key := candidate.dir + "\x00" + candidate.ref
+		if seen[key] {
+			continue
+		}
+		seen[key] = true
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return false, joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
+		}
+		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
+			return true, nil
+		} else if !gitNotAncestor(err) {
+			observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr,
+				fmt.Errorf("check %s against %s in %s: %w", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref, candidate.dir, err))
+		}
+	}
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
+	}
+	return false, observationErr
+}
+
+func gitNotAncestor(err error) bool {
+	var exitErr *exec.ExitError
+	return errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1
+}
+
+func joinReadinessError(current, next error) error {
+	if current == nil {
+		return next
+	}
+	if next == nil {
+		return current
+	}
+	return errors.Join(current, next)
+}
+
 func (s *Service) Prepare(ctx context.Context, request PrepareRequest) (*Intent, error) {
 	if s.Store == nil {
 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact service needs a store")

+	createReadinessIntent(t, store, "intent-discarded", r.Root, Discarded, "")
+	createReadinessIntent(t, store, "intent-reachable", r.Root, Finalized, reachable)
+	createReadinessIntent(t, store, "intent-unreachable", r.Root, Finalized, unreachable)

+		reachable bool

+		"intent-failed":      {state: ReadinessFailed},
+		"intent-discarded":   {state: ReadinessDiscarded},
+		"intent-reachable":   {state: ReadinessFinalizedReachable, finalized: true, reachable: true},
+		"intent-unreachable": {state: ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable, finalized: true},

+			evidence.ReceiptReachable != expected.reachable || evidence.ObservationError != nil {

+		}

+		return nil

+		t.Fatal(err)

+	marker := r.Write("rewrite-marker.txt", "rewritten receipt\n")
+	r.Git("add", "rewrite-marker.txt")
+	r.Git("commit", "--amend", "--no-edit")

+		t.Fatalf("rewritten receipt lost intent trailer:\n%s", message)

+
+	readBytes := func(path string) []byte {

+		body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		return body
+	}
+	sources := []string{transcript, plan, marker}
+	beforeSources := make(map[string][]byte, len(sources))
+	for _, path := range sources {
+		beforeSources[path] = readBytes(path)
+	}
+	intentPath := store.path(intentID)
+	beforeIntent := readBytes(intentPath)
+	beforeStatus := r.Git("status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=all")

+	if err != nil {

+		t.Fatalf("stale receipt inspection = %+v", inspection)
+	}
+	if inspection.Intents[0].Intent.ArtifactCommit != recordedReceipt {
+		t.Fatalf("inspection reconciled receipt in memory: %s", inspection.Intents[0].Intent.ArtifactCommit)
+	}
+	for path, before := range beforeSources {
+		if after := readBytes(path); !bytes.Equal(after, before) {
+			t.Errorf("source file %s changed during inspection", path)
+		}
+	}
+	if after := readBytes(intentPath); !bytes.Equal(after, beforeIntent) {
+		t.Fatal("intent record changed during inspection")
+	}
+	if after := r.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD"); after != currentReceipt {
+		t.Fatalf("inspection changed HEAD: got %s want %s", after, currentReceipt)

+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if stored.ArtifactCommit != recordedReceipt {
+		t.Fatalf("inspection reconciled durable receipt: got %s want %s", stored.ArtifactCommit, recordedReceipt)
+	}

1	---
2	description: Choose the owner and location of each worktree, then provision ignored files and dependencies safely.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-29
6	---
7	
8	# Worktrees and provisioning
9	
10	A Git worktree begins as a clean checkout. `dev` owns durable change-stream worktrees and builds an inspectable plan for the ignored files and dependencies needed to make them usable.
11	
12	## Choose one lifecycle owner
13	
14	| Worktree kind | Owner | Typical location | Lifetime |
15	|---|---|---|---|
16	| feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | `dev` | configured `paths.worktree_path` | until `dev done`, `dev wt rm`, or an approved sweep |
17	| harness-scoped isolation | Claude Code or another harness | harness-owned directory such as `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` | governed by that harness's retention and safe-cleanup rules |
18	| externally created linked worktree | external until adopted | tool-specific | visible to `dev`, unmanaged until explicit adoption |
19	
20	Use `dev` when code, history, or plans must remain reviewable or a human may return later. Do not nest a long-lived `dev` worktree inside a repository; file watchers, language servers, backup tools, and searches in the outer checkout would see a second copy of the tree.
21	
22	`dev` creates the checkout with Git at its configured path. Herdr only opens that existing path, so worktree placement remains identical on machines without Herdr.
23	
24	## Inspect before creating
25	
26	```bash
27	dev wt plan
28	dev wt plan --write          # seed repository-owned .dev-cli/config.toml
29	dev wt create feat/auth --base main
30	dev wt list
31	```
32	
33	`dev wt plan` reads lockfiles, tool availability, configured include/link rules, and Git ignore state without changing the checkout. The resulting plan shows every runnable or skipped step and any safety downgrade.
34	
35	## Carry ignored files by allowlist
36	
37	```toml
38	[worktree]
39	include = [".env", ".env.local", "config/local.json"]
40	link = []
41	post_create = "auto"
42	strategy = "reinstall"
43	```
44	
45	Only paths that are both listed and confirmed by Git as ignored are copied. A tracked file already arrives through the branch; copying a different checkout's version over it would violate branch isolation.
46	
47	Included files are copied as files, not logged. Current provisioning also rechecks the source and destination path shape while opening/copying so source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused.
48	
49	Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` globally. Include that exact file only for a deliberately chosen launcher whose behavior depends on it, and verify the copy in the plan.
50	
51	## Select dependency strategy by correctness
52	
53	| Strategy | Effect | Guidance |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| `reinstall` | run the lockfile-derived install command | safe default |
56	| `copy` | duplicate an installed dependency directory | use only where paths are portable |
57	| `link` | share one dependency directory | fastest and usually unsafe for concurrent writers |
58	| `skip` | leave dependencies absent | container- or CI-driven development |
59	
60	Per-ecosystem overrides live in the project or global config:
```
</details></tool-use>

199	## `dev done` finish flags
200	
201	`dev done` 對 branch/worktree task 透過 `--ff`（rebase 到 base 再 fast-forward）、`--pr`（push 並開啟 pull/merge request）或 `--merged`（依 `--base-ref` 驗證外部 integration）處理。未指定 integration choice 時，在 TTY 上會開啟 interactive finish wizard —— 提示內容見[變更流工作流程](../guides/change-stream-workflow.zh-TW.md)。
202	
203	Dirty checkout 由 `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` 處理（預設 `auto`）：
204	
205	| 值 | 行為 |
206	|---|---|
207	| `auto` | interactive：提示 commit 或 discard；non-interactive：直接失敗，等同 `fail` |
208	| `fail` | dirty checkout 時拒絕 finish |
209	| `commit` | 用 `--message`/`-m` commit 全部變更（未指定時 interactive 會提示輸入） |
210	| `discard` | reset tracked 變更並移除 untracked files；具破壞性，沒有 TTY 時需要 `--yes` |
211	
212	`--yes`/`-y` 用來確認選定的 finish plan；non-interactive 的 `--dirty discard` 必須要有它，其他情況則是跳過 interactive 確認步驟。`--push` 會依 selected integration push 對應 branch/base。成功的 local 或 externally verified integration 只記錄 DONE/MERGED，永遠保留 runtime、worktree 與 branch 給獨立的 `dev retire`；`--keep-worktree` 只保留為 no-op compatibility warning，`--delete-branch` 則會報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`。`--merged` 可用 `--confirm-squash <merge-commit>` 對 squash result 作明確 operator attestation，不能由 provider status 自動推斷。

214	## Configuration
215

218	dev config show
219	dev config path

233	| `[runtime]` | `auto`、Herdr、tmux、Zellij 或 none，以及 metadata settings |

241	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` 會啟用單次 TUI startup/readiness trace。
242	Target 必須是 absolute 且尚不存在；dev 絕不 overwrite。Private、bounded document
243	在 TUI teardown 後才寫入，只包含 relative categorical timings 與 aggregate row
244	counts，不包含 names、paths 或 raw payloads；它不是 configuration、cache、durable

180	
181	Publishing uses the local repository name and configured description, then asks
182	for the provider namespace/owner, visibility, and whether to push the
183	initial/current branch. Dev creates the empty GitHub or GitLab repository after
184	required local setup and commit steps succeed, then adds/verifies `origin` and
185	optionally pushes with upstream tracking. A
186	provider, name-conflict, or push failure never deletes the local checkout or
187	an upstream that was already created.
188	
189	Publishing from `repo setup` requires `--check-in=commit` (or the compatible
190	`--commit` flag), so the newly created upstream cannot omit the generated setup
191	changes. `--check-in=stage` is incompatible with any new upstream; for a new
192	repository, `none` may create an intentionally empty upstream only with
193	`--push=false`.
194	
195	### Handoff
196	
197	`stay` prints the result only. `cd` uses the trusted `shell-init` wrapper to
198	change the parent shell. `open` opens the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime
199	and falls back to `cd` when runtime is `none`. `start` continues into the
200	existing task wizard with the repository fixed, and is unavailable when setup
201	leaves uncommitted files that a new worktree would omit. Neither repository
202	bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. Explicit
203	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches one command only
204	when a newly created first-class Herdr worktree returns its exact root pane;
205	`--focus` independently controls navigation afterward.
206	
207	All shared TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards
208	use an inline editor: Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, insertion at the
209	cursor, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation work as terminal actions rather than being
210	inserted as raw escape bytes. Buffered and piped non-TTY input retains its
211	line-oriented behavior.
212	
213	## `dev done` finish flags
214	
215	`dev done` for branch/worktree tasks integrates through exactly one of `--ff` (rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it) or `--pr` (push and open a pull/merge request). Omitting both opens the interactive finish wizard on a TTY — see [Change-stream workflow](../guides/change-stream-workflow.md) for the prompts.
216	
217	A dirty checkout is handled by `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` (default `auto`):
218	
219	| Value | Behavior |
220	|---|---|
221	| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
222	| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
223	| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
224	| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |
225	
226	`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive confirmation step. `--keep-worktree` keeps the worktree after `--ff` integration (default: removed once merged), `--push` also pushes the resulting branch, and `--delete-branch` deletes the branch once its commits are contained in the base — never a branch with unpushed commits.
227	
228	## Configuration
229	
230	```bash
231	dev config init
232	dev config show
233	dev config path
234	dev config scaffolds init
235	dev config scaffolds show
236	dev config scaffolds path
237	dev config scaffolds edit
238	```
239	
240	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
241	
242	Key sections:
243	
244	| Section | Controls |
245	|---|---|
246	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
247	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
248	| `[worktree]` | ignored includes, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
249	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
250	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
251	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
252	| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
253	| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |
254	
255	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` enables a one-run TUI startup/readiness
256	trace. The target must be absolute and must not exist; dev never overwrites it.
257	The private bounded document is written after TUI teardown and contains relative
258	categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw
259	payloads. It is not configuration,
260	cache, durable stats, stdout, or network telemetry. For TUI invocations, the
261	optional update-cache network refresh is also deferred until the initial view
262	has returned.
263	
264	Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.
265	
266	### Scaffold presets
267	
268	Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
269	the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.
```

100	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
101	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
102	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
103	
104	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
105	
106	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
107	
108	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
109	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
110	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
111	
112	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
113	
114	For a release:
115	
116	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
117	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
118	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
119	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
120	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, and create the GitHub release.
121	
122	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
123	
124	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
125	
126	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
127	
128	| Change | Required synchronization |
129	|---|---|
130	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
131	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
132	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
133	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
134	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
135	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
136	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
137	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
138	
139	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
140	
141	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
142

66			Long: `Preview the repository lifecycle state machine in a full-screen interface.
67	
68	Without an argument, a checkout opens its canonical repository and focuses the
69	exact current worktree. Outside Git, dev opens an asynchronous repository
70	picker. An explicit repository reference always overrides the current directory.

81					ref = args[0]

92	func resolveFlowLaunch(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref string, deps flowCommandDeps) (flowLaunch, error) {
93		var launch flowLaunch
94		if deps.getwd == nil || deps.discover == nil || deps.resolve == nil {
95			return launch, errors.New("flow command dependencies are incomplete")
96		}
97		cwd, err := deps.getwd()
98		if err != nil {
99			return launch, fmt.Errorf("resolve flow caller directory: %w", err)
100		}
101		launch.cwd = cwd
102	
103		if ref != "" {
104			resolved, _, err := deps.resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), ref)
105			if err != nil {
106				return launch, err
107			}
108			queryPath := resolved.Path
109			if queryPath == "" {
110				queryPath = resolved.RealPath
111			}
112			discovered, err := deps.discover(ctx, queryPath)
113			if err != nil {
114				return launch, fmt.Errorf("discover explicit repository %s: %w", config.Contract(queryPath), err)
115			}
116			repository, err := availableFlowRepository(discovered, &resolved, discovered.Root)
117			if err != nil {
118				return launch, err
119			}
120			launch.repository = &repository
121			row := repository.row
122			launch.preselected = &row
123			return launch, nil
124		}
125	
126		discovered, err := deps.discover(ctx, cwd)
127		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
128			return launch, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return launch, fmt.Errorf("discover current repository from %s: %w", config.Contract(cwd), err)
132		}
133		repository, err := availableFlowRepository(discovered, nil, discovered.Root)
134		if err != nil {
135			return launch, err
136		}
137		launch.repository = &repository
138		row := repository.row
139		launch.preselected = &row
140		return launch, nil
141	}

143	func runFlow(app *App, launch flowLaunch, runProgram flowProgramRunner) error {
144		if runProgram == nil {
145			return errors.New("flow program runner is unavailable")
146		}
147		flowtui.SetColorEnabled(app.outStyle().enabled)
148		app.traceTUI = true
149		runCtx, cancelRun := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
150		finishSetup := app.trace.Start(perftrace.TUISetup, perftrace.Fields{})
151		runtimeResolver := newTUIRuntimeResolver(app)
152		loader := newFlowLoader(app, runtimeResolver, launch.cwd)
153		if launch.repository != nil {
154			loader.registerRepository(*launch.repository, true)
155		}
156		actions := loader.actions()
157		if app.deferredReleaseRefresh {
158			actions.AfterFirstView = func(context.Context) { app.refreshReleaseDetached() }
159		}
160		model := flowtui.New(actions, launch.preselected).WithContext(runCtx)
161		finishSetup(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
162		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIProgramRunBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
163		final, err := runProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen())
164		cancelRun()
165		app.finishTrace()
166		if err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		withHandoff, ok := final.(interface {
170			Handoff() (taskflow.Handoff, bool)
171		})
172		if !ok {
173			return nil
174		}
175		handoff, ok := withHandoff.Handoff()
176		if !ok {
177			return nil
178		}
179		return honorFlowHandoff(app, runtimeResolver, handoff)
180	}
181	
182	func honorFlowHandoff(app *App, resolver flowRuntimeResolver, handoff taskflow.Handoff) error {
183		switch handoff.Kind {
184		case taskflow.HandoffDirectory:
185			if handoff.Path == "" {
186				return errors.New("flow returned an empty directory handoff")
187			}
188			return app.cdDirective(handoff.Path)
189		case taskflow.HandoffRuntime:
190			if handoff.Runtime == "" || handoff.RuntimeHandle == "" {
191				return errors.New("flow returned an incomplete runtime handoff")
192			}
193			var rt runtime.Runtime
194			if resolver != nil {
195				resolved, err := resolver.Resolve(ctxOf())
196				if err != nil {
197					return err
198				}
199				if resolved != nil && resolved.Name() == handoff.Runtime {
200					rt = resolved
201				}
202			}
203			if rt == nil {
204				rt = app.runtimeNamed(handoff.Runtime)
205			}
206			if rt == nil || rt.Name() != handoff.Runtime {
207				return fmt.Errorf("flow handoff backend %q is unavailable", handoff.Runtime)
208			}
209			return activateRuntime(ctxOf(), rt, handoff.RuntimeHandle)
210		case taskflow.HandoffURL:
211			if handoff.URL == "" {
212				return errors.New("flow returned an empty URL handoff")
213			}
214			_, err := fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, handoff.URL)
215			return err
216		default:
217			return fmt.Errorf("flow returned unsupported handoff kind %q", handoff.Kind)
218		}
219	}

232	func availableFlowRepository(discovered gitx.Repo, preferred *repo.Repo, focus string) (flowRepository, error) {
233		commonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(discovered.GitCommonDir)
234		if err != nil {
235			return flowRepository{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize flow repository identity: %w", err)
236		}
237		mainRoot := discovered.MainRoot
238		if mainRoot == "" && discovered.Bare {
239			mainRoot = discovered.GitCommonDir
240		}
241		mainRoot, err = pathx.Canonical(mainRoot)
242		if err != nil {
243			return flowRepository{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize flow repository root: %w", err)
244		}
245		focusTarget := ""
246		if focus != "" {
247			focusTarget, err = pathx.Canonical(focus)
248			if err != nil {
249				return flowRepository{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize flow focus: %w", err)
250			}
251		}
252	
253		r := repo.Repo{
254			Name: discovered.Name, Path: mainRoot, RealPath: mainRoot,
255			CommonDir: commonDir, MainRoot: mainRoot, Bare: discovered.Bare, HasGit: true,
256		}
257		name := discovered.Name
258		if preferred != nil {
259			if preferred.Name != "" {
260				r.Name = preferred.Name
261			}
262			r.Root = preferred.Root
263			r.Category = preferred.Category
264			name = preferred.Display()
265			if name == "" {
266				name = r.Name
267			}
268		}
269		return flowRepository{
270			row: flowtui.RepositoryRow{
271				RepoKey: commonDir, Name: name, Path: mainRoot, Available: true,
272				FocusTarget: focusTarget,
273			},
274			repository: r,
275			available:  true,
276		}, nil
277	}

279	func unavailableFlowRepository(record task.Record, cause error) flowRepository {
280		path := record.Task.RepoPath
281		if canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(path); err == nil {
282			path = canonical
283		} else if absolute, absErr := filepath.Abs(path); absErr == nil {
284			path = filepath.Clean(absolute)
285		}
286		name := record.Task.Repo
287		if name == "" {
288			name = filepath.Base(path)
289		}
290		message := "repository is unavailable"
291		if cause != nil {
292			message += ": " + cause.Error()
293		}
294		return flowRepository{
295			row: flowtui.RepositoryRow{
296				RepoKey: "unavailable:" + path, Name: name, Path: path,
297				Available: false, Error: message,
298			},
299			available:        false,
300			unavailableTasks: []task.Record{record},
301		}
302	}

336	func newFlowLoader(app *App, resolver flowRuntimeResolver, cwd string) *flowLoader {
337		loader := &flowLoader{
338			app:          app,
339			runtime:      resolver,
340			limiter:      inventory.NewLimiter(8),
341			cwd:          cwd,
342			now:          time.Now,
343			discover:     gitx.Discover,
344			listRepo:     repo.Discover,
345			inspect:      artifact.InspectReadiness,
346			base:         gitx.DefaultBranch,
347			repositories: make(map[string]flowRepository),
348			pinned:       make(map[string]bool),
349			targets:      make(map[string]map[string]flowTarget),
350			approved:     make(map[string]flowApprovedPlan),
351			remote:       make(map[string]taskflow.RemoteObservation),
352		}
353		loader.service = func(rt runtime.Runtime) (*taskflow.Service, error) {
354			return newFlowLifecycleService(app, rt, cwd)
355		}
356		return loader

359	func newFlowLifecycleService(app *App, resolved runtime.Runtime, cwd string) (*taskflow.Service, error) {
360		if resolved == nil {
361			return nil, errors.New("flow runtime resolver returned no backend")
362		}
363		return taskflow.NewLifecycleService(taskflow.LifecycleConfig{
364			Config: app.Cfg, Tasks: app.Tasks, Artifacts: artifactStore(app),
365			DefaultRuntime: func() runtime.Runtime { return resolved },
366			NamedRuntime: func(name string) runtime.Runtime {
367				if name == "" || name == resolved.Name() {
368					return resolved
369				}
370				return app.runtimeNamed(name)
371			},
372			Host: config.Hostname(), CWD: cwd,
373			// The flow preview deliberately never inherits the expert shared-writer
374			// override. Its normal choices must remain fail-closed.
375			AllowSharedCheckout: false,
376			Logf: func(format string, args ...any) {
377				if app.Err != nil {
378					fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, format+"\n", args...)
379				}
380			},
381		})
382	}

402	func (l *flowLoader) ListRepositories(ctx context.Context) ([]flowtui.RepositoryRow, error) {
403		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
404			return nil, err
405		}
406		records, _, taskErr := l.app.Tasks.ListRecords()
407		if taskErr != nil {
408			return nil, fmt.Errorf("list task-referenced repositories: %w", taskErr)
409		}
410		discovered, err := l.listRepo(ctx, l.app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
411		if err != nil {
412			return nil, err
413		}
414	
415		fresh := make(map[string]flowRepository)
416		l.mu.Lock()
417		for key := range l.pinned {
418			if existing, ok := l.repositories[key]; ok {
419				fresh[key] = existing
420			}
421		}
422		l.mu.Unlock()
423	
424		for index := range discovered {
425			candidate := discovered[index]
426			gitRepo, discoverErr := l.discover(ctx, candidate.Path)
427			if discoverErr != nil {
428				continue
429			}
430			entry, convertErr := availableFlowRepository(gitRepo, &candidate, "")
431			if convertErr != nil {
432				continue
433			}
434			if _, exists := fresh[entry.row.RepoKey]; !exists {
435				fresh[entry.row.RepoKey] = entry
436			}
437		}
438	
439		pathResults := make(map[string]struct {
440			repository flowRepository
441			err        error
442		})
443		for _, record := range records {
444			path := record.Task.RepoPath
445			resolved, seen := pathResults[path]
446			if !seen {
447				gitRepo, discoverErr := l.discover(ctx, path)
448				if discoverErr == nil {
449					resolved.repository, discoverErr = availableFlowRepository(gitRepo, nil, "")
450				}
451				resolved.err = discoverErr
452				pathResults[path] = resolved
453			}
454			if resolved.err == nil {
455				if _, exists := fresh[resolved.repository.row.RepoKey]; !exists {
456					fresh[resolved.repository.row.RepoKey] = resolved.repository
457				}
458				continue
459			}
460			entry := unavailableFlowRepository(record, resolved.err)
461			if existing, exists := fresh[entry.row.RepoKey]; exists {
462				existing.unavailableTasks = appendUniqueFlowTaskRecord(existing.unavailableTasks, record)
463				fresh[entry.row.RepoKey] = existing
464			} else {
465				fresh[entry.row.RepoKey] = entry
466			}
467		}
468	
469		rows := make([]flowtui.RepositoryRow, 0, len(fresh))
470		for _, entry := range fresh {
471			rows = append(rows, entry.row)
472		}
473		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
474			left, right := strings.ToLower(rows[i].Name), strings.ToLower(rows[j].Name)
475			if left != right {
476				return left < right
477			}
478			if rows[i].Path != rows[j].Path {
479				return rows[i].Path < rows[j].Path
480			}
481			return rows[i].RepoKey < rows[j].RepoKey
482		})
483		l.mu.Lock()
484		l.repositories = fresh
485		l.mu.Unlock()
486		return rows, nil
487	}

489	func appendUniqueFlowTaskRecord(records []task.Record, candidate task.Record) []task.Record {
490		for _, record := range records {
491			if record.Task.ID == candidate.Task.ID {
492				return records
493			}
494		}
495		return append(records, candidate)
496	}
