```text
143	func runFlow(app *App, launch flowLaunch, runProgram flowProgramRunner) error {
144		if runProgram == nil {
145			return errors.New("flow program runner is unavailable")
146		}
147		flowtui.SetColorEnabled(app.outStyle().enabled)
148		app.traceTUI = true
149		runCtx, cancelRun := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
150		finishSetup := app.trace.Start(perftrace.TUISetup, perftrace.Fields{})
151		runtimeResolver := newTUIRuntimeResolver(app)
152		loader := newFlowLoader(app, runtimeResolver, launch.cwd)
153		if launch.repository != nil {
154			loader.registerRepository(*launch.repository, true)
155		}
156		actions := loader.actions()
157		if app.deferredReleaseRefresh {
158			actions.AfterFirstView = func(context.Context) { app.refreshReleaseDetached() }
159		}
160		model := flowtui.New(actions, launch.preselected).WithContext(runCtx)
161		finishSetup(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
162		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIProgramRunBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
163		final, err := runProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen())
164		cancelRun()
165		app.finishTrace()
166		if err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		withHandoff, ok := final.(interface {
170			Handoff() (taskflow.Handoff, bool)
171		})
172		if !ok {
173			return nil
174		}
175		handoff, ok := withHandoff.Handoff()
176		if !ok {
177			return nil
178		}
179		return honorFlowHandoff(app, runtimeResolver, handoff)
180	}
181	
182	func honorFlowHandoff(app *App, resolver flowRuntimeResolver, handoff taskflow.Handoff) error {
183		switch handoff.Kind {
184		case taskflow.HandoffDirectory:
185			if handoff.Path == "" {
186				return errors.New("flow returned an empty directory handoff")
187			}
188			return app.cdDirective(handoff.Path)
189		case taskflow.HandoffRuntime:
190			if handoff.Runtime == "" || handoff.RuntimeHandle == "" {
191				return errors.New("flow returned an incomplete runtime handoff")
192			}
193			var rt runtime.Runtime
194			if resolver != nil {
195				resolved, err := resolver.Resolve(ctxOf())
196				if err != nil {
197					return err
198				}
199				if resolved != nil && resolved.Name() == handoff.Runtime {
200					rt = resolved
201				}
202			}
203			if rt == nil {
204				rt = app.runtimeNamed(handoff.Runtime)
205			}
206			if rt == nil || rt.Name() != handoff.Runtime {
207				return fmt.Errorf("flow handoff backend %q is unavailable", handoff.Runtime)
208			}
209			return activateRuntime(ctxOf(), rt, handoff.RuntimeHandle)
210		case taskflow.HandoffURL:
211			if handoff.URL == "" {
212				return errors.New("flow returned an empty URL handoff")
213			}
214			_, err := fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, handoff.URL)
215			return err
216		default:
217			return fmt.Errorf("flow returned unsupported handoff kind %q", handoff.Kind)
218		}
219	}
```

```text
118		var created *Record

131		var updated *Record

178	// listRecordsUnlocked implements both the public read-only inventory and the
179	// transaction-scoped inventory. Callers using it for mutation authority must
180	// hold the store lock through the guarded operation.
181	func (s *Store) listRecordsUnlocked() ([]Record, []Diagnostic, error) {
182		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
183		if err != nil {
184			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
185				return nil, nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
186			}
187			return nil, nil, err
188		}
189		var records []Record
190		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
191		for _, entry := range entries {
192			name := entry.Name()
193			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
194				continue
195			}
196			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
197			record, err := s.getRecordUnlocked(id)
198			if err != nil {
199				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{
200					ID: id, Path: filepath.Join(s.Dir, name), Err: err,
201				})
202				continue
203			}
204			records = append(records, *record)
205		}
206		sortRecords(records)
207		sort.Slice(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool { return diagnostics[i].Path < diagnostics[j].Path })
208		return records, diagnostics, nil
209	}
```

```text
150						observed.taskClaims[index].Reason += " and derived task ID"
151					}
152					sortAdoptClaims(observed.taskClaims)
153					return
154				}
155			}
156			observed.taskClaims = append(observed.taskClaims, destructiveTaskClaim{
157				ID: taskID, Revision: record.Revision, Reason: "derived task ID",
158			})
159			sortAdoptClaims(observed.taskClaims)
160			return
161		}
162	}
163	
164	func sortAdoptClaims(claims []destructiveTaskClaim) {
165		sort.Slice(claims, func(i, j int) bool {
166			if claims[i].ID != claims[j].ID {
167				return claims[i].ID < claims[j].ID
168			}
169			return claims[i].Reason < claims[j].Reason
170		})
171	}
172	
173	func deriveAdoptState(observed adoptObservation) (task.State, string, string, string) {
174		rt := observed.runtime
175		switch {
176		case observed.runtimeErr != nil:
177			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime backend resolution failed; adoption remains WARM"
178		case rt == nil || strings.TrimSpace(rt.Name()) == "":
179			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime backend is unavailable; adoption remains WARM"
180		case rt.Name() == "none":
181			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime none leaves session and recognized-agent evidence unobserved; adoption remains WARM"
182		case !observed.runtimeAvailable:
183			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime backend is unavailable; adoption remains WARM"
184		case !observed.worktreeFound:
185			return task.Warm, "", "", "exact checkout is unavailable; adoption remains WARM"
186		case adoptStrictOccupancyError(observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr) != nil:
187			return task.Warm, "", "", "strict runtime occupancy is not ready; adoption remains WARM"
188		case !observed.occupancy.SessionList.Observed():
189			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime sessions were not freshly observed; adoption remains WARM"
190		case !observed.occupancy.AgentActivityList.Observed():
191			return task.Warm, "", "", "recognized-agent activity was not freshly observed; adoption remains WARM"
192		case len(observed.occupancy.Sessions) != 1:
193			return task.Warm, "", "", fmt.Sprintf("fresh runtime coverage contains %d sessions, not exactly one; adoption remains WARM", len(observed.occupancy.Sessions))
194		case len(observed.occupancy.Agents) != 0:
195			return task.Warm, "", "", "a recognized agent occupies the checkout; adoption remains WARM"
196		}
197	
198		session := observed.occupancy.Sessions[0]
199		handle := session.Runtime.Handle
200		if strings.TrimSpace(handle) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(handle) != handle || strings.ContainsRune(handle, '\x00') {
201			return task.Warm, "", "", "the sole covering runtime session has no stable nonempty handle; adoption remains WARM"
202		}
203		if !adoptSessionShellOnly(session) {
204			return task.Warm, "", "", "the sole covering runtime session is not shell-only; adoption remains WARM"
205		}
206		return task.Hot, rt.Name(), handle, "exactly one freshly observed shell-only runtime session covers the checkout with stable handle " + handle
207	}
208	
209	func adoptStrictOccupancyError(occupancy runtime.Occupancy, err error) error {
210		if occupancyErr := strictOccupancyError(occupancy, err); occupancyErr != nil {
211			return occupancyErr
212		}
213		var blockers []string
214		for _, session := range occupancy.Sessions {
215			// OccupancySession.Panes contains only panes whose live cwd covers the
216			// checkout. A mixed session may also host an unrelated agent elsewhere;
217			// that agent is not a writer claim on this checkout.
218			for _, pane := range session.Panes {
219				if strings.TrimSpace(pane.Agent) == "" && strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentSession) == "" {
220					continue
221				}
222				if occupancy.CallerPaneID != "" && pane.ID == occupancy.CallerPaneID {
223					continue
224				}
225				status := strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentStatus)
226				if status == "" {
227					status = "unknown"
228				}
229				blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("recognized agent pane %s (%s)", pane.ID, status))
230			}
231		}
232		if len(blockers) > 0 {
233			return fmt.Errorf("checkout is occupied by %s", strings.Join(blockers, ", "))
234		}
235		return nil
236	}
237	
238	func adoptSessionShellOnly(session runtime.OccupancySession) bool {
239		if strings.TrimSpace(session.Runtime.AgentStatus) != "" || len(session.Runtime.AgentSessions) != 0 {
240			return false
241		}
242		panes := session.Runtime.Panes
243		if len(panes) == 0 {
244			panes = session.Panes
245		}
246		for _, pane := range panes {
247			if strings.TrimSpace(pane.Agent) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentStatus) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentSession) != "" {
248				return false
249			}
250		}
251		return true
252	}
253	
254	func (s *lifecycleService) adoptSpec(request Request, observed adoptObservation) PlanSpec {
255		conditions := []Condition{retireRepositoryCondition(observed.destructiveObservation)}
256		conditions = append(conditions, adoptIdentityConditions(observed.destructiveObservation)...)
257		conditions = append(conditions, adoptBaseCondition(observed))
258		conditions = append(conditions, adoptTaskInventoryConditions(observed.destructiveObservation)...)
259		conditions = append(conditions, adoptRuntimeConditions(observed)...)
260		conditions = append(conditions, adoptStateCondition(request.Options.(AdoptOptions), observed))
261		conditions = append(conditions, condition(
262			ConditionOwner, VerdictMet, RequirementAdvisory,
263			"adoption assigns checkout ownership to host "+s.host, "",
264		))
265	
266		details := map[string]string{
267			"id": observed.taskID, "repo": observed.candidate.Repo,
268			"repo-path": observed.candidate.RepoPath, "checkout": observed.candidate.WorktreePath,
269			"branch": observed.candidate.Branch, "head": observed.locator.HeadOID,
270			"base": observed.candidate.Base, "base-oid": observed.baseOID,
271			"mode": string(observed.candidate.Mode), "state": string(observed.candidate.State),
272			"owner": observed.candidate.Owner, "runtime": observed.candidate.RuntimeName,
273			"runtime-handle": observed.candidate.RuntimeHandle,
274		}
275		effect := NewEffect(
276			EffectCreateTask, "create one task record for the exact unmanaged linked checkout",
277			observed.taskID, false, false, details,
278		)
279		retained := []string{
280			"checkout:" + observed.checkout,
281			"branch:" + observed.locator.Branch + "@" + observed.branchOID,
282		}
283		if observed.derivedState == task.Hot {
284			retained = append(retained, "runtime:"+observed.runtimeName+":"+observed.runtimeHandle)
285		}
286		return PlanSpec{
287			Authority:         adoptAuthority(observed),
288			Conditions:        conditions,
289			Effects:           []Effect{effect},
290			RetainedResources: retained,
291			Confirmation: Confirmation{
292				Kind:   ConfirmationApproval,
293				Prompt: "Adopt this exact unmanaged checkout as a " + strings.ToUpper(string(observed.derivedState)) + " worktree task?",
294			},
295			FallbackCommand: "dev adopt --apply --state " + shellQuote(string(observed.derivedState)),
296			Summary:         "Adopt unmanaged checkout " + observed.checkout,
297			DisplayedAt:     s.now(),
298		}
299	}
300	
301	func adoptAuthority(observed adoptObservation) map[string]string {
302		authority := observed.destructiveObservation.authority()
303		authority["adopt.base"] = observed.base
304		authority["adopt.base-exists"] = boolString(observed.baseExists)
305		authority["adopt.base-oid"] = observed.baseOID
306		authority["adopt.base-error"] = errorString(observed.baseOIDErr)
307		authority["adopt.task-id"] = observed.taskID
308		authority["adopt.task"] = adoptTaskAuthority(observed.candidate)
309		authority["adopt.occupancy"] = occupancyAuthority(observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr)
310		authority["adopt.derived-state"] = string(observed.derivedState)
311		authority["adopt.runtime-name"] = observed.runtimeName
312		authority["adopt.runtime-handle"] = observed.runtimeHandle
313		authority["adopt.state-evidence"] = observed.stateEvidence
314		return authority
315	}
316	
317	func adoptTaskAuthority(candidate task.Task) string {
318		values := []string{
319			candidate.ID, candidate.Name, candidate.Repo, candidate.RepoPath,
320			candidate.Branch, candidate.Base, candidate.WorktreePath,
321			string(candidate.Mode), string(candidate.State), candidate.Owner,
322			candidate.Next, candidate.Note, candidate.AgentSession,
323			candidate.RuntimeName, candidate.RuntimeHandle,
324		}
325		values = append(values, candidate.Tags...)
326		return authorityHash("taskflow-adopt-task-v1", values...)
327	}
328	
329	func adoptIdentityConditions(observed destructiveObservation) []Condition {
330		if !observed.worktreeFound {
331			verdict := VerdictBlocked
332			evidence := "the exact checkout is not registered"
333			if observed.worktreeErr != nil && !errors.Is(observed.worktreeErr, gitx.ErrWorktreeNotFound) {
334				verdict = VerdictError
335				evidence = observed.worktreeErr.Error()
336			}
337			return []Condition{
338				condition(ConditionCheckoutPresent, verdict, RequirementRequired, evidence, "refresh exact worktree topology"),
339				condition(ConditionCheckoutExact, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "checkout identity is unavailable", "refresh exact worktree topology"),
340				condition(ConditionCheckoutLinked, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "checkout kind is unavailable", "select a registered linked checkout"),
341				condition(ConditionCheckoutUnlocked, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "worktree flags are unavailable", "refresh exact worktree topology"),
342				condition(ConditionCheckoutBranch, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "branch identity is unavailable", "select a named non-detached checkout"),
343				condition(ConditionBranchRef, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "local branch ref is unavailable", "restore the exact local branch"),
344				condition(ConditionGitStatus, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "Git status is unavailable", "restore the exact checkout"),
345				condition(ConditionGitOperation, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "Git operation state is unavailable", "restore the exact checkout"),
346				condition(ConditionCheckoutClean, VerdictUnknown, RequirementAdvisory, "checkout bytes were not inspected", "refresh the exact checkout"),
347				condition(ConditionHarnessOwnership, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "harness ownership is unavailable", "refresh the exact checkout path"),
348			}
349		}
350	
351		exactVerdict := VerdictMet
352		exactEvidence := "selected path, repository, Git common directory, registry HEAD, and live HEAD are exact"
353		switch {
354		case observed.worktreesErr != nil:
355			exactVerdict, exactEvidence = VerdictError, observed.worktreesErr.Error()
356		case observed.worktree.Path != observed.checkout:
357			exactVerdict, exactEvidence = VerdictBlocked, "registered path differs from selected checkout"
358		case observed.worktree.RepositoryPath != observed.repoPath || observed.worktree.GitCommonDir != observed.gitCommonDir:
359			exactVerdict, exactEvidence = VerdictBlocked, "registered repository identity differs from selected repository"
360		case observed.headErr != nil:
361			exactVerdict, exactEvidence = VerdictError, observed.headErr.Error()
362		case observed.worktree.Worktree.Head != observed.head:
363			exactVerdict, exactEvidence = VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("registry HEAD %q differs from live HEAD %q", observed.worktree.Worktree.Head, observed.head)
364		case observed.locator.HeadOID != observed.head:
365			exactVerdict, exactEvidence = VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("selected HEAD %q differs from live HEAD %q", observed.locator.HeadOID, observed.head)
366		}
367	
368		kindVerdict := VerdictMet
369		kindEvidence := "registered non-main, non-bare linked worktree"
370		if !observed.worktree.IsLinkedWorktree() {
371			kindVerdict = VerdictBlocked
372			kindEvidence = fmt.Sprintf("main=%t bare=%t; canonical and bare records are never adoptable", observed.worktree.Worktree.Main, observed.worktree.Worktree.Bare)
373		}
374	
375		flagVerdict := VerdictMet
376		flagEvidence := "worktree is unlocked and non-prunable"
377		if observed.worktree.Worktree.Locked || observed.worktree.Worktree.Prunable {
378			flagVerdict = VerdictBlocked
379			flagEvidence = fmt.Sprintf("locked=%t prunable=%t", observed.worktree.Worktree.Locked, observed.worktree.Worktree.Prunable)
380		}
381	
382		branchVerdict := VerdictMet
383		branchEvidence := "registry and status identify named branch " + observed.locator.Branch
384		switch {
385		case observed.worktree.Worktree.Detached || observed.worktree.Worktree.Branch == "":
386			branchVerdict, branchEvidence = VerdictBlocked, "registered worktree is detached or unnamed"
387		case observed.statusErr != nil:
388			branchVerdict, branchEvidence = VerdictError, observed.statusErr.Error()
389		case observed.status.Detached || observed.status.Branch != observed.locator.Branch || observed.worktree.Worktree.Branch != observed.locator.Branch:
390			branchVerdict, branchEvidence = VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("registry=%q status=%q selected=%q", observed.worktree.Worktree.Branch, observed.status.Branch, observed.locator.Branch)
391		}
392	
393		branchRefVerdict := VerdictMet
394		branchRefEvidence := fmt.Sprintf("local %s is exactly selected HEAD %s", observed.branchRef, observed.locator.HeadOID)
395		switch {
396		case !observed.branchExists:
397			branchRefVerdict, branchRefEvidence = VerdictBlocked, "exact local branch ref does not exist"
398		case observed.branchOIDErr != nil:
399			branchRefVerdict, branchRefEvidence = VerdictError, observed.branchOIDErr.Error()
400		case observed.branchOID != observed.locator.HeadOID || observed.branchOID != observed.head:
401			branchRefVerdict, branchRefEvidence = VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("branch OID=%q selected HEAD=%q live HEAD=%q", observed.branchOID, observed.locator.HeadOID, observed.head)
402		}
403	
404		statusVerdict := VerdictMet
405		statusEvidence := observed.status.Summary()
406		if observed.statusErr != nil {
407			statusVerdict, statusEvidence = VerdictError, observed.statusErr.Error()
408		}
409		operationVerdict := VerdictMet
410		operationEvidence := "no Git operation is in progress"
411		if observed.operationErr != nil {
412			operationVerdict, operationEvidence = VerdictError, observed.operationErr.Error()
413		} else if observed.inProgress {
414			operationVerdict, operationEvidence = VerdictBlocked, "Git operation "+observed.operation+" is in progress"
415		}
416		cleanVerdict := VerdictMet
417		cleanEvidence := "checkout is clean; adoption writes metadata only"
418		if observed.statusErr != nil {
419			cleanVerdict, cleanEvidence = VerdictUnknown, "checkout cleanliness is unavailable; required Git status already blocks adoption"
420		} else if observed.status.Dirty() {
421			cleanEvidence = observed.status.Breakdown() + "; dirty bytes are allowed and remain untouched"
422		}
423	
424		harnessVerdict := VerdictMet
425		harnessEvidence := "no strict harness path evidence"
426		if observed.isHarness {
427			harnessVerdict = VerdictBlocked
428			harnessEvidence = "checkout is strictly under harness root " + observed.harness.Root
429		}
430		return []Condition{
431			condition(ConditionCheckoutPresent, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired, "registered checkout "+observed.checkout, ""),
432			condition(ConditionCheckoutExact, exactVerdict, RequirementRequired, exactEvidence, "refresh the exact checkout locator"),
433			condition(ConditionCheckoutLinked, kindVerdict, RequirementRequired, kindEvidence, "select a non-main linked checkout"),
434			condition(ConditionCheckoutUnlocked, flagVerdict, RequirementRequired, flagEvidence, "unlock or repair the registration; pruning is never implicit"),
435			condition(ConditionCheckoutBranch, branchVerdict, RequirementRequired, branchEvidence, "restore the exact named non-detached checkout"),
436			condition(ConditionBranchRef, branchRefVerdict, RequirementRequired, branchRefEvidence, "restore the exact local branch ref at selected HEAD"),
437			condition(ConditionGitStatus, statusVerdict, RequirementRequired, statusEvidence, "repair Git status observation"),
438			condition(ConditionGitOperation, operationVerdict, RequirementRequired, operationEvidence, "finish or abort the Git operation"),
439			condition(ConditionCheckoutClean, cleanVerdict, RequirementAdvisory, cleanEvidence, "commit later if desired; adoption never changes checkout bytes"),
440			condition(ConditionHarnessOwnership, harnessVerdict, RequirementRequired, harnessEvidence, "let the harness own its checkout"),
441		}
442	}
443	
444	func adoptBaseCondition(observed adoptObservation) Condition {
445		switch {
446		case observed.base == "":
447			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
448				"no explicit base was supplied and the repository default is unavailable", "supply an existing base ref")
449		case !observed.baseExists:
450			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
451				"base ref "+observed.base+" does not exist", "restore or select an existing base ref")
452		case observed.baseOIDErr != nil:
453			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
454				observed.baseOIDErr.Error(), "repair exact base-ref observation")
455		case observed.baseOID == "":
456			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
457				"base resolved to no commit", "restore the named base ref")
458		default:
459			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
460				fmt.Sprintf("base %s is exactly %s", observed.base, observed.baseOID), "")
461		}
462	}
463	
464	func adoptTaskInventoryConditions(observed destructiveObservation) []Condition {
465		inventoryCondition := condition(ConditionTaskInventory, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
466			"task inventory is complete, including a successful empty inventory", "")
467		switch {
468		case observed.taskInventoryErr != nil:
469			inventoryCondition = condition(ConditionTaskInventory, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
470				observed.taskInventoryErr.Error(), "repair task-store inventory before proving unmanaged ownership")
471		case len(observed.taskIncomplete) > 0:
472			inventoryCondition = condition(ConditionTaskInventory, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
473				strings.Join(observed.taskIncomplete, "; "), "repair every corrupt or unresolvable task record")
474		}
475		claimsCondition := condition(ConditionTaskClaims, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
476			"no task claims the exact checkout path, repository branch, or derived task ID", "")
477		if len(observed.taskClaims) > 0 {
478			claims := make([]string, len(observed.taskClaims))
479			for index, claim := range observed.taskClaims {
480				claims[index] = claim.ID + " (" + claim.Reason + ")"
481			}
482			claimsCondition = condition(ConditionTaskClaims, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
483				"claimed by "+strings.Join(claims, ", "), "use managed lifecycle or resolve every task claim")
484		}
485		return []Condition{inventoryCondition, claimsCondition}
486	}
487	
488	func adoptRuntimeConditions(observed adoptObservation) []Condition {
489		if observed.runtimeErr != nil {
490			return []Condition{
491				condition(ConditionRuntimeAvailable, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
492					observed.runtimeErr.Error(), "repair runtime backend resolution"),
493				condition(ConditionAgentOccupancy, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
494					observed.runtimeErr.Error(), "repair runtime session and recognized-agent observation"),
495			}
496		}
497		if observed.runtime == nil || observed.runtime.Name() == "none" {
498			return []Condition{
499				condition(ConditionRuntimeAvailable, VerdictMet, RequirementAdvisory,
500					"runtime none performs no session operation", ""),
501				condition(ConditionAgentOccupancy, VerdictUnknown, RequirementAdvisory,
502					"runtime none leaves session and recognized-agent occupancy unobserved; metadata-only adoption is retained as WARM", "inspect occupancy with a capable runtime if HOT metadata is required"),
503			}
504		}
505	
506		availableVerdict := VerdictMet
507		availableEvidence := "runtime backend " + observed.runtime.Name() + " is available for fresh strict inspection"
508		if !observed.runtimeAvailable {
509			availableVerdict = VerdictBlocked
510			availableEvidence = "runtime backend " + observed.runtime.Name() + " is unavailable"
511		}
512		occupancyVerdict := VerdictUnknown
513		occupancyEvidence := "exact checkout was unavailable for strict occupancy inspection"
514		if observed.worktreeFound {
515			occupancyErr := adoptStrictOccupancyError(observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr)
516			if occupancyErr == nil {
517				occupancyVerdict = VerdictMet
518				occupancyEvidence = "no recognized agent other than the exact caller occupies the checkout"
519				if !observed.occupancy.AgentActivityList.Observed() {
520					occupancyEvidence += "; recognized-agent absence was not strong enough to derive HOT"
521				}
522			} else {
523				occupancyVerdict = VerdictBlocked
524				occupancyEvidence = occupancyErr.Error()
525				if observed.occupancyErr != nil || observed.occupancy.CurrentPane.Err != nil ||
526					observed.occupancy.SessionCoverageErr != nil || observed.occupancy.SessionList.Err != nil ||
527					observed.occupancy.AgentActivityList.Err != nil {
528					occupancyVerdict = VerdictError
529				}
530			}
531		}
532		return []Condition{
533			condition(ConditionRuntimeAvailable, availableVerdict, RequirementRequired,
534				availableEvidence, "select or restore an available runtime backend"),
535			condition(ConditionAgentOccupancy, occupancyVerdict, RequirementRequired,
536				occupancyEvidence, "stop every other recognized agent or use another checkout"),
537		}
538	}
539	
540	func adoptStateCondition(options AdoptOptions, observed adoptObservation) Condition {
541		evidence := fmt.Sprintf("derived %s: %s", strings.ToUpper(string(observed.derivedState)), observed.stateEvidence)
542		if options.State != "" && options.State != observed.derivedState {
543			return condition(ConditionAdoptState, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
544				fmt.Sprintf("requested compatibility state %s does not equal %s", options.State, evidence),
545				"omit the requested state or pass the freshly derived state")
546		}
547		if options.State != "" {
548			evidence = fmt.Sprintf("requested compatibility state %s equals %s", options.State, evidence)
549		}
550		return condition(ConditionAdoptState, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired, evidence, "")
551	}
552	
553	func (s *lifecycleService) applyAdopt(ctx context.Context, approved Plan) (Result, error) {
554		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
555			return Result{}, err
556		}
557		if approved.Action != Adopt {
558			return Result{}, &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: approved.PlanID, Reason: "adopt handler received " + string(approved.Action)}
559		}
560		if err := validateAdoptLocator(approved.Locator); err != nil {
561			return Result{}, err
562		}
563		commonDir, err := s.canonicalPath(approved.Locator.GitCommonDir)
564		if err != nil {
565			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize approved repository lock identity: %v", ErrInvalidPlan, err)
566		}
567	
568		var result Result
569		err = s.repoLock(ctx, commonDir, func() error {
570			return s.tasks.WithLock(ctx, func(tx *task.Tx) error {
571				spec, observed, observeErr := s.observeAdopt(ctx, approved.Request, tx.ListRecords)
572				if observeErr != nil {
573					return observeErr
574				}
575				fresh, buildErr := BuildPlan(approved.Request, spec)
576				if buildErr != nil {
577					return buildErr
578				}
579				if fresh.PlanID != approved.PlanID || fresh.AuthorityFingerprint != approved.AuthorityFingerprint {
580					return &StalePlanError{
581						ExpectedPlanID: approved.PlanID, ActualPlanID: fresh.PlanID,
582						ExpectedAuthorityFingerprint: approved.AuthorityFingerprint,
583						ActualAuthorityFingerprint:   fresh.AuthorityFingerprint,
584						Reason:                       "fresh unmanaged Git, worktree, task, base, runtime, agent, or harness authority differs",
585					}
586				}
587				if fresh.Availability != AvailabilityReady {
588					notReady := &PlanNotReadyError{PlanID: fresh.PlanID, Availability: fresh.Availability, conditions: fresh.Conditions()}
589					return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: fresh.PlanID, Reason: "fresh adoption conditions are not ready", Cause: notReady}
590				}
591				execution := &executionState{service: s, plan: fresh, tx: tx}
592				result, observeErr = execution.executeAdopt(observed)
593				return observeErr
594			})
595		})
596		return result, err
597	}
598	
599	func (e *executionState) executeAdopt(observed adoptObservation) (Result, error) {
600		effects := e.plan.Effects()
601		if len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].Code != EffectCreateTask {
602			return e.fail(&InvalidPlanError{PlanID: e.plan.PlanID, Reason: "Adopt must contain exactly one create-task effect"})
603		}
604		if observed.runtime != nil && observed.runtime.Name() == "none" {
605			e.warnings = append(e.warnings, "runtime none left occupancy unobserved; the adopted task is WARM")
606		}
607	
608		effect := effects[0]
609		expected := observed.candidate
610		expected.Tags = append([]string(nil), observed.candidate.Tags...)
611		err := e.run(effect, func() (string, error) {
612			candidate := expected
613			candidate.Tags = append([]string(nil), expected.Tags...)
614			created, createErr := e.service.taskCreate(e.tx, &candidate)
615			if createErr != nil {
616				return "task create made no authorized non-task change", fmt.Errorf("create adopted task %s: %w", expected.ID, createErr)
617			}
618			if created == nil || created.Revision == "" {
619				return "task create returned no revision", errors.New("create adopted task returned no revision")
620			}
621			if adoptTaskAuthority(created.Task) != adoptTaskAuthority(expected) {
622				return "task create returned different metadata", errors.New("created task does not match the approved adoption metadata")
623			}
624			persisted, verifyErr := e.tx.GetRecord(expected.ID)
625			if verifyErr != nil {
626				return "task create was not verified", fmt.Errorf("verify created adopted task %s: %w", expected.ID, verifyErr)
627			}
628			if persisted.Revision != created.Revision || adoptTaskAuthority(persisted.Task) != adoptTaskAuthority(expected) {
629				return "task create revision or metadata was not verified", errors.New("persisted adopted task differs from the task create result")
630			}
631			e.snapshot = "task:" + persisted.Revision
632			e.milestone = MilestoneAdopted
633			return "created task " + persisted.Task.ID + " at revision " + persisted.Revision, nil
634		})
635		if err != nil {
636			return e.fail(err, "the checkout, branch, runtime, and Git bytes were not changed; repair the task-store failure and refresh adoption")
637		}
638		if e.milestone != MilestoneAdopted || e.snapshot == "" {
639			return e.fail(&InvalidPlanError{PlanID: e.plan.PlanID, Reason: "adoption ended without a created task revision"})
640		}
641		return e.result(), nil
642	}
643
```

```text
1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"strings"
16	
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
18	)
19	
20	// Pane is one terminal surface inside a runtime session.
21	type Pane struct {
22		ID           string
23		CWD          string
24		ShellCWD     string
25		Agent        string
26		AgentStatus  string
27		AgentSession string
28	}
29	
30	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
31	type Session struct {
32		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
33		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
34		Handle string
35		Label  string
36		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
37		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
38		// value.
39		Dirs []string
40		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
41		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
42		AgentStatus string
43		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
44		AgentSessions []string
45		// Panes retain the exact runtime IDs and cwd values used for caller and
46		// mixed-workspace retirement checks.
47		Panes   []Pane
48		Focused bool
49	}
50	
51	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
52	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
53		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
54			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
55			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
56			// $HOME active.
57			if inside, err := pathx.Contains(dir, d); err == nil && inside {
58				return true
59			}
60		}
61		return false
62	}
63	
64	// OpenResult is the transient result of making a checkout live. Handle may be
65	// persisted by callers, but the pane belongs to this one creation response and
66	// must never be treated as durable state.
67	type OpenResult struct {
68		Handle     string
69		Surface    string
70		Opened     bool
71		Created    bool
72		RootPaneID string
73	}
74	
75	// AgentActivity is one recognized live coding agent occupying a runtime pane.
76	// Every activity returned by a backend is occupied regardless of Status; idle,
77	// done and unknown describe lifecycle state, not permission to share a checkout.
78	type AgentActivity struct {
79		PaneID      string
80		WorkspaceID string
81		Agent       string
82		Name        string
83		Status      string
84		CWD         string
85	}
86	
87	// AgentActivityLister is an optional runtime capability. Core runtimes need not
88	// know about agents; Herdr implements it because its pane model can identify the
89	// exact process and checkout involved.
90	type AgentActivityLister interface {
91		AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error)
92	}
93	
94	// CurrentPaneResolver is an optional runtime capability for resolving the live
95	// pane behind inherited caller context. Herdr pane IDs can change after a move,
96	// so collision exclusions must not trust HERDR_PANE_ID alone.
97	type CurrentPaneResolver interface {
98		CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
99	}
100	
101	// Activator is the optional interactive half of opening a runtime surface.
102	// Open deliberately remains detached so creation commands can run in the
103	// background. Navigation commands call Activate after their own terminal UI
104	// has been torn down: inside a multiplexer this switches the current client;
105	// outside it attaches a new client and blocks until the user detaches.
106	type Activator interface {
107		Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
108	}
109	
110	// PaneRunner is the optional exact-pane command surface. The command is shell
111	// text for the pane's existing interactive shell, not argv for a child process
112	// started by dev. Implementations must not include command text in errors.
113	type PaneRunner interface {
114		RunInPane(ctx context.Context, paneID, command string) error
115	}
116	
117	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
118	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
119	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
120	type Runtime interface {
121		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
122		Name() string
123		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
124		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
125		Available() bool
126		// Open makes dir live. Its result distinguishes a newly created surface from
127		// a reused one and may carry a root pane proven by that same create response.
128		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
129		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
130		// task entry.
```

```text
244		}
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"

12		"sort"

18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory; CommonDir is shared
38		// by every linked worktree of the clone.
39		GitDir    string
40		CommonDir string
41		MainRoot  string
42		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
43		Bare bool
44		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
45		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
46		// initialise them.
47		HasGit bool
48	}
49	
50	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
51	func (r Repo) Display() string {
52		if r.Category == "" {
53			return r.Name
54		}
55		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
56	}
57	
58	// Options tunes discovery.
59	type Options struct {
60		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
61		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
62		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
63		MaxDepth int
64		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
65		IncludeNonRepos bool
66		// Fast avoids per-repository git subprocesses. It is intended for shell
67		// completion: direct .git-file checkouts are skipped as linked worktrees and
68		// symlink aliases are deduplicated by their physical path.
69		Fast bool
70	}
71	
72	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
73	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
74	
75	// CompletionOptions trades full Git metadata for interactive latency.
76	func CompletionOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3, Fast: true} }
77	
78	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
79	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
80	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
81		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
82		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
83		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
84		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
85	}
86	
87	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
88	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
89	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
90	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
91		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
92			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
93		}
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
96		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
97		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
98		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
99		identities := map[string]bool{}
100		var out []Repo
101	
102		for _, root := range roots {
103			info, err := os.Stat(root)
104			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
105				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
106			}
107			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
108	
109			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
110				if err != nil {
111					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
112				}
113				if ctx.Err() != nil {
114					return ctx.Err()
115				}
116				isRoot := path == rootClean
117				name := d.Name()
118				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
119				isDir := d.IsDir()
120				if isLink {
121					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
122					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
123					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
124					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
125						isDir = info.IsDir()
126					}
127				}
128				if !isDir {
129					return nil
130				}
131				if !isRoot && (skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare")) {
132					return filepath.SkipDir
133				}
134	
135				rel := "."
136				depth := 0
137				if !isRoot {
138					rel, _ = filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
139					depth = len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
140				}
141	
142				if isRepoDir(path) {
143					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
144					if real == "" {
145						real = path
146					}
147					bare := isBareDir(path)
148					identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot := real, real, real, real
149					if !bare && opts.Fast && gitEntryIsFile(path) {
150						// A direct .git file at a discovered root is a linked
151						// worktree. Submodules are already hidden below their parent
152						// repository because discovery never descends into one.
153						return filepath.SkipDir
154					}
155					if !bare && !opts.Fast {
156						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
157							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
158							// project in the repo inventory.
159							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
160								return filepath.SkipDir
161							}
162							identity, gitDir, commonDir, mainRoot = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitDir, g.GitCommonDir, g.MainRoot
163							real = g.MainRoot
164						}
165					}
166					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
167						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
168						out = append(out, Repo{
169							Name:      name,
170							Path:      path,
171							RealPath:  real,
172							Symlink:   isLink,
173							Root:      rootClean,
174							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
175							GitDir:    gitDir,
176							CommonDir: commonDir,
177							MainRoot:  mainRoot,
178							Bare:      bare,
179							HasGit:    true,
180						})
181					}
182					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
183					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
184					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
185					return filepath.SkipDir
186				}
187				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
188					return filepath.SkipDir
189				}
190				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
191					if !seen[path] {
192						seen[path] = true
193						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
194					}
195				}
196				return nil
197			})
198			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
199				return out, ctx.Err()
200			}
201		}
202	
203		for i := range out {
204			if out[i].Category == "." {
205				out[i].Category = ""
206			}
207		}
208		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
209			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
210				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
211			}
212			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
213		})
214		return out, nil
215	}
216	
217	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
218	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
219	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
220		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
221			return true
222		}
223		return isBareDir(path)
224	}
225	
226	func gitEntryIsFile(path string) bool {
227		info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git"))
228		return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
229	}
230	
231	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
232	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
233		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
234			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
235				return false
236			}
237		}
238		return true
239	}
240	
241	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
242	//
243	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
244	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
245	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
246	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
247		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
248	}
249	
250	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
251	// process per repository in the scan roots.
252	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
253		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
254	}
255	
256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err
260		}
261		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
262			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {
265					real = g.MainRoot
266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:
294			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
295		}
296	}
297	
298	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
299	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
300	
301	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
302	
303	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
304	type AmbiguousError struct {
305		Ref        string
306		Candidates []Repo
307	}
308	
309	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
310		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
311		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
312			names[i] = c.Display()
313		}
314		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
315	}
```

```text
3	import (

9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory. A linked worktree has
16		// its own entry below the shared common directory.
17		GitDir string
18		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
19		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
20		GitCommonDir string
21		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
22		Name string
23		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
24		// the main checkout.
25		IsLinkedWorktree bool
26		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
27		MainRoot string
28		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
29		Bare bool
30	}
31	
32	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
33	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
34	
35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}
66	
67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {
70			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
72			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
73			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
74			r.MainRoot = r.Root
75		} else {
76			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
77		}
78		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
79		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
80		if r.Bare {
81			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
82			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
83			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
84				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
85			}
86		}
87		return r, nil
88	}
89	
90	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
91	// a full Discover.
92	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
93		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
94		return err == nil
95	}
96	
97	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
98	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
99	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
100	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
101	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
102		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
103			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
104				return b
105			}
106		}
107		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
108			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
109				return cand
110			}
111		}
112		return ""
113	}
114	
115	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
116	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
117		if name == "" {
118			name = "origin"
119		}
120		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
121		if err != nil {
122			return ""
123		}
124		return out
125	}
126	
127	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
128	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
129	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
130	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
131	// semantics should use Remote instead.
132	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
133		if commonDir == "" {
134			return ""
135		}
136		if name == "" {
137			name = "origin"
138		}
139		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
140		if err != nil {
141			return ""
142		}
143		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
144		section := ""
145		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
146			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
147			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
148				continue
149			}
150			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
151				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
152				continue
153			}
154			if section != want {
155				continue
156			}
157			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
158			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
159				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
160			}
161		}
162		return ""
163	}
```

```text
94		f.BoolVarP(&yes, "yes", "y", false, "confirm the selected finish plan (required for non-interactive discard)")
95		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "dirty", fixedCompletions("auto", "fail", "commit", "discard"))
96		// Both remain accepted so existing scripts fail loudly with a pointer to
97		// dev retire rather than silently skipping cleanup they still expect.
98		f.BoolVar(&keepWorktree, "keep-worktree", false, "deprecated: worktrees are always kept until dev retire")
99		f.BoolVar(&deleteBranch, "delete-branch", false, "deprecated here: use dev retire --delete-branch")
```

```text
225	func (m Model) acceptRepositoryList(message repositoryListMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
226		if message.generation != m.listRequest.generation ||
227			message.repoKey != pickerRequestKey || m.listRequest.repoKey != pickerRequestKey {
228			return m, nil
229		}
230		if m.listRequest.cancel != nil {

232		}

234		m.listRequest.loading = false
235		m.listRequest.err = message.err

237		selectedKey := ""
238		if selected, ok := m.currentRepository(); ok {
239			selectedKey = selected.RepoKey
240		}
241		oldIndex := m.repoCursor
242		if message.err != nil {
243			m.listRequest.stale = len(m.repositories) > 0
244			m.status = ""
245			return m, nil
246		}
247	
248		m.repositories = append([]RepositoryRow(nil), message.rows...)
249		m.listRequest.stale = false
250		m.status = ""
251		m.repoCursor = nearestRepositoryIndex(m.filteredRepositories(), selectedKey, oldIndex)
252		return m, nil

255	func nearestRepositoryIndex(rows []RepositoryRow, repoKey string, oldIndex int) int {
256		if repoKey != "" {
257			for index, row := range rows {
258				if row.RepoKey == repoKey {
259					return index
260				}
261			}
262		}
263		if len(rows) == 0 {
264			return 0
265		}
266		if oldIndex < 0 {
267			return 0
268		}
269		if oldIndex >= len(rows) {
270			return len(rows) - 1
271		}
272		return oldIndex
273	}
```

```text
15	// PlanSpec is action-handler construction input. Authority holds additional
16	// exact identities such as status, runtime, artifact, or remote fingerprints.
17	// BuildPlan copies every map and slice.
18	type PlanSpec struct {
19		Authority         map[string]string
20		Conditions        []Condition
21		Effects           []Effect
22		RetainedResources []string
23		Confirmation      Confirmation
24		FallbackCommand   string
25		Summary           string
26		DisplayedAt       time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Plan is an immutable-by-interface proposal bound to one request and one
30	// authority fingerprint. Collection accessors always return copies.
31	type Plan struct {
32		PlanID                 string
33		AuthorityFingerprint   string
34		Request                Request
35		Locator                Locator
36		Action                 Action
37		Source                 task.State
38		Target                 task.State
39		HasPersistedTransition bool
40		StatePreserving        bool
41		RemovesTask            bool
42		Availability           Availability
43		Confirmation           Confirmation
44		ExpectedMilestone      Milestone
45		FallbackCommand        string
46		Summary                string
47		DisplayedAt            time.Time
48	
49		authority  Fields
50		conditions []Condition
51		effects    []Effect
52		retained   StringList
53	}
54	
55	// BuildPlan validates graph legality, derives availability, and seals a plan's
56	// deterministic authority fingerprint and PlanID.
57	func BuildPlan(request Request, spec PlanSpec) (Plan, error) {
58		normalized, err := normalizeRequest(request)
59		if err != nil {
60			return Plan{}, &InvalidPlanError{Reason: "invalid request", Cause: err}
61		}
62		if err := spec.Confirmation.Validate(); err != nil {
63			return Plan{}, &InvalidPlanError{Reason: "invalid confirmation", Cause: err}
64		}
65		conditions := append([]Condition(nil), spec.Conditions...)
66		if err := validateConditions(conditions); err != nil {
67			return Plan{}, &InvalidPlanError{Reason: "invalid conditions", Cause: err}
68		}
69		effects := cloneEffects(spec.Effects)
70		if err := validateEffects(effects); err != nil {
71			return Plan{}, &InvalidPlanError{Reason: "invalid effects", Cause: err}
72		}
73		authority := NewFields(spec.Authority)
74		if err := validateAuthority(authority); err != nil {
75			return Plan{}, &InvalidPlanError{Reason: "invalid authority", Cause: err}
76		}
77	
78		plan := Plan{
79			Request: normalized.Clone(), Locator: normalized.Locator, Action: normalized.Action,
80			Source:       normalized.Locator.State,
81			Availability: AvailabilityFor(conditions), Confirmation: spec.Confirmation,
82			FallbackCommand: spec.FallbackCommand, Summary: spec.Summary, DisplayedAt: spec.DisplayedAt,
83			authority: authority, conditions: conditions, effects: effects,
84			retained: NewStringList(spec.RetainedResources...),
85		}
86		if isTransitionAction(plan.Action) {
87			rule, transitionErr := RequireTransition(plan.Locator.Mode, plan.Locator.State, plan.Action)
88			if transitionErr != nil {
89				return Plan{}, &InvalidPlanError{Reason: "invalid transition", Cause: transitionErr}
90			}
91			plan.HasPersistedTransition = true
92			plan.Target = rule.Target
93			plan.StatePreserving = rule.StatePreserving
94			plan.RemovesTask = rule.RemovesTask
95			plan.ExpectedMilestone = rule.Milestone
96		} else {
97			switch plan.Action {
98			case Adopt:
99				plan.ExpectedMilestone = MilestoneAdopted
100			case Reconcile:
101				plan.ExpectedMilestone = MilestoneReconciled
102			}
103		}
104		plan.AuthorityFingerprint, plan.PlanID = computePlanIdentity(plan)
105		return plan.Clone(), nil
106	}
107	
108	// Clone returns a plan with independent request, map, and slice storage.
109	func (p Plan) Clone() Plan {
110		p.Request = p.Request.Clone()
111		p.authority = p.authority.clone()
112		p.conditions = append([]Condition(nil), p.conditions...)
113		p.effects = cloneEffects(p.effects)
114		p.retained = p.retained.clone()
115		return p
116	}
117	
118	// AuthorityFields returns a mutable copy of the extra authority identities.
119	func (p Plan) AuthorityFields() map[string]string { return p.authority.Map() }
120	
121	// Conditions returns the ordered conditions as a mutable copy.
122	func (p Plan) Conditions() []Condition { return append([]Condition(nil), p.conditions...) }
123	
124	// Effects returns independent copies of the ordered effects.
125	func (p Plan) Effects() []Effect { return cloneEffects(p.effects) }
126	
127	// RetainedResources returns the resources intentionally left after Apply.
128	func (p Plan) RetainedResources() []string { return p.retained.Values() }
129	
130	// InputConditions returns required operator input without conflating it with a
131	// safety override.
132	func (p Plan) InputConditions() []Condition {
133		return filterConditions(p.conditions, func(condition Condition) bool {
134			return condition.Requirement == RequirementRequired && condition.Verdict == VerdictNeedsInput
135		})
136	}
137	
138	// BlockingConditions returns every required, non-input condition that prevents
139	// READY. Advisory conditions are intentionally absent.
140	func (p Plan) BlockingConditions() []Condition {
141		return filterConditions(p.conditions, func(condition Condition) bool {
142			return condition.Requirement == RequirementRequired &&
143				condition.Verdict != VerdictMet && condition.Verdict != VerdictNeedsInput
144		})
145	}
146	
147	// AdvisoryConditions returns non-authorizing evidence for display.
148	func (p Plan) AdvisoryConditions() []Condition {
149		return filterConditions(p.conditions, func(condition Condition) bool {
150			return condition.Requirement == RequirementAdvisory
151		})
152	}
153	
154	// Validate proves that a plan is structurally consistent and still carries its
155	// original deterministic identity. It performs no live observations.
156	func (p Plan) Validate() error {
157		if p.PlanID == "" || p.AuthorityFingerprint == "" {
158			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "plan identity is missing"}
159		}
160		if !p.Action.Valid() {
161			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("unknown action %q", p.Action)}
162		}
163		if p.Request.Action != p.Action {
164			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "request action and plan action differ"}
165		}
166		if p.Request.Locator != p.Locator {
167			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "request locator and plan locator differ"}
168		}
169		if p.Request.Options == nil {
170			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "normalized request options are missing"}
171		}
172		normalized, err := normalizeRequest(p.Request)
173		if err != nil {
174			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "request is no longer valid", Cause: err}
175		}
176		if requestIdentity(normalized) != requestIdentity(p.Request) {
177			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "request options are not normalized"}
178		}
179		if err := p.Confirmation.Validate(); err != nil {
180			return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: p.PlanID, Reason: "invalid confirmation", Cause: err}
```

```text
188				}
189			}
190		}
191	
192		view = doneView(plan)
193		if mode != task.ModeDirect && selection.Integration == doneIntegrationNone {
194			if view.contained() && !(view.Status.Dirty() && selection.Dirty == flow.DirtyCommit) {
195				selection.Integration = doneIntegrationFF
196				prompted = true
197			} else {
198				choice, promptErr := p.choice("Integration (f=fast-forward, p=PR, q=cancel)", "ff",
199					"fast-forward (f), pull request (p), cancel (q)", map[string]string{
200						"f": "ff", "ff": "ff", "fast-forward": "ff",
201						"p": "pr", "pr": "pr", "pull-request": "pr",
202						"q": "cancel", "cancel": "cancel",
203					})
204				if canceledDone(app, promptErr, choice == "cancel") {
205					return nil
206				}
207				if promptErr != nil {
208					return promptErr
209				}
210				selection.Integration = doneIntegration(choice)
211				prompted = true
212				plan, err = replanDone(ctx, session, plan, doneActionOptions(selected, selection, opts))
213				if err != nil {
214					return err
215				}
216				if err := doneFatalPreflightError(selected, plan); err != nil {
217					return err
218				}
219			}
220		}
221	
222		if err := donePlanReadinessError(selected, plan, selection); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225	
226		approval := flow.Approve(plan.PlanID)
227		if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped && opts.Yes {
228			approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, plan.Confirmation.Token)
229		}
230		if prompted && !opts.Yes {
231			confirmed, token, promptErr := confirmDonePlan(app, p, selected, plan)
232			if canceledDone(app, promptErr, !confirmed) {
233				return nil
234			}
235			if promptErr != nil {
236				return promptErr
237			}
238			if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped {
239				approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, token)
240			}
241		}
242		if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped && approval.Token == "" {
243			return errors.New("destructive finish plan requires its typed confirmation")
244		}
245	
246		if opts.ConfirmSquash != "" {
247			app.warnf("accepting operator attestation that squash commit %s represents branch %s",
248				opts.ConfirmSquash, selected.Branch)
249		}
250		result, applyErr := session.apply(ctx, plan, approval)
251		renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
252		if applyErr != nil {
253			return presentDoneApplyError(result, applyErr)
254		}
255		final, err := session.finalTask(app)
256		if err != nil {
257			return err
258		}
259		return renderDoneSuccess(app, selected, final, plan, result, doneView(initial))
260	}
261	
262	func doneActionOptions(selected task.Task, selection doneSelection, opts doneOptions) flow.ActionOptions {
263		if selected.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeDirect {
264			return flow.CompleteDirectOptions{
265				Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message, Push: opts.Push,
266			}
267		}
268		switch selection.Integration {
269		case doneIntegrationPR:
270			return flow.ReviewHandoffOptions{Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message}
271		case doneIntegrationMerged:
272			return flow.VerifyMergedOptions{
273				Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message,
274				BaseRef: opts.BaseRef, SquashCommit: opts.ConfirmSquash, PushBase: opts.Push,
275			}
276		default:
277			return flow.CompleteFFOptions{
278				Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message, PushBase: opts.Push,
279			}
280		}
281	}
282	
283	func replanDone(
284		ctx context.Context,
285		session lifecycleSession,
286		previous flow.Plan,
287		options flow.ActionOptions,
288	) (flow.Plan, error) {
289		fresh, err := session.plan(ctx, options)
290		if err != nil {
291			if errors.Is(err, flow.ErrStalePlan) {
292				return flow.Plan{}, presentDoneApplyError(flow.Result{}, err)
293			}
294			return flow.Plan{}, err
295		}
296		if changed := changedDoneAuthority(previous, fresh); changed != "" {
297			stale := &flow.StalePlanError{
298				ExpectedPlanID: previous.PlanID,
299				ActualPlanID:   fresh.PlanID,
300				Reason:         changed + " changed while the finish plan was open",
301			}
302			return flow.Plan{}, presentDoneApplyError(flow.Result{}, stale)
303		}
304		return fresh, nil
305	}
306	
307	func changedDoneAuthority(previous, fresh flow.Plan) string {
308		before := previous.AuthorityFields()
309		after := fresh.AuthorityFields()
310		for _, key := range []string{
311			"task.revision", "task.mode", "task.state", "task.repo-path", "task.branch", "task.base", "task.worktree-path",
312			"repo.git-common-dir", "worktree.fingerprint",
313			"git.status-error", "git.branch", "git.detached", "git.upstream", "git.ahead", "git.behind",
314			"git.changed", "git.staged", "git.unstaged", "git.untracked", "git.conflicted", "git.head",
315			"git.base-oid", "git.upstream-oid", "git.operation", "git.operation-active", "git.operation-error",
316			"artifact.fingerprint", "finish.authority", "completion.base-ref", "completion.base-oid",
317			"completion.expected-branch", "completion.branch-oid", "runtime.backend", "runtime.available",
318			"runtime.occupancy-fingerprint", "runtime.occupancy-error",
319		} {
320			if before[key] != after[key] {
321				return key
322			}
323		}
324		return ""
325	}

327	func canceledDone(app *App, err error, canceled bool) bool {
328		if errors.Is(err, errPromptCanceled) || canceled {
329			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Canceled; nothing was changed.")
330			return true
331		}
332		return false
333	}
334	
335	func doneFatalPreflightError(selected task.Task, plan flow.Plan) error {
336		view := doneView(plan)
337		if view.Status.Conflicted > 0 {
338			return fmt.Errorf("%s has %d conflicted path(s); resolve or abort the merge/rebase before finishing",
339				config.Contract(plan.Locator.CheckoutPath), view.Status.Conflicted)
340		}
341		if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionCheckoutPresent); ok && condition.Verdict != flow.VerdictMet {
342			return fmt.Errorf("%s no longer exists — resume the task first", config.Contract(plan.Locator.CheckoutPath))
343		}
344		if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionExplicitBase); ok &&
345			condition.Requirement == flow.RequirementRequired && condition.Verdict != flow.VerdictMet {
346			return fmt.Errorf("cannot determine the base branch for %s — pass --base when starting a task", selected.Repo)
347		}
348		if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionFinishAnalysis); ok && condition.Verdict == flow.VerdictError {
349			return errors.New(condition.Evidence)
350		}
351		if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionArtifactReady); ok &&
352			(condition.Verdict == flow.VerdictBlocked || condition.Verdict == flow.VerdictError) {
353			return fmt.Errorf("artifact readiness for %s is blocked: %s; finalize or discard the intent before integration",
354				config.Contract(plan.Locator.CheckoutPath), condition.Evidence)
355		}
356		return nil
357	}
358	
359	func donePlanReadinessError(selected task.Task, plan flow.Plan, selection doneSelection) error {
360		if plan.Availability == flow.AvailabilityReady {
361			return nil
362		}
363		if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionCheckoutClean); ok &&
364			condition.Requirement == flow.RequirementRequired && condition.Verdict != flow.VerdictMet {
365			switch selection.Dirty {
366			case flow.DirtyAuto, flow.DirtyFail:
367				return dirtyFinishError(selected, plan)
368			case flow.DirtyCommit:
369				if strings.TrimSpace(selection.Message) == "" {
370					return errors.New("--message is required with --dirty=commit outside an interactive terminal")
371				}
372			}
373		}
374		if plan.Action == flow.ReviewHandoff {
375			if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionBranchRelation); ok && condition.Verdict != flow.VerdictMet {
376				base := doneView(plan).Base
377				return fmt.Errorf("%s is already contained in %s; use --ff to finalize cleanup instead of opening a PR",
378					selected.Branch, base)
379			}
380		}
381		if plan.Action == flow.VerifyMerged {
382			if condition, ok := doneCondition(plan, flow.ConditionMergeProof); ok && condition.Verdict != flow.VerdictMet {
383				fields := plan.AuthorityFields()
384				return fmt.Errorf("cannot verify %s is contained in %s", fields["completion.proof-ref"], fields["completion.base-ref"])
385			}
386		}
387		blocking := append(plan.InputConditions(), plan.BlockingConditions()...)
388		parts := make([]string, 0, len(blocking))
389		for _, condition := range blocking {
390			message := string(condition.Code) + ": " + condition.Evidence
391			if condition.Remediation != "" {
392				message += " (" + condition.Remediation + ")"
393			}
394			parts = append(parts, message)
395		}
396		if len(parts) == 0 {
397			return fmt.Errorf("finish plan is %s: %w", plan.Availability, flow.ErrPlanNotReady)
398		}
399		return fmt.Errorf("%s is %s: %s: %w", plan.Summary, plan.Availability,
400			strings.Join(parts, "; "), flow.ErrPlanNotReady)
401	}
402	
403	func dirtyFinishError(t task.Task, plan flow.Plan) error {
404		view := doneView(plan)
405		return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes: %s; branch relation to %s is behind %d, ahead %d; "+
406			"%d dirty path(s) match %s and %d contain unique content",
407			config.Contract(plan.Locator.CheckoutPath), view.Status.Breakdown(), view.Base,
408			view.BaseOnly, view.BranchOnly, view.Equivalent, view.Base, view.Unique)
409	}

411	func renderDonePreflight(app *App, t task.Task, plan flow.Plan) {
412		view := doneView(plan)

416		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s        %s\n", s.label("base"), view.Base)
417		switch {
418		case view.BaseOnly == 0 && view.BranchOnly == 0:
419			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s     %s\n", s.label("commits"), s.success(fmt.Sprintf("already equal to %s (behind 0, ahead 0)", view.Base)))
420		case view.contained():
421			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s     %s\n", s.label("commits"), s.success(fmt.Sprintf("already contained in %s (behind %d, ahead 0)", view.Base, view.BaseOnly)))
422		default:
423			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s     %s\n", s.label("commits"), s.warning(fmt.Sprintf("behind %d, ahead %d relative to %s",
424				view.BaseOnly, view.BranchOnly, view.Base)))
425		}
426		if !view.Status.Dirty() {
427			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s    %s\n", s.label("checkout"), s.success("clean"))
428			return
429		}
430		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s    %s\n", s.label("checkout"), s.warning(view.Status.Breakdown()))
431		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s    %s, %s\n", s.label("contents"),
432			s.success(fmt.Sprintf("%d match %s", view.Equivalent, view.Base)),
433			s.warning(fmt.Sprintf("%d unique", view.Unique)))
434		for _, change := range view.Changes {
435			marker := s.warning("unique")
436			if change.BaseEquivalent {
437				marker = s.success("matches " + view.Base)
438			}
439			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "    %s%s %s\n", marker,
440				strings.Repeat(" ", max(0, 12-width(marker))), change.Path)
441		}
442	}
```

```text
List pull requests in a GitHub repository. By default, this only lists open PRs.

The search query syntax is documented here:
<https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-issues-and-pull-requests>

On supported GitHub hosts, advanced issue search syntax can be used in the
`--search` query. For more information about advanced issue search, see:
<https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/filtering-and-searching-issues-and-pull-requests#building-advanced-filters-for-issues>

For more information about output formatting flags, see `gh help formatting`.

USAGE
  gh pr list [flags]

ALIASES
  gh pr ls

FLAGS
      --app string        Filter by GitHub App author
  -a, --assignee string   Filter by assignee
  -A, --author string     Filter by author (use --app to filter by a GitHub App)
  -B, --base string       Filter by base branch
  -d, --draft             Filter by draft state
  -H, --head string       Filter by head branch ("<owner>:<branch>" syntax not supported)
  -q, --jq expression     Filter JSON output using a jq expression
      --json fields       Output JSON with the specified fields
  -l, --label strings     Filter by label
  -L, --limit int         Maximum number of items to fetch (default 30)
  -S, --search query      Search pull requests with query
  -s, --state string      Filter by state: {open|closed|merged|all} (default "open")
  -t, --template string   Format JSON output using a Go template; see "gh help formatting"
  -w, --web               List pull requests in the web browser

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

JSON FIELDS
  additions, assignees, author, autoMergeRequest, baseRefName, baseRefOid, body,
  changedFiles, closed, closedAt, closingIssuesReferences, comments, commits,
  createdAt, deletions, files, fullDatabaseId, headRefName, headRefOid,
  headRepository, headRepositoryOwner, id, isCrossRepository, isDraft, labels,
  latestReviews, maintainerCanModify, mergeCommit, mergeStateStatus, mergeable,
  mergedAt, mergedBy, milestone, number, potentialMergeCommit, projectCards,
  projectItems, reactionGroups, reviewDecision, reviewRequests, reviews, state,
  statusCheckRollup, title, updatedAt, url

EXAMPLES
  # List PRs authored by you
  $ gh pr list --author "@me"
  
  # List PRs opened by a GitHub App such as Dependabot
  $ gh pr list --app dependabot
  
  # List PRs with a specific head branch name
  $ gh pr list --head "typo"
  
  # List only PRs with all of the given labels
  $ gh pr list --label bug --label "priority 1"
  
  # Filter PRs using search syntax
  $ gh pr list --search "status:success review:required"
  
  # Find a PR that introduced a given commit
  $ gh pr list --search "<SHA>" --state merged

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`
```

```text
  Defaults to open merge requests. Use `--all` to include closed                                                        
  and merged requests. Use `--group` to list for a group instead                                                        
  of the current project.                                                                                               
                                                                                                                        
         
  USAGE  
         
    glab mr list [--flags]                                            
            
  EXAMPLES  
            
    glab mr list --all                                                
    glab mr ls -a                                                     
    glab mr list --assignee=@me                                       
    glab mr list --reviewer=@me                                       
    glab mr list --source-branch=new-feature                          
    glab mr list --target-branch=main                                 
    glab mr list --search "this adds feature X"                       
    glab mr list --label needs-review                                 
    glab mr list --not-label waiting-maintainer-feedback,subsystem-x  
    glab mr list -M --per-page 10                                     
    glab mr list --draft                                              
    glab mr list --not-draft                                          
         
  FLAGS  
         
    -A --all            Get all merge requests.
    -a --assignee       Get only merge requests assigned to users. Multiple users can be comma-separated or specified by repeating the flag.
    --author            Filter merge request by author <username>.
    -c --closed         Get only closed merge requests.
    --created-after     Filter merge requests created after a certain date (ISO 8601 format).
    --created-before    Filter merge requests created before a certain date (ISO 8601 format).
    --deployed-after    Filter merge requests deployed after a certain date (ISO 8601 format).
    --deployed-before   Filter merge requests deployed before a certain date (ISO 8601 format).
    -d --draft          Filter by draft merge requests.
    --environment       Filter merge requests deployed to the given environment <name>.
    -g --group          Select a group/subgroup. This option is ignored if a repo argument is set.
    -h --help           Show help for this command.
    --jq                Filter JSON output with a jq expression.
    -l --label          Filter merge request by label <name>. Multiple labels can be comma-separated or specified by repeating the flag.
    -M --merged         Get only merged merge requests.
    -m --milestone      Filter merge request by milestone <id>.
    --not-draft         Filter by non-draft merge requests.
    --not-label         Filter merge requests by not having label <name>. Multiple labels can be comma-separated or specified by repeating the flag.
    -o --order          Order merge requests by <field>. Order options: created_at, updated_at, merged_at, title, priority, label_priority, milestone_due, and popularity.
    -F --output         Format output as: text, json. (text)
```
