76	// List implements Runtime. Pane cwd values, rather than the session's original
77	// start path, are the live filesystem ownership signal retirement needs.
78	func (t *Tmux) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
79		out, err := t.run(ctx, "list-panes", "-a", "-F",
80			"#{session_name}\t#{pane_id}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{?pane_active,1,0}\t#{?session_attached,1,0}")
81		if err != nil {
82			// "no server running on ..." is the normal idle case.
83			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no server running") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "error connecting") {
84				return nil, nil
85			}
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		var order []string
89		byName := make(map[string]*Session)
90		dirs := make(map[string]map[string]bool)
91		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
92			if line == "" {
93				continue
94			}
95			f := strings.Split(line, "\t")
96			if len(f) < 3 || f[0] == "" || f[1] == "" {
97				continue
98			}
99			s := byName[f[0]]
100			if s == nil {
101				s = &Session{Handle: f[0], Label: f[0]}
102				byName[f[0]] = s
103				order = append(order, f[0])
104				dirs[f[0]] = make(map[string]bool)
105			}
106			if f[2] != "" {
107				dirs[f[0]][f[2]] = true
108			}
109			s.Panes = append(s.Panes, Pane{ID: f[1], CWD: f[2], ShellCWD: f[2]})
110			if len(f) > 4 && f[3] == "1" && f[4] == "1" {
111				s.Focused = true
112			}
113		}
114		sessions := make([]Session, 0, len(order))
115		for _, name := range order {
116			s := byName[name]
117			s.Dirs = keys(dirs[name])
118			sessions = append(sessions, *s)
119		}
120		return sessions, nil
121	}

123	// Open implements Runtime, reusing a session that already exists under that
124	// name rather than creating a duplicate.
125	func (t *Tmux) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
126		name := SessionName(label)
127		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "has-session", "-t", "="+name); err == nil {
128			existingDir, err := t.run(ctx, "display-message", "-p", "-t", "="+name, "#{session_path}")
129			if err != nil {
130				return OpenResult{}, err
131			}
132			if !sameDirectory(existingDir, dir) {
133				return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("tmux session %s already exists at %s, not %s", name, existingDir, dir)
134			}
135			return OpenResult{Handle: name, Surface: "session", Opened: true}, nil
136		}
137		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "new-session", "-d", "-s", name, "-c", dir); err != nil {
138			return OpenResult{}, err
139		}
140		return OpenResult{Handle: name, Surface: "session", Opened: true, Created: true}, nil
141	}
142	
143	func sameDirectory(a, b string) bool {
144		canonical := func(path string) string {
145			path = filepath.Clean(path)
146			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path); err == nil {
147				return filepath.Clean(resolved)
148			}
149			return path
150		}
151		return canonical(a) == canonical(b)
152	}
153	
154	// Close implements Runtime: it kills the session only. The checkout is
155	// untouched.
156	func (t *Tmux) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
157		if handle == "" {
158			return nil
159		}
160		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "has-session", "-t", "="+handle); err != nil {
161			return nil // already gone
162		}
163		_, err := t.run(ctx, "kill-session", "-t", "="+handle)
164		return err
165	}

167	// Annotate implements Runtime. tmux has no metadata channel, so dev writes the
168	// task state into the session's user option, where a status-line format can
169	// pick it up with #{@dev_stage} if the user wants it.
170	func (t *Tmux) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
171		if handle == "" {
172			return nil
173		}
174		for k, v := range kv {
175			if _, err := t.run(ctx, "set-option", "-t", "="+handle, "-q", "@dev_"+k, v); err != nil {
176				return err
177			}
178		}

88	// Open creates a detached Zellij session rooted at dir, or reuses the named
89	// session only when its native layout confirms the same directory.
90	func (z *Zellij) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
91		name := SessionName(label)
92		sessions, err := z.List(ctx)
93		if err != nil {
94			return OpenResult{}, err
95		}
96		for _, session := range sessions {
97			if session.Handle != name {
98				continue
99			}
100			if len(session.Dirs) == 0 {
101				return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("zellij session %s exists but its cwd is unavailable", name)
102			}
103			if !sameDirectory(session.Dirs[0], dir) {
104				return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("zellij session %s already exists at %s, not %s", name, session.Dirs[0], dir)
105			}
106			return OpenResult{Handle: name, Surface: "session", Opened: true}, nil
107		}
108		if _, err := z.run(ctx, "attach", "--create-background", name, "options", "--default-cwd", dir); err != nil {
109			return OpenResult{}, err
110		}
111		return OpenResult{Handle: name, Surface: "session", Opened: true, Created: true}, nil
112	}

**Clarifying projection logic**

The snapshot data must be fully loaded before any projection begins, and it seems that various elements like tasks, discovery, and status are read multiple times.

For task-only situations, there might be no status call. In cases where paths are missing or the expected checkout fails, it seems like ResolveRegisteredWorktree isn’t called. So, not every row invokes a status check, although the candidate's analysis is likely close. A cached locator might be essential for maintaining flow and validating identities, but recomputing shared evidence for each row isn’t necessary.

553	func (s *lifecycleService) applyAdopt(ctx context.Context, approved Plan) (Result, error) {
554		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
555			return Result{}, err
556		}
557		if approved.Action != Adopt {
558			return Result{}, &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: approved.PlanID, Reason: "adopt handler received " + string(approved.Action)}
559		}
560		if err := validateAdoptLocator(approved.Locator); err != nil {
561			return Result{}, err
562		}

564		if err != nil {
565			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize approved repository lock identity: %v", ErrInvalidPlan, err)

569		err = s.repoLock(ctx, commonDir, func() error {
570			return s.tasks.WithLock(ctx, func(tx *task.Tx) error {
571				spec, observed, observeErr := s.observeAdopt(ctx, approved.Request, tx.ListRecords)
572				if observeErr != nil {
573					return observeErr
574				}
575				fresh, buildErr := BuildPlan(approved.Request, spec)
576				if buildErr != nil {

578				}
579				if fresh.PlanID != approved.PlanID || fresh.AuthorityFingerprint != approved.AuthorityFingerprint {
580					return &StalePlanError{
581						ExpectedPlanID: approved.PlanID, ActualPlanID: fresh.PlanID,
582						ExpectedAuthorityFingerprint: approved.AuthorityFingerprint,
583						ActualAuthorityFingerprint:   fresh.AuthorityFingerprint,
584						Reason:                       "fresh unmanaged Git, worktree, task, base, runtime, agent, or harness authority differs",
585					}

587				if fresh.Availability != AvailabilityReady {
588					notReady := &PlanNotReadyError{PlanID: fresh.PlanID, Availability: fresh.Availability, conditions: fresh.Conditions()}
589					return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: fresh.PlanID, Reason: "fresh adoption conditions are not ready", Cause: notReady}
590				}

629				return "task create revision or metadata was not verified", errors.New("persisted adopted task differs from the task create result")
630			}
631			e.snapshot = "task:" + persisted.Revision
632			e.milestone = MilestoneAdopted
633			return "created task " + persisted.Task.ID + " at revision " + persisted.Revision, nil
634		})
635		if err != nil {
636			return e.fail(err, "the checkout, branch, runtime, and Git bytes were not changed; repair the task-store failure and refresh adoption")
637		}
638		if e.milestone != MilestoneAdopted || e.snapshot == "" {
639			return e.fail(&InvalidPlanError{PlanID: e.plan.PlanID, Reason: "adoption ended without a created task revision"})

```text
1	# Agent-safe retirement
2	
3	A process must not delete the worktree that contains its own current directory.
4	The terminal can remain visible after Unix unlinks the path, but config reloads,
5	relative files and new subprocesses then fail. Herdr still showing a pane does
6	not mean the Git checkout is healthy.
7	
8	Use three separate milestones:
9	
10	1. **READY** — commit product work, run `dev prepare`, then exit normally so the
11	   post-SpecStory finalizer can commit the exact final transcript. A manual
12	   external finalizer must pass `--writer-stopped`; a Claude SessionEnd observer
13	   can provide the same durable proof without staging during teardown.
14	2. **MERGED** — an external coordinator runs `dev done --ff`, or verifies an
15	   external merge with `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>`. Runtime and
16	   worktree remain intact.
17	3. **RETIRED** — from outside the target workspace run `dev retire`. It closes
18	   eligible runtime sessions, waits until they disappear, revalidates Git, and
19	   removes the worktree without force.
20	
21	`dev flow [repo]` exposes Retire only for an exact DONE task. It first shows
22	conditions, ordered effects, resources retained, and a fallback command; branch
23	deletion is a separate typed option. Apply reloads the exact task revision and
24	Git/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identity under locks, repeats safety checks
25	after runtime closure and before removal, and deletes the task record last.
26	Completed steps remain visible if a later step fails; no rollback is implied.
27	
28	Retirement never overrides `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting` agents. Unknown
29	status needs external `--close-unknown`. A workspace containing panes outside
30	the target is mixed-purpose and must be reorganized or closed manually.
31	
32	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools bypass these
33	protections. Do not use them on an agent-owned checkout. Existing expert CLI
34	acknowledgements remain available, but the flow preview deliberately omits dirty
35	discard, shared-writer/takeover, and unknown-runtime overrides.
36	
37	Task-backed `dev retire` uses the guarded lifecycle service. Explicit unmanaged
38	path retirement retains an isolated compatibility implementation; do not assume
39	every cleanup or `sweep` reconciliation path has moved to the same planner.
40	
41	From the canonical main checkout, `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` reports both
42	tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are contained in
43	main. Review the exact candidates and blockers first; apply only after user
44	confirmation. Worktree retirement keeps branches unless `--delete-branches`
45	was separately requested.
46
```

1	package inventory
2	
3	import "context"
4	
5	// Limiter bounds expensive local enrichment across collectors that would
6	// otherwise each create their own worker pool.
7	type Limiter struct {
8		permits chan struct{}
9	}
10	
11	// NewLimiter returns a context-aware concurrency bound.
12	func NewLimiter(limit int) *Limiter {
13		if limit <= 0 {
14			limit = 8
15		}
16		return &Limiter{permits: make(chan struct{}, limit)}
17	}
18	
19	// Acquire waits for one permit and returns a matching release function.
20	func (l *Limiter) Acquire(ctx context.Context) (func(), bool) {
21		if l == nil {
22			return func() {}, true
23		}
24		if ctx == nil {
25			ctx = context.Background()
26		}
27		select {
28		case l.permits <- struct{}{}:
29			return func() { <-l.permits }, true
30		case <-ctx.Done():
31			return nil, false
32		}
33	}

547		builder.WriteString("\nEFFECTS (execution order)\n")

92	func resolveFlowLaunch(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref string, deps flowCommandDeps) (flowLaunch, error) {
93		var launch flowLaunch
94		if deps.getwd == nil || deps.discover == nil || deps.resolve == nil {
95			return launch, errors.New("flow command dependencies are incomplete")
96		}
97		cwd, err := deps.getwd()
98		if err != nil {
99			return launch, fmt.Errorf("resolve flow caller directory: %w", err)
100		}
101		launch.cwd = cwd
102	
103		if ref != "" {
104			resolved, _, err := deps.resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), ref)
105			if err != nil {
106				return launch, err
107			}
108			queryPath := resolved.Path
109			if queryPath == "" {
110				queryPath = resolved.RealPath
111			}
112			discovered, err := deps.discover(ctx, queryPath)
113			if err != nil {
114				return launch, fmt.Errorf("discover explicit repository %s: %w", config.Contract(queryPath), err)
115			}
116			repository, err := availableFlowRepository(discovered, &resolved, discovered.Root)
117			if err != nil {
118				return launch, err
119			}
120			launch.repository = &repository
121			row := repository.row
122			launch.preselected = &row
123			return launch, nil
124		}
125	
126		discovered, err := deps.discover(ctx, cwd)
127		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
128			return launch, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return launch, fmt.Errorf("discover current repository from %s: %w", config.Contract(cwd), err)
132		}
133		repository, err := availableFlowRepository(discovered, nil, discovered.Root)
134		if err != nil {
135			return launch, err
136		}
137		launch.repository = &repository
138		row := repository.row
139		launch.preselected = &row
140		return launch, nil
141	}

143	func runFlow(app *App, launch flowLaunch, runProgram flowProgramRunner) error {
144		if runProgram == nil {
145			return errors.New("flow program runner is unavailable")
146		}
147		flowtui.SetColorEnabled(app.outStyle().enabled)
148		app.traceTUI = true
149		runCtx, cancelRun := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
150		finishSetup := app.trace.Start(perftrace.TUISetup, perftrace.Fields{})
151		runtimeResolver := newTUIRuntimeResolver(app)
152		loader := newFlowLoader(app, runtimeResolver, launch.cwd)
153		if launch.repository != nil {
154			loader.registerRepository(*launch.repository, true)
155		}
156		actions := loader.actions()
157		if app.deferredReleaseRefresh {
158			actions.AfterFirstView = func(context.Context) { app.refreshReleaseDetached() }
159		}
160		model := flowtui.New(actions, launch.preselected).WithContext(runCtx)
161		finishSetup(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
162		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIProgramRunBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
163		final, err := runProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen())
164		cancelRun()
165		app.finishTrace()
166		if err != nil {
167			return err
168		}
169		withHandoff, ok := final.(interface {
170			Handoff() (taskflow.Handoff, bool)
171		})
172		if !ok {
173			return nil
174		}
175		handoff, ok := withHandoff.Handoff()
176		if !ok {
177			return nil
178		}
179		return honorFlowHandoff(app, runtimeResolver, handoff)
180	}
181	
182	func honorFlowHandoff(app *App, resolver flowRuntimeResolver, handoff taskflow.Handoff) error {
183		switch handoff.Kind {
184		case taskflow.HandoffDirectory:
185			if handoff.Path == "" {
186				return errors.New("flow returned an empty directory handoff")
187			}
188			return app.cdDirective(handoff.Path)
189		case taskflow.HandoffRuntime:
190			if handoff.Runtime == "" || handoff.RuntimeHandle == "" {
191				return errors.New("flow returned an incomplete runtime handoff")
192			}
193			var rt runtime.Runtime
194			if resolver != nil {
195				resolved, err := resolver.Resolve(ctxOf())
196				if err != nil {
197					return err
198				}
199				if resolved != nil && resolved.Name() == handoff.Runtime {
200					rt = resolved
201				}
202			}

402	func (l *flowLoader) ListRepositories(ctx context.Context) ([]flowtui.RepositoryRow, error) {
403		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
404			return nil, err
405		}
406		records, _, taskErr := l.app.Tasks.ListRecords()
407		if taskErr != nil {
408			return nil, fmt.Errorf("list task-referenced repositories: %w", taskErr)
409		}
410		discovered, err := l.listRepo(ctx, l.app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
411		if err != nil {
412			return nil, err
413		}
414	
415		fresh := make(map[string]flowRepository)
416		l.mu.Lock()
417		for key := range l.pinned {
418			if existing, ok := l.repositories[key]; ok {
419				fresh[key] = existing
420			}
421		}
422		l.mu.Unlock()
423	
424		for index := range discovered {
425			candidate := discovered[index]
426			gitRepo, discoverErr := l.discover(ctx, candidate.Path)
427			if discoverErr != nil {
428				continue
429			}
430			entry, convertErr := availableFlowRepository(gitRepo, &candidate, "")
431			if convertErr != nil {
432				continue
433			}
434			if _, exists := fresh[entry.row.RepoKey]; !exists {
435				fresh[entry.row.RepoKey] = entry
436			}
437		}
438	
439		pathResults := make(map[string]struct {
440			repository flowRepository
441			err        error
442		})
443		for _, record := range records {
444			path := record.Task.RepoPath
445			resolved, seen := pathResults[path]
446			if !seen {
447				gitRepo, discoverErr := l.discover(ctx, path)
448				if discoverErr == nil {
449					resolved.repository, discoverErr = availableFlowRepository(gitRepo, nil, "")
450				}
451				resolved.err = discoverErr
452				pathResults[path] = resolved
453			}
454			if resolved.err == nil {
455				if _, exists := fresh[resolved.repository.row.RepoKey]; !exists {
456					fresh[resolved.repository.row.RepoKey] = resolved.repository
457				}
458				continue
459			}
460			entry := unavailableFlowRepository(record, resolved.err)
461			if existing, exists := fresh[entry.row.RepoKey]; exists {
462				existing.unavailableTasks = appendUniqueFlowTaskRecord(existing.unavailableTasks, record)
463				fresh[entry.row.RepoKey] = existing
464			} else {
465				fresh[entry.row.RepoKey] = entry
466			}
467		}
468	
469		rows := make([]flowtui.RepositoryRow, 0, len(fresh))
470		for _, entry := range fresh {
471			rows = append(rows, entry.row)
472		}
473		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
474			left, right := strings.ToLower(rows[i].Name), strings.ToLower(rows[j].Name)
475			if left != right {
476				return left < right
477			}
478			if rows[i].Path != rows[j].Path {
479				return rows[i].Path < rows[j].Path
480			}
481			return rows[i].RepoKey < rows[j].RepoKey
482		})
483		l.mu.Lock()
484		l.repositories = fresh
485		l.mu.Unlock()
486		return rows, nil
487	}

489	func appendUniqueFlowTaskRecord(records []task.Record, candidate task.Record) []task.Record {

492				return records
493			}
494		}
495		return append(records, candidate)

630	func flowRepositoryQueryPath(contextSnapshot inventory.RepoContext) string {
631		if main, ok := contextSnapshot.Main(); ok && main.Worktree.Path != "" {
632			return main.Worktree.Path

634		for _, candidate := range []string{
635			contextSnapshot.Repo.MainRoot,
636			contextSnapshot.Repo.Path,

639		} {

642			}
643		}
644		return ""

647	func (l *flowLoader) projectRows(
648		ctx context.Context,
649		contextSnapshot inventory.RepoContext,
650		service *taskflow.Service,
651		serviceErr error,
652		taskInventoryComplete bool,
653		defaultBase string,
654	) ([]flowtui.SurfaceRow, map[string]flowTarget, []string) {
655		rows := make([]flowtui.SurfaceRow, 0, len(contextSnapshot.Rows))
656		targets := make(map[string]flowTarget)
657		var issues []string
658		for _, contextRow := range contextSnapshot.Rows {
659			projected, rowIssues := l.projectRow(ctx, contextSnapshot, contextRow, service, serviceErr, taskInventoryComplete, defaultBase)
660			issues = append(issues, rowIssues...)
661	
662			validChoices := make([]flowtui.ActionChoice, 0, projected.Actions.Len())
663			for _, choice := range projected.Actions.Values() {
664				request, err := taskflow.NewRequest(projected.Locator, choice.Options())
665				if err != nil {
666					issues = append(issues, fmt.Sprintf("row %s action %s: %v", projected.RowKey, choice.ID, err))
667					continue
668				}
669				target := flowTarget{
670					repoKey: contextSnapshot.RepositoryID, rowKey: projected.RowKey,
671					actionID: choice.ID, request: request,
672				}
673				targets[flowTargetKey(target.repoKey, target.rowKey, target.actionID)] = target
674				validChoices = append(validChoices, choice)
675			}
676			projected.Actions = flowtui.NewActionList(validChoices...)
677			rows = append(rows, projected)
678		}
679		return rows, targets, issues
680	}

19	// CreatePR opens a GitHub pull request.
20	func (g *gh) CreatePR(ctx context.Context, dir string, req PRRequest) (string, error) {
21		if !g.Available() {
22			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
23		}
24		args := []string{"pr", "create", "--base", req.Base, "--head", req.Head}
25		switch {
26		case req.Title != "":
27			args = append(args, "--title", req.Title, "--body", req.Body)
28		default:

30			// the right default for a solo workflow where the commits already say

33		}

36		}

38			args = append(args, "--web")

42	}

```text
65	The historical pages disagree about deploy-before-merge versus merge-then-deploy. That is evidence that deployment belongs to project policy, not a timeless flow invariant.
66	
67	## dev-cli mapping
68	
69	```bash
70	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
71	# commit and test in the task checkout
72	dev done --pr
73	```
74	
75	`dev done --pr` publishes the branch and opens the pull or merge request, then deliberately leaves the task active during review. It does not claim the request is merged and does not mark the task DONE.
76	
77	`dev` also permits a project-policy exception for one small safe commit directly on the trunk. That is a lightweight trunk-based choice, **not** GitHub Flow. Teams that require pull requests should always use a branch.
78	
79	## Pull-request readiness checklist
80	
81	- The branch contains one coherent change stream.
82	- The description explains why, behavior changes, and operational impact.
83	- Tests and manual verification are stated.
84	- Shared generated files and migrations have one owner.
```

134				}
135				choice, promptErr := p.choice("Dirty changes (c=commit, d=discard, q=cancel)", "cancel",
136					"commit (c), discard (d), cancel (q)", map[string]string{
137						"c": "commit", "commit": "commit",
138						"d": "discard", "discard": "discard", "drop": "discard",
139						"q": "cancel", "cancel": "cancel",
140					})
141				if canceledDone(app, promptErr, choice == "cancel") {
142					return nil
143				}
144				if promptErr != nil {
145					return promptErr
146				}
147				selection.Dirty = flow.DirtyPolicy(choice)
148				prompted = true
149				plan, err = replanDone(ctx, session, plan, doneActionOptions(selected, selection, opts))
150				if err != nil {
151					return err
152				}
153				if err := doneFatalPreflightError(selected, plan); err != nil {
154					return err
155				}
156			}
157	
158			if selection.Dirty == flow.DirtyCommit && strings.TrimSpace(selection.Message) == "" {
159				if !interactive {
160					return errors.New("--message is required with --dirty=commit outside an interactive terminal")
161				}
162				message, promptErr := p.line("Commit message", "chore: finalize "+selected.Title())
163				if canceledDone(app, promptErr, false) {
164					return nil
165				}
166				if promptErr != nil {
167					return promptErr
168				}
169				selection.Message = strings.TrimSpace(message)
170				if selection.Message == "" {
171					return errors.New("commit message must not be empty")
172				}
173				prompted = true
174				plan, err = replanDone(ctx, session, plan, doneActionOptions(selected, selection, opts))
175				if err != nil {
176					return err
177				}
178				if err := doneFatalPreflightError(selected, plan); err != nil {
179					return err
180				}
181			}
182			if selection.Dirty == flow.DirtyDiscard {
183				if !interactive && !opts.Yes {
184					return errors.New("--dirty=discard outside an interactive terminal requires --yes")
185				}
186				if interactive && !opts.Yes {
187					prompted = true
188				}
189			}
190		}
191	
192		view = doneView(plan)
193		if mode != task.ModeDirect && selection.Integration == doneIntegrationNone {
194			if view.contained() && !(view.Status.Dirty() && selection.Dirty == flow.DirtyCommit) {
195				selection.Integration = doneIntegrationFF
196				prompted = true
197			} else {
198				choice, promptErr := p.choice("Integration (f=fast-forward, p=PR, q=cancel)", "ff",
199					"fast-forward (f), pull request (p), cancel (q)", map[string]string{
200						"f": "ff", "ff": "ff", "fast-forward": "ff",
201						"p": "pr", "pr": "pr", "pull-request": "pr",
202						"q": "cancel", "cancel": "cancel",
203					})
204				if canceledDone(app, promptErr, choice == "cancel") {
205					return nil
206				}
207				if promptErr != nil {
208					return promptErr
209				}
210				selection.Integration = doneIntegration(choice)
211				prompted = true
212				plan, err = replanDone(ctx, session, plan, doneActionOptions(selected, selection, opts))
213				if err != nil {
214					return err
215				}
216				if err := doneFatalPreflightError(selected, plan); err != nil {
217					return err
218				}
219			}
220		}
221	
222		if err := donePlanReadinessError(selected, plan, selection); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225	
226		approval := flow.Approve(plan.PlanID)
227		if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped && opts.Yes {
228			approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, plan.Confirmation.Token)
229		}
230		if prompted && !opts.Yes {
231			confirmed, token, promptErr := confirmDonePlan(app, p, selected, plan)
232			if canceledDone(app, promptErr, !confirmed) {
233				return nil
234			}
235			if promptErr != nil {
236				return promptErr
237			}
238			if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped {
239				approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(plan.PlanID, token)
240			}
241		}
242		if plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped && approval.Token == "" {
243			return errors.New("destructive finish plan requires its typed confirmation")
244		}
245	
246		if opts.ConfirmSquash != "" {
247			app.warnf("accepting operator attestation that squash commit %s represents branch %s",
248				opts.ConfirmSquash, selected.Branch)
249		}
250		result, applyErr := session.apply(ctx, plan, approval)
251		renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
252		if applyErr != nil {
253			return presentDoneApplyError(result, applyErr)
254		}
255		final, err := session.finalTask(app)
256		if err != nil {
257			return err
258		}
259		return renderDoneSuccess(app, selected, final, plan, result, doneView(initial))
260	}
261	
262	func doneActionOptions(selected task.Task, selection doneSelection, opts doneOptions) flow.ActionOptions {
263		if selected.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeDirect {
264			return flow.CompleteDirectOptions{
265				Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message, Push: opts.Push,
266			}
267		}
268		switch selection.Integration {
269		case doneIntegrationPR:
270			return flow.ReviewHandoffOptions{Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message}
271		case doneIntegrationMerged:
272			return flow.VerifyMergedOptions{
273				Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message,
274				BaseRef: opts.BaseRef, SquashCommit: opts.ConfirmSquash, PushBase: opts.Push,
275			}
276		default:
277			return flow.CompleteFFOptions{
278				Dirty: selection.Dirty, CommitMessage: selection.Message, PushBase: opts.Push,
279			}
280		}

102	// Actions returns every supported action in stable display order.
103	func Actions() []Action { return append([]Action(nil), actionOrder...) }
104	
105	// Valid reports whether the action is part of this protocol version.
106	func (a Action) Valid() bool {
107		for _, candidate := range actionOrder {
108			if a == candidate {
109				return true
110			}
111		}
112		return false
113	}

146	// ObservationState says what happened when one live fact was requested. A
147	// skipped, loading, unknown, or failed observation is never equivalent to a
148	// known false value.
149	type ObservationState string
150	
151	const (
152		ObservationKnown   ObservationState = "known"
153		ObservationUnknown ObservationState = "unknown"
154		ObservationError   ObservationState = "error"
155		ObservationSkipped ObservationState = "skipped"
156		ObservationLoading ObservationState = "loading"
157	)
158	
159	// Valid reports whether the observation state has defined semantics.
160	func (s ObservationState) Valid() bool {
161		switch s {
162		case ObservationKnown, ObservationUnknown, ObservationError, ObservationSkipped, ObservationLoading:
163			return true
164		default:
165			return false
166		}
167	}
168	
169	// Observation is one fact and its provenance. ObservedAt is display/freshness
170	// metadata and is deliberately not itself plan authority.
171	type Observation struct {
172		State      ObservationState
173		Value      string
174		Evidence   string
175		Failure    string
176		ObservedAt time.Time
177		attributes Fields

1	package taskflow

3	import (
4		"context"

13	// locateExactTask builds a managed locator from one exact task record and a
14	// fresh view of its repository. Missing checkout evidence is retained as an
15	// expected path (or an intentionally empty COLD path) so Plan can explain the
16	// drift instead of losing the task before transition validation.
17	func (s *lifecycleService) locateExactTask(ctx context.Context, taskID string) (Locator, error) {
18		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
19			return Locator{}, err
20		}
21		if !exactTaskID.MatchString(taskID) || filepath.Base(taskID) != taskID || taskID == "." || taskID == ".." {
22			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid exact TaskID %q", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID)
23		}
24	
25		record, err := s.tasks.GetRecord(taskID)
26		if err != nil {
27			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: load exact task %q: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
28		}
29		candidate := record.Task
30		if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
31			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: exact task %q is invalid: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
32		}
33		mode := candidate.EffectiveMode()
34		if !validMode(mode) || !validState(candidate.State) {
35			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: exact task %q has invalid mode or state", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID)
36		}
37	
38		repository, err := s.gitDiscover(ctx, candidate.RepoPath)
39		if err != nil {
40			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: discover exact repository for task %s: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
41		}
42		repoPath, err := s.canonicalPath(repository.MainRoot)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize main checkout for task %s: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
45		}
46		commonDir, err := s.canonicalPath(repository.GitCommonDir)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize Git common directory for task %s: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
49		}
50		recordedRepo, err := s.canonicalPath(candidate.RepoPath)
51		if err != nil {
52			return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize recorded repository for task %s: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
53		}
54		if recordedRepo != repoPath {
55			return Locator{}, &StalePlanError{Reason: fmt.Sprintf(
56				"recorded repository %q resolves to %q, but Git reports main checkout %q",
57				candidate.RepoPath, recordedRepo, repoPath,
58			)}
59		}
60	
61		expectedCheckout := repoPath
62		if mode == task.ModeWorktree {
63			expectedCheckout = ""
64			if candidate.WorktreePath != "" {
65				expectedCheckout, err = s.canonicalPath(candidate.WorktreePath)
66				if err != nil {
67					return Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize expected checkout for task %s: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, taskID, err)
68				}
69			}
70		}
71	
72		locator := Locator{
73			RepoKey:      commonDir,
74			RowKey:       taskID,
75			RowKind:      "task",
76			RepositoryID: commonDir,
77			GitCommonDir: commonDir,
78			TaskID:       taskID,
79			TaskRevision: record.Revision,
80			RepoPath:     repoPath,
81			CheckoutPath: expectedCheckout,
82			Branch:       candidate.Branch,
83			Base:         candidate.Base,
84			Remote:       "origin",
85			Mode:         mode,
86			State:        candidate.State,
87		}
88	
89		registered, found := s.locateRegisteredCheckout(ctx, candidate, repoPath, expectedCheckout)
90		if found {
91			locator.RowKey = registered.Path
92			locator.RowKind = "checkout"
93			locator.HeadOID = strings.TrimSpace(registered.Worktree.Head)
94			if status, statusErr := s.gitStatus(ctx, registered.Path); statusErr == nil {
95				locator.Upstream = status.Upstream
96				if head, headErr := s.resolveRefOID(ctx, registered.Path, "HEAD"); headErr == nil {
97					locator.HeadOID = head
98				}
99			}
100		}
101		if locator.HeadOID == "" {
102			locator.HeadOID, _ = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, repoPath, localBranchRef(candidate.Branch))
103		}
104		if locator.Upstream == "" && (!found || mode == task.ModeWorktree) {
105			locator.Upstream = s.branchUpstream(ctx, repoPath, candidate.Branch)
106		}
107		locator.BaseOID, _ = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, repoPath, candidate.Base)
108		locator.UpstreamOID, _ = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, repoPath, locator.Upstream)
109	
110		current, err := s.tasks.GetRecord(taskID)
111		if err != nil {
112			return Locator{}, &StalePlanError{
113				ExpectedAuthorityFingerprint: record.Revision,
114				Reason:                       "task record disappeared while locating",
115			}
116		}
117		if current.Revision != record.Revision {
118			return Locator{}, staleTaskRevision(record.Revision, current.Revision, "task record changed while locating")
119		}
120		return locator, nil
121	}
122	
123	func (s *lifecycleService) locateRegisteredCheckout(
124		ctx context.Context,
125		candidate task.Task,
126		repoPath string,
127		expectedCheckout string,
128	) (gitx.RegisteredWorktree, bool) {
129		if expectedCheckout != "" {
130			registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, expectedCheckout)
131			return registered, err == nil
132		}
133		if candidate.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeWorktree || candidate.State != task.Cold {
134			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
135		}
136	
137		worktrees, err := s.gitWorktrees(ctx, repoPath)
138		if err != nil {
139			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
140		}
141		match := ""
142		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
143			if worktree.Branch != candidate.Branch {
144				continue
145			}
146			if match != "" {
147				return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
148			}
149			match = worktree.Path
150		}
151		if match == "" {
152			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
153		}
154		registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, match)
155		return registered, err == nil
156	}
157	
158	func (s *lifecycleService) branchUpstream(ctx context.Context, repoPath, branch string) string {
159		if branch == "" {
160			return ""
161		}
162		value, err := s.gitRun(ctx, repoPath,
163			"for-each-ref", "--format=%(upstream:short)", localBranchRef(branch),
164		)
165		if err != nil {
166			return ""
167		}
168		return strings.TrimSpace(value)
169	}
170

30		}

144	func (s *lifecycleService) completeFFSpec(request Request, observed lifecycleObservation) PlanSpec {
145		options := request.Options.(CompleteFFOptions)
146		conditions := s.completionConditions(observed, options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage)
147		relation := effectiveCompletionRelation(observed, options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage)
148		if !relation.Contained() {
149			conditions = append(conditions, completionIntegrationCondition(observed, options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage))
150			if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree {

152			}

156			observed.task.Branch, relation.BaseOnly, relation.BranchOnly, observed.completionBaseRef)
157		if relation.Contained() {
158			relationEvidence = observed.task.Branch + " is already contained in " + observed.completionBaseRef

55	// Approve constructs an affirmative approval without a typed token.
56	func Approve(planID string) Approval { return Approval{PlanID: planID, Granted: true} }
57	
58	// ApproveWithToken constructs an affirmative approval with exact typed text.
59	func ApproveWithToken(planID, token string) Approval {
60		return Approval{PlanID: planID, Granted: true, Token: token}
61	}
62	
63	// Milestone is an outcome overlay, never a persisted task state.
64	type Milestone string
65	
66	const (
67		MilestoneNone        Milestone = ""
68		MilestoneAdopted     Milestone = "adopted"
69		MilestoneReviewReady Milestone = "review-ready"
70		MilestoneMerged      Milestone = "merged"
71		MilestoneRetired     Milestone = "retired"
72		MilestoneReconciled  Milestone = "reconciled"
73	)
74	
75	// HandoffKind names work a caller may perform after leaving an alternate-screen
76	// UI. A handoff is an outcome, not proof that activation already happened.
77	type HandoffKind string
78	
79	const (
80		HandoffDirectory HandoffKind = "directory"
81		HandoffRuntime   HandoffKind = "runtime"
82		HandoffURL       HandoffKind = "url"
83	)
84	
85	// Handoff is a value-only navigation or activation target.
86	type Handoff struct {
87		Kind          HandoffKind
88		Path          string
89		Runtime       string
90		RuntimeHandle string
91		URL           string
92		Label         string
93	}
94	
95	// StepStatus is the last known state of one attempted effect.
96	type StepStatus string
97	
98	const (
99		StepAttempted StepStatus = "attempted"
100		StepCompleted StepStatus = "completed"
101		StepFailed    StepStatus = "failed"
102	)
103	
104	// StepResult is one entry in the ordered execution ledger. Failure is text
105	// because the typed operation error is returned separately from Result.
106	type StepResult struct {
107		Effect     Effect
108		Status     StepStatus
109		Detail     string
110		Failure    string
111		StartedAt  time.Time
112		FinishedAt time.Time
113	}
114	
115	// Clone returns a step with independent effect detail storage.
116	func (s StepResult) Clone() StepResult {
117		s.Effect = s.Effect.Clone()
118		return s
119	}

121	// NamedRefObservation is one exact local Git ref observation. Missing refs are
122	// represented by Exists=false; probe failures retain safe text separately and
123	// never collapse into a known missing ref.

329			}
330			line := marker + label
331			if index == m.actionCursor {

333			}
334			lines = append(lines, line)
335		}
336		if choice, ok := m.currentAction(); ok {
337			lines = append(lines, "", "selected: "+choice.Description)
338			lines = append(lines, "Enter: inspect a fresh plan; no immediate mutation.")
339			if choice.Action() == taskflow.RefreshRemote {
340				lines = append(lines, "network variant: "+remoteChoiceDescription(choice.Options()))
341			}
342		}
343		return lines
344	}

190	// WorktreeFor finds the first worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git
191	// normally refuses duplicate branch checkouts, but --force can create them;
192	// identity-sensitive callers must use ResolveRegisteredWorktree instead.
193	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
194		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
195		if err != nil {
196			return Worktree{}, false, err
197		}
198		for _, w := range list {
199			if w.Branch == branch {
200				return w, true, nil
201			}
202		}
203		return Worktree{}, false, nil
204	}
205	
206	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
207	//
208	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
209	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
210	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
211	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
212	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
213		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
214		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
215		if exists {
216			args = append(args, path, branch)
217		} else {
218			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
219			if base != "" {
220				args = append(args, base)
221			}
222		}
223		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
224		return err
225	}
226	
227	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
228	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
229	// be any checkout of the same repository.
230	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
231		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
232		return err
233	}
234	
235	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
236	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
237	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
238		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
239		if err != nil {
240			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
241		}
242		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
243		if err != nil {
244			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
245		}
246		if inside {
247			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
248		}
249		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
250		if force {
251			args = append(args, "--force")
252		}
253		args = append(args, path)
254		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
255		return err
256	}
257	
258	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
259	// were deleted behind git's back.
260	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
261		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
262		return err
263	}
264	
265	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
266	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
267		if branch == "" {
268			return false
269		}
270		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
271		return err == nil
272	}
273	
274	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
275	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
276		if ref == "" {
277			return false
278		}
279		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
280		return err == nil
281	}
282

69	func (e *ErrExists) Error() string {
70		return fmt.Sprintf("branch %s is already checked out at %s", e.Branch, e.Path)

79	// Create adds a linked worktree, provisions it and surfaces it in the runtime.
80	func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*CreateResult, error) {
81		if req.Branch == "" {
82			return nil, errors.New("branch is required")
83		}
84		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, req.RepoPath)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95	
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101	
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {
104			path, err = m.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(req.RepoName, repoPath, req.Branch, req.Category)
105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := ValidateTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114	
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {
118			if base == "" {
119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125		var provisionSettings Settings
126		if !req.NoProvision {
127			provisionSettings, err = SettingsForTrusted(ctx, m.Cfg, repoPath)
128			if err != nil {
129				return nil, err
130			}
131		}
132	
133		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
134			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
135		}
136		if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, req.Branch, base); err != nil {
137			return nil, err
138		}
139		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
140	
141		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
142	
143		if !req.NoProvision {
144			// Trusted settings fold in the repository's portable project config.
145			p := &Provisioner{
146				Settings: provisionSettings,
147				Timeout:  provisionSettings.ProvisionTimeout,
148				Log:      m.Log,
149			}
150			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
151			if err != nil {
152				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
153				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
154			}
155			res.Provision = pr
156		}
157	
158		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
159			label := req.Label
160			if label == "" {
161				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
162			}
163			opened, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
164			if err != nil {
165				m.logf("warning: could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
166			} else {
167				res.Runtime = opened
168				res.RuntimeName = m.Runtime.Name()
169			}
170		}
171		return res, nil
172	}

210	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
211	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
212	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
213		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
214		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
215		if exists {
216			args = append(args, path, branch)
217		} else {
218			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
219			if base != "" {
220				args = append(args, base)
221			}
222		}
223		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
224		return err
225	}
226	
227	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
228	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
229	// be any checkout of the same repository.
230	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
231		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
232		return err
233	}
234	
235	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
236	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
237	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
238		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
239		if err != nil {
240			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
241		}
242		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
243		if err != nil {
244			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
245		}
246		if inside {
247			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
248		}
249		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
250		if force {
251			args = append(args, "--force")
252		}
253		args = append(args, path)
254		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
255		return err
256	}
257	
258	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
259	// were deleted behind git's back.
260	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
261		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
262		return err
263	}
264	
265	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
266	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
267		if branch == "" {
268			return false
269		}
270		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
271		return err == nil
272	}
273	
274	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
275	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
276		if ref == "" {
277			return false
278		}
279		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
280		return err == nil
281	}

39		}

50				return err

52			if _, err := os.Stat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
53				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s already exists", candidate.ID)

56			}

59			}

25			Use:   "done [task]",
26			Short: "Integrate a finished change stream without destroying its workspace",
27			Long: `Finish integration while leaving runtime and filesystem cleanup to an
28	external coordinator.
29	
30	  --ff       rebase onto the base and fast-forward it locally. Use when the
31	             branch's commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
32	  --pr       push and open a pull/merge request with the detected forge CLI,
33	             leaving the merge to review and CI.
34	  --merged   verify an externally merged branch against --base-ref, for a merge
35	             performed outside dev.
36	
37	For branch/worktree tasks, omitting every mode opens a finish wizard on an
38	interactive terminal. A non-interactive caller still gets a report and must
39	pass a mode explicitly. Direct tasks need no integration mode.
40	
41	A dirty checkout is analyzed against the base, not rejected as one opaque
42	condition. Interactive use can commit everything, discard everything, or
43	cancel. Unique content requires typing DROP before discard. Scripts select an
44	explicit --dirty policy; destructive discard also requires --yes.
45	
46	A successful local or externally verified merge records DONE, meaning MERGED
47	with cleanup possibly pending. It never closes the invoking runtime, removes a
48	worktree, or deletes a branch. Run dev retire later from outside the workspace.`,
49			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
50			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
51				modes := 0
52				for _, selected := range []bool{ff, pr, merged} {
53					if selected {
54						modes++
55					}
56				}
57				if modes > 1 {
58					return fmt.Errorf("--ff, --pr and --merged are alternatives; pick one")
59				}
60				if !merged && (baseRef != "" || confirmSquash != "") {
61					return fmt.Errorf("--base-ref and --confirm-squash require --merged")
62				}
63				if deleteBranch {
64					return fmt.Errorf("--delete-branch is cleanup; run dev retire --delete-branch after integration")
65				}
66				if keepWorktree {
67					app.warnf("--keep-worktree is deprecated: dev done always keeps runtime and worktree state")
68				}
69				integration := doneIntegrationNone
70				switch {
71				case ff:
72					integration = doneIntegrationFF
73				case pr:
74					integration = doneIntegrationPR
75				case merged:
76					integration = doneIntegrationMerged
77				}
78				return runDone(ctxOf(), app, args, doneOptions{
79					Integration: integration, DirtyPolicy: doneDirtyPolicy(dirtyPolicy),
80					Message: message, Yes: yes, Push: push,

Check removal with ignored nested repository

```bash
set -euo pipefail
base=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$base"' EXIT
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=test GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=test@example.com GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=test GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=test@example.com
mkdir "$base/parent" && git -C "$base/parent" init -q
printf 'nested/\n' > "$base/parent/.gitignore" && printf 'parent\n' > "$base/parent/f"
git -C "$base/parent" add .gitignore f && git -C "$base/parent" commit -qm init
git -C "$base/parent" branch linked && git -C "$base/parent" worktree add -q "$base/linked" linked
mkdir "$base/linked/nested" && git -C "$base/linked/nested" init -q && printf 'child\n' > "$base/linked/nested/f" && git -C "$base/linked/nested" add f && git -C "$base/linked/nested" commit -qm child
printf 'parent-status=%q\n' "$(git -C "$base/linked" status --porcelain)"
set +e
out=$(git -C "$base/parent" worktree remove "$base/linked" 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
printf 'remove-status=%s\n%s\nlinked-exists=%s\n' "$rc" "$out" "$([[ -e "$base/linked" ]] && printf yes || printf no)"

547	func assertSafeFlowOptions(t *testing.T, options taskflow.ActionOptions) {
548		t.Helper()

550		case taskflow.ParkWarmOptions:
551			if value.CommitWIP || value.Push || value.KeepSession || value.CloseUnknown || value.AssumeNoRuntime {
552				t.Fatalf("unsafe ParkWarm options: %+v", value)
553			}
554		case taskflow.ParkColdOptions:
555			if value.CommitWIP || value.CloseUnknown || value.AssumeNoRuntime {
556				t.Fatalf("unsafe ParkCold options: %+v", value)
557			}
558		case taskflow.ResumeOptions:
559			if !value.FetchRefs || value.TakeOwnership || value.NoProvision {
560				t.Fatalf("unsafe Resume options: %+v", value)
561			}
562		case taskflow.CompleteDirectOptions:
563			if value.Dirty != taskflow.DirtyFail || value.CommitMessage != "" || value.Push {
564				t.Fatalf("unsafe CompleteDirect options: %+v", value)

566		case taskflow.CompleteFFOptions:

572				t.Fatalf("unsafe ReviewHandoff options: %+v", value)
573			}
574		case taskflow.VerifyMergedOptions:
575			if value.Dirty != taskflow.DirtyFail || value.CommitMessage != "" || value.PushBase {

70	// ReadinessInspection is a complete read-only observation for one exact

80	// Ready applies only the existing artifact finalization contract: an exact

82	// discarded or has a finalized receipt that is still reachable. Missing or
83	// incomplete evidence fails closed.
84	func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {
85		if i.ObservationError != nil {
86			return false
87		}
88		if len(i.Intents) == 0 {
89			return i.KnownEmpty
90		}
91		if i.KnownEmpty {
92			return false
93		}
94		for _, intent := range i.Intents {
95			if intent.ObservationError != nil {
96				return false
97			}
98			switch intent.State {
99			case ReadinessDiscarded:
100				// Discard is the existing explicit operator escape hatch.
101			case ReadinessFinalizedReachable:
102				if !intent.Finalized || !intent.ReceiptReachable {
103					return false
104				}
105			default:
106				return false
107			}
108		}
109		return true
110	}

482	func (s *Service) revalidate(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
483		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
484		if err != nil {
485			return err
486		}
487		if repository.GitCommonDir != intent.GitCommonDir {
488			return fmt.Errorf("Git common-dir changed")
489		}
490		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
491		if err != nil {
492			return err
493		}
494		if status.Branch != intent.Branch || status.Detached {
495			return fmt.Errorf("branch changed from %s to %s", intent.Branch, status.Branch)
496		}
497		if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(intent.WorktreePath); err != nil {
498			return err
499		} else if active {
500			return fmt.Errorf("Git operation %s is in progress", operation)
501		}
502		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
503		if err != nil {
504			return err
505		}
506		if head != intent.Head {
507			return fmt.Errorf("HEAD changed from %s to %s", intent.Head, head)
508		}
509		return nil
510	}

256	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
257		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
258		if err != nil {
259			return Repo{}, nil, err

263				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
264				if real == "" {

266				}
267				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
268				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
269				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
270				return Repo{
271					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
272					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
273				}, nil, nil
274			}
275		}
276		for _, r := range all {
277			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
278				return r, nil, nil
279			}
280		}
281		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
282		var hits []Repo
283		for _, r := range all {
284			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
285				hits = append(hits, r)
286			}
287		}
288		switch len(hits) {
289		case 1:
290			return hits[0], nil, nil
291		case 0:
292			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
293		default:

987	// assignSessions assigns each observed directory to the most-specific
988	// checkout. A session rooted in repo/.claude/worktrees/x therefore belongs to
989	// x, not to the canonical checkout which also happens to contain that path.
990	func assignSessions(out *RepoContext, sessions []runtime.Session) {
991		for _, session := range sessions {
992			assigned := map[int]bool{}
993			for _, dir := range session.Dirs {
994				best, bestLen := -1, -1
995				for i := range out.Checkouts {
996					for _, root := range checkoutRoots(out.Checkouts[i]) {
997						if pathContains(root, dir) && len(normalizePath(root)) > bestLen {
998							best, bestLen = i, len(normalizePath(root))
999						}
1000					}
1001				}
1002				if best >= 0 {
1003					assigned[best] = true
1004				}
1005			}
1006			for i := range assigned {
1007				out.Checkouts[i].Sessions = append(out.Checkouts[i].Sessions, session)
1008			}
1009		}
1010	}
1011	
1012	func checkoutRoots(checkout RepoCheckout) []string {
1013		return []string{checkout.Worktree.Path}
1014	}
1015	
1016	func pathContains(root, path string) bool {
1017		if root == "" || path == "" {
1018			return false
1019		}
1020		rel, err := filepath.Rel(normalizePath(root), normalizePath(path))
1021		if err != nil || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
1022			return false
1023		}
1024		return rel == "." || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
1025	}
1026	
1027	// normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
1028	// paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
1029	// also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
1030	// is not sufficient.
1031	func normalizePath(path string) string {
1032		if canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(path); err == nil {
1033			return canonical
1034		}
1035		return filepath.Clean(path)
1036	}

1038	// FormatRepoContext renders the deterministic Markdown used by both the CLI
1039	// and the TUI's yy binding. checkoutIndex < 0 means the whole repository.
1040	func FormatRepoContext(c RepoContext, checkoutIndex int) string {
1041		var b strings.Builder
1042		if checkoutIndex >= 0 && checkoutIndex < len(c.Checkouts) {
1043			checkout := c.Checkouts[checkoutIndex]
1044			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# dev worktree context: %s\n\n", displayBranch(checkout))
1045			writeCheckoutMarkdown(&b, c, checkout, false)
1046			return strings.TrimSpace(b.String()) + "\n"
1047		}
1048	
1049		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# dev repo context: %s\n\n", c.Repo.Display())
1050		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Repository: `%s`\n", c.Repo.Display())
1051		mainPath := c.Repo.Path
1052		if main, ok := c.Main(); ok {
1053			mainPath = main.Worktree.Path
1054		}
1055		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Main path: `%s`\n", mainPath)
1056		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Linked worktrees: %d\n", c.WorktreeCount)
1057		if c.Runtime != "" && c.Runtime != "none" {
1058			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Runtime: `%s`\n", c.Runtime)

250	| `cd` | enter the repository through the trusted `shell-init` wrapper |
251	| `open` | open the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime; fall back to `cd` when runtime is `none` |
252	| `start` | continue into the existing `dev start` task wizard with this repository fixed |
253	
254	Neither bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. They
255	prepare the repository, checkout, and optional runtime surface. An explicit
256	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` can dispatch one command to a
257	new first-class Herdr root pane; it never chooses an agent profile or permission
258	mode on the user's behalf.
259	
260	Global custom presets live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml`. A project
261	may commit `.dev-cli/config.toml` for allowlisted worktree/setup wizard defaults
262	and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` for project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
263	setup. Project files cannot override host paths, runtime selection, forge
264	inventory, credentials, state, stats, update policy, or TUI policy. Legacy
265	`.dev.toml` worktree settings remain readable; the `.dev-cli` files win when
266	both are present. See [Commands and configuration](docs/reference/commands-config.md#repository-bootstrap)
267	for the schema, precedence, and executable-config trust boundary.
268	
269	## The lifecycle
270	
271	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
272	|---|---|---|---|
273	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
274	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session normally closed | back within days |
275	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
276	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | **MERGED**, waiting for external retirement |
277	
278	READY/MERGED/RETIRED are derived milestones, not new persisted task states.
279	An agent prepares and exits; an external coordinator integrates and retires it.
280	
281	```bash
282	dev start                                            # interactive managed-task wizard
283	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main     # non-interactive fast path → hot
284	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main \
285	  --run 'specstory run codex -c "codex"' --focus      # dispatch, then switch to the exact new pane
286	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip      # → warm; self-runtime stays alive until exit
287	dev park --cold --push                               # → cold, only from outside the target runtime
288	dev resume "token refresh"                           # → hot, rebuilt if needed
289	dev flow api                                          # preview the repository lifecycle, plan first
290	
291	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
292	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped # manual post-wrapper proof
293	dev done                                             # TTY finish wizard
294	dev done --ff                                        # → done/MERGED; runtime + worktree kept
295	dev retire "token refresh" --delete-branch           # external close/wait/remove → RETIRED
296	
297	dev done --pr                                        # open review; keep task/worktree
298	dev done --merged --base-ref origin/main             # verify commit-preserving merge
299	dev sweep                                            # report drift and cleanup-pending work
300	dev sweep --merged-worktrees                         # from main: audit contained linked worktrees
301	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply                 # confirm each safe retirement
302	```
303	
304	On a TTY, bare `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind and classifies every
305	staged, unstaged and untracked path against the base before offering
306	commit-all, discard-all or cancel. Unique discard requires typing `DROP`;
307	scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or `--dirty=discard --yes`.
308	
309	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
310	
311	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
312	
313	```bash
314	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
315	dev repo open api
316	
317	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
318	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
319	
320	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
321	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
322	
323	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
324	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
325	```
326	
327	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
328	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
329	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
330	
331	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
332	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
333	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
334	the parallel task depends on them.
335	
336	### Guarded Git transactions
337	
338	`dev git` wraps only operations that need durable receipts or failure recovery;
339	it does not replace ordinary Git aliases:
340	
341	```bash
342	dev git uncommit              # soft reset; save old OID/message receipt
343	dev git recommit              # commit -C the receipt, then clear it
344	dev git pull-rebase           # exact stash OID + --index restore; never stash@{0}
345	dev git amend-all             # add -A + amend --no-edit, with normal hooks
346	dev git amend-all --exclude-agent-artifacts
347	dev git setup --print         # print optional aliases; never edit config
348	```
349	
350	Published commit rewrites require `--rewrite-published`. `amend-all` includes
351	agent artifacts by default only when a project scanner is present (or the user
352	explicitly accepts `--allow-unscanned-artifacts`).
353	
354	For automation, `dev start … --json` emits one pure creation object with absolute
355	paths and transient runtime facts. Only a newly created first-class Herdr
356	worktree with a non-empty exact `root_pane_id` is a launch target; reuse,
357	fallback, Tmux, none, or missing pane data fails closed. Worktree starts use the
358	same `repo/branch` label as `dev wt create` and pins the Git-derived parent
359	checkout with Herdr `--cwd`, preserving native nested repository/worktree
360	grouping without separate provenance metadata.
361	
362	For a human one-liner, `--run '<shell command>'` uses that same exact-pane proof
363	and sends the command to the new worktree's interactive shell. It is incompatible
364	with `--json`, `--direct`, `--branch-only`, and non-Herdr runtimes. It only
365	confirms dispatch, never waits for command completion or reports its exit code;
366	add `--focus` when the caller should switch or attach after dispatch.
367	
368	Herdr-aware writer claims—`start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
369	`resume`—reject another recognized agent in the same canonical Git worktree.
370	Every state, including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied. Pure
371	`repo open`, `wt open`, and TUI Enter reuse/focus the live owner without
372	claiming another writer. `--allow-shared-checkout` is only for explicitly
373	coordinated disjoint ownership; normal new-worktree creation remains allowed.
374	
375	Task runtime handles carry their backend name and are validated against live
376	checkout coverage before reuse or close. Destructive cleanup additionally
377	resolves every covering pane. A caller inside the target, a mixed workspace, or
378	a working/blocked/waiting agent always stops retirement; unknown status needs an
379	external `--close-unknown`. `dev done` never closes or removes anything.
380	
381	### Repository flow preview
382	
383	`dev flow [repo]` is a preview-labelled, full-screen, TTY-only state-machine UI.
384	It is independent of the six-view `dev tui` dashboard. From a canonical or linked
385	checkout, `dev flow` resolves the canonical repository and focuses that exact
386	surface; outside Git it opens a filterable repository picker. An explicit
387	`dev flow api` overrides cwd.
388	
389	The left panel is the union of Git's registered worktrees and task records that
390	have no checkout, including normal COLD and DONE tasks. Rows are labelled
391	`canonical`, `managed`, `unmanaged`, `harness`, `task-only`, or `conflict`.
392	Canonical worktrees are never removable; harness-owned and ambiguous/conflicting
393	rows have no destructive path. An exact unmanaged linked checkout can be
394	**Adopted** by creating task metadata without changing Git bytes, or **Removed**
395	only when clean and safe; removal is non-force and always preserves the branch.
396	
397	The center distinguishes persisted task intent (`HOT`, `WARM`, `COLD`, `DONE`)
398	from observed Git/worktree/runtime/artifact facts. Unknown, failed, loading, or
399	stale evidence never becomes a false clean/closed fact. `runtime=none` leaves
400	session occupancy unobserved, but the local Git/task snapshot can still be fresh;
401	metadata-only adoption then remains WARM.
402	
403	The right panel offers concrete mode/state actions: warm/cold park, resume,
404	direct or fast-forward completion, review handoff, verified-merge completion,
405	and DONE retirement where legal. The preview deliberately excludes dirty
406	commit/discard, WIP checkpoint, shared-writer, ownership-takeover, and unknown-
407	runtime overrides. A blocked plan shows its exact evidence, remediation, and CLI
408	fallback; existing command flags remain available outside the preview.
409	
410	```text
411	j/k or ↑/↓       choose a surface      h/l or ←/→     choose an action
412	Tab/Shift-Tab    move panel focus       Enter          build a plan, never apply
413	r                reload local facts    R              Fetch refs / Query review / Both
414	Esc              back out              ?              evidence and key help
415	```
416	
417	A READY plan shows ordered conditions/effects, retained resources, network and
418	destructive markers, and its exact PlanID. Press `y` only for a non-typed plan;
419	typed branch deletion requires the displayed token and `Enter`. Apply locks and
420	reloads the task revision plus repository, checkout, refs, runtime, artifact, and
421	remote identities. Any change rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Once an
422	effect starts, quit/refresh waits for the retained step ledger; partial success
423	means completed effects remain completed and recovery is explicit.
424	
425	Startup and `r` never fetch or query a forge. `R` runs only the confirmed choice
426	and keeps its evidence in this TUI run: named ref OIDs plus portable review
427	existence, open/draft/merged/closed state, URL, provider, and observation time.
428	It does not query review decisions or checks. Completion records DONE while
429	keeping branch, checkout, and runtime resources; Retire cleans them from outside
430	the target. Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside these
431	`dev`-mediated locks and safety checks.
432	
433	### The dashboard
434	
435	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens six lists, switched with `tab`:
436	
437	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
438	- **REPOS** — durable repositories under the scan roots, with branch, dirty
439	  state, owned size, runtime, worktrees and task tally. What do I have here.

69	
70	`dev flow [repo]` makes the underlying hybrid model visible: persisted intent,

73	worktree/runtime/artifact identity before mutation. See [Repository lifecycle
74	flow](../guides/repository-flow.md).
75	
76	## Checkout modes
77	
78	A task records intent; it does not always require a linked worktree.
79	
80	| Mode | Use | Lifecycle limit |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| direct | one small change in the canonical checkout | HOT ↔ WARM; canonical checkout cannot be removed |
83	| branch-only | isolated history without a second directory | can go COLD after push and switching the canonical checkout away |
84	| worktree | independent mutation, parallel streams, durable feature work | full lifecycle |
85	
86	The mode is selected by collision and recovery needs, not by ceremony.
87	
88	## Runtime is deliberately lossy
89	
90	`runtime.Runtime` exposes `Open`, `Close`, `List`, and `Annotate`. `auto` selects Herdr when available, then tmux, then Zellij, then the always-available `none` backend. Closing any backend must not remove the checkout, branch, or task entry.
91	
92	This separation is why rebooting, closing a multiplexer, or changing runtime backend does not abandon work. `dev sweep` can compare the registry with live Git/runtime facts and report drift.
93	
94	## Cross-machine handoff
95	
96	The branch is the transport boundary:
97	
98	```bash
99	# machine A
100	dev park --cold --push
101	
102	# machine B
103	dev resume <task> --fetch
104	```
105	
106	One writer owns a branch at a time. If two machines or agents need to mutate the same feature concurrently, split the change stream and integrate afterwards.

12	## Lifecycle at a glance
