22	
23	    Direct -->|dev park --next| WarmDirect["WARM: checkout kept"]
24	    WarmDirect -->|dev resume| Direct
25	    Managed -->|dev park --next| WarmManaged["WARM: checkout kept"]
26	    WarmManaged -->|dev resume| Managed
27	    Managed -->|dev park --cold --push| Cold["COLD: pushed and reconstructible"]
28	    WarmManaged -->|dev park --cold --push| Cold
29	    Cold -->|dev resume --fetch| Managed
30	
31	    Direct -->|dev done| Done["DONE: integration confirmed"]
32	    WarmDirect -->|dev done| Done
33	    Managed -->|dev done --ff| Done
34	    WarmManaged -->|dev done --ff| Done
35	
36	    Managed -->|dev done --pr| Review["push / review handoff: task stays active"]
37	    WarmManaged -->|dev done --pr| Review
38	    Review -->|feedback: dev resume if WARM| Managed
39	    Review -->|merged externally| Reconcile["dev done --merged: verify exact ancestry"]
40	    Reconcile --> Done
41	
42	    Done -->|dev retire from outside target| Reaped["RETIRED: clean resources and reap task"]
43	    Done -.->|dev sweep| Report["report cleanup candidates"]
44	    Report -.->|approved apply| Reaped
45	    Reaped --> Next["next change stream"]
46	    Next --> Start
47	```
48	
49	The handoff path deliberately stops at manual reconciliation: `dev done --pr` leaves the task active and may only push when no supported forge CLI is available. `dev flow` can explicitly query run-local review existence/state/draft/URL evidence, but neither it nor `sweep` infers DONE from a forge response. Use `dev done --merged` with exact local ancestry evidence.
50	
51	## 1. Select the checkout mode
52	
53	| Mode | Command | Use when |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| direct | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --direct` | one small reversible change in the canonical checkout |
56	| branch-only | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --branch-only --base <ref>` | history isolation is useful but a second directory is not |
57	| worktree | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --base <ref>` | independent mutation, parallel work, or a stream that may outlive the session |
58	
59	Worktree mode is the default. If no branch is supplied, `dev` derives `feat/<task-slug>`; automation should still pass the intended base explicitly.
60	
61	Before changing the canonical checkout in direct or branch-only mode, `dev` guards against sharing it with another active agent/runtime.
62	
63	## 2. Start and inspect
64	
65	```bash
66	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main --next "reproduce expiry race"
67	dev ls
68	dev status
69	dev flow api   # preview all repository surfaces and exact guarded actions
70	```
71	
72	Starting work resolves the repository, validates branch/base, creates or switches the checkout, provisions a worktree when needed, opens the selected runtime, and saves the task. If the branch is already tracked, use `dev resume` instead of creating a duplicate.
73	
74	## 3. Park intentionally
75	
76	```bash
77	dev park --next "add the failing expiry test"
78	```
79	
80	The normal transition is HOT → WARM: close the runtime but keep the checkout. Choose the field by scope:
81	
82	- `--next` is the next executable task action and removes the need to re-derive the first step;
83	- `dev park --note` preserves free-form context for this one task;
84	- `dev repo mark --note` replaces the catalog's single repository summary;
85	- `dev note` stores multiple durable repository observations outside task lifecycle state.
86	
87	If the tree is dirty:
88	
89	```bash
90	dev park --wip --next "finish the expiry test"
91	```
92	
93	This creates a temporary `wip: checkpoint — …` commit. It is searchable and pushable; rewrite or squash it before integrating if it is not useful product history.
94	
95	To release local disk and hand off across machines:
96	
97	```bash
98	dev park --cold --push
99	```
100	
101	COLD requires recoverable commits on the remote. Direct tasks cannot go cold because the canonical checkout is not disposable.
102	
103	## 4. Resume from live facts
104	
105	```bash
106	dev resume "token refresh" --fetch
107	```
108	
109	- WARM: reuse the checkout and reopen the runtime.
110	- COLD: fetch, recreate the branch/worktree if needed, reprovision, and reopen.
111	- Work owned by another host: refuse unless ownership has been deliberately transferred or overridden.
112	
113	Runtime handles are advisory. `dev` re-resolves live sessions instead of assuming a recorded handle still exists.
114	
115	## 5. Integrate or hand off to review
116	
117	Preserve meaningful construction commits:
118	
119	```bash
120	dev done --ff
121	```
122	
123	This requires a clean tree, rebases the task branch onto the base when needed, and runs a fast-forward-only merge in the canonical checkout. It records DONE last while retaining the runtime, worktree, and branch. Run `dev retire` separately from outside the target.
124	
125	Use review/CI instead:
126	
127	```bash
128	dev done --pr
129	```
130	
131	This pushes the branch and opens a GitHub pull request or GitLab merge request when the corresponding CLI is available. It **does not** mark the task DONE or clean up the checkout. Current `dev sweep` also does not infer remote request merges, so confirm integration before finishing the local lifecycle.
132	
133	## The interactive `dev done` finish wizard
134	
135	Running `dev done` with neither `--ff` nor `--pr` on an interactive terminal opens a finish wizard instead of failing. It never guesses which integration mode you want; it walks the actual state of the checkout and asks only what it cannot infer.
136	
137	The wizard runs in up to three steps:
138	
139	1. **Preflight.** It reports the branch, the base, the branch/base commit relation (ahead/behind, or already contained), and — if the checkout is dirty — a path-by-path breakdown of which changes already match the base tree and which are unique.
140	2. **Dirty changes**, only if the checkout is dirty: `c` commits everything with a message you supply, `d` discards everything (tracked and untracked), `q` cancels with nothing changed. Discarding unique content — anything not already equivalent to the base — requires typing `DROP` at a follow-up confirmation; discarding paths that already match the base does not.
141	3. **Integration**, only if neither `--ff` nor `--pr` was passed and the branch is not already fully contained in the base: `f` rebases the branch onto the base and fast-forwards it (same as `--ff`), `p` pushes and opens a pull/merge request (same as `--pr`), `q` cancels. When the branch is already contained in the base, the wizard skips this step and can record DONE; cleanup still belongs to `dev retire`.
142	
143	Passing `--ff` or `--pr` up front answers step 3 for the wizard, so it only prompts for whatever the flags left unresolved — with both a clean tree and an explicit integration flag, nothing is prompted at all. A final summary lists the dirty action and the integration mode before anything runs; confirm it, or add `--yes` to skip that confirmation once the plan is fully specified by flags. If the checkout or branch changes while the plan is open, `dev` detects the drift after confirmation and refuses to apply the stale plan — rerun `dev done` to see the current state.
144	
145	Non-interactively — no TTY, or a script — the wizard never prompts. `dev done` with no integration flag just reports the same preflight and exits; pass `--ff` or `--pr` explicitly. A dirty checkout defaults to failing outside a TTY (`--dirty auto` behaves like `--dirty fail`), so scripts choose an explicit policy:
146	
147	```bash
148	dev done --ff --dirty commit -m "chore: finalize before merge"
149	dev done --pr --dirty discard --yes   # destructive; --yes is mandatory here
150	```
151	
152	`--message`/`-m` only applies with `--dirty commit`. `--dirty discard` outside a TTY requires `--yes`; the `DROP` confirmation is an interactive-only safeguard.
153	
154	## Repository flow preview
155	
156	Use `dev flow [repo]` when the question is not only “what state is this task?”
157	but “which exact action is legal for each checkout?” It is a TTY-only interface
158	independent of the dashboard. It includes every registered worktree plus task-
159	only COLD/DONE rows, separates observed facts from persisted state, and requires
160	Enter-to-plan followed by action-specific approval.
161	
162	Normal managed actions, exact unmanaged metadata-only Adopt/clean branch-
163	preserving Remove, explicit remote fetch/query, revision revalidation, and
164	partial result ledgers are described in [Repository lifecycle
165	flow](repository-flow.md). Flow omits dirty/WIP/shared-writer/takeover/unknown-
166	runtime overrides; use a blocked plan's CLI fallback when those expert flags are
167	actually needed.
168	
169	## 6. Sweep drift and stale state
170	
171	```bash
172	dev sweep                 # report only
173	dev sweep --apply         # confirm each suggested action
174	dev sweep --apply --yes   # automation after reviewing the report
175	```
176	
177	Sweep can propose:
178	
179	- HOT → WARM when no live session exists;
180	- old, clean, pushed WARM → COLD;
181	- removing the registry entry for an already-DONE task;
182	- clearing a worktree path Git no longer knows;
183	- reviewing live runtime sessions no task claims.
184	
185	It never deletes uncommitted work. Reporting first is part of the safety model.
186	
187	## Recovery rules
188	
189	- Rebase conflict: resolve it, run `git rebase --continue`, then retry `dev done --ff`; use `git rebase --abort` to return to the pre-rebase state.
190	- Missing worktree directory: run `dev sweep` or `dev wt rm` to prune stale Git administration, then resume.
191	- Wrong owner host: verify the other writer has stopped and pushed before using an override.
192	- Unsure whether work is merged: keep the branch and task; deletion is cheaper after verification than recovery after guessing.
193	
194	## Sources
195

197	- [`internal/cli/park.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/park.go)
198	- [`internal/cli/resume.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/resume.go)
199	- [`internal/cli/done.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/done.go)

```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2	
3	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
4	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
5	
6	## The problem
7	
8	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
9	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
10	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
11	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
12	
13	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
14	not the runtime.
15	
16	## Pick a checkout mode before a lifecycle
17	
18	A task records human intent; it does not imply a worktree:
19	
20	| Command | Checkout boundary | Use when |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| `dev repo open api` | none; no task | browsing or truly ad-hoc work |
23	| `dev start api -t typo --direct` | current branch, usually main | one short tracked change |
24	| `dev start api -t small --branch-only` | branch in canonical checkout | lightweight isolation, no concurrency |
25	| `dev start api -t auth --base main` | branch + linked worktree | interruption, experiment, parallel writer |
26	
27	In an interactive terminal, bare `dev start` opens the same managed flow as a
28	context-aware wizard. It prompts for repo, task, mode, branch, base and next,
29	then shows the computed checkout/runtime summary before creating anything.
30	`dev start -t <name>` remains the fast path; `--json` and non-TTY use never
31	prompt.
32	
33	With a newly created first-class Herdr worktree, `--run '<shell command>'` can
34	dispatch one reviewed command to the exact root pane. It is separate from the
35	pure `--json` contract, and `--focus` independently controls whether the caller
36	switches after dispatch.
37	
38	Direct tasks go HOT ↔ WARM and finish with plain `dev done`; they cannot go
39	COLD because the canonical checkout cannot be removed. Branch-only tasks can go
40	cold after push by switching the canonical checkout back to base. The full
41	state machine below describes the default worktree mode.
42	
43	Do not create isolation before it has a job. Equally, a new parallel worktree
44	starts from committed HEAD — it does not carry dirty main changes — so
45	checkpoint first when the new task depends on them.
46	
47	## The four states
48	
49	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
50	|---|---|---|---|
51	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
52	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
53	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
54	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
55	
56	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
57	
58	```
59	        dev start
60	            │
61	            ▼
62	         🔥 hot ── prepare/exit/finalize ──► READY
63	          │  ▲                                  │
64	   dev park│  │dev resume                       │ dev done
65	          ▼  │                                  ▼
66	        🌤 warm                             ✅ done / MERGED
67	          │  ▲                                  │
68	dev park  │  │dev resume                        │ external dev retire
69	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)          ▼
70	        ❄️ cold                              RETIRED (entry removed)
71	```
72	
73	The enforced graph is mode-aware: worktree/branch HOT or WARM can park WARM or
74	COLD; WARM/COLD resume HOT; HOT/WARM can complete or hand off review; DONE can
75	only Retire. Direct tasks omit COLD and branch integration. Review handoff is
76	state-preserving. COLD must resume before completion, and no ordinary action
77	moves DONE backward.
78	
79	### Plan it by repository
80	
81	`dev flow [repo]` is an independent preview-labelled, full-screen TUI, not a mode
82	of the dashboard. From a canonical or linked checkout it opens the canonical
83	repository and focuses that exact surface; outside Git it opens a repository
84	picker. It projects every Git-registered worktree plus task-only records such as
85	COLD/DONE tasks without a checkout.
86	
87	The UI shows three layers separately:
88	
89	1. persisted task intent: mode, HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, owner, next, branch/base, and
90	   expected checkout;
91	2. observed facts: exact worktree identity, Git status/operation/refs, runtime and
92	   agent occupancy, artifact readiness, each kept as known/unknown/error/skipped/
93	   loading rather than converting probe failure into false;
94	3. a guarded plan: availability, evidence/remediation, ordered effects, retained
95	   resources, confirmation, exact fallback, task revision, and PlanID.
96	
97	Enter creates the plan; it never applies. READY non-typed plans need `y`; typed
98	plans need the displayed token plus Enter. Apply locks and reloads the task
99	revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority. If any
100	identity changed, it rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Apply itself is
101	not canceled by row movement/refresh/quit; the UI retains completed/failed steps
102	and recovery, then starts a new local read.
103	
104	The preview offers the normal managed choices but no dirty commit/discard, WIP,
105	shared-writer, ownership takeover, or unknown-runtime acknowledgement. Blocked
106	plans point to the compatible CLI fallback instead of adding a force path.
107	`r` reads local state only; `R` explicitly plans fetch, portable review query, or
108	both. Remote evidence is run-local and limited to named refs plus review
109	existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time—not checks or review decisions.
110	
111	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
112	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
113	
114	## Parking
115	
116	```bash
117	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
118	```
119	
120	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
121	next and leaves the checkout boundary exactly where it is. An external caller
122	may close an eligible runtime; when park is invoked from inside its own runtime,
123	it records WARM but deliberately leaves that runtime alive so the agent can exit
124	normally. In direct mode the boundary is the current branch; in worktree mode it
125	is the branch and linked checkout.
126	
127	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
128	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
129	supply one.
130	
131	Before finishing agent work, run `dev prepare` with the exact session UUID and
132	exit normally. The post-writer finalizer—not the still-running agent—stages and
133	commits the exact transcript/plan. A settled Herdr `done` state is not evidence
134	that history, review or commits are complete.
135	
136	Useful variations:
137	
138	```bash
139	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
140	dev park --cold --push            # close session, push, remove worktree
141	dev park --keep-session           # warm only: record state, keep session
142	```
143	
144	`--cold --keep-session` is rejected because a runtime must not remain pointed at
145	a checkout that cold parking removes. A verified runtime-close failure likewise
146	stops cold cleanup before deleting the checkout; warm park reports the close
147	failure and keeps the recorded handle for reconciliation.
148	
149	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
150	
151	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
152	
153	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
154	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
155	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
156	
157	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
158	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
159	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
160	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
161	
162	## Cold, and why it is safe
163	
164	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
165	
166	- the branch still holds every commit;
167	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
168	  them too;
169	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
170	
171	Resume rebuilds/reopens checkout and runtime state only. Persisted runtime
172	handles carry their backend name and are validated against live checkout
173	coverage; stale/missing handles reopen instead of making a task falsely HOT.
174	Production `dev` does not currently attach a Claude/Codex conversation; an agent
175	handoff must supply explicit session/launcher arguments.
176	
177	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
178	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
179	
180	## Moving work between machines
181	
182	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
183	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
184	
185	On the machine holding the work:
186	
187	```bash
188	dev park --cold --push
189	```
190	
191	On the machine picking it up:
192	
193	```bash
194	dev resume <task> --fetch
195	```
196	
197	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
198	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
199	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
200	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
201	
202	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
203	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
204	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
205	
206	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
207	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
208	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
209	
210	## Sweeping
211	
212	```bash
213	dev sweep            # report only
214	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
215	dev sweep --merged-worktrees  # from main, include untracked contained worktrees
216	```
217	
218	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
219	
220	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
```

18	
19	const DefaultLargeLimit int64 = 2 << 20
20	
21	type PrepareRequest struct {
22		Worktree   string
23		TaskID     string
24		Session    string
25		RunID      string
26		Base       string
27		Plans      []string
28		AllowLarge bool
29	}

31	type FinalizeRequest struct {
32		IntentID      string
33		RunID         string
34		Settle        time.Duration
35		WriterStopped bool
36	}
37	
38	// Scanner must redact/scan the staged paths without emitting secret values.
39	type Scanner func(context.Context, string, []string) error
40	
41	// Service coordinates Git with the durable intent store.
42	type Service struct {
43		Store      *Store
44		ScanStaged Scanner
45		LargeLimit int64
46	}
47	
48	// ReadinessState classifies one intent without changing its durable record.
49	type ReadinessState string
50	
51	const (
52		ReadinessPending              ReadinessState = "pending"
53		ReadinessFailed               ReadinessState = "failed"
54		ReadinessDiscarded            ReadinessState = "discarded"
55		ReadinessFinalizedReachable   ReadinessState = "finalized-reachable"
56		ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable ReadinessState = "finalized-unreachable"
57		ReadinessObservationError     ReadinessState = "observation-error"
58	)
59	
60	// IntentReadiness is the read-only finalization evidence for one intent whose
61	// recorded worktree is the exact checkout being inspected.
62	type IntentReadiness struct {
63		Intent           Intent
64		State            ReadinessState
65		Finalized        bool
66		ReceiptReachable bool
67		ObservationError error
68	}
69	
70	// ReadinessInspection is a complete read-only observation for one exact
71	// checkout. KnownEmpty is true only when the store was read successfully and no
72	// intent matched the checkout; it distinguishes absence from failed observation.
73	type ReadinessInspection struct {
74		Checkout         string
75		KnownEmpty       bool
76		Intents          []IntentReadiness
77		ObservationError error
78	}
79	
80	// Ready applies only the existing artifact finalization contract: an exact
81	// checkout is ready when it has no intents, or every intent was explicitly
82	// discarded or has a finalized receipt that is still reachable. Missing or
83	// incomplete evidence fails closed.
84	func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {
85		if i.ObservationError != nil {
86			return false
87		}
88		if len(i.Intents) == 0 {
89			return i.KnownEmpty
90		}
91		if i.KnownEmpty {
92			return false
93		}
94		for _, intent := range i.Intents {
95			if intent.ObservationError != nil {
96				return false
97			}
98			switch intent.State {
99			case ReadinessDiscarded:
100				// Discard is the existing explicit operator escape hatch.
101			case ReadinessFinalizedReachable:
102				if !intent.Finalized || !intent.ReceiptReachable {
103					return false
104				}
105			default:
106				return false
107			}
108		}
109		return true
110	}
111	
112	// InspectReadiness gathers artifact finalization evidence for one exact
113	// checkout. It never reconciles receipts, finalizes intents, or writes either
114	// source files or intent records. The returned inspection retains partial
115	// evidence and the same wrapped error returned separately to ordinary callers.
116	func InspectReadiness(ctx context.Context, store *Store, checkout string) (ReadinessInspection, error) {
117		inspection := ReadinessInspection{}
118		if ctx == nil {
119			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a context")
120			inspection.ObservationError = err
121			return inspection, err
122		}
123		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
124			inspection.ObservationError = err
125			return inspection, err
126		}
127		if store == nil {
128			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a store")
129			inspection.ObservationError = err
130			return inspection, err
131		}
132	
133		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout)
134		if err != nil {
135			err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness checkout: %w", err)
136			inspection.ObservationError = err
137			return inspection, err
138		}
139		inspection.Checkout = canonical
140	
141		intents, err := store.List()
142		if err != nil {
143			err = fmt.Errorf("list artifact intents: %w", err)
144			inspection.ObservationError = err

1	// Package artifact finalizes agent transcripts only after their writer exits.
2	package artifact
3	
4	import (
5		"fmt"
6		"regexp"
7		"strings"
8		"time"
9	)
10	
11	const SchemaVersion = 1
12	
13	type Status string
14	
15	const (
16		Armed      Status = "armed"
17		Finalizing Status = "finalizing"
18		Finalized  Status = "finalized"
19		Failed     Status = "failed"
20		// Discarded records an operator's explicit decision that an intent can
21		// never be finalized — its transcript is gone, or its HEAD no longer
22		// exists. It is deliberately distinct from Finalized: nothing was
23		// committed, and the record survives to say so.
24		Discarded Status = "discarded"
25	)
26	
27	// Intent is a durable handoff from an active agent to an external finalizer.
28	type Intent struct {
29		SchemaVersion      int      `json:"schema_version"`
30		ID                 string   `json:"id"`
31		RunID              string   `json:"run_id"`
32		Provider           string   `json:"provider"`
33		SessionID          string   `json:"session_id"`
34		TaskID             string   `json:"task_id,omitempty"`
35		RepoPath           string   `json:"repo_path"`
36		GitCommonDir       string   `json:"git_common_dir"`
37		WorktreePath       string   `json:"worktree_path"`
38		Branch             string   `json:"branch"`
39		Base               string   `json:"base,omitempty"`
40		Head               string   `json:"head"`
41		PlanPaths          []string `json:"plan_paths,omitempty"`
42		UnrelatedArtifacts []string `json:"unrelated_artifacts,omitempty"`
43		AllowLarge         bool     `json:"allow_large,omitempty"`
44	
45		Status         Status    `json:"status"`
46		TranscriptPath string    `json:"transcript_path,omitempty"`
47		ArtifactCommit string    `json:"artifact_commit,omitempty"`
48		FailureCode    string    `json:"failure_code,omitempty"`
49		SessionEndedAt time.Time `json:"session_ended_at,omitempty"`
50		CreatedAt      time.Time `json:"created_at"`
51		UpdatedAt      time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
52	}
53	
54	var (
55		idPattern      = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`)
56		sessionPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+:[0-9a-fA-F-]{16,}$`)
57	)
58	
59	func (i Intent) Validate() error {
60		switch {
61		case i.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion:
62			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact intent schema %d", i.SchemaVersion)
63		case !idPattern.MatchString(i.ID):
64			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", i.ID)
65		case i.RunID == "" || !idPattern.MatchString(i.RunID):
66			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact run id %q", i.RunID)
67		case i.Provider == "" || i.SessionID == "":
68			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs provider and session id")
69		case i.RepoPath == "" || i.WorktreePath == "" || i.GitCommonDir == "":
70			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs repository, worktree and git common-dir paths")
71		case i.Branch == "" || i.Head == "":
72			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs branch and head")
73		}
74		if !sessionPattern.MatchString(i.Provider + ":" + i.SessionID) {
75			return fmt.Errorf("invalid agent session %q", i.Provider+":"+i.SessionID)
76		}
77		switch i.Status {
78		case Armed, Finalizing, Finalized, Failed, Discarded:
79			return nil
80		default:
81			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent status %q", i.Status)
82		}
83	}
84	
85	func ParseSession(value string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
86		provider, sessionID, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
87		provider = strings.ToLower(provider)
88		if !ok || !sessionPattern.MatchString(provider+":"+sessionID) {
89			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session %q: want provider:uuid", value)
90		}
91		return provider, sessionID, nil
92	}

1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
18	)
19	
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98		// Sessions lets a coordinating caller share one runtime query across task,
99		// repository, and Try inventories.
100		Sessions        []runtime.Session
101		SessionsSet     bool
102		SessionsTracked bool
103		// Limiter shares one process-heavy enrichment bound across collectors.
104		Limiter *Limiter
105	}
106	
107	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
108	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
109	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
110	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
111		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
112	
113		sessions := opts.Sessions
114		tracked := opts.SessionsTracked
115		if !opts.SessionsSet && !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
116			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
117				sessions, tracked = s, true
118			}
119		}
120	
121		var wg sync.WaitGroup
122		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
123		// large inventory would thrash. Coordinated TUI loads share this limiter with
124		// repository enrichment.
125		limiter := opts.Limiter
126		if limiter == nil {
127			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
128		}
129	
130		for i, t := range tasks {
131			rows[i].Task = t
132			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
133	
134			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			wg.Add(1)
138			go func(i int) {
139				defer wg.Done()
140				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
141				if !ok {
142					return
143				}
144				defer release()
145				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
146			}(i)
147		}
148		wg.Wait()
149	
150		for i := range rows {
151			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
152			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
153		}
154		return rows
155	}
156	
157	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
158		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
159			return t.WorktreePath
160		}
161		return t.RepoPath
162	}
163	
164	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
165		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
166		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
167		if !r.CheckoutExists {
168			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
169				r.WorktreeMissing = true
170			}
171			return
172		}
173		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
174			r.StatusErr = err
175		} else {
176			r.Status = st
177		}
178		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
179			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
180		}
181		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
182		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
183		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
184			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
185				r.WorktreeMissing = true
186			}
187		}
188	}
189	
190	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
191	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
192	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
193	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
194		if r.Checkout == "" {
195			return nil
196		}
197		var contains *runtime.Session
198		for i := range sessions {
199			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
200				if d == r.Checkout {
201					return &sessions[i]
202				}
203				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
204					contains = &sessions[i]
205				}
206			}
207		}
208		return contains
209	}
210	
211	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
212	type Filter struct {
213		States []task.State
214		Repo   string
215		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
216		LiveOnly bool
217		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
218		DirtyOnly bool
219	}
220	
221	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
222	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
223		out := rows[:0:0]
224		for _, r := range rows {
225			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
226				continue
227			}

148	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration, retireOptions sweepRetireOptions) []suggestion {
149		t := r.Task
150		var out []suggestion
151		current, currentErr := app.Tasks.GetRecord(t.ID)
152		if currentErr != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(current.Task, *t) {
153			detail := "task changed after the sweep inventory snapshot"
154			if currentErr != nil {
155				detail = "task could not be reloaded after the sweep inventory snapshot: " + currentErr.Error()
156			}
157			return []suggestion{{
158				row: r, reason: detail,
159				action: "rerun sweep to inspect the current task revision — not changed automatically",
160			}}
161		}
162		revision := current.Revision
163	
164		// A task whose repository is gone cannot be finished, resumed, parked or
165		// retired: every one of those resolves the repository first, and `dev done`
166		// refuses outright once the checkout is missing. Nothing else in this
167		// function reaches it either — the dead-branch rule below excludes direct
168		// mode, and the stale-worktree rule needs a recorded worktree path. Left
169		// alone, the record is unreachable by any command in the binary.
170		//
171		// Reaping removes dev's record of intent and nothing else; the branch, the
172		// commits and the remote are untouched. A live session proves the directory
173		// is there, so it is the one condition that rules this out.
174		if t.RepoPath != "" && !r.Live() && !dirExists(t.RepoPath) {
175			out = append(out, suggestion{
176				row:    r,
177				reason: fmt.Sprintf("repository %s no longer exists", config.Contract(t.RepoPath)),
178				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s (Git keeps any work; this drops only dev's record)", t.ID),
179				apply:  func() error { return sweepDeleteTask(ctx, app.Tasks, t.ID, revision) },
180			})
181			return out
182		}
183	
184		out = append(out, orphanSuggestions(app, r)...)
185	
186		switch {
187		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
188		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
189		case t.State == task.Hot && r.StateDrift() == "no live session":
190			reason := fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
191			session, plan, planErr := sweepTaskPlan(ctx, app, t.ID, flow.ParkWarmOptions{})
192			if planErr != nil || plan.Availability != flow.AvailabilityReady {
193				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but guarded warm parking is blocked",
194					action: sweepPlanBlocker(plan, planErr) + " — not changed automatically"})
195				break
196			}
197			out = append(out, suggestion{
198				row: r, reason: reason, action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
199				apply: func() error {
200					result, err := session.apply(ctx, plan, flow.Approve(plan.PlanID))
201					renderLifecycleResult(app, plan, result)
202					return err
203				},
204			})
205	
206		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
207		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
208		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
209			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
210			if t.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeDirect {
211				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but direct tasks cannot go cold",
212					action: "keep it warm or finish it — not changed automatically"})
213				break
214			}
215			if r.Status.Dirty() {
216				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
217					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
218				break
219			}
220			if !r.Status.Synced() {
221				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
222					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})

224			}
225			session, plan, planErr := sweepTaskPlan(ctx, app, t.ID, flow.ParkColdOptions{})

229					action: detail + " — not changed automatically"})
230				break
231			}
232			out = append(out, suggestion{
233				row:    r,
234				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
235				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
236				apply: func() error {

358	// RepoContextOptions extends repository collection without changing the
359	// original CollectRepoContext API used by CLI and dashboard callers.
360	type RepoContextOptions struct {
361		Runtime         string
362		Sessions        []runtime.Session
363		RuntimeObserved bool
364		RuntimeErr      error
365		// Limiter shares one process-heavy enrichment bound across collectors.
366		Limiter *Limiter
367	}
368	
369	// CollectRepoContext joins Git, task and runtime state for one repository. The
370	// legacy entry point can prove observation only when sessions are present;
371	// callers that need a proven empty observation or typed failure use
372	// CollectRepoContextWithOptions.
373	func CollectRepoContext(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, tasks []*task.Task,
374		sessions []runtime.Session, runtimeName string) RepoContext {
375		return CollectRepoContextWithOptions(ctx, r, tasks, RepoContextOptions{
376			Runtime: runtimeName, Sessions: sessions, RuntimeObserved: len(sessions) > 0,
377		})
378	}
379	
380	// CollectRepoContextWithOptions builds repository topology from Git's complete
381	// registered worktree list. It never synthesizes a main checkout after a Git
382	// query failure.
383	func CollectRepoContextWithOptions(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, tasks []*task.Task,
384		opts RepoContextOptions) RepoContext {
385		if ctx == nil {
386			ctx = context.Background()
387		}
388		out := RepoContext{
389			Repo: r, Runtime: opts.Runtime,
390			WorktreeObservation: TopologyObservation{State: ObservationUnobserved},
391			RuntimeObservation:  runtimeObservation(opts),
392		}
393		queryPath := repoQueryPath(r)
394		out.RepositoryID, out.IdentityErr = canonicalRepositoryID(ctx, r, queryPath)
395		out.WorktreeCount = linkedAdminCount(r.CommonDir)
396	
397		var (
398			worktrees []gitx.Worktree
399			err       error
400		)
401		if queryPath == "" {
402			err = fmt.Errorf("repository has no Git query path")
403		} else {
404			worktrees, err = gitx.Worktrees(ctx, queryPath)
405		}
406		if err != nil {
407			listErr := &WorktreeListError{Path: queryPath, Err: err}
408			out.WorktreeErr = listErr
409			out.WorktreeObservation = TopologyObservation{State: ObservationFailed, Err: listErr}
410			assignTasksWithoutTopology(&out, tasks)
411			finishRepoContext(&out)
412			return out
413		}
414		out.WorktreeObservation = TopologyObservation{State: ObservationAvailable}
415		out.WorktreeCount = 0
416		out.Checkouts = make([]RepoCheckout, 0, len(worktrees))
417		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
418			canonicalPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(worktree.Path)
419			if canonicalPath == "" {
420				canonicalPath = filepath.Clean(worktree.Path)
421			}
422			checkout := RepoCheckout{
423				ID: canonicalPath, RepositoryID: out.RepositoryID,
424				IdentityErr: canonicalErr,
425				Worktree:    worktree, Exists: pathIsDir(worktree.Path),
426				RuntimeObservation: out.RuntimeObservation,
427				Ownership:          CheckoutExternal,
428			}
429			if canonicalErr != nil {
430				checkout.ConflictReasons = appendReason(checkout.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
431					Code: ReasonCanonicalPathUnavailable, Detail: canonicalErr.Error(),
432				})
433			}
434			if worktree.Main {
435				checkout.OwnershipEvidence = append(checkout.OwnershipEvidence, OwnershipEvidence{
436					Kind: OwnershipEvidenceGitMain, Path: canonicalPath,
437				})
438			} else {
439				out.WorktreeCount++
440			}
441			out.Checkouts = append(out.Checkouts, checkout)
442		}
443	
444		enrichRepoCheckouts(ctx, out.Checkouts, opts.Limiter)
445		assignHarnessEvidence(&out)
446		assignTasks(&out, tasks)
447		if out.RuntimeObservation.Available() {
448			assignSessions(&out, opts.Sessions)
449		}
450		finishRepoContext(&out)
451		return out
452	}
453	
454	func runtimeObservation(opts RepoContextOptions) TopologyObservation {
455		if opts.RuntimeErr != nil {
456			err := &RuntimeListError{Runtime: opts.Runtime, Err: opts.RuntimeErr}
457			return TopologyObservation{State: ObservationFailed, Err: err}
458		}
459		if opts.RuntimeObserved {
460			return TopologyObservation{State: ObservationAvailable}
461		}
462		return TopologyObservation{State: ObservationUnobserved}
463	}
464	
465	func repoQueryPath(r repo.Repo) string {
466		for _, candidate := range []string{r.Path, r.RealPath, r.MainRoot, r.CommonDir} {
467			if candidate != "" {
468				return candidate
469			}
470		}
471		return ""
472	}
473	
474	func canonicalRepositoryID(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, queryPath string) (string, error) {
475		commonDir := r.CommonDir
476		if commonDir == "" && r.Bare {
477			commonDir = queryPath
478		}
479		if commonDir == "" && queryPath != "" {
480			if discovered, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, queryPath); err == nil {
481				commonDir = discovered.GitCommonDir
482			}
483		}
484		if commonDir == "" {
485			err := fmt.Errorf("Git common directory is empty")
486			return "", &RepositoryIdentityError{Path: commonDir, Err: err}
487		}
488		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
489		if err != nil {
490			return "", &RepositoryIdentityError{Path: commonDir, Err: err}
491		}
492		return canonical, nil
493	}
494	
495	func enrichRepoCheckouts(ctx context.Context, checkouts []RepoCheckout, limiter *Limiter) {
496		if limiter == nil {
497			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
498		}
499		var wg sync.WaitGroup
500		for i := range checkouts {
501			if checkouts[i].Worktree.Bare || checkouts[i].Worktree.Prunable || !checkouts[i].Exists {
502				continue
503			}
504			wg.Add(1)
505			go func(index int) {
506				defer wg.Done()
507				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
508				if !ok {
509					checkouts[index].StatusErr = ctx.Err()
510					return
511				}
512				defer release()
513				checkout := &checkouts[index]
514				checkout.Status, checkout.StatusErr = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout.Worktree.Path)
515				checkout.LastActivity, checkout.LastCommit, checkout.LastSubject = checkoutActivity(
516					ctx, checkout.Worktree.Path, checkout.Status,
517				)
518			}(i)
519		}
520		wg.Wait()
521	}
522	
523	func assignHarnessEvidence(out *RepoContext) {
524		mainRoot := ""
525		for i := range out.Checkouts {
526			if out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Main && !out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Bare {
527				mainRoot = out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Path
528				break
529			}
530		}
531		if mainRoot == "" {
532			return
533		}
534		for i := range out.Checkouts {
535			checkout := &out.Checkouts[i]
536			if checkout.Worktree.Main {
537				continue
538			}
539			evidence, ok := DetectClaudeHarnessWorktree(mainRoot, checkout.Worktree.Path)
540			if !ok {
541				continue
542			}
543			checkout.HarnessEvidence = &evidence
544			checkout.OwnershipEvidence = append(checkout.OwnershipEvidence, OwnershipEvidence{
545				Kind: OwnershipEvidenceClaudeHarness, Path: evidence.Root,
546			})
547		}
548	}

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix

20	
21	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
22	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
23	type Error struct {
24		Args   []string
25		Dir    string
26		Stderr string
27		Err    error
28	}

30	func (e *Error) Error() string {
31		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
32		if msg == "" {
33			msg = e.Err.Error()
34		}
35		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
36	}
37	
38	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
39

41	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
42		return runEnv(ctx, dir, nil, args...)
43	}

45	// runEnv executes git with task-scoped environment overrides. It is used for
46	// alternate-index analysis that must never touch the user's real index.
47	func runEnv(ctx context.Context, dir string, overrides []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
48		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
49		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
50		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
51		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
52		cmd.Dir = dir
53		if len(overrides) > 0 {
54			keys := make(map[string]bool, len(overrides))
55			for _, override := range overrides {
56				key, _, _ := strings.Cut(override, "=")
57				keys[key] = true
58			}
59			env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+len(overrides))
60			for _, entry := range os.Environ() {
61				key, _, _ := strings.Cut(entry, "=")
62				if !keys[key] {
63					env = append(env, entry)
64				}
65			}
66			env = append(env, overrides...)
67			cmd.Env = env
68		}
69		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
70		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
71		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
72		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
73			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
74			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
75				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
76			}
77			return "", gerr
78		}
79		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
80	}

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
101		if err != nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
103		}
104	
105		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
106		if err != nil {
107			// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
108			// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
109			// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
110			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
111		}
112		switch {
113		case rel == ".":
114			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
115		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
117		default:
118			return canonicalCandidate, nil
119		}
120	}
121	
122	// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
123	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
124	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
125		_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
126		if err == nil {
127			return true, nil
128		}
129		if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
130			return false, nil
131		}
132		return false, err
133	}
134	
135	// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
136	func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
137		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
138		if err != nil {
139			return false, err
140		}
141		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
142		if err != nil {
143			return false, err
144		}
145		if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
146			return true, nil
147		}
148		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
149	}
150	
151	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
152	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
153	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
154	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
155		switch {
156		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
157			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
158		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
159			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
160		case component == "." || component == "..":
161			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
162		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
163			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
164		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
165			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
166		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
167			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
168		default:
169			return nil
170		}
171	}
172	
173	// JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
174	// canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
175	// <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
176	// single component.
177	func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
178		if len(components) == 0 {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
180		}
181		for i, component := range components {
182			if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
183				return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
184			}
185		}
186		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
187		if err != nil {
188			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
189		}
190		return CanonicalChild(canonicalRoot, filepath.Join(append([]string{canonicalRoot}, components...)...))
191	}
192	
193	func driveQualified(component string) bool {
194		if len(component) < 2 || component[1] != ':' {
195			return false
196		}
197		letter := component[0]
198		return letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z'
199	}
200	
201	func hasParentTraversal(path string) bool {
202		for _, component := range strings.FieldsFunc(path, func(r rune) bool {
203			return r == '/' || r == '\\'
204		}) {
205			if component == ".." {
206				return true
207			}
208		}
209		return false
210	}
211

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
19	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
20	
21	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
22	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
23	type Error struct {
24		Args   []string
25		Dir    string
26		Stderr string
27		Err    error
28	}
29	
30	func (e *Error) Error() string {
31		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
32		if msg == "" {
33			msg = e.Err.Error()
34		}
35		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
36	}
37	
38	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
39	
40	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
41	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
42		return runEnv(ctx, dir, nil, args...)
43	}
44	
45	// runEnv executes git with task-scoped environment overrides. It is used for
46	// alternate-index analysis that must never touch the user's real index.
47	func runEnv(ctx context.Context, dir string, overrides []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
48		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
49		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
50		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
51		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
52		cmd.Dir = dir
53		if len(overrides) > 0 {
54			keys := make(map[string]bool, len(overrides))
55			for _, override := range overrides {
56				key, _, _ := strings.Cut(override, "=")
57				keys[key] = true
58			}
59			env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+len(overrides))
60			for _, entry := range os.Environ() {
61				key, _, _ := strings.Cut(entry, "=")
62				if !keys[key] {
63					env = append(env, entry)
64				}
65			}
66			env = append(env, overrides...)
67			cmd.Env = env
68		}
69		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
70		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
71		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
72		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
73			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
74			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
75				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
76			}
77			return "", gerr
78		}
79		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
80	}
81	
82	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
83	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
84	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
85		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
86	}
87	
88	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
89	func lines(s string) []string {
90		if s == "" {
91			return nil
92		}
93		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
94		filtered := out[:0]
95		for _, l := range out {
96			if l != "" {
97				filtered = append(filtered, l)
98			}
99		}
100		return filtered
101	}
102	
103	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
104	func nulLines(s string) []string {
105		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
106		if s == "" {
107			return nil
108		}

83		}

85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95	
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101	
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {

105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := ValidateTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114	
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {

119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125		var provisionSettings Settings
126		if !req.NoProvision {
127			provisionSettings, err = SettingsForTrusted(ctx, m.Cfg, repoPath)
128			if err != nil {
129				return nil, err
130			}
131		}
132	
133		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
134			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
135		}
136		if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, req.Branch, base); err != nil {
137			return nil, err
138		}
139		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
140	
141		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
142	
143		if !req.NoProvision {
144			// Trusted settings fold in the repository's portable project config.
145			p := &Provisioner{
146				Settings: provisionSettings,
147				Timeout:  provisionSettings.ProvisionTimeout,
148				Log:      m.Log,
149			}
150			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
151			if err != nil {
152				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
153				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
154			}
155			res.Provision = pr
156		}
157	
158		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
159			label := req.Label
160			if label == "" {
161				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
162			}
163			opened, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
164			if err != nil {
165				m.logf("warning: could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
166			} else {
167				res.Runtime = opened
168				res.RuntimeName = m.Runtime.Name()
169			}
170		}
171		return res, nil
172	}

174	// surface registers the checkout with the runtime. When the backend
175	// understands git worktrees it is asked to open it as one, which is what makes
176	// the checkout appear grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
177	// ahead/behind row rather than as an unrelated directory.
178	func (m *Manager) surface(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
179		if wo, ok := m.Runtime.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
180			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, path, label)
181		}
182		return m.Runtime.Open(ctx, path, label)
183	}

Prepare then writes an Armed intent under only the artifact-store lock, and ParkCold removes the clean worktree and records the task COLD. 13	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
14	type Worktree struct {
15		Path string
16		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
17		Head string
18		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
19		Branch   string
20		Detached bool
21		Bare     bool
22		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
23		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
24		Locked         bool
25		LockedReason   string
26		Prunable       bool
27		PrunableReason string
28		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
29		Main bool
30	}
31	
32	var (
33		// ErrWorktreeNotFound reports that Git's current registry has no worktree at
34		// the requested canonical path.
35		ErrWorktreeNotFound = errors.New("registered worktree not found")
36		// ErrWorktreeAmbiguous reports that multiple Git records resolve to the same
37		// canonical path. Callers must not choose one of the aliases implicitly.
38		ErrWorktreeAmbiguous = errors.New("registered worktree path is ambiguous")
39	)
40	
41	// RegisteredWorktree is an identity snapshot from Git's worktree registry.
42	// Worktree preserves the complete parsed Git record; the other fields are canonical
43	// filesystem identities suitable for exact comparison across symlink and macOS
44	// path aliases. A snapshot proves registration, not permission to remove it.
45	type RegisteredWorktree struct {
46		Worktree       Worktree
47		RepositoryPath string
48		GitCommonDir   string
49		Path           string
50	}
51	
52	// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether the record is a linked checkout rather than
53	// Git's main checkout or a bare repository. It is classification, not a removal
54	// safety decision.
55	func (w RegisteredWorktree) IsLinkedWorktree() bool {
56		return !w.Worktree.Main && !w.Worktree.Bare
57	}
58	
59	// ResolveRegisteredWorktree resolves exactPath against a fresh authoritative
60	// `git worktree list --porcelain` query for the repository containing repoPath.
61	// Matching is exclusively by canonical filesystem identity, never by branch.
62	// It performs no prune, removal, or other mutation.
63	func ResolveRegisteredWorktree(ctx context.Context, repoPath, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
64		worktrees, err := Worktrees(ctx, repoPath)
65		if err != nil {
66			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("query registered worktrees: %w", err)
67		}
68		commonDir, err := run(ctx, repoPath, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
69		if err != nil {
70			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve Git common directory: %w", err)
71		}
72		return resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees, commonDir, exactPath)
73	}
74	
75	func resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees []Worktree, commonDir, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
76		path, err := pathx.Canonical(exactPath)
77		if err != nil {
78			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize requested worktree %q: %w", exactPath, err)
79		}
80		canonicalCommonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
81		if err != nil {
82			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git common directory %q: %w", commonDir, err)
83		}
84	
85		type match struct {
86			worktree Worktree
87			path     string
88		}
89		var (
90			repositoryPath string
91			matches        []match
92		)
93		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
94			canonicalPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(worktree.Path)
95			if canonicalErr != nil {
96				return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize registered worktree %q: %w", worktree.Path, canonicalErr)
97			}
98			if worktree.Main {
99				repositoryPath = canonicalPath
100			}
101			if sameCanonicalPath(path, canonicalPath) {
102				matches = append(matches, match{worktree: worktree, path: canonicalPath})
103			}
104		}
105	
106		switch len(matches) {
107		case 0:
108			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrWorktreeNotFound, path)
109		case 1:
110			if repositoryPath == "" {
111				return RegisteredWorktree{}, errors.New("registered worktree query has no main repository record")
112			}
113			return RegisteredWorktree{
114				Worktree:       matches[0].worktree,
115				RepositoryPath: repositoryPath,
116				GitCommonDir:   canonicalCommonDir,
117				Path:           matches[0].path,
118			}, nil
119		default:
120			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s resolves to %d records", ErrWorktreeAmbiguous, path, len(matches))
121		}
122	}
123	
124	func sameCanonicalPath(left, right string) bool {
125		if left == right {
126			return true
127		}
128		leftInfo, leftErr := os.Stat(left)
129		rightInfo, rightErr := os.Stat(right)
130		return leftErr == nil && rightErr == nil && os.SameFile(leftInfo, rightInfo)
131	}
132	
133	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
134	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
135	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
136		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
137		if err != nil {
138			return nil, err
139		}
140		var (
141			list []Worktree
142			cur  *Worktree
143		)
144		flush := func() {
145			if cur != nil {
146				list = append(list, *cur)
147				cur = nil
148			}
149		}
150		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
151			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
152				flush()
153				continue
154			}
155			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
156			switch key {
157			case "worktree":
158				flush()
159				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
160			case "HEAD":
161				if cur != nil {
162					cur.Head = val
163				}
164			case "branch":
165				if cur != nil {
166					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
167				}
168			case "detached":
169				if cur != nil {
170					cur.Detached = true
171				}
172			case "bare":
173				if cur != nil {
174					cur.Bare = true
175				}
