1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
101		if err != nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
103		}
104	
105		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
106		if err != nil {
107			// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
108			// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
109			// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
110			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
111		}
112		switch {
113		case rel == ".":
114			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
115		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
117		default:
118			return canonicalCandidate, nil
119		}
120	}
121	
122	// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
123	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
124	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
125		_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
126		if err == nil {
127			return true, nil
128		}
129		if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
130			return false, nil
131		}
132		return false, err
133	}
134	
135	// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
136	func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
137		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
138		if err != nil {
139			return false, err
140		}
141		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
142		if err != nil {
143			return false, err
144		}
145		if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
146			return true, nil
147		}
148		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
149	}
150	
151	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
152	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
153	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
154	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
155		switch {
156		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
157			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
158		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
159			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
160		case component == "." || component == "..":
161			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
162		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
163			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
164		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
165			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
166		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
167			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
168		default:
169			return nil
170		}
171	}
172	
173	// JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
174	// canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
175	// <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
176	// single component.
177	func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
178		if len(components) == 0 {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
180		}
181		for i, component := range components {
182			if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
183				return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
184			}
185		}
186		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
187		if err != nil {
188			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
189		}
190		return CanonicalChild(canonicalRoot, filepath.Join(append([]string{canonicalRoot}, components...)...))
191	}
192	
193	func driveQualified(component string) bool {
194		if len(component) < 2 || component[1] != ':' {
195			return false
196		}
197		letter := component[0]
198		return letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z'
199	}
200	
201	func hasParentTraversal(path string) bool {
202		for _, component := range strings.FieldsFunc(path, func(r rune) bool {
203			return r == '/' || r == '\\'
204		}) {
205			if component == ".." {
206				return true
207			}
208		}
209		return false
210	}

197	func shellQuote(s string) string {
198		if s == "" {
199			return "''"
200		}
201		safe := true
202		for _, r := range s {
203			if !(r == '/' || r == '.' || r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '~' ||

209		if safe && utf8.ValidString(s) {

211		}
212		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"

14	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			next            string
17			note            string
18			wip             bool
19			push            bool
20			cold            bool
21			keepRT          bool
22			closeUnknown    bool
23			assumeNoRuntime bool
24			timeout         time.Duration
25		)
26		cmd := &cobra.Command{
27			Use:   "park [task]",
28			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
29			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
30	
31	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
32	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
33	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
34	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
35	
36	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
37	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, session closed, worktree
38	                  removed. Reconstruct it anywhere later with dev resume.
39	
40	--cold and --keep-session are incompatible: a runtime cannot stay pointed at a
41	checkout that cold parking removes.
42	
43	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
44	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
45	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
46			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
47			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
48				ctx := ctxOf()
49				if cold && keepRT {
50					return fmt.Errorf("--cold and --keep-session cannot be combined: a session must not remain pointed at a removed checkout")
51				}
52	
53				var options taskflow.ActionOptions
54				if cold {
55					options = taskflow.ParkColdOptions{
56						Next: next, Note: note, CommitWIP: wip, Push: push,
57						CloseUnknown: closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: assumeNoRuntime, Timeout: timeout,
58					}
59				} else {
60					options = taskflow.ParkWarmOptions{
61						Next: next, Note: note, CommitWIP: wip, Push: push, KeepSession: keepRT,
62						CloseUnknown: closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: assumeNoRuntime, Timeout: timeout,
63					}
64				}
65				execution, err := executeTaskLifecycle(ctx, app, func() (*task.Task, error) {
66					return resolveTask(app, args)
67				}, options)
68				if err != nil {
69					return err
70				}
71	
72				parked := &execution.Task
73				style := app.outStyle()
74				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", parked.State.Icon(), parked.Title(),
75					style.taskStateFor(string(parked.State), parked.State.Label()))
76				if parked.Next != "" {
77					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — %s %s", style.label("next:"), parked.Next)
78				}
79				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
80				return nil
81			},
82		}
83		f := cmd.Flags()
84		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
85		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
86		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
87		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
88		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
89		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
90		f.BoolVar(&closeUnknown, "close-unknown", false, "allow external closure of unknown runtime status")
91		f.BoolVar(&assumeNoRuntime, "assume-no-runtime", false, "continue when runtime enumeration fails")
92		f.DurationVar(&timeout, "timeout", 5*time.Second, "maximum time to wait for runtime closure")
93		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Hot, task.Warm)
94		return cmd
95	}

97	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
98	// directory when no argument is given.
99	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
100		if len(args) == 1 {
101			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
102		}
103		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
104		if err != nil {
105			return nil, err
106		}
107		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
110				config.Contract(cwd))
111		}
112		return t, nil
113	}

897	func fleetConfigEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
898		path := fleetConfigPath(app)
899		if _, err := os.Stat(path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
900			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
901				return nil, err
902			}

905				return nil, err
906			}

909		if err != nil {
910			return nil, err
911		}
912		process := exec.Command(shellPath(), "-c", chosen+" "+shellQuote(path))
913		process.Stdin, process.Stdout, process.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
914		return process, nil
915	}

427	func (s *lifecycleService) handler(action Action) Handler {
428		return Handler{
429			Plan: func(ctx context.Context, request Request) (PlanSpec, error) {
430				return s.planSpec(ctx, request)
431			},
432			Apply: func(ctx context.Context, plan Plan) (Result, error) {
433				return s.applyGuarded(ctx, action, plan)
434			},
435		}
436	}
437	
438	func (s *lifecycleService) now() time.Time { return s.clock().UTC() }
439	
440	func (s *lifecycleService) runtimeFor(candidate task.Task) (runtime.Runtime, error) {
441		var rt runtime.Runtime
442		if candidate.RuntimeHandle != "" && candidate.RuntimeName != "" {
443			rt = s.namedRuntime(candidate.RuntimeName)
444			if rt == nil {
445				return nil, fmt.Errorf("recorded runtime backend %q is unavailable", candidate.RuntimeName)
446			}
447			if rt.Name() != candidate.RuntimeName {
448				return nil, fmt.Errorf("recorded runtime backend %q resolved to %q", candidate.RuntimeName, rt.Name())
449			}
450		} else {
451			rt = s.defaultRuntime()
452		}
453		if rt == nil || strings.TrimSpace(rt.Name()) == "" {
454			return nil, errors.New("taskflow runtime resolver returned no backend")
455		}
456		return rt, nil
457	}
458	
459	func openRuntimeSurface(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, path, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
460		if rt == nil {
461			return runtime.OpenResult{}, errors.New("open runtime: no backend")
462		}
463		if worktreeRuntime, ok := rt.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
464			return worktreeRuntime.OpenWorktree(ctx, path, label)
465		}
466		return rt.Open(ctx, path, label)
467	}

469	type lifecycleLogWriter struct{ logf LogFunc }
470	
471	func (w lifecycleLogWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
472		for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(string(data), "\n"), "\n") {
473			if line != "" {
474				w.logf("%s", line)
475			}
476		}
477		return len(data), nil
478	}

163	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
164	// flight but is not yet recorded.
165	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
166		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
167	
168		var out []candidate
169		seen := map[string]bool{}
170	
171		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
172			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
173				return
174			}
175			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
176			if known[id] {
177				return
178			}
179			seen[branch] = true
180			mode := task.ModeBranch
181			if worktree != "" {
182				mode = task.ModeWorktree
183			}
184			out = append(out, candidate{
185				Reason: reason,
186				Task: &task.Task{
187					ID:           id,
188					Name:         branch,
189					Repo:         r.Name,
190					RepoPath:     r.Path,
191					Branch:       branch,
192					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
193					WorktreePath: worktree,
194					Mode:         mode,
195					State:        state,
196					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
197				},
198			})
199		}
200	
201		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
202		if err != nil {
203			return nil
204		}
205	
206		if doWorktrees {
207			for _, w := range worktrees {
208				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
209					continue
210				}
211				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
212				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
213				// the harness will delete on its own.
214				if inventory.IsEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
215					continue
216				}
217				state := target
218				reason := "existing worktree"
219				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
220					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
221				}
222				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
223			}
224		}
225	
226		if doSessions {
227			for i := range sessions {
228				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
229					if d != r.Path {
230						continue
231					}
232					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
233					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
234						continue
235					}
236					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
237				}
238			}
239		}
240	
241		if doBranches {
242			for _, branch := range unmergedBranches(ctx, r.Path) {
243				add(branch, worktreePathFor(worktrees, branch), "branch ahead of the base", target)
244			}
245		}
246		return out
247	}
248	
249	func sessionAt(sessions []runtime.Session, dir string) *runtime.Session {
250		for i := range sessions {
251			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
252				if d == dir {
253					return &sessions[i]
254				}
255			}
256		}
257		return nil
258	}
259	
260	func worktreePathFor(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch string) string {
261		for _, w := range worktrees {
262			if w.Branch == branch && !w.Main {
263				return w.Path
264			}
265		}
266		return ""
267	}
268	
269	// unmergedBranches lists local branches carrying commits the default branch
270	// does not — unfinished work that would otherwise be invisible to dev.
271	func unmergedBranches(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) []string {
272		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
273		if base == "" {
274			return nil
275		}
276		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/heads/")
277		if err != nil {
278			return nil
279		}
280		var branches []string
281		for _, b := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
282			b = strings.TrimSpace(b)
283			if b == "" || b == base || inventory.IsEphemeralWorktree("", b) {
284				continue
285			}
286			// Contained in the base means the work has already landed.
287			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", b, base); err == nil {
288				continue
289			}
290			branches = append(branches, b)
291		}
292		return branches
293	}

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Identifying a major bug**

I’m noticing some issues with the status update logic. The `sameStatus` seems to ignore changes in content and only uses counts and references, which is problematic. This leads to major bugs because, in the ParkWarm/Cold WIP, an immediate rebuild happens but allows modifications without tracking them. `revalidateGitBaseline` fails to consider these untracked content changes, which could lead to issues before applying commits, and that could mess everything up! I need to ensure we account for those content fingerprints. 

**Analyzing plan and concurrency issues**

I’m realizing there’s a serious issue with the contract plan regarding status and worktree management. The destructive discard mechanism is using a Finish fingerprint, but the Park WIP doesn’t have that, which introduces a concurrency bug. If a user asks about removing guards, it's specific to a HOT checkout scenario. Even when contents change, the status counts remain unchanged, leading to problematic commits. The plan should really hash the bytes to ensure any modifications by users during prompts are captured. It all feels a bit chaotic, and I need to clarify these processes! 

**Clarifying WIP and commit processes**

I'm considering how to structure the reporting for `baseAuthority` in relation to status and `revalidateGitBaseline`. It seems like there could be about six candidates that fit in. For ParkCold, without WIP, there should be a clean state—but what happens if another writer modifies an existing file? The status counts would change from clean to dirty, but the plan is blocked without WIP. Meanwhile, the Warm state keeps the bytes intact, allowing pushes even if they’re dirty. I’m thinking that the WIP process is crucial for tracking mutations into commits, especially remotely.

242			Runtime: startRuntimeJSON{

274	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
275	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
276	// anyone having to ask dev.
277	//
278	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
279	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
280	//
281	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
282	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
283	//
284	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
285	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
286	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
287		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
288			return
289		}
290		kv := map[string]string{
291			"stage": t.State.Label(),
292			"next":  t.Next,
293		}
294		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
295			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
296		}
297	}
298	
299	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
300		p := res.Provision
301		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
302			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
303		}
304		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
305			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
306		}
307		for _, e := range p.Failures {
308			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
309		}
310	}
311

61	func resolveStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref string) (repo.Repo, error) {
62		if ref != "" {
63			r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), ref)
64			return r, err
65		}
66		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
67		if err != nil {
68			return repo.Repo{}, err
69		}
70		g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
71		if err != nil {
72			return repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("no repo argument and %s is not a git repository", config.Contract(cwd))
73		}
74		return repo.Repo{
75			Name: g.Name, Path: g.MainRoot, RealPath: g.MainRoot,
76			MainRoot: g.MainRoot, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
77		}, nil
78	}
79	
80	func buildStartSpec(ctx context.Context, app *App, req startRequest) (*startSpec, error) {
81		r, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, req.RepoRef)
82		if err != nil {
83			return nil, err
84		}
85		return buildStartSpecForRepository(ctx, app, r, req)
86	}
87	
88	func buildStartSpecForRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, req startRequest) (*startSpec, error) {
89		if r.Bare {
90			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is a bare repository and cannot host a task checkout", r.Display())
91		}
92	
93		name := strings.TrimSpace(req.Name)
94		if name == "" && req.Branch != "" && req.Mode != task.ModeDirect {
95			name = req.Branch
96		}
97		if name == "" {
98			return nil, errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
99		}
100	
101		branch, base := strings.TrimSpace(req.Branch), strings.TrimSpace(req.Base)
102		mode := req.Mode
103		if mode == "" {
104			mode = task.ModeWorktree
105		}
106		switch mode {
107		case task.ModeDirect:
108			st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			if st.Detached || st.Branch == "" {
113				return nil, errors.New("--direct needs a named branch; this checkout has detached HEAD")
114			}
115			if branch != "" && branch != st.Branch {
116				return nil, fmt.Errorf("--direct tracks the branch already checked out (%s), not --branch %s; "+
117					"omit --branch or use --branch-only", st.Branch, branch)
118			}
119			branch, base = st.Branch, st.Branch
120	
121		case task.ModeBranch, task.ModeWorktree:
122			if branch == "" {
123				branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
124			}
125			if base == "" {
126				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path)
127			}
128			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, "check-ref-format", "--branch", branch); err != nil {
129				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid branch %q: %w", branch, err)
130			}
131			if !gitx.BranchExists(ctx, r.Path, branch) {
132				if base == "" {
133					return nil, errors.New("cannot determine a base ref; enter one explicitly")
134				}
135				if !gitx.RefExists(ctx, r.Path, base) {
136					return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, r.Path)
137				}
138			}
139	
140		default:
141			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown start mode %q", mode)
142		}
143		if req.Run != "" && mode != task.ModeWorktree {
144			return nil, errors.New("--run requires the default worktree mode; it cannot be used with --direct or --branch-only")
145		}
146	
147		id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
148		if existing, err := app.Tasks.Get(id); err == nil && existing.State != task.Done {
149			return nil, fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
150				existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
151		}
152	
153		spec := &startSpec{
154			RepoPath: r.Path, RepoName: r.Name, Category: r.Category,
155			Name: name, Branch: branch, Base: base, Next: req.Next, Run: req.Run, Mode: mode,
156			NoProvision: req.NoProvision, Focus: req.Focus,
157		}
158		if mode == task.ModeWorktree {
159			if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Path, branch); err != nil {
160				return nil, err
161			} else if ok {
162				return nil, &wt.ErrExists{Branch: branch, Path: existing.Path}
163			}
164			path, err := app.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(r.Name, r.Path, branch, r.Category)
165			if err != nil {
166				return nil, err
167			}
168			if err := wt.ValidateTarget(path, r.Path); err != nil {
169				return nil, err
170			}
171			spec.WorktreePath = path
172		}
173		return spec, nil
174	}
175	
176	func executeStartSpec(ctx context.Context, app *App, spec *startSpec, log io.Writer) (*startResult, error) {
177		id := task.MakeID(spec.RepoName, spec.Branch)
178		if existing, err := app.Tasks.Get(id); err == nil && existing.State != task.Done {
179			return nil, fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
180				existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
181		}
182	
183		t := &task.Task{
184			Name: spec.Name, Repo: spec.RepoName, RepoPath: spec.RepoPath,
185			Branch: spec.Branch, Base: spec.Base, Mode: spec.Mode,
186			State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(), Next: spec.Next,
187		}
188		rt := app.Runtime()
189		label := worktreeRuntimeLabel(spec.RepoName, spec.Branch)
190		if spec.Mode == task.ModeDirect {
191			label = spec.RepoName + "/" + spec.Name
192		}
193		result := &startResult{Task: t, Runtime: rt}
194	
195		switch spec.Mode {
196		case task.ModeDirect:
197			if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, spec.RepoPath); err != nil {
198				return nil, err
199			}
200			opened, err := rt.Open(ctx, spec.RepoPath, label)
201			if err != nil {
202				app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
203			} else {
204				result.Opened = opened
205			}
206	
207		case task.ModeBranch:
208			if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, spec.RepoPath); err != nil {
209				return nil, err
210			}
211			if gitx.BranchExists(ctx, spec.RepoPath, spec.Branch) {
212				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, spec.RepoPath, "switch", spec.Branch); err != nil {
213					return nil, fmt.Errorf("switch to %s: %w", spec.Branch, err)
214				}
215			} else if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, spec.RepoPath, "switch", "-c", spec.Branch, spec.Base); err != nil {
216				return nil, fmt.Errorf("create and switch to %s from %s: %w", spec.Branch, spec.Base, err)
217			}
218			opened, err := rt.Open(ctx, spec.RepoPath, label)
219			if err != nil {
220				app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
221			} else {
222				result.Opened = opened
223			}
224	
225		case task.ModeWorktree:
226			m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: log}
227			created, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
228				RepoPath: spec.RepoPath, RepoName: spec.RepoName,
229				Branch: spec.Branch, Base: spec.Base, Category: spec.Category,
230				Path: spec.WorktreePath, Label: label,
231				NoProvision: spec.NoProvision, Focus: spec.Focus,
232			})
233			if err != nil {
234				return nil, err
235			}
236			t.WorktreePath, result.Opened, result.Worktree = created.Path, created.Runtime, created
237		}
238	
239		setTaskRuntime(t, rt, result.Opened)
240		if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
241			return nil, err
242		}
243		annotate(app, rt, t)
244		return result, nil
245	}

13	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
14		var (
15			noProvision bool
16			fetch       bool
17			force       bool
18		)
19		cmd := &cobra.Command{
20			Use:   "resume <task>",
21			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
22			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
23	
24	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
25	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
26	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
27	identity.
28	
29	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
30	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
31	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
32			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
33			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
34				ctx := ctxOf()
35				execution, err := executeTaskLifecycle(ctx, app, func() (*task.Task, error) {
36					return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				}, taskflow.ResumeOptions{
38					FetchRefs: fetch, NoProvision: noProvision, TakeOwnership: force,
39				})
40				if err != nil {
41					return err
42				}
43	
44				resumed := &execution.Task
45				handoff, ok := execution.Result.Handoff()
46				if !ok || handoff.Path == "" {
47					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is HOT, but resume returned no activation handoff", resumed.ID)
48				}
49				checkout := handoff.Path
50				var activationRuntime runtime.Runtime
51				switch handoff.Kind {
52				case taskflow.HandoffDirectory:
53					if resumed.RuntimeName != "" || resumed.RuntimeHandle != "" {
54						return fmt.Errorf("task %s returned a directory handoff with persisted runtime %s/%s",
55							resumed.ID, resumed.RuntimeName, resumed.RuntimeHandle)
56					}
57				case taskflow.HandoffRuntime:
58					activationRuntime = app.runtimeNamed(handoff.Runtime)
59					if activationRuntime == nil || activationRuntime.Name() != handoff.Runtime {
60						return fmt.Errorf("resume handoff backend %q is unavailable", handoff.Runtime)
61					}
62					if resumed.RuntimeName != handoff.Runtime || resumed.RuntimeHandle != handoff.RuntimeHandle {
63						return fmt.Errorf("task %s persisted runtime %s/%s, but resume handed off %s/%s",
64							resumed.ID, resumed.RuntimeName, resumed.RuntimeHandle, handoff.Runtime, handoff.RuntimeHandle)
65					}
66					annotate(app, activationRuntime, resumed)
67				default:
68					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is HOT, but resume returned unsupported %s handoff", resumed.ID, handoff.Kind)
69				}
70	
71				mode := resumed.EffectiveMode()
72				style := app.outStyle()
73				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
74					task.Hot.Icon(), resumed.Title(), resumed.Repo, resumed.Branch, style.dim(string(mode)))
75				if resumed.Next != "" {
76					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s      %s\n", style.label("next"), resumed.Next)
77				}
78				if resumed.AgentSession != "" {
79					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s     %s (resumable)\n", style.label("agent"), resumed.AgentSession)
80				}
81				if st, statusErr := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); statusErr == nil {
82					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s       %s\n", style.label("git"), style.git(st.Summary()))
83					if st.Behind > 0 {
84						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
85					}
86				}
87				if handoff.Kind == taskflow.HandoffDirectory {
88					return app.cdDirective(checkout)
89				}
90				return activateRuntime(ctx, activationRuntime, handoff.RuntimeHandle)
91			},
92		}
93		f := cmd.Flags()
94		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
95		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
96		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
97		cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Warm, task.Cold)
98		return cmd
99	}
100

122	// exactUnmanagedWorktreeLocator converts a branch-selected checkout into the
123	// canonical identity taskflow requires. Branch lookup is only selection; fresh
124	// Git registry evidence supplies every authority field used by the plan.
125	func exactUnmanagedWorktreeLocator(ctx context.Context, repoPath, checkoutPath string) (flow.Locator, error) {
126		registered, err := gitx.ResolveRegisteredWorktree(ctx, repoPath, checkoutPath)
127		if err != nil {
128			return flow.Locator{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve exact registered worktree %s: %w", config.Contract(checkoutPath), err)
129		}
130		return flow.Locator{
131			RepoKey:      registered.GitCommonDir,
132			RowKey:       registered.Path,
133			RowKind:      "unmanaged",
134			RepositoryID: registered.GitCommonDir,
135			GitCommonDir: registered.GitCommonDir,
136			RepoPath:     registered.RepositoryPath,
137			CheckoutPath: registered.Path,
138			Branch:       registered.Worktree.Branch,
139			HeadOID:      registered.Worktree.Head,
140		}, nil
141	}

143	// executeNonTaskLifecycle applies an exact non-task plan as an explicitly
144	// invoked CLI action. Destructive compatibility flags authorize only the typed
145	// token sealed into that same plan; they do not change readiness or blockers.
146	func executeNonTaskLifecycle(
147		ctx context.Context,
148		app *App,
149		locator flow.Locator,
150		options flow.ActionOptions,
151		authorizeTyped bool,
152	) (nonTaskLifecycleExecution, error) {
153		var execution nonTaskLifecycleExecution
154		service, err := newCLILifecycleService(app)
155		if err != nil {
156			return execution, err
157		}
158		request, err := flow.NewRequest(locator, options)
159		if err != nil {
160			return execution, err
161		}
162		execution.Plan, err = service.Plan(ctx, request)
163		if err != nil {
164			return execution, err
165		}
166		approval := flow.Approve(execution.Plan.PlanID)
167		if execution.Plan.Confirmation.Kind == flow.ConfirmationTyped {
168			if !authorizeTyped {
169				return execution, fmt.Errorf("%s requires its exact typed confirmation", execution.Plan.Summary)
170			}
171			approval = flow.ApproveWithToken(execution.Plan.PlanID, execution.Plan.Confirmation.Token)
172		}
173		execution.Result, err = service.Apply(ctx, execution.Plan, approval)
174		renderLifecycleResult(app, execution.Plan, execution.Result)
175		if err != nil {
176			return execution, presentLifecycleApplyError(execution.Plan, err)
177		}
178		return execution, nil
179	}

267	// WipCommit stages non-agent product work and records a checkpoint commit.
268	// Moving transcripts/plans are deliberately excluded: their exact final bytes
269	// belong to the post-writer artifact finalizer, never an in-process checkpoint.
270	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
271		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
272		if err != nil {
273			return false, err
274		}
275		if !st.Dirty() {
276			return false, nil
277		}
278		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
279			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
280				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
281		}
282		paths, err := ChangedPaths(ctx, dir)
283		if err != nil {
284			return false, err
285		}
286		hasProductWork := false
287		for _, path := range paths {
288			if !IsAgentArtifact(path) {
289				hasProductWork = true
290				break
291			}
292		}
293		if !hasProductWork {
294			return false, nil
295		}
296		args := []string{"add", "-A", "--", "."}
297		for _, pattern := range AgentArtifactPathspecs() {
298			args = append(args, ":(exclude)"+pattern)
299		}

```text
1	# Adopting an existing setup
2	
3	What to do on a machine that already has repositories, worktrees and sessions.
4	
5	## There is nothing to migrate
6	
7	`dev` does not own a directory layout. It discovers repositories below
8	`paths.scan_roots` and at exact `paths.repo_paths`, and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you
9	already have. Whatever your projects tree looks like — `~/Documents/Program`,
10	`~/src`, `~/code`, a ghq root, several of them — it keeps working as is.
11	
12	```bash
13	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots and writes a config
14	dev repo list       # confirm it found what you expected
15	```
16	
17	`config init` probes the conventional locations, counts the repositories in
18	each, and writes only the ones that exist. If it guessed wrong, the generated
19	file is ordinary TOML — edit `scan_roots`, or add an exact checkout such as
20	`~/.local/share/chezmoi` to `repo_paths`.
21	
22	## Importing work already in flight
23	
24	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work that
25	is already happening and offers to record it:
26	
27	```bash
28	dev adopt                   # report only
29	dev adopt --apply           # record, confirming each one
30	```
31	
32	It looks for three things:
33	
34	- **linked worktrees** git already knows about, from any tool;
35	- **live runtime sessions** sitting in a repository;
36	- **local branches ahead of the default branch** — unfinished work that is
37	  otherwise invisible.
38	
39	It skips branches already contained in the base (that work has landed) and the
40	turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness creates and cleans up itself.
41	
42	Nothing on disk changes either way. Adopting only writes task entries.
43	
44	For one exact linked checkout, `dev flow [repo]` offers the same metadata-only
45	boundary without applying the command-wide candidate report. Select an
46	`unmanaged` row, choose **Adopt**, inspect the plan, then approve it. The plan
47	revalidates Git/worktree/task/base/runtime/agent identity and refuses canonical,
48	harness-owned, already-claimed, locked/prunable, detached, or ambiguous rows.
49	A dirty checkout may be adopted because no bytes change. With runtime `none`,
50	occupancy is unobserved and the new task remains WARM rather than being called
51	falsely HOT.
52	
53	Afterwards, give the ones you care about a next action — that is what makes
54	parking them cheap later:
55	
56	```bash
57	dev park <task> --next "…"
58	```
59	
60	## Worktrees you already have elsewhere
61	
62	A worktree created by hand, or by another tool, in a location that is not
63	`paths.worktree_path` keeps working exactly as it did. `dev` records the path
64	git reports; it does not relocate it.
65	
66	New worktrees go to the configured template. If you want the old ones there
67	too, move them the way git expects:
68	
69	```bash
70	git worktree move <old-path> ~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
71	```
72	
73	There is no need to. Consistency is nice; disruption is not.
74	
75	## A different projects root
76	
77	```toml
78	[paths]
79	scan_roots    = ["/mnt/work/repos", "~/code"]
80	project_root  = "/mnt/work/repos"
81	worktree_root = "/mnt/work/worktrees"
82	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
83	```
84	
85	`project_root` is only used by `dev repo new|clone` and `dev graduate` to
86	decide where a *new* project goes. Existing ones are found through
87	`scan_roots` regardless.
88	
89	## Trying it without committing to anything
90	
91	Every path is overridable per invocation, so you can point a throwaway config
92	at a sandbox and see what happens:
93	
94	```bash
95	dev --config /tmp/try-dev.toml config init
96	dev --config /tmp/try-dev.toml ls
97	```
98	
99	And `dev --no-runtime` keeps it from touching your multiplexer at all.
100
```

327	// Focus selects a workspace without attaching a client. Remote fleet
328	// navigation uses it before launching a local `herdr --remote` thin client.
329	func (h *Herdr) Focus(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
330		if handle == "" {
331			return nil
332		}
333		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", handle)
334	}
335	
336	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
337	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
338	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
339	// ahead/behind row.
340	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
341		args := []string{"worktree", "open"}
342		if source := h.parentWorktreeSource(ctx, path); source != "" {
343			// Pin the canonical parent checkout instead of relying on the calling
344			// pane. This preserves native nested grouping even when dev is invoked
345			// from a different Herdr workspace.
346			args = append(args, "--cwd", source)
347		}
348		args = append(args, "--path", path, "--no-focus")
349		if label != "" {
350			args = append(args, "--label", label)
351		}
352		var res struct {
353			Workspace   herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
354			Worktree    herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
355			RootPane    herdrPane      `json:"root_pane"`
356			AlreadyOpen *bool          `json:"already_open"`
357		}
358		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
359			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
360			// more than it being tagged with git provenance. A fallback root pane is
361			// withheld so callers cannot mistake it for a first-class worktree target.
362			fallback, fallbackErr := h.Open(ctx, path, label)
363			fallback.RootPaneID = ""
364			fallback.Surface = "workspace"
365			return fallback, fallbackErr
366		}
367		handle := res.Workspace.WorkspaceID
368		if handle == "" {
369			handle = res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID
370		}
371		if handle == "" {
372			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response has no workspace id")
373		}
374		if res.AlreadyOpen == nil {
375			// Without this protocol field, the handle may belong to a reused
376			// workspace. Do not close it or expose its pane as newly created.
377			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response does not say whether the workspace was reused")
378		}
379		created := !*res.AlreadyOpen
380		if created && (res.RootPane.PaneID == "" || res.RootPane.WorkspaceID != handle) {
381			return OpenResult{}, h.rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx, handle,
382				"herdr worktree open: new workspace response has no correlated root pane")
383		}
384		rootPaneID := ""
385		if created {
386			rootPaneID = res.RootPane.PaneID
387		}
388		return OpenResult{
389			Handle: handle, Surface: "worktree", Opened: true,
390			Created: created, RootPaneID: rootPaneID,
391		}, nil
392	}
393	
394	func (h *Herdr) rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx context.Context, handle, reason string) error {
395		if err := h.Close(ctx, handle); err != nil {
396			return fmt.Errorf("%s; could not close incomplete workspace %s: %w", reason, handle, err)
397		}
398		return fmt.Errorf("%s; closed incomplete workspace %s", reason, handle)
399	}
400	
401	func (h *Herdr) parentWorktreeSource(ctx context.Context, path string) string {
402		if h.worktreeSource != nil {
403			return h.worktreeSource(ctx, path)
404		}
405		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-C", path, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
406		out, err := cmd.Output()
407		if err != nil {
408			return ""
409		}
410		var parent string
411		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
412			switch {
413			case strings.HasPrefix(line, "worktree ") && parent == "":
414				parent = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "worktree "))
415			case line == "" && parent != "":
416				if info, err := os.Stat(parent); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
417					return filepath.Clean(parent)
418				}
419				return ""

**Analyzing agent efficiency**

I’m thinking about how each agent saves around 60ms during inspections, while the plan and apply steps take about 120ms plus some extra revalidation time, which seems realistic. If there are a lot of unrelated sessions or panes, this could lead to several seconds lost if there are 39 sessions—definitely significant. I need precision here: just one agent at the target means an inspection target of one, a session pane of one, and an activity of one. 

**Considering agent functions**

I’m realizing that the candidates are roughly twice as efficient per agent. It’s important to note that all session panes, not just agents, get discovery. The fallback for AgentActivityLister is somewhat limited; it only appends occupancy for agents from covering sessions and repeats CWD, but just for those covering sessions. Herdr does support AgentActivities, while Tmux avoids repeating activities unless they have the same CWD across panes or targets. Each call in Plan and Apply observes things freshly.

857		lines := []string{

859			"branch: " + branch,

861				checkout.Worktree.Main, checkout.Worktree.Locked, checkout.Worktree.Prunable,
862				checkout.Worktree.Bare, checkout.Worktree.Detached, emptyEvidence(checkout.Worktree.Head)),
863		}

865			lines = append(lines, "registered lock reason: "+emptyEvidence(checkout.Worktree.LockedReason))
866		}
867		if checkout.Worktree.Prunable {
868			lines = append(lines, "registered prunable reason: "+emptyEvidence(checkout.Worktree.PrunableReason))
869		}
870		switch {
871		case checkout.StatusErr != nil:
872			lines = append(lines, "git: ERROR "+checkout.StatusErr.Error())
873		case checkout.Worktree.Bare:
874			lines = append(lines, "git: status unobserved (bare repository)")
875		case checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists:
876			lines = append(lines, "git: status unobserved (checkout unavailable)")
877		default:
878			cleanliness := "clean"
879			if checkout.Status.Dirty() {
880				cleanliness = "dirty — " + checkout.Status.Breakdown()
881			}
882			lines = append(lines,
883				"git: "+cleanliness,
884				"upstream: "+emptyEvidence(checkout.Status.Upstream),
885				fmt.Sprintf("ahead=%d behind=%d conflicted=%d", checkout.Status.Ahead, checkout.Status.Behind, checkout.Status.Conflicted),
886			)
887		}
888	
889		observation := checkout.RuntimeObservation
890		if observation.State == "" {
891			observation = contextSnapshot.RuntimeObservation
892		}
893		switch observation.State {
894		case inventory.ObservationAvailable:
895			if len(checkout.Sessions) == 0 {
896				lines = append(lines, "runtime "+emptyEvidence(contextSnapshot.Runtime)+": observed; no covering sessions")
897			} else {

905					if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
906						line += " agents=" + strings.Join(session.AgentSessions, ",")
907					}
908					lines = append(lines, line)
909					for _, pane := range session.Panes {
910						if pane.Agent == "" && pane.AgentSession == "" && pane.AgentStatus == "" {
911							continue
912						}
913						paneStatus := pane.AgentStatus
914						if paneStatus == "" {
915							paneStatus = "unknown"
916						}
917						lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("runtime agent pane: %s agent=%s state=%s session=%s",
918							emptyEvidence(pane.ID), emptyEvidence(pane.Agent), paneStatus, emptyEvidence(pane.AgentSession)))
919					}
920				}
921			}

924			if observation.Err != nil {

926			}

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-02 05:18:44Z)**_

A concrete accepted value is `Next: "#resume-later"`: park option validation checks only timeout, and the Cobra string flag imposes no character restriction. The renderer therefore emits `--next #resume-later`; POSIX `sh` receives `--next` with no following argument because the `#` begins a comment, whereas the correctly quoted form preserves five arguments.

317	func checkoutExactVerdict(observed lifecycleObservation) (Verdict, string) {
318		if observed.worktree.GitCommonDir != observed.gitCommonDir {
319			return VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("worktree common directory %q differs from %q", observed.worktree.GitCommonDir, observed.gitCommonDir)
320		}
321		if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree {
322			if observed.task.WorktreePath == "" {
323				if observed.task.State != task.Cold || observed.branchMatches != 1 {
324					return VerdictBlocked, "the task has no exact persisted checkout identity"
325				}
326			} else {
327				// ResolveRegisteredWorktree matched the recorded hint by canonical path;
328				// subsequent operations use only the returned registered identity.
329				if observed.worktree.Path == "" {
330					return VerdictBlocked, "the exact registered worktree path is empty"
331				}
332			}
333		} else {
334			if observed.task.WorktreePath != "" {
335				return VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("%s task unexpectedly retains worktree path %q", observed.mode, observed.task.WorktreePath)
336			}
337			if observed.worktree.Path != observed.repoPath {
338				return VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("registered main path %q differs from %q", observed.worktree.Path, observed.repoPath)
339			}
340		}
341		if observed.headErr != nil {
342			return VerdictError, observed.headErr.Error()
343		}
344		if observed.worktree.Worktree.Head != observed.head {
345			return VerdictBlocked, fmt.Sprintf("worktree registry HEAD %q differs from checkout HEAD %q", observed.worktree.Worktree.Head, observed.head)
346		}
347		return VerdictMet, "exact path, Git common directory, and HEAD match"
348	}

353		}

35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}
66	
67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {
70			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
72			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
73			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
74			r.MainRoot = r.Root
75		} else {
76			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
77		}
78		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
79		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
80		if r.Bare {
81			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
82			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
83			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
84				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
85			}
86		}
87		return r, nil
88	}

138		t.Helper()
139		service, err := NewLifecycleService(LifecycleConfig{
140			Config: h.cfg, Tasks: h.tasks, Artifacts: h.artifacts,
141			Host: "test-host", CWD: h.repo,
142			Clock: func() time.Time { return h.clock },
143			Hooks: LifecycleHooks{
144				RepoLock: func(_ context.Context, commonDir string, operation func() error) error {
145					h.calls = append(h.calls, "repo-lock:"+commonDir)
146					return operation()
147				},
148				GitDiscover: func(_ context.Context, dir string) (gitx.Repo, error) {
149					root := h.discoverAt
150					gitDir := h.common
151					linked := false
152					if dir == h.checkout {
153						root = h.checkout
154						gitDir = filepath.Join(h.common, "worktrees", "topic")
155						linked = true
156					}
157					return gitx.Repo{
158						Root: root, GitDir: gitDir, GitCommonDir: h.common,
159						MainRoot: h.discoverAt, Name: "repo", IsLinkedWorktree: linked,
160					}, nil
161				},
162				GitRun: func(_ context.Context, _ string, args ...string) (string, error) {
163					if len(args) == 0 {
164						return "", errors.New("empty Git invocation")
165					}
166					switch args[0] {
167					case "check-ref-format":
168						if len(args) != 2 || strings.Contains(args[1], "..") || strings.ContainsAny(args[1], " ~^:?*[\\") {
169							return "", errors.New("invalid ref")
170						}
171						return "", nil
172					case "rev-parse":
173						if len(args) != 3 || args[1] != "--verify" {
174							return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected rev-parse args %q", args)
175						}
176						ref := strings.TrimSuffix(args[2], "^{commit}")
177						if ref == "HEAD" {
178							ref = "refs/heads/topic"
179						}
180						oid, ok := h.refs[ref]
181						if !ok {
182							return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown ref %s", ref)
183						}
184						return oid, nil
185					case "fetch":
186						h.calls = append(h.calls, "fetch:"+strings.Join(args[1:], " "))
187						if h.fetchErr != nil {
188							return "", h.fetchErr
189						}
190						return "", nil
191					default:
192						return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected Git invocation %q", args)
193					}
194				},
195				GitRemote: func(_ context.Context, _ string, name string) string {
196					h.remoteNames = append(h.remoteNames, name)
197					return h.remoteURL
198				},
199				GitRefExists: func(_ context.Context, _ string, ref string) bool {
200					_, ok := h.refs[ref]
201					return ok
202				},
203				ResolveWorktree: func(_ context.Context, _ string, exact string) (gitx.RegisteredWorktree, error) {
204					want, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(h.checkout)
205					if canonicalErr != nil || exact != want {
206						return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", gitx.ErrWorktreeNotFound, exact)
207					}
208					repoPath, _ := pathx.Canonical(h.repo)
209					commonDir, _ := pathx.Canonical(h.common)
210					return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{
211						RepositoryPath: repoPath, GitCommonDir: commonDir, Path: want,
212						Worktree: gitx.Worktree{Path: want, Head: h.refs["refs/heads/topic"], Branch: "topic"},
213					}, nil
214				},
215				ResolveForge: func(kind forge.Kind) (forge.Forge, error) {
216					if h.resolveErr != nil {
217						return nil, h.resolveErr
218					}
219					if h.provider == nil {
220						return nil, nil
221					}
222					if h.provider.Kind() != kind {
223						return h.provider, nil
224					}
225					return h.provider, nil
226				},
227				QueryReview: func(_ context.Context, _ forge.Forge, _ string, query forge.ReviewQuery) (*forge.Review, error) {
228					h.calls = append(h.calls, "query:"+query.Repository+":"+query.Head+":"+query.Base)
229					h.queries = append(h.queries, query)
230					if h.queryReview == nil {
231						return nil, h.queryErr
232					}
233					copy := *h.queryReview
234					return &copy, h.queryErr
235				},
236				TaskCreate: func(*task.Tx, *task.Task) (*task.Record, error) {
237					h.taskWriteCalls++
238					return nil, errors.New("unexpected task create")
239				},
240				TaskUpdate: func(*task.Tx, *task.Task, string) (*task.Record, error) {
241					h.taskWriteCalls++
242					return nil, errors.New("unexpected task update")
243				},
244				TaskDelete: func(*task.Tx, string, string) error {
245					h.taskWriteCalls++
246					return errors.New("unexpected task delete")
247				},
248			},
249		})
250		if err != nil {
251			t.Fatalf("NewLifecycleService: %v", err)
252		}
253		return service

483	func presentDoneApplyError(result flow.Result, err error) error {
484		for _, step := range result.FailedSteps() {
485			switch step.Effect.Code {
486			case flow.EffectCommitAll:
487				return fmt.Errorf("commit dirty checkout: %w", err)
488			case flow.EffectDiscardAll:
489				return fmt.Errorf("discard dirty checkout: %w", err)
490			}
491		}
492		if errors.Is(err, flow.ErrStalePlan) {
493			for _, step := range result.CompletedSteps() {
494				if step.Effect.Code == flow.EffectCommitAll || step.Effect.Code == flow.EffectDiscardAll {
495					return fmt.Errorf("checkout changed again during finalization; stop the active writer and rerun dev done: %w", err)
496				}
497			}
498			return fmt.Errorf("checkout or branch changed while the finish plan was open; review the new state and rerun dev done: %w", err)
499		}
500		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "changed again after") {
501			return fmt.Errorf("checkout changed again during finalization; stop the active writer and rerun dev done: %w", err)
502		}
503		return err
504	}

299				ActualPlanID:   fresh.PlanID,
300				Reason:         changed + " changed while the finish plan was open",
301			}
302			return flow.Plan{}, presentDoneApplyError(flow.Result{}, stale)
303		}
304		return fresh, nil
305	}

// count impossible to explain.
type CheckoutOwnership string

const (
	CheckoutCanonical CheckoutOwnership = "canonical"
	CheckoutDev       CheckoutOwnership = "dev"
	CheckoutExternal  CheckoutOwnership = "external"
	CheckoutEphemeral CheckoutOwnership = "ephemeral"
)

// RepoCheckout is one checkout in a repository context. The first checkout is
// always the canonical checkout; the rest are linked worktrees in Git order.
type RepoCheckout struct {
	Worktree gitx.Worktree
	Status   gitx.Status
	// StatusErr is retained so a prunable or unreadable checkout can remain
	// visible without pretending its Git state was successfully inspected.
	StatusErr    error
	Exists       bool
	LastActivity time.Time
	LastCommit   time.Time
	LastSubject  string
	Sessions     []runtime.Session
	Tasks        []*task.Task
	Ownership    CheckoutOwnership
}

// Branch returns the named branch, falling back to the live status for the
// synthetic canonical checkout.
func (c RepoCheckout) Branch() string {
	if c.Worktree.Branch != "" {
		return c.Worktree.Branch
	}
	return c.Status.Branch
}

// RepoContext is the complete operational context for one discovered repo.
type RepoContext struct {
	Repo repo.Repo
	// Checkouts contains the canonical checkout followed by linked worktrees.
	Checkouts []RepoCheckout
	// OtherTasks are tracked branches which are not checked out here (for
	// example cold or branch-only tasks on another branch).
	OtherTasks []*task.Task
	Runtime    string
	// WorktreeCount is kept separately so a failed Git query can still explain
	// the number shown from the administrative worktrees directory.
	WorktreeCount int
	WorktreeErr   error
	LastActivity  time.Time
}

// Main returns the canonical checkout.
func (c RepoContext) Main() (RepoCheckout, bool) {
	if len(c.Checkouts) == 0 {
		return RepoCheckout{}, false
	}
	return c.Checkouts[0], true
}

// Linked returns only linked worktrees.
func (c RepoContext) Linked() []RepoCheckout {
	if len(c.Checkouts) < 2 {
		return nil
	}
	return c.Checkouts[1:]
}

// Sessions returns the repo's live sessions once each, preserving checkout
// order so a pasted context reads canonical-first.
func (c RepoContext) Sessions() []runtime.Session {
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	var out []runtime.Session
	for _, checkout := range c.Checkouts {
		for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
			key := session.Handle
			if key == "" {
				key = session.Label + "\x00" + strings.Join(session.Dirs, "\x00")
			}
			if seen[key] {
				continue
			}
			seen[key] = true
			out = append(out, session)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// CollectRepoContext joins Git, task and runtime state for one repository.
// Repositories with no linked-worktree admin entries deliberately skip
// `git worktree list`; this keeps the common whole-machine inventory path fast.
func CollectRepoContext(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, tasks []*task.Task,
	sessions []runtime.Session, runtimeName string) RepoContext {

	out := RepoContext{Repo: r, Runtime: runtimeName}
	main := RepoCheckout{
		Worktree: gitx.Worktree{Path: r.Path, Main: true},
		Exists:   pathIsDir(r.Path), Ownership: CheckoutCanonical,
	}
	if r.Bare {
		main.Worktree.Bare = true
	} else {
		main.Status, main.StatusErr = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
		main.Worktree.Branch = main.Status.Branch
		main.Worktree.Detached = main.Status.Detached
		main.LastActivity, main.LastCommit, main.LastSubject = checkoutActivity(ctx, r.Path, main.Status)
	}
	out.Checkouts = append(out.Checkouts, main)

	out.WorktreeCount = linkedAdminCount(r.CommonDir)
	if !r.Bare && out.WorktreeCount > 0 {
		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
		if err != nil {
			out.WorktreeErr = err
		} else {
			out.WorktreeCount = 0
			for _, w := range worktrees {
				if w.Main {
					continue
				}
				checkout := RepoCheckout{
					Worktree: w, Exists: pathIsDir(w.Path), Ownership: CheckoutExternal,
				}
				if checkout.Exists && !w.Prunable {
					checkout.Status, checkout.StatusErr = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, w.Path)
					checkout.LastActivity, checkout.LastCommit, checkout.LastSubject = checkoutActivity(ctx, w.Path, checkout.Status)
				}
				if IsEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
					checkout.Ownership = CheckoutEphemeral
				}
				out.Checkouts = append(out.Checkouts, checkout)
				out.WorktreeCount++
			}
		}
	}

	assignTasks(&out, tasks)
	assignSessions(&out, sessions)
	for _, checkout := range out.Checkouts {
		if checkout.LastActivity.After(out.LastActivity) {
			out.LastActivity = checkout.LastActivity
		}
		for _, t := range checkout.Tasks {
			if t.Updated.After(out.LastActivity) {
				out.LastActivity = t.Updated
			}
		}
	}
	for _, t := range out.OtherTasks {
		if t.Updated.After(out.LastActivity) {
			out.LastActivity = t.Updated
		}
	}
	return out
}

// IsEphemeralWorktree recognises turn-scoped checkouts owned by an agent
// harness. They stay visible, but the label prevents an agent from treating
// them like durable dev-owned work.
func IsEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {
	slashPath := filepath.ToSlash(path)
	return strings.Contains(slashPath, "/.claude/worktrees/") ||
		strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")
}

func linkedAdminCount(commonDir string) int {
	if commonDir == "" {
		return 0
	}
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(commonDir, "worktrees"))
	if err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	n := 0
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if entry.IsDir() {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

func pathIsDir(path string) bool {
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	return err == nil && info.IsDir()
}

func checkoutActivity(ctx context.Context, path string, status gitx.Status) (time.Time, time.Time, string) {
	latest := status.LatestChange
	var commit time.Time
	var subject string
	if unix, lastSubject, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, path); err == nil && unix > 0 {
		commit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
		if commit.After(latest) {
			latest = commit
		}
		subject = lastSubject
	}
	return latest, commit, subject
}

func assignTasks(out *RepoContext, tasks []*task.Task) {
	for _, t := range tasks {
		assigned := false
		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
			for i := 1; i < len(out.Checkouts); i++ {
				if samePath(t.WorktreePath, out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Path) {
					out.Checkouts[i].Tasks = append(out.Checkouts[i].Tasks, t)
					out.Checkouts[i].Ownership = CheckoutDev
					assigned = true
					break
				}
			}
		} else if len(out.Checkouts) > 0 && t.Branch == out.Checkouts[0].Branch() {
			out.Checkouts[0].Tasks = append(out.Checkouts[0].Tasks, t)
			assigned = true
		}
		if !assigned {
			out.OtherTasks = append(out.OtherTasks, t)
		}
	}
	for i := range out.Checkouts {
		sort.SliceStable(out.Checkouts[i].Tasks, func(a, b int) bool {
			return out.Checkouts[i].Tasks[a].ID < out.Checkouts[i].Tasks[b].ID
		})
	}
	sort.SliceStable(out.OtherTasks, func(i, j int) bool {
		return out.OtherTasks[i].ID < out.OtherTasks[j].ID
	})
}

// assignSessions assigns each observed directory to the most-specific
// checkout. A session rooted in repo/.claude/worktrees/x therefore belongs to
// x, not to the canonical checkout which also happens to contain that path.
func assignSessions(out *RepoContext, sessions []runtime.Session) {
	for _, session := range sessions {
		assigned := map[int]bool{}
		for _, dir := range session.Dirs {
			best, bestLen := -1, -1
			for i := range out.Checkouts {
				for _, root := range checkoutRoots(out.Repo, i, out.Checkouts[i]) {
					if pathContains(root, dir) && len(filepath.Clean(root)) > bestLen {
						best, bestLen = i, len(filepath.Clean(root))
					}
				}
			}
			if best >= 0 {
				assigned[best] = true
			}
		}
		for i := range assigned {
			out.Checkouts[i].Sessions = append(out.Checkouts[i].Sessions, session)
		}
	}
}

func checkoutRoots(r repo.Repo, index int, checkout RepoCheckout) []string {
	roots := []string{checkout.Worktree.Path}
	if index == 0 && r.RealPath != "" && !samePath(r.RealPath, r.Path) {
		roots = append(roots, r.RealPath)
	}
	return roots
}

func pathContains(root, path string) bool {
	if root == "" || path == "" {
		return false
	}
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(normalizePath(root), normalizePath(path))
	if err != nil || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
		return false
	}
	return rel == "." || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
}

func samePath(a, b string) bool {
	return a != "" && b != "" && normalizePath(a) == normalizePath(b)
}

// normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
// paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
// also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
// is not sufficient.
func normalizePath(path string) string {
	clean := filepath.Clean(path)
	cur := clean
	for {
		if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur); err == nil {
			rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(cur, clean)
			if relErr == nil && rel != "." {
				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(real, rel))
			}
			return filepath.Clean(real)
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(cur)
		if parent == cur {
			return clean
		}
		cur = parent
	}
}

// FormatRepoContext renders the deterministic Markdown used by both the CLI
// and the TUI's yy binding. checkoutIndex < 0 means the whole repository.
func FormatRepoContext(c RepoContext, checkoutIndex int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if checkoutIndex >= 0 && checkoutIndex < len(c.Checkouts) {
		checkout := c.Checkouts[checkoutIndex]
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# dev worktree context: %s\n\n", displayBranch(checkout))
		writeCheckoutMarkdown(&b, c, checkout, false)
		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String()) + "\n"
	}

	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# dev repo context: %s\n\n", c.Repo.Display())
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Repository: `%s`\n", c.Repo.Display())
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Main path: `%s`\n", c.Repo.Path)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Linked worktrees: %d\n", c.WorktreeCount)
	if c.Runtime != "" && c.Runtime != "none" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Runtime: `%s`\n", c.Runtime)
	}
	if c.WorktreeErr != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Worktree inventory error: %s\n", c.WorktreeErr)
	}
	b.WriteString("\n## Checkouts\n")
	for i, checkout := range c.Checkouts {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		writeCheckoutMarkdown(&b, c, checkout, i == 0)
	}
	if len(c.OtherTasks) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n## Other tracked tasks\n\n")
		for _, t := range c.OtherTasks {
			writeTaskMarkdown(&b, t)
		}
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(b.String()) + "\n"
}

func writeCheckoutMarkdown(b *strings.Builder, c RepoContext, checkout RepoCheckout, canonical bool) {
	label := string(checkout.Ownership)
	if canonical {
		label = "canonical"
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(b, "### %s — %s\n\n", displayBranch(checkout), label)
	fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Path: `%s`\n", checkout.Worktree.Path)
	fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Branch: `%s`\n", displayBranch(checkout))
	if checkout.Worktree.Bare {
		b.WriteString("- Git: bare repository\n")
	} else if checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists {
		b.WriteString("- Git: unavailable (checkout path is missing)\n")
	} else if checkout.StatusErr != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: unavailable (%s)\n", checkout.StatusErr)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: %s", checkout.Status.Summary())
		if checkout.Status.Dirty() {
			fmt.Fprintf(b, " — %s", checkout.Status.Breakdown())
		}
		b.WriteString("\n")
		if checkout.Status.Upstream != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Upstream: `%s`\n", checkout.Status.Upstream)
		} else {
			b.WriteString("- Upstream: not published\n")
		}
	}
	if checkout.Worktree.Locked {
		reason := strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.LockedReason)
		if reason == "" {
			reason = "no reason recorded"
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Worktree: locked — %s\n", reason)
	}
	if checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists {
		reason := strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.PrunableReason)
		if reason == "" {
			reason = "checkout path is missing"
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Worktree: prunable — %s\n", reason)
	}
	if len(checkout.Sessions) == 0 {
		b.WriteString("- Runtime: closed\n")
	} else {
		for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
			status := session.AgentStatus
			if status == "" {
				status = "unknown"
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Runtime: `%s %s` (%s)\n", c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
			if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
				fmt.Fprintf(b, "  - Agent sessions: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))
			}
		}
	}
	if len(checkout.Tasks) == 0 {
		b.WriteString("- Task: untracked\n")
	} else {
		for _, t := range checkout.Tasks {
			writeTaskMarkdown(b, t)
		}
	}
}

func writeTaskMarkdown(b *strings.Builder, t *task.Task) {
	fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Task: `%s` — %s", t.ID, t.State)
	if t.Next != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "; next: %s", t.Next)
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")
	if t.AgentSession != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "  - Recorded agent: `%s`\n", t.AgentSession)
	}
}

func displayBranch(checkout RepoCheckout) string {
	if branch := checkout.Branch(); branch != "" {
		return branch
	}
	if checkout.Worktree.Detached || checkout.Status.Detached {
		return "(detached HEAD)"
	}
	return "(unknown branch)"
}

func markdownCodes(values []string) string {
	quoted := make([]string, 0, len(values))
	for _, value := range values {
		quoted = append(quoted, "`"+value+"`")
	}
	return strings.Join(quoted, ", ")
}

// FormatSessions renders the ys payload. checkoutIndex < 0 selects the whole
// repository; otherwise it selects one checkout.
func FormatSessions(c RepoContext, checkoutIndex int) string {
	indices := make([]int, 0, len(c.Checkouts))
	if checkoutIndex >= 0 && checkoutIndex < len(c.Checkouts) {
		indices = append(indices, checkoutIndex)
	} else {
		for i := range c.Checkouts {
			indices = append(indices, i)
		}
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, i := range indices {
		checkout := c.Checkouts[i]
		for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
			status := session.AgentStatus
			if status == "" {
				status = "unknown"
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s`: `%s %s` (%s)\n",
				checkout.Worktree.Path, c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
			if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - agents: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))
			}
		}
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
}

// LinkedWorktreePaths returns the yw payload: absolute linked-worktree paths,
// one per line. The canonical checkout is intentionally excluded because WT
// counts linked worktrees only.
func LinkedWorktreePaths(c RepoContext) string {
	paths := make([]string, 0, len(c.Linked()))
	for _, checkout := range c.Linked() {
		paths = append(paths, checkout.Worktree.Path)
	}
	return strings.Join(paths, "\n")
}

```text
1	---
2	description: Use the preview dev flow interface to inspect one repository and apply revision-bound lifecycle, adoption, removal, retirement, and remote-evidence plans.
3	authority: project
4	status: evolving
5	verified_on: 2026-09-01
6	---
7	
8	# Repository lifecycle flow
9	
10	`dev flow [repo]` is a preview-labelled, full-screen, TTY-only interface for one
11	repository's lifecycle. It is independent of the six-view `dev tui` dashboard:
12	its only job is to show repository surfaces, observed evidence, and exact guarded
13	actions.
14	
15	```bash
16	dev flow              # current repository, or a picker outside Git
17	dev flow api          # explicit repository overrides cwd
18	```
19	
20	From either the canonical checkout or a linked worktree, bare `dev flow` resolves
21	the canonical Git common-directory identity and focuses the exact current
22	surface. Outside Git it loads a filterable repository picker asynchronously. A
23	repository that is referenced by task metadata but temporarily unavailable
24	remains inspectable as unavailable task-only rows.
25	
26	## Repository surfaces
27	
28	The left panel starts from every record in `git worktree list --porcelain`, then
29	adds task records that have no checkout. Normal COLD and DONE tasks therefore do
30	not disappear merely because no directory exists.
31	
32	| Row kind | Meaning | Guarded actions |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| `canonical` | the worktree Git marks Main, regardless of branch name | legal task actions when exactly bound; never checkout removal |
35	| `managed` | a non-main checkout with one exact task binding | mode/state lifecycle actions |
36	| `unmanaged` | a registered linked checkout with no task or harness claim | Adopt; clean branch-preserving Remove Checkout |
37	| `harness` | strict path evidence places it under `.claude/worktrees` | inspect and eligible remote evidence only; harness owns cleanup |
38	| `task-only` | task metadata has no registered checkout, normally COLD or DONE | Resume or Retire only when exact task identity permits it |
39	| `conflict` | duplicate claims, mismatched identity, incomplete inventory, or other ambiguity | inspect/remediate; destructive actions fail closed |
40	
41	A branch name prefix is not harness ownership proof. Canonical, harness-owned,
42	locked/prunable, detached, ambiguously claimed, or incompletely observed rows are
43	never treated as removable merely because they look inactive.
44	
45	For an eligible unmanaged row:
46	
47	- **Adopt** creates one worktree-mode task record and does not change checkout
48	  content, refs, runtime layout, or path. A dirty checkout may be adopted because
49	  its bytes remain untouched. Fresh strict runtime evidence may derive HOT only
50	  for one stable shell-only covering session with no recognized agent; otherwise
51	  adoption is WARM. `runtime=none` is unobserved, so it derives WARM.
52	- **Remove Checkout** requires an exact named clean linked checkout, complete task
53	  inventory with no claims, ready artifacts, safe external runtime cleanup, and
54	  no harness evidence. It uses non-force removal and verifies that the local
55	  branch remains at the same OID.
56	
57	Repository-wide prune and drift reconciliation are not hidden Remove variants.
58	The flow reports those conditions and leaves them for explicit recovery.
59	
60	## Intent, facts, and plans
61	
62	The three panels keep different kinds of truth separate:
63	
64	1. **Persisted intent** — task mode, HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, owner, next action,
65	   branch/base, expected checkout, and runtime hint.
66	2. **Observed facts** — repository/worktree identity, HEAD and refs, Git status and
67	   in-progress operations, artifact readiness, runtime sessions, and recognized
68	   agents. A fact remains known, unknown, error, skipped, loading, or stale; a
69	   failed observation never becomes false, clean, or closed.
70	3. **Guarded plan** — legal source/target edge, READY/NEEDS INPUT/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN/
71	   ERROR availability, ordered conditions and effects, remediation, resources
72	   retained, confirmation class, PlanID, and CLI fallback.
73	
74	`runtime=none` cannot observe session or agent occupancy. That does not turn the
75	observation into “closed,” but a complete local Git/task snapshot can still be
76	fresh and useful for non-runtime facts.
77	
78	## Managed lifecycle choices
79	
80	Actions are concrete variants, not a generic force menu:
81	
82	| Current intent | Flow choices |
83	|---|---|
84	| HOT/WARM worktree or branch task | Park Warm; Park Cold; Park Cold + Push; Complete FF; Review Handoff; Verify Merged |
85	| HOT/WARM direct task | Park Warm; Complete Direct |
86	| WARM task | Resume (with an explicit fetch effect) |
87	| COLD worktree/branch task | Resume and reconstruct/reopen; completion remains unavailable until HOT |
88	| DONE task | Retire (Keep Branch); for eligible non-direct tasks, Retire + Delete Contained Branch |
89	
90	Review Handoff publishes the branch and creates a pull/merge request when the
91	available provider supports it, but preserves HOT/WARM. Direct/FF/verified
92	completion writes DONE last and keeps branch, checkout, and runtime resources.
93	Retire is the separate externally safe close/wait/remove/task-reap operation.
94	
95	The preview always uses a fail-on-dirty completion policy. It intentionally does
96	not expose dirty commit/discard, WIP checkpoint, shared-writer, ownership
97	takeover, force removal, `--close-unknown`, or `--assume-no-runtime` choices.
98	Blocked plans show the precise evidence, remediation, and compatible CLI
99	fallback instead of manufacturing an override.
100

200	func appendOccupancyAgent(ctx context.Context, result *Occupancy, checkout checkoutIdentity, opts OccupancyOptions, activity AgentActivity) error {
201		covered, err := activityCoversCheckout(ctx, checkout, activity.CWD)
202		if err != nil {
203			return fmt.Errorf("classify recognized agent pane %s: %w", activity.PaneID, err)
204		}
205		if !covered {
206			return nil
207		}
208		status := normalizeOccupancyStatus(activity.Status)

210		handle := correlatedSession(result.Sessions, activity)
211		result.Agents = append(result.Agents, OccupancyAgent{

214			SessionHandle: handle,
215			IsCaller:      caller,
216			Blocking:      occupancyAgentBlocks(opts, status, caller, handle != ""),
217		})

219	}
