```text
+// RegisteredWorktree is an identity snapshot from Git's worktree registry.
+// Worktree preserves the complete parsed Git record; the other fields are canonical
+// filesystem identities suitable for exact comparison across symlink and macOS
+// path aliases. A snapshot proves registration, not permission to remove it.
+type RegisteredWorktree struct {
+	Worktree       Worktree
+	RepositoryPath string
+	GitCommonDir   string
+	Path           string
+}
+
+// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether the record is a linked checkout rather than
+// Git's main checkout or a bare repository. It is classification, not a removal
+// safety decision.
+func (w RegisteredWorktree) IsLinkedWorktree() bool {
+	return !w.Worktree.Main && !w.Worktree.Bare
+}
+
+// ResolveRegisteredWorktree resolves exactPath against a fresh authoritative
+// `git worktree list --porcelain` query for the repository containing repoPath.
+// Matching is exclusively by canonical filesystem identity, never by branch.
+// It performs no prune, removal, or other mutation.
+func ResolveRegisteredWorktree(ctx context.Context, repoPath, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
+	worktrees, err := Worktrees(ctx, repoPath)
+	if err != nil {
+		return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("query registered worktrees: %w", err)
+	}
+	commonDir, err := run(ctx, repoPath, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
+	if err != nil {
+		return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve Git common directory: %w", err)
+	}
+	return resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees, commonDir, exactPath)
+}
+
+func resolveRegisteredWorktree(worktrees []Worktree, commonDir, exactPath string) (RegisteredWorktree, error) {
+	path, err := pathx.Canonical(exactPath)
+	if err != nil {
+		return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize requested worktree %q: %w", exactPath, err)
+	}
+	canonicalCommonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
+	if err != nil {
+		return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git common directory %q: %w", commonDir, err)
+	}
+
+	type match struct {
+		worktree Worktree
+		path     string
+	}
+	var (
+		repositoryPath string
+		matches        []match
+	)
+	for _, worktree := range worktrees {
+		canonicalPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(worktree.Path)
+		if canonicalErr != nil {
+			return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize registered worktree %q: %w", worktree.Path, canonicalErr)
+		}
+		if worktree.Main {
+			repositoryPath = canonicalPath
+		}
+		if sameCanonicalPath(path, canonicalPath) {
+			matches = append(matches, match{worktree: worktree, path: canonicalPath})
+		}
+	}
+
+	switch len(matches) {
+	case 0:
+		return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrWorktreeNotFound, path)
+	case 1:
+		if repositoryPath == "" {
+			return RegisteredWorktree{}, errors.New("registered worktree query has no main repository record")
+		}
+		return RegisteredWorktree{
+			Worktree:       matches[0].worktree,
+			RepositoryPath: repositoryPath,
+			GitCommonDir:   canonicalCommonDir,
+			Path:           matches[0].path,
+		}, nil
+	default:
+		return RegisteredWorktree{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s resolves to %d records", ErrWorktreeAmbiguous, path, len(matches))
+	}
+}
+
+func sameCanonicalPath(left, right string) bool {
+	if left == right {
+		return true
+	}
+	leftInfo, leftErr := os.Stat(left)
+	rightInfo, rightErr := os.Stat(right)
+	return leftErr == nil && rightErr == nil && os.SameFile(leftInfo, rightInfo)
+}
```

130	
131	Before finishing agent work, run `dev prepare` with the exact session UUID and
132	exit normally. The post-writer finalizer—not the still-running agent—stages and
133	commits the exact transcript/plan. A settled Herdr `done` state is not evidence
134	that history, review or commits are complete.
135	
136	Useful variations:
137	
138	```bash
139	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
140	dev park --cold --push            # close session, push, remove worktree
141	dev park --keep-session           # warm only: record state, keep session
142	```
143	
144	`--cold --keep-session` is rejected because a runtime must not remain pointed at
145	a checkout that cold parking removes. A verified runtime-close failure likewise
146	stops cold cleanup before deleting the checkout; warm park reports the close
147	failure and keeps the recorded handle for reconciliation.
148	
149	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
150	
151	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
152	
153	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
154	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
155	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
156	
157	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
158	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
159	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
160	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
161	
162	## Cold, and why it is safe
163	
164	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
165	
166	- the branch still holds every commit;
167	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
168	  them too;
169	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
170	
171	Resume rebuilds/reopens checkout and runtime state only. Persisted runtime
172	handles carry their backend name and are validated against live checkout
173	coverage; stale/missing handles reopen instead of making a task falsely HOT.
174	Production `dev` does not currently attach a Claude/Codex conversation; an agent
175	handoff must supply explicit session/launcher arguments.
176	
177	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
178	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
179	
180	## Moving work between machines
181	
182	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
183	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
184	
185	On the machine holding the work:
186	
187	```bash
188	dev park --cold --push
189	```
190	
191	On the machine picking it up:
192	
193	```bash
194	dev resume <task> --fetch
195	```
196	
197	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
198	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
199	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
200	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
201	
202	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
203	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
204	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
205	
206	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
207	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
208	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
209

 external `--close-unknown`. `dev done` never closes or removes anything.
 
+### Repository flow preview
+
+`dev flow [repo]` is a preview-labelled, full-screen, TTY-only state-machine UI.
+It is independent of the six-view `dev tui` dashboard. From a canonical or linked
+checkout, `dev flow` resolves the canonical repository and focuses that exact
+surface; outside Git it opens a filterable repository picker. An explicit
+`dev flow api` overrides cwd.
+
+The left panel is the union of Git's registered worktrees and task records that
+have no checkout, including normal COLD and DONE tasks. Rows are labelled
+`canonical`, `managed`, `unmanaged`, `harness`, `task-only`, or `conflict`.
+Canonical worktrees are never removable; harness-owned and ambiguous/conflicting
+rows have no destructive path. An exact unmanaged linked checkout can be
+**Adopted** by creating task metadata without changing Git bytes, or **Removed**
+only when clean and safe; removal is non-force and always preserves the branch.
+
+The center distinguishes persisted task intent (`HOT`, `WARM`, `COLD`, `DONE`)
+from observed Git/worktree/runtime/artifact facts. Unknown, failed, loading, or
+stale evidence never becomes a false clean/closed fact. `runtime=none` leaves
+session occupancy unobserved, but the local Git/task snapshot can still be fresh;
+metadata-only adoption then remains WARM.
+
+The right panel offers concrete mode/state actions: warm/cold park, resume,
+direct or fast-forward completion, review handoff, verified-merge completion,
+and DONE retirement where legal. The preview deliberately excludes dirty
+commit/discard, WIP checkpoint, shared-writer, ownership-takeover, and unknown-
+runtime overrides. A blocked plan shows its exact evidence, remediation, and CLI
+fallback; existing command flags remain available outside the preview.
+
+```text
+j/k or ↑/↓       choose a surface      h/l or ←/→     choose an action
+Tab/Shift-Tab    move panel focus       Enter          build a plan, never apply
+r                reload local facts    R              Fetch refs / Query review / Both
+Esc              back out              ?              evidence and key help
+```
+
+A READY plan shows ordered conditions/effects, retained resources, network and
+destructive markers, and its exact PlanID. Press `y` only for a non-typed plan;
+typed branch deletion requires the displayed token and `Enter`. Apply locks and
+reloads the task revision plus repository, checkout, refs, runtime, artifact, and
+remote identities. Any change rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Once an
+effect starts, quit/refresh waits for the retained step ledger; partial success
+means completed effects remain completed and recovery is explicit.
+
+Startup and `r` never fetch or query a forge. `R` runs only the confirmed choice
+and keeps its evidence in this TUI run: named ref OIDs plus portable review
+existence, open/draft/merged/closed state, URL, provider, and observation time.
+It does not query review decisions or checks. Completion records DONE while
+keeping branch, checkout, and runtime resources; Retire cleans them from outside
+the target. Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside these
+`dev`-mediated locks and safety checks.
+

 | State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |

 ```
+The enforced graph is mode-aware: worktree/branch HOT or WARM can park WARM or
+COLD; WARM/COLD resume HOT; HOT/WARM can complete or hand off review; DONE can
+only Retire. Direct tasks omit COLD and branch integration. Review handoff is
+state-preserving. COLD must resume before completion, and no ordinary action
+moves DONE backward.
+
+### Plan it by repository
+
+`dev flow [repo]` is an independent preview-labelled, full-screen TUI, not a mode
+of the dashboard. From a canonical or linked checkout it opens the canonical
+repository and focuses that exact surface; outside Git it opens a repository
+picker. It projects every Git-registered worktree plus task-only records such as
+COLD/DONE tasks without a checkout.
+
+The UI shows three layers separately:
+
+1. persisted task intent: mode, HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, owner, next, branch/base, and
+   expected checkout;
+2. observed facts: exact worktree identity, Git status/operation/refs, runtime and
+   agent occupancy, artifact readiness, each kept as known/unknown/error/skipped/
+   loading rather than converting probe failure into false;
+3. a guarded plan: availability, evidence/remediation, ordered effects, retained
+   resources, confirmation, exact fallback, task revision, and PlanID.
+
+Enter creates the plan; it never applies. READY non-typed plans need `y`; typed
+plans need the displayed token plus Enter. Apply locks and reloads the task
+revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority. If any
+identity changed, it rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Apply itself is
+not canceled by row movement/refresh/quit; the UI retains completed/failed steps
+and recovery, then starts a new local read.
+
+The preview offers the normal managed choices but no dirty commit/discard, WIP,
+shared-writer, ownership takeover, or unknown-runtime acknowledgement. Blocked
+plans point to the compatible CLI fallback instead of adding a force path.
+`r` reads local state only; `R` explicitly plans fetch, portable review query, or
+both. Remote evidence is run-local and limited to named refs plus review
+existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time—not checks or review decisions.
+
 **A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
 cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
```

```text
HEAD:docs/guides/remote-fleet.md:86:Each successful probe writes a per-host JSON snapshot under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/fleet/v1/<host-name-slug>.json`. That cache is a disposable accelerator, not durable data: it is fingerprinted with an "endpoint ID" derived from the host's connection fields and timeouts, so editing a host's `ssh_alias`, `hostname`, `user`, `port`, `identity_file`, `dev_path`, or timeouts automatically invalidates its old cache the next time `dev` reads it. Oversized snapshots, future timestamps, invalid counts, and oversized/NUL-containing identity or path fields are ignored rather than displayed. `dev cache list` shows its path, size, and age; `dev cache clear fleet` (or `dev cache clear all`) removes it outright. There is nothing to "rebuild" explicitly — the next `dev fleet list`, `dev fleet status`, or TUI FLEET reload regenerates it from a fresh probe.
HEAD:docs/guides/tui-repos-bootstrap.md:60:A COLD worktree task must be rebuilt with `dev resume`; the TUI does not silently recreate it through a generic open action. A missing or unregistered worktree points to `dev sweep` first, so unique agent artifacts are reported for salvage before the task is resumed or reaped. Enter never opens an abandoned artifact-only directory.
HEAD:docs/guides/tui-repos-bootstrap.md:138:Markdown under configured `paths.state_dir/notes` is durable; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is only a rebuildable search index. **Exploring lock mechanisms**
```

I'm thinking about locking in a process and how a lock can't be acquired until it's released, even if there's an initial validation that occurs before removal. Maybe waiting for about 50ms isn't ideal for testing stability. I could set a hook in the Service before the lock to signal it's not present. 

I also wonder about using a goroutine to wait 100ms before removal, but that may not be enough to ensure robustness in tests. Instead, a marker from the lock file could help track acquisition attempts better. 

**Analyzing lock behavior**

I'm considering the process where, inside the WithDir lock, I call Prepare with a 50ms timeout. This does validations and tries to lock but ends up timing out. Calling this synchronously while holding the lock seems like a good approach, even if the lock isn't reentrant.

After closing the checkout while still holding the lock, running Prepare again fails. This setup doesn't perfectly simulate ongoing preparations overlapping during a release, but it shows how shared locks work and the need for revalidation during this process.

```text
406		payload = append(payload, id...)
407		payload = append(payload, 0)
408		payload = append(payload, data...)
409		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256(payload))

417	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
418	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
419	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
420	// than a silent pick.
421	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
422		if ref == "" {
423			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
424		}
425		all, err := s.List()
426		if err != nil {
427			return nil, err
428		}
429		for _, t := range all {
430			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
431				return t, nil
432			}
433		}
434		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
435		var hits []*Task
436		for _, t := range all {
437			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
438			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
439				hits = append(hits, t)
440			}
441		}
442		switch len(hits) {
443		case 1:
444			return hits[0], nil
445		case 0:
446			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
447		default:
448			names := make([]string, len(hits))
449			for i, t := range hits {
450				names[i] = t.ID
451			}
452			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
453		}
454	}
455	
456	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
457	//
458	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
459	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
460	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
461	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
462	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
463	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
464		all, err := s.List()
465		if err != nil {
466			return nil, err
467		}
468		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
469			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
470		}
471		var best *Task
472		var bestLen int
473		for _, t := range all {
474			root := t.WorktreePath
475			if root == "" {
476				root = t.RepoPath
477			}
478			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
479				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
480			}
481		}
482		if best == nil {
483			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
484		}
485		return best, nil
486	}
```

```text
80	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
81	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
82	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
83	- The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
84	
85	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
86	
87	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
88	
89	### Flow intentionally omits expert overrides
90	
91	`dev flow` offers normal managed lifecycle actions, exact unmanaged metadata-only
92	Adopt/clean branch-preserving Remove, and explicit remote evidence. It does not
93	offer dirty commit/discard, WIP, shared-writer, ownership takeover, force, unknown-
94	runtime, or assume-no-runtime choices. A blocked plan shows remediation and the
95	compatible CLI fallback; existing command flags and structured contracts remain
96	available.
97	
98	Task-backed lifecycle and exact unmanaged linked-checkout actions share
99	`internal/taskflow`. Explicit unmanaged path retirement remains an isolated
100	compatibility implementation, while `sweep` retains record-only reaping, orphan
101	salvage, and other narrow reconciliation paths. Do not assume every cleanup path
102	has the same planner. Raw Git and configured external tools also bypass dev's
103	PlanID, locks, revalidation, and result ledger.
104	
105	## Current behaviors that are implemented
106	
107	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
108	
109	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
110	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
111	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
112	- Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The `agent-history-hygiene` initializer writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
113	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
114	
115	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
116	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches only to an exact root pane from
117	  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
118	  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
119	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
120	- Preview-labelled `dev flow [repo]` is an independent full-screen TTY model. It resolves canonical/linked cwd to the exact surface, uses a picker outside Git, shows every registered worktree plus task-only records, and makes every mutation Enter-to-plan then approve. Apply revalidates task revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority and retains partial step results. Local `r` is network-free; `R` explicitly selects fetch/query/both and keeps minimal review evidence run-local.
121	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
122	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
123	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
124
```

```text
package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/wt"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	var (
		noProvision bool
		fetch       bool
		force       bool
	)
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "resume <task>",
		Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
		Long: `Make a parked task hot again.

Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
identity.

If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
		Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			ctx := ctxOf()
			t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}

			host := config.Hostname()
			if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
				return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
					"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
					t.ID, t.Owner)
			}

			if fetch {
				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
					app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
				}
			}

			rt := runtimeForTask(app, t)
			mode := t.EffectiveMode()
			checkout := checkoutOf(t)

			switch mode {
			case task.ModeWorktree:
				_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
				if t.WorktreePath != "" && statErr == nil {
					if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, checkout); err != nil {
						return err
					}
				}
				// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
				if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
					base := t.Base
					// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
					// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
					if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
						base = remote
					}
					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
					res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
						Base: base, Label: worktreeRuntimeLabel(t.Repo, t.Branch), NoProvision: noProvision,
					})
					if err != nil {
						var exists *wt.ErrExists
						if asError(err, &exists) {
							t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
							if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, exists.Path); err != nil {
								return err
							}
						} else {
							return err
						}
					} else {
						t.WorktreePath = res.Path
						setTaskRuntime(t, rt, res.Runtime)
						reportProvision(app, res)
						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s    %s\n", app.outStyle().label("rebuilt"), config.Contract(res.Path))
					}
					checkout = t.WorktreePath
				}

			case task.ModeBranch:
				checkout = t.RepoPath
				if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, checkout); err != nil {
					return err
				}
				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				if st.Branch != t.Branch {
					if st.Dirty() {
						return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
							st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
					}
					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
						return err
					}
				}

			case task.ModeDirect:
				checkout = t.RepoPath
				if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, checkout); err != nil {
					return err
				}
				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				if st.Branch != t.Branch {
					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
						"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
				}
			}
			if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
				live, err := runtimeHandleCovers(ctx, rt, t.RuntimeHandle, checkout)
				if err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("validate saved %s runtime session %s: %w", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle, err)
				}
				if !live {
					clearTaskRuntime(t)
				}
			}
			if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
				label := t.Title()
				if mode == task.ModeWorktree {
					label = worktreeRuntimeLabel(t.Repo, t.Branch)
				}
				opened, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, label)
				if err != nil {
					app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
				}
				setTaskRuntime(t, rt, opened)
			}

			t.State = task.Hot
			t.Owner = host
			if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			annotate(app, rt, t)

			style := app.outStyle()
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
				task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, style.dim(string(mode)))
			if t.Next != "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s      %s\n", style.label("next"), t.Next)
			}
			if t.AgentSession != "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s     %s (resumable)\n", style.label("agent"), t.AgentSession)
			}
			if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s       %s\n", style.label("git"), style.git(st.Summary()))
				if st.Behind > 0 {
					app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
				}
			}
			if rt.Name() == "none" {
				return app.cdDirective(checkout)
			}
			return activateRuntime(ctx, rt, t.RuntimeHandle)
		},
	}
	f := cmd.Flags()
	f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
	f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
	f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
	cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeTasks(app, task.Warm, task.Cold)
	return cmd
}
```

```text
36		// branches from the current HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on

80	func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*CreateResult, error) {
81		if req.Branch == "" {
82			return nil, errors.New("branch is required")
83		}
84		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, req.RepoPath)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95	
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101	
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {
104			path, err = m.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(req.RepoName, repoPath, req.Branch, req.Category)
105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := ValidateTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114	
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {
118			if base == "" {
119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125		var provisionSettings Settings
126		if !req.NoProvision {
127			provisionSettings, err = SettingsForTrusted(ctx, m.Cfg, repoPath)
128			if err != nil {
129				return nil, err
130			}
131		}
132

135		}

137			return nil, err
138		}
139		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
140	
141		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
142	
143		if !req.NoProvision {
144			// Trusted settings fold in the repository's portable project config.
145			p := &Provisioner{
146				Settings: provisionSettings,
147				Timeout:  provisionSettings.ProvisionTimeout,
148				Log:      m.Log,
149			}
150			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
151			if err != nil {
152				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
153				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
154			}
155			res.Provision = pr
156		}
157	
158		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
159			label := req.Label
160			if label == "" {
161				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
162			}
163			opened, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
164			if err != nil {
165				m.logf("warning: could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
166			} else {
167				res.Runtime = opened
168				res.RuntimeName = m.Runtime.Name()
169			}
170		}
171		return res, nil
172	}
```

```text
35	// NewService copies handlers so later mutation of the caller's map cannot
36	// redirect a planned action.
37	func NewService(handlers Handlers) *Service {
38		copied := make(map[Action]Handler, len(handlers))
39		for action, handler := range handlers {
40			copied[action] = handler
41		}
42		return &Service{handlers: copied}
43	}

47	// locator because guessing task, repository, or checkout identity is unsafe.
48	func (s *Service) LocateTask(ctx context.Context, taskID string) (Locator, error) {
49		if s == nil || s.locateTask == nil {
50			return Locator{}, ErrLocatorUnavailable
51		}
52		return s.locateTask(ctx, taskID)

56	// then centrally builds the immutable plan.
57	func (s *Service) Plan(ctx context.Context, request Request) (Plan, error) {
58		normalized, err := normalizeRequest(request)
59		if err != nil {
60			return Plan{}, err
61		}
62		handler, ok := s.handlers[normalized.Action]
63		if !ok || handler.Plan == nil {
64			return Plan{}, &HandlerUnavailableError{Action: normalized.Action, Stage: "plan"}
65		}
66		spec, err := handler.Plan(ctx, normalized.Clone())
67		if err != nil {
68			return Plan{}, err
69		}
70		return BuildPlan(normalized, spec)
71	}

74	// delegates only to the handler registered for the plan's exact action. A
75	// handler's partial Result is returned unchanged in meaning alongside errors.
76	func (s *Service) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, approval Approval) (Result, error) {
77		frozen := plan.Clone()
78		if err := frozen.Validate(); err != nil {
79			return Result{}, err
80		}
81		if err := frozen.ValidateApproval(approval); err != nil {
82			return Result{}, err
83		}
84		if frozen.Availability != AvailabilityReady {
85			notReady := &PlanNotReadyError{
86				PlanID: frozen.PlanID, Availability: frozen.Availability,
87				conditions: frozen.Conditions(),
88			}
89			return Result{}, &InvalidPlanError{
90				PlanID: frozen.PlanID, Reason: "required conditions are not ready", Cause: notReady,
91			}
92		}
93		handler, ok := s.handlers[frozen.Action]
94		if !ok || handler.Apply == nil {
95			return Result{}, &HandlerUnavailableError{Action: frozen.Action, Stage: "apply"}
96		}
97		result, err := handler.Apply(ctx, frozen.Clone())
98		result = result.Clone()
99		if err != nil && len(result.CompletedSteps()) > 0 {
100			result.PartialSuccess = true
101		}
102		return result, err
103	}
```

```text
153		}
```

```text
209	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the

211	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
212	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
213		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
214		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
215		if exists {
216			args = append(args, path, branch)
217		} else {
218			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
219			if base != "" {
220				args = append(args, base)
221			}
222		}
223		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
224		return err
225	}

227	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
228	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
229	// be any checkout of the same repository.
230	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
231		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
232		return err
233	}

236	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
237	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
238		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
239		if err != nil {
240			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
241		}
242		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
243		if err != nil {
244			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
245		}
246		if inside {
247			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
248		}
249		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
250		if force {
251			args = append(args, "--force")
252		}
253		args = append(args, path)
254		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
255		return err
256	}

259	// were deleted behind git's back.

263	}
```

```text
229	func parseAzureReviewCandidates(out string) ([]reviewCandidate, error) {
230		var raw []struct {
231			PullRequestID       *int   `json:"pullRequestId"`
232			Status              string `json:"status"`
233			IsDraft             *bool  `json:"isDraft"`
234			SourceRefName       string `json:"sourceRefName"`
235			TargetRefName       string `json:"targetRefName"`
236			RemoteURL           string `json:"remoteUrl"`
237			RepositoryRemoteURL string `json:"repositoryRemoteUrl"`
238		}
239		if err := decodeReviewJSON(AzureDevOps, out, &raw); err != nil {
240			return nil, err
241		}
242		candidates := make([]reviewCandidate, 0, len(raw))
243		for _, item := range raw {
244			id, number := "", 0
245			if item.PullRequestID != nil {
246				number = *item.PullRequestID
247				id = strconv.Itoa(number)
248			}
249			reviewURL := item.RemoteURL
250			if !validReviewURL(reviewURL) && item.RepositoryRemoteURL != "" && number > 0 {
251				if _, repositoryURL, ok := parseAzureDevOpsRemote(item.RepositoryRemoteURL); ok {
252					reviewURL = strings.TrimRight(repositoryURL, "/") + "/pullrequest/" + strconv.Itoa(number)
253				}
254			}
255			candidates = append(candidates, reviewCandidate{
256				ID: id, Number: number, State: item.Status, Draft: item.IsDraft,
257				URL: reviewURL, Head: azureReviewBranch(item.SourceRefName), Base: azureReviewBranch(item.TargetRefName),
258			})
259		}
260		return candidates, nil
261	}
262	
263	func azureReviewBranch(ref string) string {
264		return strings.TrimPrefix(ref, "refs/heads/")
265	}
266	
267	func normalizeAzureReviewState(state string, draft bool) (ReviewState, error) {
268		switch strings.ToLower(state) {
269		case "active":
270			if draft {
271				return ReviewDraft, nil
272			}
273			return ReviewOpen, nil
274		case "completed":
275			return ReviewMerged, nil
276		case "abandoned":
277			return ReviewClosed, nil
278		default:
279			return "", errors.New("unrecognized Azure DevOps review state")
280		}
281	}
```

```text
115			}
116		}

123	func (s *lifecycleService) locateRegisteredCheckout(
124		ctx context.Context,
125		candidate task.Task,
126		repoPath string,
127		expectedCheckout string,
128	) (gitx.RegisteredWorktree, bool) {
129		if expectedCheckout != "" {
130			registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, expectedCheckout)
131			return registered, err == nil
132		}
133		if candidate.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeWorktree || candidate.State != task.Cold {
134			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
135		}
136	
137		worktrees, err := s.gitWorktrees(ctx, repoPath)
138		if err != nil {
139			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
140		}
141		match := ""
142		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
143			if worktree.Branch != candidate.Branch {
144				continue
145			}
146			if match != "" {
147				return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
148			}
149			match = worktree.Path
150		}
151		if match == "" {
152			return gitx.RegisteredWorktree{}, false
153		}
154		registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, repoPath, match)
155		return registered, err == nil
156	}
157	
158	func (s *lifecycleService) branchUpstream(ctx context.Context, repoPath, branch string) string {
159		if branch == "" {
160			return ""
161		}
162		value, err := s.gitRun(ctx, repoPath,
163			"for-each-ref", "--format=%(upstream:short)", localBranchRef(branch),
164		)
165		if err != nil {
166			return ""
167		}
168		return strings.TrimSpace(value)
169	}
```

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-02 05:54:06Z)**_

writer occupancy 會區分「觀察完成且沒有 covering surface」與「unsupported/unattempted」：SessionList 未觀察一律 error；有 covering session時，若 agent inventory unsupported且 pane fallback也沒有 recognized-agent evidence，亦 error。COLD/WARM checkout重建在 `runtime=none` 下會在 Plan 階段阻止，不會先建立 checkout再 partial fail。測試 fixture 的一般成功案例會改用可觀察的空 fake runtime，`None`只留給明確 fail-closed測試。

```text
352	func (e *executionState) applyCompletionDirtyEffect(ctx context.Context, effect Effect) error {
353		observed := &e.observed
354		if err := e.service.revalidateCompletionSafety(ctx, observed); err != nil {
355			return err
356		}

358		beforeBranchOID := observed.completionBranchOID
359		err := e.run(effect, func() (string, error) {
360			switch effect.Code {
361			case EffectCommitAll:
362				message := effect.Details.Map()["message"]
363				if commitErr := e.service.commitAll(ctx, observed.checkout, message); commitErr != nil {
364					return "commit-all may have changed the index", fmt.Errorf("commit all checkout changes: %w", commitErr)
365				}
366				return "committed all checkout changes", nil
367			case EffectDiscardAll:
368				if discardErr := e.service.discardAll(ctx, observed.checkout); discardErr != nil {
369					return "discard-all may have partially reset checkout content", fmt.Errorf("discard all checkout changes: %w", discardErr)
370				}
371				return "discarded all staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked changes", nil
372			default:
373				return "", &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: e.plan.PlanID, Reason: "unexpected dirty effect " + string(effect.Code)}
374			}
375		})
376		if err != nil {
377			e.partial = true
378			return err
379		}
380		allowBaseMove := observed.mode == task.ModeDirect && effect.Code == EffectCommitAll
381		if err := e.service.refreshCompletionCheckout(ctx, observed, observed.task.Branch, allowBaseMove); err != nil {
382			return fmt.Errorf("refresh after %s: %w", effect.Code, err)
383		}
384		if observed.finish.Status.Dirty() || observed.finish.Status.Conflicted > 0 || observed.inProgress {
385			return fmt.Errorf("checkout changed again after %s: %s", effect.Code, observed.finish.Status.Breakdown())
386		}
387		switch effect.Code {
388		case EffectCommitAll:
389			parent, parentErr := e.service.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.completionBranchOID+"^")
390			if parentErr != nil || parent != beforeBranchOID {

392			}
393			if observed.mode == task.ModeDirect {
394				if observed.finish.Relation != (gitx.BranchRelation{}) {
395					return staleBoundary("direct commit changed the self-relation unexpectedly")
396				}
397			} else if observed.finish.Relation.BaseOnly != before.Relation.BaseOnly ||
398				observed.finish.Relation.BranchOnly != before.Relation.BranchOnly+1 {

401		case EffectDiscardAll:

404			}
405		}
406		if observed.proofRef == observed.task.Branch {
407			observed.proofOID = observed.completionBranchOID
408		}
409		return nil
410	}

414			candidate := e.observed.task
415			candidate.State = task.Done
416			updated, updateErr := e.service.taskUpdate(e.tx, &candidate, e.revision)

418				return "", fmt.Errorf("write DONE task state: %w", updateErr)
419			}

422			}
423			e.snapshot = "task:" + updated.Revision
424			e.observed.task = updated.Task
425			e.milestone = MilestoneMerged
426			return "recorded DONE at revision " + updated.Revision, nil
427		})
428	}
```

```text
388		} else if !observed.branchExists {
389			if noCheckout {
390				branchCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRef, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
391					"local task branch is already absent for a persisted DONE task with no checkout", "")
392			} else {
393				branchCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRef, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
394					"local task branch "+observed.branchRef+" is missing", "restore the task branch before retiring its checkout")
395			}
396		} else if observed.branchOID == "" {
397			branchCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRef, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
398				"local task branch resolved to no commit", "restore the local task branch")
399		}
400	
401		relationCondition := condition(ConditionBranchRelation, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
402			fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) is contained in %s (%s)", candidate.Branch, observed.branchOID, candidate.Base, observed.baseOID), "")
403		switch {
404		case !observed.branchExists && noCheckout:
405			relationCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRelation, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
406				"missing branch is accepted only because persisted DONE records no checkout", "")
407		case observed.containedErr != nil:
408			relationCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRelation, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
409				observed.containedErr.Error(), "repair local containment observation")
410		case observed.branchExists && observed.baseExists && observed.branchOIDErr == nil && observed.baseOIDErr == nil && !observed.contained:
411			relationCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRelation, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
412				fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) is not contained in %s (%s)", candidate.Branch, observed.branchOID, candidate.Base, observed.baseOID),
413				"integrate the task branch into the named local base first")
414		case !observed.branchExists || !observed.baseExists || observed.branchOID == "" || observed.baseOID == "":
415			relationCondition = condition(ConditionBranchRelation, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired,
416				"containment cannot be proved from exact local branch and base OIDs", "restore both local refs")
417		}
418		return []Condition{baseCondition, branchCondition, relationCondition}
419	}
```

```text
48			t.Fatal(err)

52		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
53		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
```

Review target: `/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-state-machine read-only targeted verification of the 15 listed previously confirmed issues; no edits, no subagents, no broad/full tests`

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

```bash
import hashlib, os, subprocess
root='/Users/david/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-state-machine'

tracked={}
for rec in raw.split(b'\0'):

    meta,path=rec.split(b'\t',1)
    mode,typ,obj=meta.decode().split()
    tracked[path.decode()]=(mode,obj)
changed=[]; deleted=[]
for path,(mode,obj) in tracked.items():
    full=os.path.join(root,path)
    if not os.path.lexists(full):
        deleted.append(path); continue
    if mode=='120000':
        data=os.readlink(full).encode()
    elif os.path.isfile(full):
        with open(full,'rb') as f: data=f.read()
    else:
        continue
    digest=hashlib.sha1(b'blob '+str(len(data)).encode()+b'\0'+data).hexdigest()
    if digest!=obj: changed.append(path)
extras=[]
for dirpath,dirs,files in os.walk(root):

    for name in files:
        p=os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath,name),root)
        if p not in tracked:
            extras.append(p)
print('CHANGED',len(changed)); print('\n'.join(changed))
print('DELETED',len(deleted)); print('\n'.join(deleted))
print('EXTRA',len(extras)); print('\n'.join(extras[:300]))
PY
```

```text
247	func (s *lifecycleService) verifyMergedSpec(request Request, observed lifecycleObservation) PlanSpec {
248		options := request.Options.(VerifyMergedOptions)
249		conditions := s.completionConditions(observed, options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage)
250		proofCondition := completionProofCondition(observed)
251		proofSurvivesDirtyPolicy := true
252		if options.SquashCommit != "" && observed.statusErr == nil && observed.status.Dirty() && options.Dirty == DirtyCommit {
253			proofSurvivesDirtyPolicy = false
254			proofCondition = condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
255				"the squash attestation predates the new commit requested by --dirty=commit",
256				"commit and integrate the dirty work before supplying a fresh squash attestation")
257		}
258		conditions = append(conditions,
259			condition(ConditionBranchRelation, VerdictMet, RequirementAdvisory,
260				fmt.Sprintf("local relation to %s is behind %d and ahead %d",
261					observed.completionBaseRef, observed.finish.Relation.BaseOnly, observed.finish.Relation.BranchOnly), ""),
262			proofCondition,
263		)
264	
265		effects := s.completionDirtyEffects(observed, options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage)
266		if !proofSurvivesDirtyPolicy {
267			effects = nil
268		} else if completionDirtyExecutable(observed, options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage) {
269			effects = append(effects, NewEffect(
270				EffectVerifyAncestry, "prove exact merge ancestry", observed.completionBaseRef, false, false,
271				map[string]string{
272					"proof-ref": observed.proofRef, "proof-oid": observed.proofOID,
273					"base-ref": observed.completionBaseRef, "base-oid": observed.completionBaseOID,
274				},
275			))
276			if options.PushBase {
277				effects = append(effects, completionPushBaseEffect(observed))
278			}
279			effects = append(effects, completionTaskUpdateEffect(observed))
280		}
281		return s.completionPlanSpec(
282			request, observed, conditions, effects,
283			completionConfirmation(observed, options.Dirty, "Verify this merge and record DONE?"),
284			completionFallback(observed.task.ID, "--merged", options.Dirty, options.CommitMessage,
285				options.PushBase, options.BaseRef, options.SquashCommit),
286			"Verify "+observed.task.Title()+" merged into "+observed.completionBaseRef,
287		)
288	}
289	
290	func (s *lifecycleService) completionPlanSpec(
291		request Request,
292		observed lifecycleObservation,
293		conditions []Condition,
294		effects []Effect,
295		confirmation Confirmation,
296		fallback string,
297		summary string,
298	) PlanSpec {
299		return PlanSpec{
300			Authority:         s.baseAuthority(request, observed),
301			Conditions:        conditions,
302			Effects:           effects,
303			RetainedResources: completionRetainedResources(observed),
304			Confirmation:      confirmation,
305			FallbackCommand:   fallback,
306			Summary:           summary,
307			DisplayedAt:       s.now(),
308		}
309	}
310	
311	func (s *lifecycleService) completionConditions(
312		observed lifecycleObservation,
313		dirty DirtyPolicy,
314		message string,
315	) []Condition {
316		conditions := []Condition{
317			condition(ConditionTaskCurrent, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
318				"task "+observed.task.ID+" revision "+observed.record.Revision, ""),
319			condition(ConditionRepoIdentity, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
320				"Git common directory "+observed.gitCommonDir, ""),
321		}
322		conditions = append(conditions, completionCheckoutConditions(observed)...)
323		conditions = append(conditions, completionGitConditions(observed, dirty, message)...)
324		conditions = append(conditions, completionArtifactCondition(observed))
325		conditions = append(conditions, s.completionRuntimeConditions(observed)...)
326		conditions = append(conditions, completionBaseCondition(observed))
327		return conditions
328	}
329	
330	func completionCheckoutConditions(observed lifecycleObservation) []Condition {
331		if !observed.hasCheckout() {
332			verdict := VerdictBlocked
333			evidence := "the exact task checkout is not registered"
334			if observed.worktreeErr != nil && !isWorktreeNotFound(observed.worktreeErr) {
335				verdict = VerdictError
336				evidence = observed.worktreeErr.Error()
337			}
338			return []Condition{
339				condition(ConditionCheckoutPresent, verdict, RequirementRequired, evidence, "resume or reconcile the exact checkout"),
340				condition(ConditionCheckoutExact, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "checkout identity is unavailable", "refresh worktree topology"),
341				condition(ConditionCheckoutLinked, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "checkout kind is unavailable", "refresh worktree topology"),
342				condition(ConditionCheckoutBranch, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired, "checkout branch is unavailable", "restore the named task branch"),
343			}
344		}
345	
346		exactVerdict, exactEvidence := checkoutExactVerdict(observed)
347		kindVerdict := VerdictMet
348		kindEvidence := "canonical main checkout"
349		if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree {
350			kindEvidence = "exact linked worktree"
351			if !observed.isLinkedWorktree() {
352				kindVerdict = VerdictBlocked
353				kindEvidence = "worktree task does not resolve to a linked checkout"
354			}
355		} else if !observed.worktree.Worktree.Main || observed.worktree.Worktree.Bare {
356			kindVerdict = VerdictBlocked
357			kindEvidence = "branch or direct task does not resolve to Git's canonical main checkout"
358		}
359	
360		branchVerdict := VerdictMet
361		branchEvidence := "checkout and registry name task branch " + observed.task.Branch
362		if observed.task.Branch == "" || observed.statusErr != nil || observed.status.Detached ||
363			observed.status.Branch != observed.task.Branch || observed.worktree.Worktree.Detached ||
364			observed.worktree.Worktree.Branch != observed.task.Branch {
365			branchVerdict = VerdictBlocked
366			branchEvidence = fmt.Sprintf("registry=%q status=%q expected=%q detached=%t",
367				observed.worktree.Worktree.Branch, observed.status.Branch, observed.task.Branch,
368				observed.status.Detached || observed.worktree.Worktree.Detached)
369			if observed.statusErr != nil {
370				branchVerdict = VerdictError
371				branchEvidence = observed.statusErr.Error()
372			}
373		}
374		return []Condition{
375			condition(ConditionCheckoutPresent, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired, "registered checkout "+observed.checkout, ""),
376			condition(ConditionCheckoutExact, exactVerdict, RequirementRequired, exactEvidence, "reconcile task and worktree identity"),
377			condition(ConditionCheckoutLinked, kindVerdict, RequirementRequired, kindEvidence, "reconcile the task checkout mode"),
378			condition(ConditionCheckoutBranch, branchVerdict, RequirementRequired, branchEvidence, "restore the exact named task branch"),
379		}
380	}
381	
382	func completionGitConditions(observed lifecycleObservation, dirty DirtyPolicy, message string) []Condition {
383		status := observed.status
384		statusVerdict := VerdictMet
385		statusEvidence := status.Summary()
386		if observed.statusErr != nil {
387			statusVerdict = VerdictError
388			statusEvidence = observed.statusErr.Error()
389		}
390	
391		finishVerdict := VerdictMet
392		finishEvidence := fmt.Sprintf("fingerprint %s; base-only=%d branch-only=%d",
393			observed.finish.Fingerprint, observed.finish.Relation.BaseOnly, observed.finish.Relation.BranchOnly)
394		switch {
395		case !observed.hasCheckout():
396			finishVerdict = VerdictUnknown
397			finishEvidence = "finish analysis requires the exact checkout"
398		case observed.completionBaseRef == "":
399			finishVerdict = VerdictBlocked
400			finishEvidence = "finish analysis requires an explicit base ref"
401		case observed.finishErr != nil:
402			finishVerdict = VerdictError
403			finishEvidence = observed.finishErr.Error()
404		case observed.finish.Fingerprint == "":
405			finishVerdict = VerdictError
406			finishEvidence = "finish analysis returned no content fingerprint"
407		}
408	
409		operationVerdict := VerdictMet
410		operationEvidence := "no Git operation is in progress"
411		if observed.operationErr != nil {
412			operationVerdict = VerdictError
413			operationEvidence = observed.operationErr.Error()
414		} else if observed.inProgress {
415			operationVerdict = VerdictBlocked
416			operationEvidence = "Git operation " + observed.operation + " is in progress"
417		}
418	
419		conflictVerdict := VerdictMet
420		conflictEvidence := "no unmerged paths"
421		if observed.statusErr != nil {
422			conflictVerdict = VerdictError
423			conflictEvidence = observed.statusErr.Error()
424		} else if observed.status.Conflicted > 0 || observed.finish.Status.Conflicted > 0 {
425			conflictVerdict = VerdictBlocked
426			conflictEvidence = strconv.Itoa(max(observed.status.Conflicted, observed.finish.Status.Conflicted)) + " conflicted path(s)"
427		}
428	
429		cleanVerdict, cleanEvidence := completionDirtyCondition(observed, dirty, message)
430		return []Condition{
431			condition(ConditionGitStatus, statusVerdict, RequirementRequired, statusEvidence, "repair Git status observation"),
432			condition(ConditionFinishAnalysis, finishVerdict, RequirementRequired, finishEvidence, "refresh the exact finish analysis"),
433			condition(ConditionGitOperation, operationVerdict, RequirementRequired, operationEvidence, "finish or abort the Git operation"),
434			condition(ConditionGitConflict, conflictVerdict, RequirementRequired, conflictEvidence, "resolve or abort conflicts before completion"),
435			condition(ConditionCheckoutClean, cleanVerdict, RequirementRequired, cleanEvidence, "select fail, commit with a message, or discard"),
436		}
437	}
438	
439	func completionDirtyCondition(observed lifecycleObservation, dirty DirtyPolicy, message string) (Verdict, string) {
440		if observed.statusErr != nil {
441			return VerdictError, observed.statusErr.Error()
442		}
443		if !observed.status.Dirty() {
444			return VerdictMet, "checkout is clean; dirty policy " + string(dirty) + " causes no content mutation"
445		}
446		evidence := observed.status.Breakdown()
447		if observed.finishErr == nil {
448			evidence += fmt.Sprintf("; %d path(s) match %s and %d contain unique content",
449				observed.finish.EquivalentDirty(), observed.completionBaseRef, observed.finish.UniqueDirty())
450		}
451		switch dirty {
452		case DirtyAuto:
453			return VerdictNeedsInput, evidence + "; choose an explicit dirty policy"
454		case DirtyFail:
455			return VerdictBlocked, evidence + "; fail policy refuses dirty completion"
456		case DirtyCommit:
457			if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
458				return VerdictNeedsInput, evidence + "; commit-all requires a nonempty message"
459			}
460			return VerdictMet, evidence + "; commit-all was explicitly selected"
461		case DirtyDiscard:
462			if observed.finish.UniqueDirty() > 0 {
463				return VerdictMet, evidence + "; discard-all was explicitly selected and requires DROP"
464			}
465			return VerdictMet, evidence + "; discard-all was explicitly selected and requires approval"
466		default:
467			return VerdictError, "unknown dirty policy " + string(dirty)
468		}
469	}
470	
471	func completionArtifactCondition(observed lifecycleObservation) Condition {
472		switch {
473		case !observed.hasCheckout():
474			return condition(ConditionArtifactReady, VerdictUnknown, RequirementRequired,
475				"artifact readiness requires the exact checkout", "restore the checkout")
476		case observed.artifactErr != nil:
477			return condition(ConditionArtifactReady, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
478				observed.artifactErr.Error(), "repair artifact readiness observation")
479		case observed.artifact.Ready():
480			return condition(ConditionArtifactReady, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired, artifactEvidence(observed), "")
481		default:
482			return condition(ConditionArtifactReady, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
483				artifactEvidence(observed), "finalize or explicitly discard every artifact intent")
484		}
485	}
486	
487	func (s *lifecycleService) completionRuntimeConditions(observed lifecycleObservation) []Condition {
488		if observed.runtimeErr != nil {
489			return []Condition{
490				condition(ConditionRuntimeAvailable, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
491					observed.runtimeErr.Error(), "repair runtime backend resolution"),
492				condition(ConditionAgentOccupancy, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
493					observed.runtimeErr.Error(), "repair recognized-agent observation"),
494			}
495		}
496		availableVerdict := VerdictMet
497		availableEvidence := "runtime backend " + runtimeName(observed.runtime) + " was available for strict inspection"
498		if observed.runtime != nil && observed.runtime.Name() != "none" && !observed.runtimeAvailable {
499			availableVerdict = VerdictBlocked
500			availableEvidence = "runtime backend " + observed.runtime.Name() + " is unavailable"
501		}
502		occupancyVerdict, occupancyEvidence := s.completionOccupancyVerdict(observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr)
503		return []Condition{
504			condition(ConditionRuntimeAvailable, availableVerdict, RequirementRequired,
505				availableEvidence, "select an available runtime backend"),
506			condition(ConditionAgentOccupancy, occupancyVerdict, RequirementRequired,
507				occupancyEvidence, "stop every other recognized agent or use another checkout"),
508		}
509	}
510	
511	func (s *lifecycleService) completionOccupancyVerdict(occupancy runtime.Occupancy, err error) (Verdict, string) {
512		occupancyErr := s.writerOccupancyError(occupancy, err)
513		if occupancyErr == nil {
514			if s.allowSharedCheckout {
515				return VerdictMet, "shared-checkout override accepts the observed or explicitly unobserved runtime occupancy"
516			}
517			return VerdictMet, "no other recognized agent occupies the checkout; only the exact caller pane is excluded"
518		}
519		verdict := VerdictBlocked
520		if err != nil || occupancy.CurrentPane.Err != nil || occupancy.SessionCoverageErr != nil ||
521			occupancy.SessionList.Err != nil || occupancy.AgentActivityList.Err != nil || occupancyObservationIncomplete(occupancy) {
522			verdict = VerdictError
523		}
524		return verdict, occupancyErr.Error()
525	}
526	
527	func completionBaseCondition(observed lifecycleObservation) Condition {
528		requirement := RequirementRequired
529		if observed.mode == task.ModeDirect {
530			requirement = RequirementAdvisory
531		}
532		switch {
533		case observed.completionBaseRef == "":
534			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictBlocked, requirement,
535				"completion has no explicit base ref", "record or select an explicit base ref")
536		case observed.completionBaseOIDErr != nil:
537			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictError, requirement,
538				observed.completionBaseOIDErr.Error(), "restore the exact base ref")
539		case observed.completionBaseOID == "":
540			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictBlocked, requirement,
541				"base ref "+observed.completionBaseRef+" resolved to no commit", "restore the exact base ref")
542		default:
543			return condition(ConditionExplicitBase, VerdictMet, requirement,
544				fmt.Sprintf("base %s at %s", observed.completionBaseRef, observed.completionBaseOID), "")
545		}
546	}
547	
548	func completionIntegrationCondition(observed lifecycleObservation, dirty DirtyPolicy, message string) Condition {
549		if observed.mode == task.ModeBranch {
550			verdict, _ := completionDirtyCondition(observed, dirty, message)
551			if verdict == VerdictMet {
552				return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
553					"the exact canonical task checkout will be clean before switching to "+observed.completionBaseRef, "")
554			}
555			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, verdict, RequirementRequired,
556				"the canonical task checkout is not yet switchable", "finalize its dirty policy")
557		}
558		integration := observed.integration
559		switch {
560		case integration.worktreeErr != nil:
561			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
562				integration.worktreeErr.Error(), "repair canonical main worktree identity")
563		case !integration.worktreeFound:
564			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
565				"canonical main checkout is not registered", "restore the canonical main checkout")
566		case integration.worktree.Path != observed.repoPath || integration.worktree.GitCommonDir != observed.gitCommonDir ||
567			!integration.worktree.Worktree.Main || integration.worktree.Worktree.Bare:
568			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
569				"integration target is not the exact canonical main checkout", "repair worktree topology")
570		case integration.statusErr != nil:
571			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
572				integration.statusErr.Error(), "repair canonical checkout status observation")
573		case integration.headErr != nil:
574			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
575				integration.headErr.Error(), "repair canonical checkout HEAD observation")
576		case integration.operationErr != nil:
577			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
578				integration.operationErr.Error(), "repair canonical checkout Git-operation observation")
579		case integration.inProgress:
580			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
581				"canonical checkout has Git operation "+integration.operation+" in progress", "finish or abort it")
582		case integration.status.Conflicted > 0:
583			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
584				fmt.Sprintf("canonical checkout has %d conflicted path(s)", integration.status.Conflicted), "resolve or abort conflicts")
585		case integration.status.Dirty():
586			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
587				"canonical checkout is dirty: "+integration.status.Breakdown(), "preserve its unrelated bytes before integration")
588		case integration.worktree.Worktree.Head != integration.head:
589			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
590				"canonical worktree registry HEAD differs from checkout HEAD", "refresh worktree topology")
591		default:
592			return condition(ConditionIntegrationTarget, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
593				"canonical main checkout is exact, clean, conflict-free, and switchable", "")
594		}
595	}
596	
597	func (s *lifecycleService) completionIntegrationOccupancyCondition(observed lifecycleObservation) Condition {
598		if observed.runtimeErr != nil {
599			return condition(ConditionIntegrationOccupancy, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
600				observed.runtimeErr.Error(), "repair runtime backend resolution")
601		}
602		verdict, evidence := s.completionOccupancyVerdict(observed.integration.occupancy, observed.integration.occupancyErr)
603		return condition(ConditionIntegrationOccupancy, verdict, RequirementRequired, evidence,
604			"stop every other recognized agent in the canonical integration checkout")
605	}
606	
607	func completionReviewProviderCondition(observed lifecycleObservation) Condition {
608		switch {
609		case observed.reviewResolveErr != nil:
610			return condition(ConditionReviewProvider, VerdictUnsupported, RequirementAdvisory,
611				observed.reviewResolveErr.Error()+"; a successful branch push remains a valid publication", "open the review manually")
612		case observed.reviewProvider == nil:
613			return condition(ConditionReviewProvider, VerdictUnsupported, RequirementAdvisory,
614				"no forge provider was resolved; a successful branch push remains a valid publication", "open the review manually")
615		case !observed.reviewAvailable:
616			return condition(ConditionReviewProvider, VerdictUnsupported, RequirementAdvisory,
617				fmt.Sprintf("%s provider CLI %s is unavailable; a successful branch push remains a valid publication",
618					observed.reviewKind, observed.reviewProvider.Bin()), "install or authenticate the provider CLI, or open the review manually")
619		default:
620			return condition(ConditionReviewProvider, VerdictMet, RequirementAdvisory,
621				fmt.Sprintf("%s provider CLI %s will create the review", observed.reviewKind, observed.reviewProvider.Bin()), "")
622		}
623	}
624	
625	func completionProofCondition(observed lifecycleObservation) Condition {
626		switch {
627		case observed.completionBaseRef == "":
628			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
629				"merge proof requires an exact base ref", "select a local or explicit remote-tracking base ref")
630		case observed.completionBaseOIDErr != nil:
631			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
632				observed.completionBaseOIDErr.Error(), "restore the selected base ref")
633		case observed.completionBaseOID == "":
634			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
635				"merge proof requires an exact base OID", "restore the selected base ref")
636		case observed.proofRef == "":
637			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
638				"merge proof ref is empty", "restore the task branch or name an exact squash commit")
639		case observed.proofOIDErr != nil:
640			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
641				observed.proofOIDErr.Error(), "restore the exact proof ref")
642		case observed.proofOID == "":
643			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
644				"proof ref "+observed.proofRef+" resolved to no commit", "restore the exact proof commit")
645		case observed.proofErr != nil:
646			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictError, RequirementRequired,
647				observed.proofErr.Error(), "repair local ancestry observation")
648		case !observed.proofContained:
649			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictBlocked, RequirementRequired,
650				fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) is not an ancestor of %s (%s)",
651					observed.proofRef, observed.proofOID, observed.completionBaseRef, observed.completionBaseOID),
652				"fetch explicitly if desired, then select the freshly observed ref; no fetch is assumed")
653		default:
654			return condition(ConditionMergeProof, VerdictMet, RequirementRequired,
655				fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) is an ancestor of %s (%s)",
656					observed.proofRef, observed.proofOID, observed.completionBaseRef, observed.completionBaseOID), "")
657		}
658	}
659	
660	func (s *lifecycleService) completionDirtyEffects(
661		observed lifecycleObservation,
662		dirty DirtyPolicy,
663		message string,
664	) []Effect {
665		if observed.statusErr != nil || !observed.status.Dirty() {
666			return nil
667		}
668		switch dirty {
669		case DirtyCommit:
670			if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
671				return nil
672			}
673			return []Effect{NewEffect(
674				EffectCommitAll, "commit every staged, unstaged, and untracked change", observed.checkout, false, false,
675				map[string]string{"message": strings.TrimSpace(message), "scope": "all"},
676			)}
677		case DirtyDiscard:
678			details := map[string]string{"scope": "all", "finish-fingerprint": observed.finish.Fingerprint}
679			if observed.finish.UniqueDirty() > 0 {
680				details["token"] = "DROP"
681			}
682			return []Effect{NewEffect(
683				EffectDiscardAll, "discard every staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked change", observed.checkout, true, false,
684				details,
685			)}
686		default:
687			return nil
688		}
689	}
690	
691	func completionDirtyExecutable(observed lifecycleObservation, dirty DirtyPolicy, message string) bool {
692		if observed.statusErr != nil || !observed.status.Dirty() {
693			return true
694		}
695		switch dirty {
696		case DirtyCommit:
697			return strings.TrimSpace(message) != ""
698		case DirtyDiscard:
699			return true
700		default:
701			return false
702		}
703	}
704	
705	func effectiveCompletionRelation(observed lifecycleObservation, dirty DirtyPolicy, message string) gitx.BranchRelation {
706		relation := observed.finish.Relation
707		if observed.statusErr == nil && observed.status.Dirty() && dirty == DirtyCommit && strings.TrimSpace(message) != "" {
708			relation.BranchOnly++
709		}
710		return relation
711	}
712	
713	func completionConfirmation(observed lifecycleObservation, dirty DirtyPolicy, prompt string) Confirmation {
714		if observed.statusErr == nil && observed.status.Dirty() && dirty == DirtyDiscard && observed.finish.UniqueDirty() > 0 {
715			return Confirmation{
716				Kind:   ConfirmationTyped,
717				Prompt: fmt.Sprintf("Type DROP to discard %d unique path(s) under this exact plan", observed.finish.UniqueDirty()),
718				Token:  "DROP",
719			}
720		}
721		return Confirmation{Kind: ConfirmationApproval, Prompt: prompt}
722	}
723	
724	func completionPushBaseEffect(observed lifecycleObservation) Effect {
725		return NewEffect(
726			EffectPushBase, "optionally push the selected base", observed.completionBaseRef, false, true,
727			map[string]string{"remote": "origin", "base": observed.completionBaseRef, "warning-on-failure": "true"},
728		)
729	}
730	
731	func completionTaskUpdateEffect(observed lifecycleObservation) Effect {
732		return NewEffect(
733			EffectUpdateTask, "write DONE lifecycle state last", observed.task.ID, false, false,
734			map[string]string{
735				"expected-revision": observed.record.Revision, "state": string(task.Done),
736				"owner": "retain", "worktree-path": observed.task.WorktreePath,
737				"runtime-name": observed.task.RuntimeName, "runtime-handle": observed.task.RuntimeHandle,
738			},
739		)
740	}
741	
742	func completionRetainedResources(observed lifecycleObservation) []string {
743		retained := []string{"branch:" + observed.task.Branch}
744		if observed.checkout != "" {
745			retained = append(retained, "checkout:"+observed.checkout)
746		}
747		if observed.task.RuntimeName != "" || observed.task.RuntimeHandle != "" {
748			retained = append(retained, "runtime:"+observed.task.RuntimeName+":"+observed.task.RuntimeHandle)
749		}
750		return retained
751	}
752	
753	func completionFallback(id, mode string, dirty DirtyPolicy, message string, push bool, baseRef, squash string) string {
754		parts := []string{"dev", "done", shellQuote(id)}
755		if mode != "" {
756			parts = append(parts, mode)
757		}
758		if dirty != DirtyAuto {
759			parts = append(parts, "--dirty="+string(dirty))
760		}
761		if dirty == DirtyCommit && strings.TrimSpace(message) != "" {
762			parts = append(parts, "--message", shellQuote(strings.TrimSpace(message)))
763		}
764		if baseRef != "" {
765			parts = append(parts, "--base-ref", shellQuote(baseRef))
766		}
767		if squash != "" {
768			parts = append(parts, "--confirm-squash", shellQuote(squash))
769		}
770		if push {
771			parts = append(parts, "--push")
772		}
773		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
774	}
```
