Review target: `-- read-only review of the current uncommitted working tree; do not edit, delegate, or run broad/full tests. Focus only on the invariants named in the user request and report only concrete remaining correctness defects.`

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

380	func (s *lifecycleService) observeActionRefs(ctx context.Context, request Request, observed *lifecycleObservation) {
381		observed.localBranchExists, observed.localBranchOIDErr = s.gitRefState(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Branch)
382		if observed.localBranchExists && observed.localBranchOIDErr == nil {
383			observed.localBranchOID, observed.localBranchOIDErr = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Branch)
384		}
385		observed.remoteBranch = "origin/" + observed.task.Branch
386		observed.remoteBranchExists, observed.remoteBranchOIDErr = s.gitRefState(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteBranch)
387		if observed.remoteBranchExists && observed.remoteBranchOIDErr == nil {
388			observed.remoteBranchOID, observed.remoteBranchOIDErr = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteBranch)
389		}
390	
391		switch request.Action {
392		case ParkCold:
393			if observed.mode == task.ModeBranch {
394				observed.baseRef = observed.task.Base
395				if observed.baseRef == "" {
396					observed.baseRef = s.gitDefaultBranch(ctx, observed.repoPath)
397				}
398				if observed.baseRef != "" {
399					observed.baseRefExists, observed.baseRefExistsErr = s.gitRefState(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.baseRef)
400				}
401			}
402		case Resume:
403			observed.baseRef = observed.task.Base
404			if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree && !observed.hasCheckout() {
405				switch {
406				case observed.localBranchExists:
407					observed.baseRef = observed.task.Branch
408					observed.baseRefExists = true
409					observed.baseRefExistsErr = observed.localBranchOIDErr
410				case observed.remoteBranchOIDErr != nil:
411					observed.baseRef = observed.remoteBranch
412					observed.baseRefExistsErr = observed.remoteBranchOIDErr
413				default:
414					observed.baseRef = observed.remoteBranch
415					observed.baseRefExists = observed.remoteBranchExists
416				}
417			} else {
418				if observed.remoteBranchExists {
419					observed.baseRef = observed.remoteBranch
420				}
421				if observed.baseRef != "" {
422					observed.baseRefExists, observed.baseRefExistsErr = s.gitRefState(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.baseRef)
423				}
424			}
425			if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree && !observed.hasCheckout() &&
426				(observed.task.State == task.Warm || observed.task.State == task.Cold) {
427				if observed.task.State == task.Warm && observed.task.WorktreePath != "" {
428					observed.desiredWorktree, observed.desiredWorktreeErr = s.canonicalPath(observed.task.WorktreePath)
429				} else {
430					observed.desiredWorktree, observed.desiredWorktreeErr = s.renderWorktreePath(observed.task)
431				}
432				if observed.desiredWorktreeErr == nil {
433					observed.desiredWorktreeErr = wt.ValidateTarget(observed.desiredWorktree, observed.repoPath)
434				}
435			}
436		case CompleteDirect:
437			observed.completionBaseRef = observed.task.Branch
438		case CompleteFF, ReviewHandoff:
439			observed.completionBaseRef = observed.task.Base
440		case VerifyMerged:
441			options := request.Options.(VerifyMergedOptions)
442			observed.completionBaseRef = options.BaseRef
443			if observed.completionBaseRef == "" {
444				observed.completionBaseRef = observed.task.Base
445			}
446		}

397	func (e *executionState) applyResume(ctx context.Context) (Result, error) {
398		options := e.plan.Request.Options.(ResumeOptions)
399		observed := &e.observed
400		e.resumePath = observed.checkout
401		if observed.runtime != nil && observed.runtime.Name() != "none" && observed.savedRuntimeLive {
402			e.resumeRuntimeName = observed.runtime.Name()
403			e.resumeRuntimeHandle = observed.task.RuntimeHandle
404		}
405		runtimeMutated := false
406		checkoutMutated := false
407	
408		for _, effect := range e.plan.Effects() {
409			switch effect.Code {
410			case EffectFetchRefs:
411				if err := e.service.revalidateRepository(ctx, *observed); err != nil {
412					return e.fail(err, "refresh the canonical repository before fetching")
413				}
414				if observed.hasCheckout() {
415					if err := e.service.revalidateGitBaseline(ctx, *observed); err != nil {
416						return e.fail(err, "refresh checkout authority before fetching")
417					}
418				} else if matches, err := e.service.branchCheckoutCount(ctx, *observed); err != nil || matches != observed.branchMatches {
419					if err != nil {
420						return e.fail(err, "refresh worktree topology before fetching")
421					}
422					return e.fail(staleBoundary("task branch checkout topology changed before fetch"), "refresh resume")
423				}
424				e.runWarning(effect, func() (string, error) {
425					_, fetchErr := e.service.gitRun(ctx, observed.repoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin")
426					if fetchErr != nil {
427						return "", fetchErr
428					}
429					return "fetched origin", nil
430				}, "fetch failed")
431				if observed.hasCheckout() {
432					if err := e.service.refreshCheckout(ctx, observed, resumeExpectedBranchBeforeSwitch(*observed)); err != nil {
433						return e.fail(fmt.Errorf("refresh checkout after fetch: %w", err), "inspect fetched refs and retry resume")
434					}
435				}
436			case EffectCreateWorktree:
437				if err := e.service.revalidateResumeBranchRefs(ctx, observed, options.FetchRefs); err != nil {
438					return e.fail(err, "refresh the task branch before rebuilding its checkout")
439				}
440				localExists, localErr := e.service.gitRefState(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Branch)
441				if localErr != nil {
442					return e.fail(fmt.Errorf("observe local task branch before reconstruction: %w", localErr), "repair Git ref observation and retry")
443				}
444				remoteExists, remoteErr := e.service.gitRefState(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.remoteBranch)
445				if remoteErr != nil {
446					return e.fail(fmt.Errorf("observe published task branch before reconstruction: %w", remoteErr), "repair Git ref observation and retry")
447				}
448				base := observed.task.Branch
449				if !localExists {
450					base = observed.remoteBranch
451				}
452				if !localExists && !remoteExists {
453					return e.fail(staleBoundary("local and published task branches are unavailable after fetch"), "restore origin/"+observed.task.Branch+" before reconstructing the checkout")
454				}
455				if matches, err := e.service.branchCheckoutCount(ctx, *observed); err != nil {
456					return e.fail(err, "refresh repository topology before rebuilding")
457				} else if matches != 0 {
458					return e.fail(staleBoundary("the task branch acquired a checkout before reconstruction"), "refresh and reuse the newly registered exact checkout")
459				}
460				err := e.run(effect, func() (string, error) {
461					created, createErr := e.service.createWorktree(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
462						RepoPath: observed.repoPath, RepoName: observed.task.Repo,
463						Branch: observed.task.Branch, Base: base,
464						Path: effect.Target, Label: resumeRuntimeLabel(observed.task),
465						NoProvision: options.NoProvision, NoRuntime: true,
466					})
467					if createErr != nil {
468						var exists *wt.ErrExists
469						if errors.As(createErr, &exists) {
470							return "", staleBoundary("the task branch became checked out at " + exists.Path)
471						}
472						return "", createErr
473					}
474					if created == nil || created.Path == "" {
475						return "", errors.New("worktree manager returned no checkout path")
476					}
477					path, canonicalErr := e.service.canonicalPath(created.Path)
478					if canonicalErr != nil {
479						return "", canonicalErr
480					}
481					target, targetErr := e.service.canonicalPath(effect.Target)
482					if targetErr != nil || path != target {
483						return "", fmt.Errorf("worktree manager created %q, approved target is %q", path, target)
484					}
485					e.resumePath = path
486					return "rebuilt linked worktree from " + base, nil
487				})
488				if err != nil {
489					return e.fail(err, "inspect any partially created checkout, then refresh resume before retrying")
490				}
491				registered, resolveErr := e.service.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, e.resumePath)
492				if resolveErr != nil {
493					return e.fail(fmt.Errorf("resolve rebuilt exact worktree: %w", resolveErr), "preserve the rebuilt checkout and reconcile its registration")
494				}
495				observed.worktree = registered
496				observed.worktreeFound = true
497				observed.worktreeErr = nil
498				observed.checkout = registered.Path
499				if !registered.IsLinkedWorktree() || registered.Worktree.Branch != observed.task.Branch {
500					return e.fail(errors.New("rebuilt checkout is not the exact linked task branch"), "preserve and reconcile the rebuilt checkout")
501				}
502				if err := e.service.refreshCheckout(ctx, observed, observed.task.Branch); err != nil {
503					return e.fail(fmt.Errorf("verify rebuilt worktree: %w", err), "preserve and inspect the rebuilt checkout")
504				}

629	func (s *lifecycleService) revalidateGitBaseline(ctx context.Context, observed lifecycleObservation) error {
630		registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.checkout)
631		if err != nil {
632			return staleBoundary("exact worktree registration changed: " + err.Error())
633		}
634		if registered != observed.worktree {
635			return staleBoundary("exact worktree path, branch, HEAD, Main, locked, or prunable flags changed")
636		}
637		status, err := s.gitStatus(ctx, observed.checkout)
638		if err != nil {
639			return staleBoundary("Git status observation changed: " + err.Error())
640		}
641		if !sameStatus(status, observed.status) {
642			return staleBoundary("Git status, branch, upstream, ahead, behind, dirty, or conflict evidence changed")
643		}
644		head, err := s.gitRun(ctx, observed.checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
645		if err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(head) != observed.head {
646			return staleBoundary("checkout HEAD changed")
647		}
648		baseOID, baseErr := s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Base)
649		upstreamOID, upstreamErr := s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, status.Upstream)
650		if errorString(baseErr) != errorString(observed.baseOIDErr) || baseOID != observed.baseOID ||
651			errorString(upstreamErr) != errorString(observed.upstreamOIDErr) || upstreamOID != observed.upstreamOID {
652			return staleBoundary("base or upstream ref OID changed")
653		}
654		operation, active, err := s.gitInProgress(ctx, observed.checkout)
655		if err != nil || operation != observed.operation || active != observed.inProgress {
656			return staleBoundary("Git operation evidence changed")
657		}
658		return nil
659	}

661	func (s *lifecycleService) refreshCheckout(ctx context.Context, observed *lifecycleObservation, expectedBranch string) error {
662		registered, err := s.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.checkout)
663		if err != nil {
664			return err
665		}
666		if registered.Path != observed.checkout || registered.GitCommonDir != observed.gitCommonDir {
667			return errors.New("checkout path or Git common directory changed")
668		}
669		if observed.mode == task.ModeWorktree && !registered.IsLinkedWorktree() {
670			return errors.New("worktree task no longer resolves to a linked checkout")
671		}
672		if observed.mode != task.ModeWorktree && (!registered.Worktree.Main || registered.Worktree.Bare) {
673			return errors.New("canonical task no longer resolves to the main checkout")
674		}
675		status, err := s.gitStatus(ctx, observed.checkout)
676		if err != nil {
677			return err
678		}
679		if status.Detached || expectedBranch != "" && status.Branch != expectedBranch || registered.Worktree.Branch != status.Branch {
680			return fmt.Errorf("checkout branch changed: registry=%q status=%q expected=%q", registered.Worktree.Branch, status.Branch, expectedBranch)
681		}
682		head, err := s.gitRun(ctx, observed.checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
683		if err != nil {
684			return err
685		}
686		head = strings.TrimSpace(head)
687		if registered.Worktree.Head != head {
688			return fmt.Errorf("worktree registry HEAD %q differs from checkout HEAD %q", registered.Worktree.Head, head)
689		}
690		baseOID, baseOIDErr := s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.task.Base)
691		upstreamOID, upstreamOIDErr := s.resolveRefOID(ctx, observed.repoPath, status.Upstream)
692		operation, active, operationErr := s.gitInProgress(ctx, observed.checkout)

726			return fmt.Errorf("cold parking requires a clean checkout: %s", observed.status.Breakdown())

728		if observed.status.Detached || observed.status.Branch != observed.task.Branch {
729			return errors.New("cold parking checkout is no longer on the task branch")
730		}

732			return errors.New("cold parking refuses an active Git operation or unresolved conflict")

735			return fmt.Errorf("cold parking requires a published ahead=0 branch; status is %s", observed.status.Summary())
736		}
737		return nil
738	}

+		key := candidate.dir + "\x00" + candidate.ref
+		if seen[key] {
+			continue
+		}
+		seen[key] = true
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return false, joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
+		}
+		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
+			return true, nil
+		} else if !gitNotAncestor(err) {
+			observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr,
+				fmt.Errorf("check %s against %s in %s: %w", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref, candidate.dir, err))
+		}
+	}
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
+	}
+	return false, observationErr
+}
+
+func gitNotAncestor(err error) bool {
+	var exitErr *exec.ExitError
+	return errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1
+}
+
+func joinReadinessError(current, next error) error {
+	if current == nil {
+		return next
+	}
+	if next == nil {
+		return current
+	}
+	return errors.Join(current, next)

+func revalidatePreparedIntent(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
+	repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact checkout before arming intent: %w", err)
+	}
+	checkout, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.Root)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize revalidated artifact checkout: %w", err)
+	}
+	expectedCheckout, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize prepared artifact checkout: %w", err)
+	}
+	commonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize revalidated artifact Git common directory: %w", err)
+	}
+	expectedCommon, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.GitCommonDir)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize prepared artifact Git common directory: %w", err)
+	}
+	if checkout != expectedCheckout || commonDir != expectedCommon {
+		return fmt.Errorf("artifact checkout identity changed before intent creation")
+	}
+	status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact checkout status: %w", err)
+	}
+	if status.Detached || status.Branch != intent.Branch {
+		return fmt.Errorf("artifact checkout branch changed from %s to %s before intent creation", intent.Branch, status.Branch)
+	}
+	if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(checkout); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact Git operation: %w", err)
+	} else if active {
+		return fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation refuses Git operation %s that started before intent creation", operation)
+	}
+	head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact checkout HEAD: %w", err)
+	}
+	if strings.TrimSpace(head) != strings.TrimSpace(intent.Head) {
+		return fmt.Errorf("artifact checkout HEAD changed before intent creation")
+	}
+	return nil
+}

```text
--- repo CLAUDE
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.

## Toolchain and commands

- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.

```bash
make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
make test                          # go test ./...
go test -race ./...                # CI test command
go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
make vet                           # go vet ./...
files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
```

Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:

```bash
uv sync --frozen --extra docs
uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
uv run mkdocs build --strict
uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
```

If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.

## Architecture

The executable path is deliberately shallow:

```text
cmd/dev/main.go
  -> cli.Execute()
  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
  -> App.Load()
  -> Cobra command handler
  -> domain package(s)
```

`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:

- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.

The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.

State is split intentionally:

- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.

## Behavioral contracts

- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.

## Versioning and changelog

The current published baseline is `v0.2.3` (2026-09-01). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:

- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.

Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.

**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.

- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.

**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.

For a release:

1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, and create the GitHub release.

Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.

## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned

`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.

| Change | Required synchronization |
|---|---|
| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |

`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.

English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.

68		}

84		}

88			path     string
89		}

96			if canonicalErr != nil {

136	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {

177			case "locked":

181			case "prunable":
182				if cur != nil {
183					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
184				}
185			}
186		}

188		return list, nil
189	}

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
19	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
20	
21	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
22	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
23	type Error struct {
24		Args   []string
25		Dir    string
26		Stderr string
27		Err    error
28	}
29	
30	func (e *Error) Error() string {
31		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
32		if msg == "" {
33			msg = e.Err.Error()
34		}
35		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
36	}
37	
38	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
39	
40	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
41	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
42		return runEnv(ctx, dir, nil, args...)
43	}
44	
45	// runEnv executes git with task-scoped environment overrides. It is used for
46	// alternate-index analysis that must never touch the user's real index.
47	func runEnv(ctx context.Context, dir string, overrides []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
48		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
49		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
50		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
51		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
52		cmd.Dir = dir
53		if len(overrides) > 0 {
54			keys := make(map[string]bool, len(overrides))
55			for _, override := range overrides {
56				key, _, _ := strings.Cut(override, "=")
57				keys[key] = true
58			}
59			env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+len(overrides))
60			for _, entry := range os.Environ() {
61				key, _, _ := strings.Cut(entry, "=")
62				if !keys[key] {
63					env = append(env, entry)
64				}
65			}
66			env = append(env, overrides...)
67			cmd.Env = env
68		}
69		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
70		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
71		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
72		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
73			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
74			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
75				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
76			}
77			return "", gerr
78		}
79		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
80	}
81	
82	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
83	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
84	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
85		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
86	}
87	
88	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
89	func lines(s string) []string {
90		if s == "" {
91			return nil
92		}
93		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
94		filtered := out[:0]
95		for _, l := range out {
96			if l != "" {
97				filtered = append(filtered, l)
98			}
99		}
100		return filtered
101	}
102	
103	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
104	func nulLines(s string) []string {
105		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
106		if s == "" {
107			return nil
108		}
109		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
110	}
111

582	func effectCodes(plan Plan) []EffectCode {
583		effects := plan.Effects()
584		codes := make([]EffectCode, len(effects))
585		for index, effect := range effects {
586			codes[index] = effect.Code
587		}
588		return codes

591	func mustGitCommand(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) string {
592		t.Helper()
593		var command *exec.Cmd
594		if len(args) > 0 && args[0] == "init" && len(args) >= 3 && args[1] == "--bare" {
595			command = exec.Command("git", args...)
596			command.Dir = dir
597		} else if len(args) > 0 && args[0] == "init" && len(args) >= 3 && args[1] == "-b" {
598			command = exec.Command("git", args...)
599			command.Dir = dir
600		} else {
601			commandArgs := append([]string{"-C", dir}, args...)
602			command = exec.Command("git", commandArgs...)
603		}
604		output, err := command.CombinedOutput()
605		if err != nil {
606			t.Fatalf("git in %s %s: %v\n%s", dir, strings.Join(args, " "), err, output)
607		}
608		return strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
609	}

 			if cur != nil {
 				cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
 			}
 		}

+		Status              string          `json:"status"`
+		IsDraft             *bool           `json:"isDraft"`
+		SourceRefName       string          `json:"sourceRefName"`
+		TargetRefName       string          `json:"targetRefName"`
+		RemoteURL           string          `json:"remoteUrl"`
+		RepositoryRemoteURL string          `json:"repositoryRemoteUrl"`
+		ForkSource          json.RawMessage `json:"forkSource"`
+	}
+	if err := decodeReviewJSON(AzureDevOps, out, &raw); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	candidates := make([]reviewCandidate, 0, len(raw))
+	for _, item := range raw {
+		id, number := "", 0
+		if item.PullRequestID != nil {
+			number = *item.PullRequestID
+			id = strconv.Itoa(number)
+		}
+		reviewURL := item.RemoteURL

+			URL: reviewURL, Head: azureReviewBranch(item.SourceRefName), Base: azureReviewBranch(item.TargetRefName),

35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}

67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {

71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {

107		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
108			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
109				return cand

115	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
116	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
117		if name == "" {
118			name = "origin"
119		}
120		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
121		if err != nil {
122			return ""
123		}
124		return out
125	}
126	
127	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
128	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
129	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
130	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
131	// semantics should use Remote instead.
132	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
133		if commonDir == "" {
134			return ""
135		}
136		if name == "" {
137			name = "origin"
138		}
139		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
140		if err != nil {
141			return ""
142		}
143		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
144		section := ""
145		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
146			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
147			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
148				continue
149			}
150			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
151				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
152				continue
153			}
154			if section != want {
155				continue
156			}
157			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
158			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
159				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
160			}
161		}
162		return ""
163	}
164

12	// Status is the live git state of one checkout — everything dev's inventory

44	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
45	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
46	
47	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
48	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
49	
50	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
51	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
52	
53	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
54	//
55	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
56	//
57	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
58	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
59	func (s Status) Summary() string {
60		var parts []string
61		switch {
62		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
63			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
64		case s.Ahead > 0:
65			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
66		case s.Behind > 0:
67			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
68		}
69		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
70			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
71		}
72		if s.Staged > 0 {
73			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
74		}
75		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
76			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
77		}
78		if s.Untracked > 0 {
79			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
80		}
81		if len(parts) == 0 {
82			if !s.Published() {
83				return "local"
84			}
85			return "clean"
86		}
87		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
88	}

90	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
91	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
92	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
93	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
94		if s.Changed == 0 {
95			return "0 changed paths"

98		if s.Staged > 0 {
99			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")

114	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {

116		for _, item := range []struct {

118			name string
119		}{

121			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
122		} {

125			}

130	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
131	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
132	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
133	// everything it needs.
134	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
135		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
136		if err != nil {
137			return Status{}, err
138		}
139		return statusFromOutput(dir, out), nil
140	}
141	
142	func statusFromOutput(dir, out string) Status {
143		var s Status
144		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
145			if rec == "" {
146				continue
147			}
148			switch rec[0] {
149			case '#':
150				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
151			case '1', '2':
152				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
153				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
154				// when both sides are non-dot.
155				f := strings.Fields(rec)
156				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
157					continue
158				}
159				s.Changed++
160				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
161				if x != '.' {
162					s.Staged++
163				}
164				if y != '.' {
165					s.Unstaged++
166				}
167				classifyChange(x, &s)
168				classifyChange(y, &s)
169				updateLatestChange(dir, statusPath(rec), &s)
170			case 'u':
171				s.Changed++
172				s.Conflicted++
173				updateLatestChange(dir, statusPath(rec), &s)
174			case '?':
175				s.Changed++
176				s.Untracked++
177				updateLatestChange(dir, strings.TrimPrefix(rec, "? "), &s)
178			}
179		}
180		return s
181	}
182	
183	// statusPath extracts the final pathname from a porcelain-v2 record while
184	// preserving spaces in it. Rename records have one extra score field; their
185	// old path arrives as the next NUL record and is intentionally ignored.
186	func statusPath(rec string) string {
187		if rec == "" {
188			return ""
189		}
190		var fields int
191		switch rec[0] {
192		case '1':
193			fields = 9
194		case '2':
195			fields = 10
196		case 'u':
197			fields = 11
198		default:
199			return ""
200		}
201		parts := strings.SplitN(rec, " ", fields)
202		if len(parts) != fields {
203			return ""
204		}
205		return parts[fields-1]
206	}
207	
208	func updateLatestChange(dir, path string, s *Status) {
209		if path == "" {
210			return
211		}
212		info, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, filepath.FromSlash(path)))
213		if err == nil && info.ModTime().After(s.LatestChange) {
214			s.LatestChange = info.ModTime()
215		}
216	}
217	
218	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
219		switch code {
220		case 'A':
221			s.Added++
222		case 'M', 'T':
223			s.Modified++
224		case 'D':
225			s.Deleted++
226		case 'R', 'C':
227			s.Renamed++
228		}
229	}
230	
231	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
232		f := strings.Fields(rec)
233		if len(f) < 3 {
234			return
235		}
236		switch f[1] {
237		case "branch.head":
238			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
239				s.Detached = true
240			} else {
241				s.Branch = f[2]
242			}
243		case "branch.upstream":
244			s.Upstream = f[2]
245		case "branch.ab":
246			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
247			if len(f) < 4 {
248				return
249			}
250			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))

docs/guides/agent-safe-retirement.zh-TW.md:110:`--close-unknown` 與 `--assume-no-runtime` 只放寬 fail-closed 的*觀測結果*（無法讀取的 status、無法列舉的 runtime list）。這兩個 flag 都絕不會 bypass caller containment 或 active-agent state。`retirement.Service.Retire` 在 runtime session 關閉後，也會重新驗證 target identity、Git ancestry、進行中的 Git operation（`gitx.InProgress`，檢查 `MERGE_HEAD`、`CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`、`REVERT_HEAD`、`rebase-merge`、`rebase-apply`、`sequencer`；不含 `REBASE_HEAD`，因為 Git 在 rebase 完成後仍會保留它）以及 worktree 是否 clean——因為 runtime draining 期間現實可能已改變，先前的驗證結果不會跨越這個邊界沿用。

323			if len(c.Checkouts) < 2 {
324				return nil
325			}
326			return c.Checkouts[1:]
327		}
328		out := make([]RepoCheckout, 0, len(c.Checkouts)-1)
329		for _, checkout := range c.Checkouts {
330			if !checkout.Worktree.Main {
331				out = append(out, checkout)
332			}
333		}
334		return out
335	}
336	
337	// Sessions returns the repo's live sessions once each, preserving checkout
338	// order so a pasted context reads canonical-first.
339	func (c RepoContext) Sessions() []runtime.Session {
340		seen := map[string]bool{}
341		var out []runtime.Session
342		for _, checkout := range c.Checkouts {
343			for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
344				key := session.Handle
345				if key == "" {
346					key = session.Label + "\x00" + strings.Join(session.Dirs, "\x00")
347				}
348				if seen[key] {
349					continue
350				}
351				seen[key] = true
352				out = append(out, session)
353			}
354		}
355		return out
356	}
357	
358	// RepoContextOptions extends repository collection without changing the
359	// original CollectRepoContext API used by CLI and dashboard callers.
360	type RepoContextOptions struct {
361		Runtime         string
362		Sessions        []runtime.Session
363		RuntimeObserved bool
364		RuntimeErr      error
365		// Limiter shares one process-heavy enrichment bound across collectors.
366		Limiter *Limiter
367	}
368	
369	// CollectRepoContext joins Git, task and runtime state for one repository. The
370	// legacy entry point can prove observation only when sessions are present;
371	// callers that need a proven empty observation or typed failure use
372	// CollectRepoContextWithOptions.
373	func CollectRepoContext(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, tasks []*task.Task,
374		sessions []runtime.Session, runtimeName string) RepoContext {
375		return CollectRepoContextWithOptions(ctx, r, tasks, RepoContextOptions{
376			Runtime: runtimeName, Sessions: sessions, RuntimeObserved: len(sessions) > 0,
377		})
378	}
379	
380	// CollectRepoContextWithOptions builds repository topology from Git's complete
381	// registered worktree list. It never synthesizes a main checkout after a Git
382	// query failure.
383	func CollectRepoContextWithOptions(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, tasks []*task.Task,
384		opts RepoContextOptions) RepoContext {
385		if ctx == nil {
386			ctx = context.Background()
387		}
388		out := RepoContext{
389			Repo: r, Runtime: opts.Runtime,
390			WorktreeObservation: TopologyObservation{State: ObservationUnobserved},
391			RuntimeObservation:  runtimeObservation(opts),
392		}
393		queryPath := repoQueryPath(r)
394		out.RepositoryID, out.IdentityErr = canonicalRepositoryID(ctx, r, queryPath)
395		out.WorktreeCount = linkedAdminCount(r.CommonDir)
396	
397		var (
398			worktrees []gitx.Worktree
399			err       error
400		)
401		if queryPath == "" {
402			err = fmt.Errorf("repository has no Git query path")
403		} else {
404			worktrees, err = gitx.Worktrees(ctx, queryPath)
405		}
406		if err != nil {
407			listErr := &WorktreeListError{Path: queryPath, Err: err}
408			out.WorktreeErr = listErr
409			out.WorktreeObservation = TopologyObservation{State: ObservationFailed, Err: listErr}
410			assignTasksWithoutTopology(&out, tasks)
411			finishRepoContext(&out)
412			return out
413		}
414		out.WorktreeObservation = TopologyObservation{State: ObservationAvailable}
415		out.WorktreeCount = 0
416		out.Checkouts = make([]RepoCheckout, 0, len(worktrees))
417		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
418			canonicalPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(worktree.Path)
419			if canonicalPath == "" {
420				canonicalPath = filepath.Clean(worktree.Path)
421			}
422			checkout := RepoCheckout{
423				ID: canonicalPath, RepositoryID: out.RepositoryID,
424				IdentityErr: canonicalErr,
425				Worktree:    worktree, Exists: pathIsDir(worktree.Path),
426				RuntimeObservation: out.RuntimeObservation,
427				Ownership:          CheckoutExternal,
428			}
429			if canonicalErr != nil {
430				checkout.ConflictReasons = appendReason(checkout.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
431					Code: ReasonCanonicalPathUnavailable, Detail: canonicalErr.Error(),
432				})
433			}
434			if worktree.Main {
435				checkout.OwnershipEvidence = append(checkout.OwnershipEvidence, OwnershipEvidence{
436					Kind: OwnershipEvidenceGitMain, Path: canonicalPath,
437				})
438			} else {
439				out.WorktreeCount++
440			}
441			out.Checkouts = append(out.Checkouts, checkout)
442		}
443	
444		enrichRepoCheckouts(ctx, out.Checkouts, opts.Limiter)
445		assignHarnessEvidence(&out)
446		assignTasks(&out, tasks)
447		if out.RuntimeObservation.Available() {
448			assignSessions(&out, opts.Sessions)
449		}
450		finishRepoContext(&out)
451		return out
452	}
453	
454	func runtimeObservation(opts RepoContextOptions) TopologyObservation {
455		if opts.RuntimeErr != nil {
456			err := &RuntimeListError{Runtime: opts.Runtime, Err: opts.RuntimeErr}
457			return TopologyObservation{State: ObservationFailed, Err: err}
458		}
459		if opts.RuntimeObserved {
460			return TopologyObservation{State: ObservationAvailable}
461		}
462		return TopologyObservation{State: ObservationUnobserved}
463	}
464	
465	func repoQueryPath(r repo.Repo) string {
466		for _, candidate := range []string{r.Path, r.RealPath, r.MainRoot, r.CommonDir} {
467			if candidate != "" {
468				return candidate
469			}
470		}
471		return ""
472	}
473	
474	func canonicalRepositoryID(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, queryPath string) (string, error) {
475		commonDir := r.CommonDir
476		if commonDir == "" && r.Bare {
477			commonDir = queryPath
478		}
479		if commonDir == "" && queryPath != "" {
480			if discovered, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, queryPath); err == nil {
481				commonDir = discovered.GitCommonDir
482			}
483		}
484		if commonDir == "" {
485			err := fmt.Errorf("Git common directory is empty")
486			return "", &RepositoryIdentityError{Path: commonDir, Err: err}
487		}
488		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(commonDir)
489		if err != nil {
490			return "", &RepositoryIdentityError{Path: commonDir, Err: err}
491		}
492		return canonical, nil
493	}
494	
495	func enrichRepoCheckouts(ctx context.Context, checkouts []RepoCheckout, limiter *Limiter) {
496		if limiter == nil {
497			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
498		}
499		var wg sync.WaitGroup
500		for i := range checkouts {
501			if checkouts[i].Worktree.Bare || checkouts[i].Worktree.Prunable || !checkouts[i].Exists {
502				continue
503			}
504			wg.Add(1)
505			go func(index int) {
506				defer wg.Done()
507				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
508				if !ok {
509					checkouts[index].StatusErr = ctx.Err()
510					return
511				}
512				defer release()
513				checkout := &checkouts[index]
514				checkout.Status, checkout.StatusErr = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout.Worktree.Path)
515				checkout.LastActivity, checkout.LastCommit, checkout.LastSubject = checkoutActivity(
516					ctx, checkout.Worktree.Path, checkout.Status,
517				)
518			}(i)
519		}
520		wg.Wait()
521	}
522	
523	func assignHarnessEvidence(out *RepoContext) {
524		mainRoot := ""
525		for i := range out.Checkouts {
526			if out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Main && !out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Bare {
527				mainRoot = out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Path
528				break
529			}
530		}
531		if mainRoot == "" {
532			return
533		}
534		for i := range out.Checkouts {
535			checkout := &out.Checkouts[i]
536			if checkout.Worktree.Main {
537				continue
538			}
539			evidence, ok := DetectClaudeHarnessWorktree(mainRoot, checkout.Worktree.Path)
540			if !ok {
541				continue
542			}
543			checkout.HarnessEvidence = &evidence
544			checkout.OwnershipEvidence = append(checkout.OwnershipEvidence, OwnershipEvidence{
545				Kind: OwnershipEvidenceClaudeHarness, Path: evidence.Root,
546			})
547		}
548	}
549	
550	// IsEphemeralWorktree is the legacy broad display heuristic. Its branch-prefix
551	// compatibility is retained for existing adopters, but authoritative topology
552	// uses DetectClaudeHarnessWorktree: a worktree-* branch alone is not ownership
553	// evidence.
554	func IsEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {
555		slashPath := filepath.ToSlash(path)
556		return strings.Contains(slashPath, "/.claude/worktrees/") ||
557			strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")
558	}
559	
560	func linkedAdminCount(commonDir string) int {
561		if commonDir == "" {
562			return 0
563		}
564		entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(commonDir, "worktrees"))
565		if err != nil {
566			return 0
567		}
568		n := 0
569		for _, entry := range entries {
570			if entry.IsDir() {
571				n++
572			}
573		}
574		return n
575	}
576	
577	func pathIsDir(path string) bool {
578		info, err := os.Stat(path)
579		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
580	}
581	
582	func checkoutActivity(ctx context.Context, path string, status gitx.Status) (time.Time, time.Time, string) {
583		latest := status.LatestChange
584		var commit time.Time
585		var subject string
586		if unix, lastSubject, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, path); err == nil && unix > 0 {
587			commit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
588			if commit.After(latest) {
589				latest = commit
590			}
591			subject = lastSubject
592		}
593		return latest, commit, subject
594	}
595	
596	func assignTasksWithoutTopology(out *RepoContext, tasks []*task.Task) {
597		for _, tracked := range sortedUniqueTasks(tasks) {
598			binding := TaskBinding{
599				Task: tracked, Kind: TaskBindingUnbound,
600				ConflictReasons: []TopologyReason{{
601					Code:   ReasonWorktreeInventoryUnavailable,
602					Detail: "registered worktrees could not be observed",
603				}},
604			}
605			out.OtherTasks = append(out.OtherTasks, tracked)
606			out.OtherTaskBindings = append(out.OtherTaskBindings, binding)
607		}
608	}
609	
610	func assignTasks(out *RepoContext, tasks []*task.Task) {
611		paths := map[string][]int{}
612		branches := map[string][]int{}
613		mainIndex := -1
614		for i := range out.Checkouts {
615			checkout := &out.Checkouts[i]
616			if checkout.ID != "" {
617				paths[checkout.ID] = append(paths[checkout.ID], i)
618			}
619			if branch := checkout.Branch(); branch != "" && !checkout.Worktree.Bare {
620				branches[branch] = append(branches[branch], i)
621			}
622			if checkout.Worktree.Main {
623				mainIndex = i
624			}
625		}
626	
627		for _, tracked := range sortedUniqueTasks(tasks) {
628			binding := TaskBinding{Task: tracked, Kind: TaskBindingUnbound}
629			mode := tracked.EffectiveMode()
630			var recordedPathIssue *TopologyReason
631			if tracked.WorktreePath != "" {
632				canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(tracked.WorktreePath)
633				if err != nil {
634					reason := TopologyReason{Code: ReasonCanonicalPathUnavailable, Detail: err.Error()}
635					recordedPathIssue = &reason
636				} else if mode == task.ModeWorktree {
637					if matches := paths[canonical]; len(matches) > 0 {
638						if len(matches) == 1 {
639							binding.Kind = TaskBindingExactPath
640							bindTask(out, matches[0], annotateBoundTask(binding, out.Checkouts[matches[0]]))
641							continue
642						}
643						reason := TopologyReason{
644							Code:   ReasonAmbiguousCheckout,
645							Detail: fmt.Sprintf("task %s path matches %d registered checkout records", tracked.ID, len(matches)),
646						}
647						binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, reason)
648						for _, index := range matches {
649							out.Checkouts[index].ConflictReasons = appendReason(out.Checkouts[index].ConflictReasons, reason)
650						}
651						appendOtherTask(out, binding)
652						continue
653					}
654				}
655				if mode != task.ModeWorktree {
656					binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
657						Code: ReasonTaskModeMismatch,
658						Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s task %s records worktree_path %s",
659							mode, tracked.ID, tracked.WorktreePath),
660					})
661				}
662			}
663	
664			if mode == task.ModeWorktree {
665				matches := branches[tracked.Branch]
666				switch len(matches) {
667				case 1:
668					binding.Kind = TaskBindingMovedPath
669					binding.DriftReasons = appendReason(binding.DriftReasons, movedPathReason(tracked, out.Checkouts[matches[0]]))
670					if recordedPathIssue != nil {
671						binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, *recordedPathIssue)
672					}
673					bindTask(out, matches[0], annotateBoundTask(binding, out.Checkouts[matches[0]]))
674					continue
675				case 0:
676					if recordedPathIssue != nil {
677						binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, *recordedPathIssue)
678					}
679					if tracked.WorktreePath != "" || taskExpectsCheckout(tracked) {
680						binding.DriftReasons = appendReason(binding.DriftReasons, TopologyReason{
681							Code:   ReasonWorktreePathMissing,
682							Detail: fmt.Sprintf("task %s has no registered checkout for branch %s", tracked.ID, tracked.Branch),
683						})
684					}
685				default:
686					reason := TopologyReason{
687						Code:   ReasonAmbiguousCheckout,
688						Detail: fmt.Sprintf("task %s branch %s matches %d registered checkouts", tracked.ID, tracked.Branch, len(matches)),
689					}
690					binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, reason)
691					for _, index := range matches {
692						out.Checkouts[index].ConflictReasons = appendReason(out.Checkouts[index].ConflictReasons, reason)
693					}
694				}
695				appendOtherTask(out, binding)
696				continue
697			}
698	
699			if mainIndex >= 0 {
700				main := out.Checkouts[mainIndex]
701				if checkoutActionable(main) && main.Branch() == tracked.Branch {
702					binding.Kind = TaskBindingMainBranch
703					if recordedPathIssue != nil {
704						binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, *recordedPathIssue)
705					}
706					bindTask(out, mainIndex, annotateBoundTask(binding, main))
707					continue
708				}
709			}
710	
711			if recordedPathIssue != nil {
712				binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, *recordedPathIssue)
713			}
714			for _, index := range branches[tracked.Branch] {
715				if index == mainIndex {
716					continue
717				}
718				reason := TopologyReason{
719					Code: ReasonTaskModeMismatch,
720					Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s task %s branch is checked out outside Git main at %s",
721						mode, tracked.ID, out.Checkouts[index].Worktree.Path),
722				}
723				binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, reason)
724				out.Checkouts[index].ConflictReasons = appendReason(out.Checkouts[index].ConflictReasons, reason)
725			}
726			if taskExpectsCheckout(tracked) {
727				detail := fmt.Sprintf("task %s expects branch %s in Git main", tracked.ID, tracked.Branch)
728				switch {
729				case mainIndex < 0:
730					detail += ", but no Git main record exists"
731				case !checkoutActionable(out.Checkouts[mainIndex]):
732					detail += ", but Git main is missing, prunable, bare, or unreadable"
733				default:
734					detail += fmt.Sprintf(", which is on %s", displayBranch(out.Checkouts[mainIndex]))
735				}
736				binding.DriftReasons = appendReason(binding.DriftReasons, TopologyReason{
737					Code: ReasonMainBranchMismatch, Detail: detail,
738				})
739			}
740			appendOtherTask(out, binding)
741		}
742	
743		finalizeCheckoutClaims(out)
744	}
745	
746	func sortedUniqueTasks(tasks []*task.Task) []*task.Task {
747		ordered := append([]*task.Task(nil), tasks...)
748		sort.SliceStable(ordered, func(i, j int) bool {
749			if ordered[i] == nil {
750				return false
751			}
752			if ordered[j] == nil {
753				return true
754			}
755			return ordered[i].ID < ordered[j].ID
756		})
757		seen := map[string]bool{}
758		out := make([]*task.Task, 0, len(ordered))
759		for _, tracked := range ordered {
760			if tracked == nil {
761				continue
762			}
763			if tracked.ID != "" && seen[tracked.ID] {
764				continue
765			}
766			if tracked.ID != "" {
767				seen[tracked.ID] = true
768			}
769			out = append(out, tracked)
770		}
771		return out
772	}
773	
774	func movedPathReason(tracked *task.Task, checkout RepoCheckout) TopologyReason {
775		if tracked.WorktreePath == "" {
776			return TopologyReason{
777				Code: ReasonWorktreePathMoved,
778				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("task %s has no recorded worktree path; branch %s is registered at %s",
779					tracked.ID, tracked.Branch, checkout.Worktree.Path),
780			}
781		}
782		return TopologyReason{
783			Code: ReasonWorktreePathMoved,
784			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("task %s records %s; branch %s is registered at %s",
785				tracked.ID, tracked.WorktreePath, tracked.Branch, checkout.Worktree.Path),
786		}
787	}
788	
789	func annotateBoundTask(binding TaskBinding, checkout RepoCheckout) TaskBinding {
790		tracked := binding.Task
791		if tracked == nil {
792			return binding
793		}
794		if !checkoutActionable(checkout) {
795			binding.DriftReasons = appendReason(binding.DriftReasons, TopologyReason{
796				Code: ReasonCheckoutUnavailable,
797				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("registered checkout %s is missing, prunable, bare, or unreadable",
798					checkout.Worktree.Path),
799			})
800		}
801		if checkout.Branch() != tracked.Branch {
802			binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
803				Code: ReasonBranchMismatch,
804				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("task %s expects branch %s; registered checkout is on %s",
805					tracked.ID, tracked.Branch, displayBranch(checkout)),
806			})
807		}
808		mode := tracked.EffectiveMode()
809		switch {
810		case mode == task.ModeWorktree && checkout.Worktree.Main:
811			binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
812				Code:   ReasonTaskModeMismatch,
813				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("worktree task %s resolved to Git main", tracked.ID),
814			})
815		case mode != task.ModeWorktree && !checkout.Worktree.Main:
816			binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
817				Code: ReasonTaskModeMismatch,
818				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s task %s resolved to linked worktree %s",
819					mode, tracked.ID, checkout.Worktree.Path),
820			})
821		}
822		if mode != task.ModeWorktree && tracked.WorktreePath != "" {
823			binding.ConflictReasons = appendReason(binding.ConflictReasons, TopologyReason{
824				Code: ReasonTaskModeMismatch,
825				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s task %s records worktree_path %s",
826					mode, tracked.ID, tracked.WorktreePath),
827			})
828		}
829		if !taskExpectsCheckout(tracked) {
830			binding.DriftReasons = appendReason(binding.DriftReasons, TopologyReason{
831				Code: ReasonUnexpectedCheckout,
832				Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s task %s still has registered checkout %s",
833					tracked.State, tracked.ID, checkout.Worktree.Path),
834			})
835		}
836		return binding
837	}
838	
839	func taskExpectsCheckout(tracked *task.Task) bool {
840		if tracked == nil || tracked.State == task.Cold {
841			return false
842		}
843		if tracked.State == task.Done && tracked.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeWorktree {
844			return tracked.WorktreePath != ""
845		}
846		return true
847	}
848	
849	func checkoutActionable(checkout RepoCheckout) bool {
850		return !checkout.Worktree.Bare && !checkout.Worktree.Prunable && checkout.Exists && checkout.StatusErr == nil
851	}
852	
853	func bindTask(out *RepoContext, index int, binding TaskBinding) {
854		checkout := &out.Checkouts[index]
855		binding.CheckoutID = checkout.ID
856		checkout.TaskBindings = append(checkout.TaskBindings, binding)
857		checkout.Tasks = append(checkout.Tasks, binding.Task)
858		if binding.Task.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeWorktree {
859			checkout.OwnershipEvidence = append(checkout.OwnershipEvidence, OwnershipEvidence{
860				Kind: OwnershipEvidenceManagedTask, Path: checkout.ID,
861				TaskID: binding.Task.ID, Owner: binding.Task.Owner,
862			})
863		}
864	}
865	
866	func appendOtherTask(out *RepoContext, binding TaskBinding) {
867		out.OtherTasks = append(out.OtherTasks, binding.Task)
868		out.OtherTaskBindings = append(out.OtherTaskBindings, binding)
869	}
870	
871	func finalizeCheckoutClaims(out *RepoContext) {
872		for i := range out.Checkouts {
873			checkout := &out.Checkouts[i]
874			sort.SliceStable(checkout.TaskBindings, func(a, b int) bool {
875				return checkout.TaskBindings[a].Task.ID < checkout.TaskBindings[b].Task.ID
876			})
877			sort.SliceStable(checkout.Tasks, func(a, b int) bool {
878				return checkout.Tasks[a].ID < checkout.Tasks[b].ID
879			})
880			if len(checkout.TaskBindings) > 1 {
881				ids := make([]string, len(checkout.TaskBindings))
882				for j := range checkout.TaskBindings {
883					ids[j] = checkout.TaskBindings[j].Task.ID
884				}
885				reason := TopologyReason{
886					Code:   ReasonMultipleTaskClaims,
887					Detail: fmt.Sprintf("registered checkout is claimed by tasks %s", strings.Join(ids, ", ")),
888				}
889				checkout.ConflictReasons = appendReason(checkout.ConflictReasons, reason)
890				for j := range checkout.TaskBindings {
891					checkout.TaskBindings[j].ConflictReasons = appendReason(
892						checkout.TaskBindings[j].ConflictReasons, reason,
893					)
894				}
895			}
896			if checkout.HarnessEvidence != nil && len(checkout.TaskBindings) > 0 {
897				reason := TopologyReason{
898					Code: ReasonHarnessTaskConflict,
899					Detail: fmt.Sprintf("checkout has Claude harness evidence and %d managed task claim(s)",
900						len(checkout.TaskBindings)),
901				}
902				checkout.ConflictReasons = appendReason(checkout.ConflictReasons, reason)
903				for j := range checkout.TaskBindings {
904					checkout.TaskBindings[j].ConflictReasons = appendReason(
905						checkout.TaskBindings[j].ConflictReasons, reason,
906					)
907				}
908			}
909			for _, binding := range checkout.TaskBindings {
910				for _, reason := range binding.DriftReasons {
911					checkout.DriftReasons = appendReason(checkout.DriftReasons, reason)
912				}
913				for _, reason := range binding.ConflictReasons {
914					checkout.ConflictReasons = appendReason(checkout.ConflictReasons, reason)
915				}
916			}
917			checkout.Ownership = displayOwnership(*checkout)
918		}
919	}
920	
921	func displayOwnership(checkout RepoCheckout) CheckoutOwnership {
922		if checkout.Worktree.Main {
923			return CheckoutCanonical
924		}
925		if checkout.HarnessEvidence != nil {
926			return CheckoutEphemeral
927		}
928		for _, evidence := range checkout.OwnershipEvidence {
929			if evidence.Kind == OwnershipEvidenceManagedTask {
930				return CheckoutDev
931			}

987	// assignSessions assigns each observed directory to the most-specific
988	// checkout. A session rooted in repo/.claude/worktrees/x therefore belongs to
989	// x, not to the canonical checkout which also happens to contain that path.
990	func assignSessions(out *RepoContext, sessions []runtime.Session) {
991		for _, session := range sessions {
992			assigned := map[int]bool{}
993			for _, dir := range session.Dirs {
994				best, bestLen := -1, -1
995				for i := range out.Checkouts {
996					for _, root := range checkoutRoots(out.Checkouts[i]) {
997						if pathContains(root, dir) && len(normalizePath(root)) > bestLen {
998							best, bestLen = i, len(normalizePath(root))
999						}
1000					}
1001				}
1002				if best >= 0 {
1003					assigned[best] = true
1004				}
1005			}
1006			for i := range assigned {
1007				out.Checkouts[i].Sessions = append(out.Checkouts[i].Sessions, session)
1008			}
1009		}
1010	}

1012	func checkoutRoots(checkout RepoCheckout) []string {
1013		return []string{checkout.Worktree.Path}

1016	func pathContains(root, path string) bool {
1017		if root == "" || path == "" {
1018			return false
1019		}
1020		rel, err := filepath.Rel(normalizePath(root), normalizePath(path))
1021		if err != nil || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
1022			return false
1023		}
1024		return rel == "." || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
1025	}
1026	
1027	// normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
1028	// paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
1029	// also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
1030	// is not sufficient.
1031	func normalizePath(path string) string {
1032		if canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(path); err == nil {
1033			return canonical
1034		}
1035		return filepath.Clean(path)
1036	}

1084	func writeCheckoutMarkdown(b *strings.Builder, c RepoContext, checkout RepoCheckout, canonical bool) {
1085		label := string(checkout.Ownership)
1086		if canonical {
1087			label = "canonical"
1088		}
1089		fmt.Fprintf(b, "### %s — %s\n\n", displayBranch(checkout), label)
1090		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Path: `%s`\n", checkout.Worktree.Path)
1091		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Branch: `%s`\n", displayBranch(checkout))
1092		if checkout.Worktree.Bare {
1093			b.WriteString("- Git: bare repository\n")
1094		} else if checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists {
1095			b.WriteString("- Git: unavailable (checkout path is missing)\n")
1096		} else if checkout.StatusErr != nil {
1097			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: unavailable (%s)\n", checkout.StatusErr)
1098		} else {
1099			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: %s", checkout.Status.Summary())
1100			if checkout.Status.Dirty() {
1101				fmt.Fprintf(b, " — %s", checkout.Status.Breakdown())
1102			}
1103			b.WriteString("\n")
1104			if checkout.Status.Upstream != "" {
1105				fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Upstream: `%s`\n", checkout.Status.Upstream)
1106			} else {
1107				b.WriteString("- Upstream: not published\n")
1108			}
1109		}
1110		if checkout.Worktree.Locked {
1111			reason := strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.LockedReason)
1112			if reason == "" {
1113				reason = "no reason recorded"
1114			}
1115			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Worktree: locked — %s\n", reason)
1116		}
1117		if checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists {
1118			reason := strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.PrunableReason)
1119			if reason == "" {
1120				reason = "checkout path is missing"
1121			}
1122			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Worktree: prunable — %s\n", reason)
1123		}
1124		if len(checkout.Sessions) == 0 {
1125			b.WriteString("- Runtime: closed\n")
1126		} else {
1127			for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
1128				status := session.AgentStatus
1129				if status == "" {
1130					status = "unknown"
1131				}
1132				fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Runtime: `%s %s` (%s)\n", c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
1133				if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
1134					fmt.Fprintf(b, "  - Agent sessions: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))
1135				}
1136			}
1137		}
1138		if len(checkout.Tasks) == 0 {
1139			b.WriteString("- Task: untracked\n")
1140		} else {
1141			for _, tracked := range checkout.Tasks {
1142				writeTaskMarkdown(b, tracked)
1143			}
1144		}
1145		writeTopologyReasons(b, checkout.DriftReasons, checkout.ConflictReasons)
1146	}

1188	func FormatSessions(c RepoContext, checkoutIndex int) string {
1189		indices := make([]int, 0, len(c.Checkouts))
1190		if checkoutIndex >= 0 && checkoutIndex < len(c.Checkouts) {
1191			indices = append(indices, checkoutIndex)

1193			for i := range c.Checkouts {
1194				indices = append(indices, i)

1196		}
1197		var b strings.Builder
1198		for _, i := range indices {
1199			checkout := c.Checkouts[i]
1200			for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
1201				status := session.AgentStatus
1202				if status == "" {
1203					status = "unknown"
1204				}
1205				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s`: `%s %s` (%s)\n",
1206					checkout.Worktree.Path, c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
1207				if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
1208					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - agents: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))
1209				}
1210			}
1211		}
1212		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
1213	}
